2:
Steel cannonballs are ammunition used for a dwarf multicannon, as well as for a boat cannon during boat combat. They can be fired from steel cannons or stronger.

Four can be made from a single steel bar with level 35 Smithing, granting 25.6 experience per bar. Smithing cannonballs require the use of an ammo mould, which requires partial completion of Dwarf Cannon to obtain. Alternatively, a double ammo mould (requiring Foundry Reputation to purchase via the Giants' Foundry minigame) allows players to process two bars into eight cannonballs at the same speed as a regular ammo mould processes one bar into four.

Players with level 87 Sailing can further speed up smithing cannonballs by using the ancient furnace in the Grimstone Dungeon, which halves the time it takes to create cannonballs from 8 ticks to 4 ticks. Combining this with a double ammo mould, players can smith cannonballs at four times the normal speed.

Lastly, players with level 50 Smithing can use granite dust on steel cannonballs to create granite cannonballs, which gives superior stats on boat cannons, and increases the max hit of dwarf multicannons by 5. This yields no experience.
6:
The cannon base is the first part of the dwarf multicannon to be set up, followed by the stand. The Dwarf Cannon quest must be completed to use it. It is purchased from Multicannon parts for sale for 200,625 coins.

The cannon base by itself can decay without having the full cannon set up. When lost, a new cannon base can be obtained from Nulodion, free of charge.
10: Cannon barrels are the third part of the dwarf multicannon set up on top of the cannon base after placing the cannon stand and before the cannon furnace. They shoot the enemy with a barrage of steel cannonballs or granite cannonballs. It is purchased from Multicannon parts for sale for 200,625 coins.
28:
Insect repellent is a container of bug spray that can be used on beehives, large mosquitoes, and mosquito swarms.

Using insect repellent on beehives, located in the apiary west of Catherby and in southern Seers' Village, causes the bees to leave. Using a bucket on the beehive then gives a bucket of wax, which is used in Merlin's Crystal and Troll Romance. Insect repellent must be used on the beehive every time, otherwise the bees will have returned and no wax will be collected.

It is also used on large mosquitoes and mosquito swarms encountered in the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup minigame to halve their combat stats and prevent them from attacking for six seconds. This can be done multiple times until their stats are reduced to 1. Giant mosquitoes found on Mos Le'Harmless are unaffected.
36:
A candle is the lowest tier of Firemaking light sources. It can be lit with a tinderbox. Lit candles can be extinguished by clicking extinguish on them or falling into swamp water in the Lumbridge Caves. Candles may be acquired through various means such as finding them within certain houses, purchasing them from a candle seller or candle maker, or by trading with other players.

A candle is a required item for Enlightened Journey and Enakhra's Lament.
39: I can make some arrows with these.
40:
Iron arrowtips are made with an iron bar requiring 20 Smithing, yielding Smithing 25 experience and 15 iron arrowtips. They are made into iron arrows when used with headless arrows, requiring 15 Fletching, yielding 37.5 experience per 15 arrows.

They are purchased for 2 coins at the ranging shops: Hickton's Archery Emporium in Catherby, Dargaud's Bow and Arrows in the Ranging Guild, Gulluck and Sons on the 2nd floor of the Grand Tree, Void Knight Archery Store at the Void Knights' Outpost, and Ava's Odds and Ends in Draynor Manor. They are purchased for 3 coins at the Armoury in the Combat Training Camp.

44:
Rune arrowtips are made with a runite bar requiring 90 Smithing, yielding 75 Smithing experience and 15 rune arrowtips. They are made into rune arrows when used with headless arrows, requiring 75 Fletching, yielding 187.5 experience per 15 arrows.

They are purchased for 200 coins at the ranging shops: Hickton's Archery Emporium in Catherby, Dargaud's Bow and Arrows in the Ranging Guild, and Void Knight Archery Store at the Void Knights' Outpost.
47: I can make bolts with these.

60: A willow shortbow (u) is made using a knife with willow logs, requiring 35 Fletching and yielding 33.3 Fletching experience. Stringing a willow shortbow (u) with a bowstring makes a willow shortbow, also requiring 35 Fletching and yielding an additional 33.3 Fletching experience.
62: A maple longbow (u) is made using a knife with maple logs, requiring 55 Fletching and yielding 58.3 Fletching experience. Stringing a maple longbow (u) with a bowstring makes a maple longbow, also requiring 55 Fletching and yielding an additional 58.2 Fletching experience.
64: An unstrung maple shortbow; I need a bowstring for this.
66: An unstrung yew longbow; I need a bowstring for this.
68: An unstrung yew shortbow; I need a bowstring for this.
70: A magic longbow (u) is made using a knife with magic logs, requiring 85 Fletching and yielding 91.5 Fletching experience. Stringing a magic longbow (u) with a bowstring makes a magic longbow, also requiring 85 Fletching and yielding an additional 91.5 Fletching experience.

91: I need another ingredient to finish this Guam potion.
93: I need another ingredient to finish this Marrentill potion.
95: A tarromin potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a tarromin on a vial of water, requiring 12 Herblore. Using a limpwurt root on a tarromin potion (unf) with 12 Herblore yields a Strength potion(3) and 50 Herblore experience. In the Shades of Mort'ton quest, after reading the diary of Herbi Flax, using ashes on a tarromin potion (unf) with 15 Herblore yields a Serum 207 (3) and 50 Herblore experience. 97: I need another ingredient to finish this Harralander potion.
99: I need another ingredient to finish this Ranarr potion.

Using a unicorn horn dust on an irit potion (unf) with 48 Herblore yields a superantipoison(3) and 106.3 Herblore experience.
103: An avantoe potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using an avantoe on a vial of water, requiring 50 Herblore. 187: For use on daggers and projectiles.
197: A poison chalice is a cocktail obtained for free from Stankers, a dwarven miner near the Coal Trucks west of Seers' Village. Drinking a poison chalice applies a random effect, and leaves behind an empty cocktail glass. Drinking the poison chalice cannot lower your Hitpoints past 4.
221:
An eye of newt is used in Herblore to make attack potions and super attack potions. They can obtained in bulk by purchasing eye of newt packs from various herblore shops.

One eye of newt is needed for the Witch's Potion and Recipe for Disaster quests. After completing Tower of Life, they can be used in the Creature Creation activity together with a feather to create a newtroost.
225: The root of a limpwurt plant.
231:
Snape grass is a Herblore secondary ingredient that can be grown through the Farming skill at level 61 with snape grass seeds. 8 snape grass are needed to protect growing potato cactus.

It is used to make prayer potions and fishing potions. It is also used when making the hangover cure quest item. When placed in a compost bin, snape grass will create supercompost.

Farming snape grass gives a decent amount of experience and thus is a great way for players (especially ironmen) to train the skill.
233: I can grind things for potions in this.
239:
White berries can be harvested from a bush patch after planting whiteberry seeds. They are used in Herblore to make defence potions and super defences.

Adding them to a compost bin makes supercompost, though this is not recommended as watermelons or pineapples are far cheaper and have the same effect.

Farmers can be paid 10 white berries to protect a camphor tree.
243: Blue dragon scales are an indirect secondary ingredient in Herblore that is ground with a pestle and mortar to create dragon scale dust, which can then be used to make antifire potions and weapon poison. Scales can be found on the ground by the blue dragons in Taverley Dungeon, Corsair Cove Dungeon, part of the Myths' Guild, in the Isle of Souls Dungeon, and in the Ruins of Tapoyauik. They can also be obtained as an uncommon drop from brutal blue dragons located within the Catacombs of Kourend. All variants of blue dragons also have a chance to drop scaly blue dragonhide, which can be cut with a knife to get 50 blue dragon scales.
245:
Wine of Zamorak is a secondary ingredient used in Herblore. It can be found on both floors of Asgarnia's Chaos Temple and the Chaos Temple south-west of the Chaos Fanatic in level 38 Wilderness, in which both locations have their wine respawn by default every 30 seconds. It can also be found at the end of the Deep Wilderness Dungeon, where it respawns every 6.6 seconds and is obtained in noted form if players have completed the hard Wilderness Diary. Respawn rates for wines are affected by the amount of players on a world, reducing the time to spawn with more players on a world; Asgarnia's Chaos Temple on high population worlds has an approximate respawn rate of 16 seconds, and Deep Wilderness Dungeon has an approximate respawn rate of every 4.2 seconds.

The wine can also be made by using Zamorak's grapes with a jug of water, requiring Level 65 Cooking and granting 200 Cooking experience.

Wines of Zamorak cannot be consumed, but are used as a secondary ingredient in creating ranging and bastion potions. The bloody grimoire states that the wine is incredibly unholy but has a sweet taste that makes it easily addictive. Additionally, using Telekinetic Grab on the wine in Asgarnia's Chaos Temple is a medium task in the Falador Diary.
251: A herb used in poison cures.
253:
Tarromin is the third lowest level herb. It can be cleaned at level 11 Herblore, and it is used for making strength potions, serum 207, shrink-me-quick and tarromin tar. It can be grown with the Farming skill with a level of 19, by planting a tarromin seed in a herb patch. To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create a tarromin potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient.

According to the book Gielinor's flora - herbs, tarromin are native to tropical regions and it is believed to be one of the earliest cultivated plants of Gielinor.
259:
Irit leaf (Jagex: ih-RIT) is a mid level herb that can be cleaned at level 40 Herblore. Each cleaned irit leaf yields 8.8 Herblore experience. It is commonly dropped while fighting chaos druids, but can be dropped by almost every monster capable of dropping herbs.

To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create an irit potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient. You can create super attack potions by adding an eye of newt. Creating super attack potions is considered one of the easiest methods to train Herblore, especially for ironmen, as eyes of newt are very easy to obtain, and the finished product is very useful for combat purposes. Eye of newt packs can be bought for 300 gp at various shops, and contain 100 eyes of newt. You can also create superantipoison potions by adding unicorn horn dust. In order to create an antidote++ however, you need to add the irit leaf to a vial of coconut milk, creating antidote++ (unf), and add magic roots as secondary ingredients.

According to the book Gielinor's flora - herbs, irit has always had cultural significance due to its connection with the dead and is often synonymous with Icthlarin, the Menaphite god of death, and is often found growing in or near graveyards.
261:
Avantoe is a mid-level herb, requiring a Herblore level of 48 to clean from the grimy version. It can be obtained as a monster drop or through the Farming skill, with a level of 50, by planting an avantoe seed in a herb patch. It is used to make fishing potions, super energy potions, and hunter potions. To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create an avantoe potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient.

According to the book Gielinor's flora - herbs, the name means "moment", likely due to its unusual lifecycle caused by the harsh climate of the Kharidian Desert. Avantoe sprouts only after rain and then dies shortly in a matter of days.
269:
Torstol is the highest level herb, which requires level 75 Herblore to clean and yields 15 experience. Torstol can be grown in herb patches at level 85 Farming with a torstol seed.

Obtaining torstol herbs may be difficult as they are only rarely dropped by monsters. They can be obtained by Farming, looting nature implings, or rarely as drops from Zulrah and the Kalphite Queen. They can also be obtained in their grimy form from the Sinister chest, Skotizo, Cerberus, and the Chambers of Xeric. To create a Zamorak brew, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create a torstol potion (unf), and then add jangerberries.

According to the book Gielinor's flora - herbs, the name comes from torst, an old Fremennik word meaning "thirsty". This refers to the plant's need for a lot of water, and as such is often found growing near rivers and ponds.

A torstol may also be given to the Dr Jekyll random event in exchange for a Stamina potion(4).
272: Keeps your pet fish strong and healthy.
273:
Poison is an item used during the Ernest the Chicken and Hazeel Cult quests. It can be found as a spawn inside Draynor Manor, or purchased from Rasolo near the Baxtorian Falls or Jossik in the Lighthouse.

It is used to poison the fish food and the piranhas found in the fountain on the grounds of Draynor Manor during the Ernest the Chicken quest. Finally, it is used to poison the Carnillean household's food in Hazeel Cult. You can try to use the poison obtained from the Hazeel Cult to poison the sheep in Sheep Herder, but a message will appear saying: "The sheep isn't going to drink the poison from the bottle. Perhaps you should try feeding it something else more appropriate."

Attempting to use poison on the Carnillean household stove before picking a side or siding with the Carnilleans will yield the message, "Random murder isn't good".
288:
Goblin mail is armour for goblins. Although this item has the "Wear" option, this item cannot be equipped by players as it is too small to fit humans. However, during the Land of the Goblins quest, the player can turn into a goblin using a transmogrification potion and wear the goblin mail.

It can be dyed into various colours, in which certain colours are used for the Land of the Goblins quest.

Goblin mail is obtained as an uncommon drop from goblins. In addition, three goblin mails can be found in Goblin Village, north of Falador. One can be found in a crate in a building west of General Bentnoze and General Wartface, another in a crate on the balcony up the ladder near the entrance, and a third one in a crate just north of the building of Bentnoze and Wartface. Three are used in the Goblin Diplomacy quest. During the Land of the Goblins quest, there are crates which contain infinite goblin mail in the Goblin Temple.
299:
Mithril seeds are a magical type of seed that can be planted almost anywhere to grow some flowers in the ground, and are purchasable from the Legends Guild Shop of Useful Items.

Upon planting the seeds, the player will move one adjacent square west if possible; if there's an obstacle preventing movement to the west, the flowers will attempt to move the player to the east first, then south, then north. Once the flower is grown, players are then given the option to pick them, producing one of nine different colours of flowers.

Mithril seeds are primarily used in PvP activities in the Wilderness, or in minigames such as Last Man Standing, as it forces the user to move one tile even if the player is frozen. Adamant seeds, a variant of the item, will move the opposite direction from mithril seeds.

Seeds are sometimes used to grief players training Hunter and Firemaking as well, as traps and fires cannot be placed on the same tile as a planted flower.

40 seeds are awarded upon completion of the Waterfall Quest. Players can buy them at the Legends' Guild.
305: Useful for catching lots of fish.
307:
The fishing rod is an item used to catch fish through the Fishing skill. It can be bought from various fishing shops. To use a fishing rod, one will need fishing bait (except sandworms for anglerfish) to catch fish. It can be bought from fishing stores for 5 coins. There is also a fishing rod spawn in a house on south-eastern side of Entrana.

The equipable version of the fishing rod, the pearl fishing rod, can be bought with molch pearls from Alry the Angler.

The following fish are caught with a fishing rod:
309:
A fly fishing rod can be used to fish trout, salmon (both with feathers), and rainbow fish (with stripy feathers). They can be bought from various fishing shops. Fly fishing rods are used at fishing spots with the lure option. Popular fishing spots include the Barbarian Village, the Grand Tree, and Shilo Village. Fly fishing rods use feathers as bait. Feathers are dropped frequently from chickens or purchased from fishing shops.

The equipable version of the fly fishing rod, the pearl fly fishing rod, can be bought with molch pearls from Alry the Angler.

A fly fishing rod also spawns on the Isle of Souls in the south-east region.

The following fish are caught with a fly fishing rod:
311: Useful for catching really big fish.
313: For use with a fishing rod.
314:
Feathers are used in the Fishing and Fletching skills. In Fishing, feathers are used as lures for fly fishing. Feathers may also be used as bait for barbarian heavy-rod fishing, as a cheaper alternative to fishing bait. In Fletching, feathers are used to make arrows, darts, and bolts. Feathers cannot be noted, as they are stackable.

These are the only feathers that can be used to summon a newtroost during the Creature Creation activity in the Tower of Life, as coloured feathers are not accepted by the altar.

Most shops that sell feathers also sell feather packs which contain 100 feathers per pack.

In fletching recipes, blue, orange, red, yellow, stripy, gryphon, and stymphike feathers can all be used in place of regular feathers.
319:
Anchovies are a type of fish that restores 1 Hitpoint when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw anchovies on a fire or cooking range, granting 30 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt anchovies. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Anchovies are one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 34, or 31 when using the Lumbridge range.

Anchovies are an ingredient in anchovy pizzas, and are also used in the creation of impling jars.
329:
Salmon is a type of fish that restores 9 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw salmon on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 25 Cooking and granting 90 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt fish. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Salmon is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 58, or 55 when using the Lumbridge range.

Salmon is one of the fish required by Caleb during the quest Family Crest.

Salmon is used as an ingredient for admiral pie which requires Cooking level 70 to make.

When eaten, the message You eat the salmon. is displayed.
333:
Trout is a type of fish that restores 7 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw trout on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 15 Cooking and granting 70 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt trout. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Trout is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 49, or 45 when using the Lumbridge range.

Trout is used as an ingredient in fish pie which requires Cooking level 47 to make. 10 Trout are required during the Death Plateau quest.

When eaten, the message You eat the trout. is displayed.
339:
Cod is a type of fish that restores 7 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw cod on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 18 Cooking and granting 75 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt fish. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Cod is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 51 on a fire, 49 on a range, or 46 when using the Lumbridge range.

Cod is used as an ingredient in fish pie which requires Cooking level 47 to make.
341:
Raw cod is a fish that can be caught with a big fishing net at any fishing spot. It requires a Fishing level of 23 to catch and grants 45 fishing experience per catch. It can be cooked into cod with level 18 Cooking. The most common spot to fish cod is Catherby.

Raw cod is used for the Freeing Pirate Pete section of the Recipe for Disaster quest. It is also used for the Cold War quest, but it can be substituted with the use of the Ring of Charos(a).
345:
Raw herring is an item that is obtained through the Fishing skill by using a fishing rod with fishing bait on a net/bait fishing spot using the bait option. Herrings can only be caught in fishing spots by the sea. Catching a raw herring grants 30 Fishing experience. It can be cooked into herring with a Cooking level of 5, granting 50 Cooking experience.

This fish can be caught at level 10 Fishing and cooked at level 5 Cooking.

River fishing spots do not provide raw herring.
351: Pike is a type of fish that restores 8 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw pike on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 20 Cooking and granting 80 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt pike. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Pike is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 54, or 49 when using the Lumbridge range.
355: Mackerel is a type of fish that restores 6 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw mackerel on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 10 Cooking and granting 60 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt fish. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Mackerel is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 45, or 41 when using the Lumbridge range.
361:
Tuna is a type of fish that restores 10 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw tuna on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 30 Cooking and granting 100 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt tuna. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 63 on both ranges and fires.

Tuna is one of the fish required by Caleb in the quest Family Crest.

Tuna is used with sweetcorn to make tuna and corn which requires Cooking level 67 to make and restores 13 hitpoints when eaten. Potato with butter can also be added to tuna and corn to create a tuna potato which requires Cooking level 68 to make, restoring 22 Hitpoints when eaten.

When eaten, the message You eat the tuna. is displayed.
365: Wow, this is a big fish.
373: I'd better be careful eating this!
385: I'd better be careful eating this.
391:
The manta ray is a type of food that restores 22 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw manta ray on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 91 Cooking and granting 216.3 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt manta ray. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. It will only stop burning entirely when the Cooking cape is worn.

The manta ray is the second highest instant-health single consumption food, behind the marlin, alongside the dark crab, bluefin, anglerfish, and tuna potato. It is recommended to check the prices before using manta rays as a primary source of healing, as they are often more expensive than the other fish that heal the same amount.

Cooked moonlight antelope and cooked dashing kebbit heals 26 and 23 health respectively, but part of the healing is delayed, making them not always practical in the same situations.

Catching and cooking a manta ray is a requirement for the elite Ardougne Diary.
405: I hope there's treasure in it.
407: An oyster has a chance to contain an oyster pearl or be an empty oyster. They can sometimes be obtained by fishing with a big fishing net (requires 16 Fishing), by drift net fishing, or through panning at the Digsite. They can also be obtained as a drop from various monsters. The pearls found from an oyster can be made into pearl bolt tips at level 41 Fletching by using a chisel on them.
411: I could work wonders with a chisel on this pearl.
413: I could work wonders with a chisel on these pearls.
426:
Priest gown (top) is top half of the Priest gown set. A priest gown set is used in the Biohazard quest.

It can be bought from Thessalia's Fine Clothes in Varrock.
428:
Priest gown (bottom) is the bottom half of the Priest gown set. A priest gown set is used in the Biohazard quest.

It can be bought from Thessalia's Fine Clothes in Varrock.
436: Copper ore can be mined at level 1 Mining providing 17.5 Mining experience. After mining copper rocks, it will take 2.4 seconds until it reappears. Copper ore is used with tin ore to smelt bronze bars, or used with nickel ore to smelt Cupronickel bars. Smelting a bronze bar gives 6.2 Smithing experience.
440: Iron ore can be mined from iron rocks at level 15 Mining, providing 35 Mining experience. It can be smelted at a furnace into an iron bar at level 15 Smithing, or along with two coal into a steel bar at level 30 Smithing. Smelting iron bars has a 50% success rate, unless the player is wearing a ring of forging, using the Superheat Item spell, or using the Blast Furnace. Smelting iron ore into a bar gives 12.5 Smithing experience, and smelting a steel bar gives 17.5 Smithing experience.
442:
Silver ore can be mined at level 20 Mining, providing 40 Mining experience. After silver rocks are mined, it takes 60 seconds for them to respawn. Smelting silver ore will turn it into a silver bar, requiring 20 Smithing and giving 13.7 Smithing experience. The bar can then be crafted into various types of jewellery through the Crafting skill at a furnace, rather than at an anvil like other metallic bars. Doing so requires the usage of a mould, depending on the type of jewellery desired.

Wearing mining gloves, superior mining gloves, or expert mining gloves allows 1, 2, or 3 additional ores (respectively) to be mined before depletion.
451:
Runite ore can be mined at level 85 Mining providing 125 Mining experience. After runite rocks are mined, it will take twelve minutes until it reappears. Runite ore is used with eight coal to smelt runite bars. Smelting a runite bar gives 50 Smithing experience.

Wearing expert mining gloves while mining a runite rock grants a guaranteed extra gather before depleting.
453:
Coal can be mined at level 30 Mining providing 50 Mining experience. After coal rocks are mined, it will take 30 seconds until it reappears. Coal is required to smelt all ores above iron (other than gold, silver, lead, and nickel), in increasing amounts.

Members can store 27 pieces of coal in one inventory space by using a coal bag, obtained from Prospector Percy's Nugget Shop for 100 golden nuggets at Motherlode Mine.

Wearing mining gloves, superior mining gloves, or expert mining gloves while mining coal rocks makes the rock not deplete upon mining coal, allowing you to mine one, two, or three additional coal, respectively, before depleting.
464: I wonder what this tastes like?
530:
Bat bones are a type of bone which are dropped by bats and giant bats. Players will need bat bones for some quests, including Merlin's Crystal, Forgettable Tale..., and Watchtower.

Bat bones give 5.3 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

15.9 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

15.9 XP when offered at the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

18.5 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit or at the Chaos Temple.

21.2 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of bat bonemeal.

25 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl, or 30 XP when offered with a jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.
532: Ew it's a pile of bones.
534:
Babydragon bones are dropped by baby green, blue, red and black dragons. They can also be obtained as a common loot from dragon impling jars and crystal impling jars.

Babydragon bones give 30 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

90 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

90 XP when offered at the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

105 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit.

120 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of Baby dragon bonemeal.

120 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl, or 144 XP when offered with a jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

210 XP on average when offered at the Chaos Temple in the Wilderness. Each offering gives 105 XP, which is the same as the gilded altar with two burners lit, but with an additional 50% chance to not consume the bones.

Using babydragon bones instead of dragon bones is a slower but cheaper method to gain Prayer experience.

A babydragon bone is on the item list that Thorgel gives you. Giving him all of the items on the list rewards the player with a Death talisman.
536:
Dragon bones are bones dropped by most adult dragons, which give 72 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

216 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

216 XP when offered at the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

252 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit.

288 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of dragon bonemeal.

290 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl, or 348 XP when offered with a jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

504 XP on average when offered at the Chaos Temple in the Wilderness. Each offering gives 252 XP, which is the same as the gilded altars with two burners lit, but providing a 50% chance to not consume the bones.

The relative ease of collecting dragon bones, combined with the amount of experience earned from them, makes them widely viewed as a fast, cost-effective way to train Prayer.

A set of dragon bones is required for the Watchtower quest.

556:
Air runes are one of the four elemental runes. They are used in every combat spell and most teleportation spells in the standard spellbook, as well as in many spells from other spellbooks. Because they are used very often, players are recommended to purchase an item that can provide infinite air runes while equipped, such as a staff of air.

A common way for beginning players to obtain air runes is to talk to the magic tutor in Lumbridge. She will give you 30 air and mind runes if you don't have any in your inventory or bank. Air runes or packs can be bought from Magic shops, such as Aubury's Rune Shop in Varrock. Non-ironman players can also purchase them from the Nightmare Zone using 25 reward points.
557: Earth runes are one of the four elemental runes. They are used to cast earth-based combat spells in the standard spellbook, as well as many spells found in other spellbooks; Earth runes are used especially often for spells in the Lunar spellbook. The Confuse, Weaken, and Curse spells, often regarded as an inexpensive source of Magic experience, require earth runes in conjunction with body and water runes to cast. Some items, such as a staff of earth, provide infinite earth runes while equipped.
558:
The mind rune is used for the strike spells including Wind Strike, Water Strike, Earth Strike, and Fire Strike, as well as the Magic Dart spell.

Mind runes are craftable at level 2 Runecraft. Crafting mind runes provides 5.5 Runecraft experience per rune or pure essence used. Using mind cores in place of essences will yield an increased amount of mind runes. Members can also use Warped extracts to increase the quantity of crafted mind runes by 250 per pure essence, requiring partial completion of Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire and access to the Scar essence mine.

The Mind Altar is located north of Falador, in between Goblin Village and Ice Mountain, very near to the Wilderness. The Arceuus spellbook teleport to the Mind Altar can be used in conjunction with rings of dueling and essence pouches to achieve approximately 30k experience to upwards of 43k experience per hour at level 99 when crafting mind runes.

If you have no mind runes in your bank or inventory, and you have not dropped any right under you, you can obtain 30 new ones from the magic tutor in Lumbridge along with 30 air runes. Mind runes can be purchased from a myriad of shops, such as Betty in Port Sarim, the Void Knight Magic Store on Pest Control Island, or from Aubury just south of Varrock east bank in Aubury's Rune Shop.

There is a Falador Diary task in the hard section to craft 140 Mind runes at the same time. This requires level 56 Runecraft.
559:
Body runes are low level runes used for confuse, weaken, curse and Monster Inspect spells in the standard spellbook, as well as Dream and Stat Spy in the Lunar spellbook. They are also used for the reanimation spells Basic Reanimation and Adept Reanimation in the Arceuus spellbook.

Body runes can be created using Runecraft skill at level 20 at the Body Altar south of Edgeville Monastery, providing 7.5 Runecraft experience per essence. They are the highest level rune Free to Play players can craft.

2 body runes can be consistently found outside of the eastern wall of the Grand Exchange in Varrock, respawning approximately every 20 seconds. 15 body runes can be found among lesser demons at the Lava Maze deep within the Wilderness.

566: Used for high level curse spells.

573:

The spell requires an unpowered orb, 30 air runes, and 3 cosmic runes, yielding 76 Magic experience. The Air Obelisk is located in level 7 Wilderness, north of Edgeville. To get there, climb the ladder north of the black demons in Edgeville Dungeon.

An air orb can be used on a battlestaff, requiring 66 Crafting, yielding an air battlestaff and 137.5 Crafting experience. Charging air orbs is also a hard Wilderness Diary task.
575:
An earth orb is a glass orb that has been charged at the Obelisk of Earth by using the Charge Earth Orb spell, requiring 60 Magic, on the obelisk. The spell requires an unpowered orb, 30 earth runes, and 3 cosmic runes, yielding 70 Magic experience. The Earth Obelisk is located in the Edgeville Dungeon, south of the black demons beyond the poison spiders and Chronozon.

It can be created by using black dye on a blue wizard robe; similarly, it can also be turned into a blue wizard robe by using blue dye on it.

The black robe is often worn with the black wizard hat and black skirt for aesthetics. The hat has a slightly darker tone than the robes, instead more closely matching the priest gown. This is not the case with the robe's trimmed versions.

One of only three free-to-play bodies with a magic attack bonus, the Black robe, Blue wizard robe, and their ornamental variants get +1 Magic attack and -3 Prayer bonus compared to the Zamorak monk top.

751:
Gnomeballs are received by winning 5 points in a game of Gnome Ball, from the gnome restaurant minigame, or as a drop from dolphins. With the item in your inventory, you can click "Use" with it, and click another player. If that player has their right hand empty, they will catch the ball, and it will end up in their weapon slot. It is not advised that you throw it to a player you do not know, as they can very easily walk away with it.

Gnomeballs cannot be used on or by Ironman Mode players.
800: The bronze thrownaxe is a Ranged throwing weapon. There are no requirements to wield a bronze throwing axe. They can be obtained either by buying from the Tribal Weapons store at the Ranging Guild or trading with another player. The bronze throwing axe can be wielded with a shield or prayer book for protection.
802: The steel thrownaxe is a Ranged throwing weapon. To wield a steel throwing axe the player must have at least level 5 Ranged. They can be obtained either by buying from the Tribal Weapons store at the Ranging Guild or trading with another player. The steel throwing axe can be wielded with a shield or prayer book for protection.

808:
Steel darts are Ranged throwing weapons. To wield steel darts, players must have at least level 5 Ranged. They can be obtained by either using the Smithing and Fletching skills or trading with another player. Steel darts can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

To create steel darts, the player must have completed the Tourist Trap quest and have at least level 34 Smithing and level 37 Fletching. Each steel bar will create 10 steel dart tips and the player will receive 37.5 Smithing experience. When feathers are added the player will receive 10 steel darts and 7.5 Fletching experience per steel dart.

Steel darts have almost the same stats and speed as iron knives, which are often used for Ranged training at lower levels - however, they are far cheaper in price than iron knives due to people training Fletching.

A steel dart is one of the possible items requested by the rowdy dwarf during the Forgettable Tale quest.
809:
Mithril darts are Ranged throwing weapons made from mithril that are only available to members. Mithril darts require level 20 Ranged to wield. They can be obtained by either using the Smithing and Fletching skills or trading with another player. Mithril darts can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

Mithril darts are one of the most cost effective Ranged training weapons for lower level players, as they have an extremely quick rate of fire and cost very little compared to similar training methods like throwing knives or arrows. They can be bought in large numbers from the Grand Exchange, costing less than half of what similar tier ranged ammunition costs.

To create mithril darts the player must have completed The Tourist Trap quest and have at least level 54 Smithing and level 52 Fletching. Players can smith mithril bars into mithril dart tips. Each mithril bar creates 10 mithril dart tips and gives the player 50 Smithing experience. Feathers or Stripy Feathers then must be added to create the mithril darts. 11.2 Fletching experience is rewarded per mithril dart.
810:
Adamant darts are Ranged throwing weapons. To wield the player must have at least 30 Ranged. They can be obtained by either using the Smithing and Fletching skills or trading with another player. Adamant darts can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

To make adamant darts, the player must have completed the Tourist Trap quest and have at least 74 Smithing and 67 Fletching. Each adamant bar will create 10 adamant dart tips and the player will receive 62.5 Smithing experience. When feathers are added the player will receive 10 adamant darts and 15 Fletching experience per adamant dart.
811:
Rune darts are throwing weapons requiring level 40 Ranged to wield. They are created by combining rune dart tips with feathers. Rune darts can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

To create rune darts the player must have completed the Tourist Trap quest and have at least level 89 Smithing and level 81 Fletching. Players can smith rune bars into rune dart tips. Each rune bar creates 10 rune dart tips and gives the player 75 Smithing experience. Feathers then must be added to create the rune darts. 18.8 Fletching experience is rewarded per rune dart.

Smithing and fletching 10 rune darts while in Varrock is required to complete the Elite Varrock Diary. Fletching a rune dart is required to complete a master clue scroll skill challenge assigned by Sherlock.

824:

825:
The bronze javelin is a type of member's only Ranged ammunition used by the light and heavy ballistas. They are the weakest type of javelin. As with most javelins, they can be poisoned.

They can be fletched by attaching bronze javelin tips to javelin shafts at level 3 Fletching, granting 15 experience per 15 javelins made. They can also be obtained by buying them from the Ranging Guild, the Void Knight Archery Store or from Oobapohk's Javelin Store after Monkey Madness II.
826:

They can be fletched by attaching iron javelin tips to javelin shafts at level 17 Fletching, granting 30 experience per 15 javelins made. They can also be obtained by buying them from the Ranging Guild, the Void Knight Archery Store or from Oobapohk's Javelin Store after Monkey Madness II.

841:
The shortbow is the weakest bow in Old School RuneScape and can use arrows up to iron. Players can purchase this bow from Lowe's Archery Emporium in Varrock.

Players are supplied with this bow along with several bronze arrows as their first ranged weapon on Tutorial Island.

Members can make a shortbow through the Fletching skill at level 5. First, a player must cut an unstrung shortbow from logs, granting 5 Fletching experience. Then, the player must string the unstrung shortbow with a bow string, granting 5 experience.
843: A shortbow made out of oak, still effective.
845: A nice sturdy bow made out of oak.
847:
The willow longbow is a longbow made from willow logs. It requires 20 Ranged to equip and can fire arrows up to mithril. It has a longer attack range than its shortbow counterpart, but has a slower attack speed. It can be purchased from Lowe's Archery Emporium in Varrock.

Willow longbows can be created at level 40 Fletching by using a knife on willow logs to create a willow longbow (u), granting 41.5 experience, and then using a bowstring on the unstrung bow, granting another 41.5 experience.

Fletching a willow longbow from willow logs and a bow string will profit −78 while fletching a willow longbow from a willow longbow (u) and a bow string will profit −70.

Four willow longbows are required in the quest Shadows of Custodia.
849:
The willow shortbow is a two-handed ranged weapon stronger than the oak shortbow, but weaker than the maple shortbow. It can use arrows up to mithril. The willow shortbow requires a Ranged level of 20 or higher to wield. Players can purchase this bow from Lowe's Archery Emporium in Varrock.

Members can also make a willow shortbow through the Fletching skill at level 35. First, a player must cut an unstrung willow shortbow from willow logs, granting 33.3 Fletching experience. Then, the player must string the unstrung willow shortbow with a bow string, granting an additional 33.2 experience.
851:
A maple longbow is created by attaching a bow string to a maple longbow (u) with at least level 55 Fletching. Fletching from a maple log yields a total of 116.5 experience (58.3 for fletching and 58.2 for stringing). The bow can use arrows up to adamant and requires level 30 Ranged to wield.

The maple longbow differs from the shortbow only in terms of speed and attack range. However, the shortbow is preferred over the longbow due to its faster attack speed. It can also be a reward for the Observatory Quest.

Fletching a maple longbow from maple logs and a bow string will profit 99 while fletching a maple longbow from a maple longbow (u) and a bow string will profit 38.

The magic longbow is a longbow fletched from magic logs. It requires a Ranged level of 50 to wield and can fire arrows up to amethyst.

Players can make a magic longbow with a Fletching level of 85 by cutting an unstrung magic longbow from magic logs, granting 91.5 Fletching experience, and then stringing unstrung magic longbow with a bow string, granting a further 91.5 experience.

Fletching a magic longbow from magic logs and a bow string will profit 202 while fletching a magic longbow from a magic longbow (u) and a bow string will profit 185.
861:
The Magic shortbow is a bow that requires level 50 Ranged in order to use and can fire arrows up to amethyst. It is one of the few shortbows in the game with a Special attack. The bow has an attack range of 7, with longrange increasing attack range by 2.

To make this bow, players must use a magic shortbow (u) on a bow string. This requires 80 Fletching, and grants 83 experience. They can also be received from hard clue scrolls, or as a rare drop from spiritual rangers.

The Magic shortbow can be imbued by using a magic shortbow scroll on it to make a magic shortbow (i). The imbue increases its ranged attack bonus to +75 and lowers the special attack cost to 50%.

The magic shortbow is often the most powerful ranged weapon available to mid-level players. Because of its fast attack speed and ability to fire rune and amethyst arrows, it is usually an effective ranged weapon for completing Slayer tasks. The rune crossbow is a viable alternative for players who desire a shield, the special effects of enchanted bolts, or the easy availability of broad bolts. The Dorgeshuun crossbow can also achieve very similar damage-per-second to a magic bow with lower-level arrows (such as steel arrows), due to its higher firing speed than normal crossbows, while using very cheap and easily-obtainable ammunition in the form of bone bolts.

Despite its low max hit, the magic shortbow is popular for player killing due to the ease of stacking its damage with a more powerful melee attack for a knockout blow.
863:
The iron knife is a throwing knife that does not require a Ranged level to wield. It is stronger than a bronze knife but weaker than a steel knife. To create iron knives, the player must have at least 22 Smithing. Each iron bar will create 5 iron knives and give the player 25 Smithing experience. They can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

Throwing knives are among the fastest weapons in the game (along with darts), and are commonly used for PKing or training Ranged. Iron knives can be purchased from Martin Thwait's Lost and Found shop in the Rogues' Den with 50 Thieving and 50 Agility.
864:

Bronze knives can be created from a bronze bar at level 7 Smithing. Each bar makes 5 knives, and grants the player 12.5 Smithing experience. The knives can also be purchased from Martin Thwait's Lost and Found shop in the Rogues' Den, requiring 50 Thieving and 50 Agility.

Throwing knives are among the fastest weapons in the game (along with darts), and are commonly used for player-killing, training Ranged, or tagging enemies for barraging.

They can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

Throwing knives are among the fastest weapons in the game (along with darts), and are commonly used for PKing or training Ranged.
