To create iron knives, the player must have at least 22 Smithing. Each iron bar will create 5 iron knives and give the player 25 Smithing experience. They can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

Throwing knives are among the fastest weapons in the game (along with darts), and are commonly used for PKing or training Ranged. Iron knives can be purchased from Martin Thwait's Lost and Found shop in the Rogues' Den with 50 Thieving and 50 Agility.
876:
The rune knife is a throwing knife that requires a Ranged level of 40 to wield. It is the second strongest throwing knife in the game. To create rune knives, the player must have at least 92 Smithing. Each runite bar will create 5 rune knives and give the player 75 Smithing experience. They can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

Throwing knives are among the fastest weapons in the game (along with darts), and are commonly used for PKing or training Ranged.

Despite having lower ranged strength, rune knives in particular are sometimes used over dragon knives in PKing since their throwing animation can be cancelled earlier, allowing users to be more mobile and unpredictable while attacking.
881: Great if you have a crossbow!
884:
Iron arrows are stronger than bronze arrows, and are compatible with most bows. Iron arrows can be made at level 15 Fletching by using 15 iron arrowtips on 15 headless arrows, granting 37.5 Fletching experience. As with most arrows, they can be poisoned.

Iron arrows can be purchased from Lowe's Archery Emporium in Varrock.
885:
Iron arrows are stronger than bronze arrows, and are compatible with most bows. Iron arrows can be made at level 15 Fletching by using 15 iron arrowtips on 15 headless arrows, granting 37.5 Fletching experience. As with most arrows, they can be poisoned.

Iron arrows can be purchased from Lowe's Archery Emporium in Varrock.
892:
Rune arrows are stronger than adamant arrows, are stackable, and can be used on any bow of yew or stronger. They can be created through the Fletching skill at level 75 by using 15 rune arrowtips on 15 headless arrows, granting 187.5 Fletching experience. As with most arrows, they can be poisoned.

Rune arrows with a Magic shortbow (i) are a powerful weapon for Ironmen before obtaining the Toxic blowpipe, however they are outclassed by Karil's crossbow.

Players may also obtain 50 rune arrows from the Ranging Guild in exchange for 2,000 archery tickets, or obtain 300 at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing in Ferox Enclave in exchange for 3 Last Man Standing points.
893:
Rune arrows are stronger than adamant arrows, are stackable, and can be used on any bow of yew or stronger. They can be created through the Fletching skill at level 75 by using 15 rune arrowtips on 15 headless arrows, granting 187.5 Fletching experience. As with most arrows, they can be poisoned.

Rune arrows with a Magic shortbow (i) are a powerful weapon for Ironmen before obtaining the Toxic blowpipe, however they are outclassed by Karil's crossbow.

Players may also obtain 50 rune arrows from the Ranging Guild in exchange for 2,000 archery tickets, or obtain 300 at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing in Ferox Enclave in exchange for 3 Last Man Standing points.
948:
Bear fur is an item obtained by killing a bear. It can be sold to Baraek for 12 coins, or 20 with the Ring of Charos(a). Bears are located in, among other places, north-east of East Ardougne, the Wilderness, near Goblin Village, in Isafdar, east of Varrock and north of Falador. Bear fur can also be purchased from the fur merchant in the marketplace in East Ardougne.

Although the examine text says, "This would make warm clothing," currently no clothing can actually be made by players from the fur. Wooden cats, used in the The Great Brain Robbery quest, can be made with bear fur.

One piece of bear fur is needed during the quest Mourning's End Part I and the quest Getting Ahead.
950:
Silk can be bought from various silk traders around Gielinor.

Silk can be stolen from silk stalls with a Thieving level of 20, yielding 24 experience. The Silk merchant who runs the silk stall in Ardougne will buy silk from the player for as much as 60 coins through his dialogue, if the player first offers to sell them for 120 coins each.
954:
Rope is an item used for many things, such as quests and the creation of certain items. It can be obtained by purchasing at a shop, trading with Ned in exchange for 4 balls of wool, or by a player spinning yak hair on a spinning wheel.

The best store to buy rope, without requirements, is at Ned's shop in Draynor Village. However, you can get a full inventory of rope for free from the Tempoross minigame in the ropes container. A convenient place to get rope is in the Ardougne general store (helpful for those doing the Waterfall Quest and Plague City) where there is a stock of 20, but Martin Thwait's Lost and Found at Rogues' Den is a far better option since it stocks 50 and is next to a bank (although it requires 50 Thieving and 50 Agility to access his shop). Khazard General Store is also within close proximity of a bank.
958:
Grey wolf fur is an item dropped by werewolves. Grey wolf fur can also be bought, or stolen from the East Ardougne fur trader, the Port Roberts fur stall and the Rellekka fur trader (after The Fremennik Trials quest).

Grey wolf fur can also be obtained from salvaging at merchant shipwrecks and sorting the Opulent salvage recovered. Level 87 sailing is required.

Baraek the fur trader will buy grey wolf furs for 120 coins, or 150 coins with the Ring of Charos(a). He will not buy any noted fur.
973: Charcoal is used as a writing and sketching tool in quests. It is often used with papyrus.
975:
The machete is an item used in the Woodcutting skill. It can be obtained from the mainland Karamja general store and Shilo Village general store or by trading with another player. It can also be found by looking in Radimus Erkle's cupboard in the Legends' Guild; however, after the quest is complete you may no longer search the cupboard for a machete and are given the message "You don't think Radimus Erkle would be very pleased if he caught you rifling through his possessions".

The machete can be used as a weapon but is primarily used to cut Jungle during the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup minigame. It has no requirements to wield though cutting Light, Medium, and Dense jungle requires 10, 20, and 35 Woodcutting to harvest respectively. A machete is also required to gain access to Kharazi Jungle if the player doesn't have access to the level 79 agility shortcut to the south-east of Shilo Village.

You can also obtain opal, jade, and red topaz machetes, which have a progressively higher speed at chopping down the jungles. To obtain these machetes, you can buy them from Gabooty in Tai Bwo Wannai, or speak to Safta Doc and make an exchange with him. Alternatively you can buy them from players or on the Grand Exchange.
981:
The disk of returning is an item purchased from Diango's Toy Store for 21,000 coins. Players can activate the disk, which requires them to be inside the Dwarven Mine; when activated, the player is teleported into the Blackhole, where Thordur resides. To leave, simply activate the disk again. This will cause players to reappear in the Dwarven Mine, next to Boot and the sign in the north-western corner of the mine. This means it could conceivably be used to quickly travel from the south-eastern part of the mine to the north-western part. This can be useful for Free-to-play Ultimate Ironmen to train their Smithing with Superheat Item in the mines, by accessing the anvils next to the respawn location after leaving the black hole, or for players running from Falador to the Ruins of Camdozaal.

The 'blackout' option on the disk may also be used in the easternmost part of the White Knights' Castle Crypt, although the 'activate' option does not work. This may be used to quickly reach certain clue step locations by teleporting to Falador, entering the crypt, and then entering and leaving the blackhole.

If not inside the Dwarven Mines, activating the disk of returning simply returns the message You can only enter Thordur's Blackholes from the Dwarven Mines, beneath Falador.

Attempting to drop it while inside the blackhole will result in a confirmation message asking, "Really drop your Disk of Returning?" Choosing "Yes, something cool might happen" will give the message "That was disappointing". Occasionally, though, the chatbox message will state "Something cool happens" as the player performs the dance and clap emotes. This interaction is a reference to a scam that frequently occurred in RuneScape Classic, where visitors of the blackhole were told "something interesting would happen" if they dropped their disk of returning, resulting in a significant number of unoffending players getting stuck inside.

Note: You can still get out of both holes after dropping the disk of returning, either by talking to Thordur and asking how to get out, or by exiting through the light in the blacker blackhole. Any items dropped on the ground in either hole will be deleted upon leaving.
983:
The brass key is a key which allows the player to enter the locked shed found west of the Cooking Guild. The shed provides an alternate entrance to the Edgeville Dungeon, entering north of the Hill Giant room.

To get the key, you must enter the Edgeville Dungeon through the entrance south of the Edgeville bank and make your way through the dungeon. Just north of the hill giant room, there is a small circular room with the key on the ground. It re-spawns every minute.

This key is tradeable and can also be placed on the steel key ring.
985: The tooth end of the mysterious Crystal Key. Can you find the other half?
987: The loop end of the mysterious Crystal Key. Can you find the other half?
989:
The crystal key is created by combining a tooth half of key with a loop half of key, displaying the message, "You join the two halves of the key together." Key halves can be obtained as rewards from Barrows, the Gnome Restaurant minigame, Managing Miscellania, Treasure Trails, looting magpie implings, random events, the rare drop table, etc.

It is used to open the crystal chest located inside a house in Taverley. The chest always contains an uncut dragonstone in addition to a variety of other items. Some items of note are 3 runite bars, rune platelegs/plateskirt (depending on the player's gender), or another half of the crystal key. After the key is used, it disappears and the player must use another one if they want to open the chest again.

The crystal key may not be placed on the steel key ring, as it is non-reusable.

The crystal key can be upgraded to an enhanced crystal key at a singing bowl in Prifddinas, for the cost of 10 crystal shards.

One is required for a medium Falador Diary task of opening a Crystal chest.
991:
The muddy key is a key that can be used to open the muddy chest in the centre of the Lava Maze in the Wilderness. You will need a knife or sword to access it. It can be obtained as a drop from chaos dwarves (in both the Wilderness and Taverley Dungeon), and the crazy archaeologist.

Using a muddy key to open the muddy chest is a medium Wilderness Diary task.
993:
The sinister key is used to open the sinister chest in the Yanille Agility dungeon. The sinister chest contains nine noted grimy herbs: 2 harralanders, 3 ranarr weeds, 1 irit leaf, 1 avantoe, 1 kwuarm, and 1 torstol. The sinister key is dropped by Salarin the twisted and the Chaos Fanatic, and can also be looted from a Magpie impling.

The value of the sinister key is linked to the value of the herbs contained in the sinister chest. Buying a key, opening the chest, and selling the grimy herbs from it currently produces a profit of 4,538.

A lockpick is required if you're entering the dungeon via the house in Yanille.
1007: A red cape can be made by using red dye on another coloured cape, or purchased from Thessalia's Fine Clothes in Varrock or Barkers' Haberdashery in Canifis.
1009:
A brass necklace is a cosmetic piece of jewellery. It provides no stat bonuses and does not have any uses.

The necklace cannot be made using the Crafting skill; it can only be obtained as a drop from goblins and cave goblins, or as an item spawn in Edgeville Dungeon near the hobgoblins and in the Varrock west bank basement (requires the Telekinetic Grab spell or completion of Crack the Clue III to obtain).
1011: Leg covering favoured by women and wizards.
1015: Clothing favoured by women and dark wizards.
1017:
A black wizard hat is an item of clothing that can be worn in the head slot. It has the same bonuses as the blue wizard hat. It can be purchased from Betty's Magic Emporium in Port Sarim, and can be found as a drop from the dark wizards south of Varrock.

It can be created by using black dye on a blue wizard hat; similarly, blue dye can be used on it to create a blue wizard hat.
1023: A yellow cape can be made by using yellow dye on another coloured cape and can be purchased from Barkers' Haberdashery in Canifis, Fancy Clothes Store in the Varrock, or Shayzien Styles in Shayzien.
1025:
A right eye patch is an item commonly worn by pirates, and can be obtained as a drop from them. An eye patch can be bought from the Fancy Dress Shop or Trader Stan's Trading Post. When equipped, the eye patch takes place in the head slot, which means players may not wear a helmet or any other headgear at the same time.

Players who have completed Cabin Fever can pay Patchy 500 coins to sew together an eye patch and pirate bandana to create a bandana eyepatch. Players can also bring Patchy an eye patch and pirate's hat, to create a hat eyepatch, or a big pirate hat and eye patch to create a pirate hat & patch. It is also possible to ask Patchy to combine this item with a left eye patch to create a double eye patch. A book o' Piracy is not required.

It is one of the possible items that the rowdy dwarf may ask players to bring him during the Forgettable Tale of a Drunken Dwarf quest. It is also a possible request from Gunslik or the rowdy dwarf when doing Keldagrim tasks.

This item can be stored in the mahogany treasure chest of a costume room under master tier.
1031: An orange cape is made by using orange dye on another coloured cape.
1033:
The Zamorak monk bottom is part of the Zamorak monk robes set. They are bright red, and like the related Zamorak monk top they are dropped by disciples of Iban and monks of Zamorak.

Zamorak monk robes are commonly used by mages in the Wilderness due to providing decent Prayer and Magic bonuses and being easy to replace if lost. They can also be used to telegrab Wine of Zamorak at the Chaos Temple (Asgarnia) without being attacked.

The Zamorak monk bottom counts as a Zamorak item in the God Wars Dungeon.

The Zamorak monk bottom is notable for being the only free-to-play leg slot item with a Magic attack bonus.
1035:
The Zamorak monk top is part of the Zamorak monk robes set. They are bright red, and like the related Zamorak monk bottom they are dropped by disciples of Iban, necromancers and monks of Zamorak.

Zamorak monk robes are commonly used by mages in the Wilderness due to providing decent Prayer and Magic bonuses and being easy to replace if lost. They can also be used to telegrab Wine of Zamorak at the Chaos Temple (Asgarnia) without being attacked.

One of only three free-to-play bodies with a magic attack bonus, the Zamorak monk top has 1 less Magic attack and 3 more Prayer bonus when compared to the Black robe, Blue wizard robe, and their ornamental variants.

The Zamorak monk top counts as a Zamorak item in the God Wars Dungeon.
1038: A nice hat from a cracker.
1040: A nice hat from a cracker.
1042: A nice hat from a cracker.
1044:
Green partyhats are tradeable cosmetic items obtained by completing one of the Christmas holiday events that occur once per year.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 4 July to 14 July) as part of a rare item drop.
1046: A nice hat from a cracker.
1048: A nice hat from a cracker.
1059: These will keep my hands warm!
1069:
Steel platelegs are the third weakest platelegs in the game. They have the same bonuses and penalties as a steel plateskirt but weigh more. A player with 46 Smithing can make them by using three steel bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 112.5 Smithing experience. They can also be bought from Louie's Armoured Legs Bazaar. They require 5 Defence to wear.

As they spawn in the Wilderness at the Ruins north of the Graveyard of Shadows, they are one of the most easily accessible and most popular money making methods for new Ironman accounts when being sold to Louie's Armoured Legs Bazaar starting at 650 each at base stock of 2, reducing by 10 per extra set.

Their respawn rate in the Wilderness is between 10 and 20 minutes, depending on the number of players in a world.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Ardougne knight armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
1071: Mithril platelegs are the third best free-to-play platelegs. They require level 20 Defence to equip. A player with 66 Smithing can make it by using three mithril bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 150 Smithing experience. Mithril platelegs offer similar stats to a mithril plateskirt but weigh more.
1073:
Adamant platelegs are platelegs made of Adamant and, as such, require a Defence level of 30 to wear. These platelegs have the same stats as the Adamant plateskirt, but are 1kg heavier.

Adamant platelegs can be smithed using 3 adamant bars at level 86 Smithing, granting 187.5 experience.
1077:
Black platelegs have the same bonuses as the black plateskirt but weigh more. They require level 10 Defence to wear. They can be bought from Louie's Armoured Legs Bazaar in Al Kharid or Valaine's Shop of Champions in the Champions' Guild. Like all other black armour, it cannot be made with the Smithing skill.

Black platelegs are used in King's Ransom and Heroes' Quest if you're part of the Black Arm Gang.

Black platelegs (t) and (g) can both be obtained as a reward from easy Treasure Trails. They provide no extra bonuses than regular black platelegs other than being aesthetically improved.
1079:
Rune platelegs are platelegs made of runite. They require level 40 Defence to wear. Rune platelegs are identical in function to the rune plateskirt, but is 1kg heavier. Players may receive these from the crystal chest if they are a body type A character.

They can be created with the Smithing skill by using 3 runite bars and a hammer on an anvil; this requires level 99 Smithing and yields 225 Smithing experience.

Along with the rune plateskirt and two-handed sword, this is the best bar-per-alch item in the game. If smithing for money, rune platelegs, plateskirt and two-handed sword will give the best value for each bar.

They can also be put into the nest found on top of the Aldarin windmill in Varlamore in order to get a runite bar.
1083: The Steel plateskirt is a plateskirt made from steel, requiring level 5 Defence to wear. It can be made at level 46 Smithing by using 3 Steel bars on an anvil with a hammer in the inventory. It has identical stats to the steel platelegs, with the notable exception that it weighs less.
1085: Mithril plateskirts give the fifth best stat bonuses of all plateskirts. This piece of armour can be made with Level 66 Smithing by using 3 mithril bars on an anvil, therefore granting the player with 150 smithing experience. At least 20 Defence is required to wear it. Mithril plateskirts have similar stats to mithril platelegs but weigh less.
1089:
The black plateskirt has the same stats as black platelegs but weighs less. The black plateskirt requires 10 Defence to wear. One can be bought from Ranael's Super Skirt Store in Al Kharid.

As with all black and white equipment, the black plateskirt cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
1091:
The Adamant plateskirt is a plateskirt made out of adamant. At least 30 Defence is required to wear it. The plateskirt has the same stats as the Adamant platelegs, but are 1kg lighter.

They can be made at level 86 Smithing using 3 adamantite bars, which grants 187.5 experience.
1097: Studded chaps are part of studded leather armour set and they require 20 Ranged to equip.
1101: A series of connected metal rings.
1103: A series of connected metal rings.
1105:
The Steel chainbody is the third weakest chainbody, and it can be worn by a player with level 5 Defence.

A player with level 41 Smithing can forge the steel chainbody by using three steel bars on an anvil with a hammer in their inventory, granting 112.5 Smithing experience. It can also be bought from Wayne's Chains in Falador, or Horvik's Armour Shop in Varrock.
1107: A series of connected metal rings.
1109:
The Mithril chainbody is a chainbody made out of mithril. As with all mithril armour, it requires 20 Defence to wear.

Like all chainbodies, it provides better Crush defence than a platebody made of the same material, at the cost of lower Stab and Slash defence.

The Mithril chainbody can be made with level 61 Smithing using 3 mithril bars, and grants 150 Smithing experience.
1111: Adamant chainbody is piece of armour made from adamantite. A player can create an adamant chainbody by using an adamantite bar on an anvil while a hammer and 3 adamantite bars are in the player's inventory. A Smithing level of 81 is required to make an adamant chainbody and doing so will grant the player 187.5 Smithing experience. Level 30 Defence is required to wear an adamant chainbody. It can also be bought from Wayne's Chains in south Falador. One adamant chainbody is required for Song of the Elves.
1113:
A rune chainbody is a chainbody made of runite. To wear this chainbody, a player needs at least level 40 Defence. This piece of body armour is less resistant than the rune platebody in all stats except crush and magic and wearing it does not require completion of Dragon Slayer I. For this reason it is commonly worn by players who have not finished said quest or who are fighting against monsters that use crush attacks. It is also useful for rangers since it has higher defence bonuses than the green d'hide body and it does not penalise ranged attack.

A player with 96 Smithing can make the chainbody by using three runite bars on an anvil, granting 225 Smithing experience. It can also be bought at Scavvo's Rune Store in the Champions' Guild, or for members, at Seddu's Adventurer's Store in Nardah.
1115:
The iron platebody is an armour used in melee with stat bonuses between bronze and steel. It has no Defence requirement to equip, which makes it the best platebody for players just starting out. It also provides greater protection than an iron chainbody. Like all platebodies, however, it gives a crippling negative bonus to the user's Ranged and Magic stats.

If playing as an Ironman, an ironman platebody with equivalent stats can be acquired by talking to the Ironman tutor in Lumbridge.

Players with level 33 Smithing can make one by using 5 iron bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 125 experience. Alternatively, they can be bought from Horvik's Smithy or Zenesha's Plate Mail Body Shop.
1119:
The steel platebody is an armour used in melee with stat bonuses between iron and mithril (not including the black and white platebodies). It requires 5 Defence to equip and provides greater protection than a steel chainbody. Like all platebodies, however, it gives a crippling negative bonus to the user's Ranged and Magic stats.

Players with level 48 Smithing can make one by using 5 steel bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 187.5 experience. Alternatively, they can be bought from Horvik's Smithy, Zenesha's Plate Mail Body Shop, or in Varlamore.
1123:
The adamant platebody is an armour used in melee with stat bonuses between mithril and rune. It requires 30 Defence to equip and provides greater protection than an adamant chainbody. Like all platebodies, however, it gives a crippling negative bonus to the user's Ranged and Magic stats.

Players with level 88 Smithing can make one by using 5 adamantite bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 312.5 experience.

Smithing an adamant platebody is a requirement for the elite Lumbridge & Draynor Diary.
1125:
The black platebody is an armour used in melee with the same stat bonuses as a white platebody, excluding the Prayer bonus. It requires 10 Defence to equip and provides greater protection than a black chainbody. Like all platebodies, however, it gives a crippling negative bonus to the user's Ranged and Magic stats.

It cannot be made using the Smithing skill, though it's easily obtainable as it can be bought from Horvik, Zenesha or another player.

A black platebody is used in King's Ransom and Heroes' Quest if the player joins the Black Arm Gang.
1127:
The rune platebody is an armour used in melee and the strongest of all free-to-play platebodies. It requires 40 Defence and completion of the quest Dragon Slayer I to equip. It also provides greater protection than a rune chainbody, with the exception of a slightly lower crush defence. Like all platebodies, however, it gives a crippling negative bonus to the user's Ranged and Magic stats.

Players with level 99 Smithing can make one by using 5 runite bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 375 experience.
1131: The hardleather body is low-level ranged armour. It may be equipped in the torso slot by players with 1 Ranged and 10 Defence. It provides better protection from melee, Magic, and Ranged attacks than the leather body and grants a modest boost to one's Ranged accuracy.
1133: A studded body is a part of studded leather armour set and it requires 20 Ranged and Defence to equip.
1137: The iron med helm is the second weakest medium helmet. A player with 18 Smithing can make the helmet by using one iron bar on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 25 Smithing experience.
1145:
The adamant med helm is a medium helmet made of adamantite. This helm requires 30 Defence to wear. It provides more protection than its mithril counterpart. It can be made at level 73 Smithing using an adamantite bar, granting 62.5 experience.

Though the helmet provides a smaller Defence bonus than that of an adamant full helm, it has a lower penalty to Magic and Ranged attack. This means it is potentially more useful than the full helm to players who are training the Magic skill.
1147: The rune med helm is a medium helmet made out of rune, requiring a Defence level of 40 to wear. A Smithing level of 88 is required to smith one from a runite bar, granting 75 experience. It can also be obtained as a drop from a variety of monsters.
1149:
The dragon med helm is a piece of armour which requires 60 Defence to equip. It was the first piece of dragon armour to be released.

Zulrah, revenants, Sarachnis and some dragons can drop the dragon med helm. Any monster that has access to the standard rare drop table can also drop the dragon med helm. It can also be found in the Barrows chest as a separate item with 1012 rewards potential and all brothers killed.

Offering slightly more defensive power than the helm of Neitiznot, many players favour other helmets that provide offensive bonuses, or penalise magic attack bonus less. The dragon med helm is often considered less prestigious than other helmets due to its lack of any quest requirements.

As with most Dragon equipment, players cannot make this item using the Smithing skill.
1155:
The bronze full helmet is the weakest full helmet in Old School RuneScape. The bronze full helmet grants greater defensive bonuses than its medium helmet counterpart, though at a cost of offensive bonuses for Ranged and Magic. There are no Defence requirements for wearing this helmet.

To create a bronze full helmet the player needs at least 7 Smithing, a hammer and 2 bronze bars. To make a helmet use one of the bars on an anvil with the hammer in the inventory. This grants 25 Smithing experience.
1157:
The steel full helm is the third weakest full helm. The steel full helm grants greater defensive bonuses than its medium helmet counterpart, though at a cost of offensive bonuses for Ranged and Magic. Wearing this helmet requires at least 5 Defence.

To create a steel full helmet you need at least 37 Smithing, a hammer, and two steel bars. Then use one of the bars on an anvil with the hammer in your inventory. This will grant 75 Smithing experience.

Members with 16+ Construction can use a steel full helmet on a pluming stand to make a steel heraldic helm, a steel full helm designed in the colours of the player's family crest. Family crests are obtained from Sir Renitee in Falador Castle.
1159: The mithril full helm is the fourth best full helmet. It requires 20 Defence to equip. It offers better defensive stats than its med helm counterpart, at the cost of having lower magic and ranged attack, and greater weight. One can be made by a player with level 57 Smithing at any anvil with a hammer and 2 mithril bars.
1161: An adamant full helm is a full helmet made out of adamant. It can be worn with at least level 30 in Defence and can be smithed with at least level 77 Smithing using 2 adamantite bars (this grants 125 Smithing experience). These helms are stronger than mithril full helms but weaker than rune full helms.
1165:
The black full helm is a full helmet that requires 10 Defence to equip. As with all black armour, it cannot be made using the Smithing skill. It can be bought at Valaine's Shop of Champions in the Champions' Guild for 1,372 coins. It can also be obtained as a Treasure Trails reward.

A black full helm is used in King's Ransom and, if you're part of the Black Arm Gang, Heroes' Quest.
1169:
A coif is an improved cowl that requires 20 Ranged to equip. Coifs are the best ranged headgear available for free to play. It can be made by members at level 38 Crafting with one leather (soft), a needle, and thread.

Making a coif in the Lumbridge cow field is a requirement for the medium Lumbridge & Draynor Diary.
1173: The Bronze sq shield is the lowest level defence square shield in Old School RuneScape. It can be equipped to give a player better defence bonuses in combat. Its recommended use is in melee combat. Players can make a bronze square shield with 2 bronze bars at level 8 Smithing, granting 25 Smithing experience. It can also be bought from Cassie's Shield Shop in Falador.
1177: A steel sq shield is the third weakest square shield. It requires 5 Defence to equip. A player with 38 Smithing can make the shield by using two steel bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 75 experience.
1181:
A mithril square shield is the fourth strongest square shield. Players with level 58 Smithing can make the shield by using two mithril bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 100 Smithing experience.

This shield can be bought from Raum Urda-Stein on Jatizso. This shield provides less defence than the mithril kiteshield, but is much lighter. As with all pieces of mithril armour, it requires 20 Defence to wield.
1187: An ancient and powerful looking Dragon Square shield.
1189: The Bronze kiteshield is the weakest smithable kiteshield, requiring 1 Defence to wield. A player with 12 Smithing can make the shield by using 3 bronze bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 37.5 Smithing experience. It can also be bought from Cassie's Shield Shop in Falador.
1191:
The Iron kiteshield is the second-weakest smithable kiteshield, requiring 1 Defence to wield. A player with 27 Smithing can make the shield by using three iron bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 75 Smithing experience. It cannot be bought from Cassie's Shield Shop for ironmen, as there is no stock available.

The iron kiteshield yields the highest melee defence bonuses for any shield slot item at 1 Defence.
1201:
The Rune kiteshield is the second best smithable kiteshield, surpassed only by the Dragon kiteshield. The rune kiteshield requires 40 Defence to wield. A player with 97 Smithing can make the shield by using three runite bars and a hammer on an anvil, granting 225 Smithing experience.

The rune kiteshield is often used as a tank shield by low-risk and void rangers; despite the negative ranged attack bonus, it is much cheaper, and provides a substantial melee defence bonus, which the Odium ward lacks.

Players with at least level 43 Crafting are also able to paint the rune kiteshield at a player-owned house to create an untradeable heraldic shield, provided that they have visited Sir Renitee to obtain a crest in advance. A painted rune kiteshield will provide protection in the God Wars Dungeon. It will also turn bandits hostile, if painted in the colours of Saradomin or Zamorak.

Any monster that has access to the rare drop table can also drop the rune kiteshield.
1207:
The steel dagger is the third-weakest dagger, requiring level 5 Attack to wield. They can be bought from shops and obtained drops from monsters, and can also be smithed from a steel bar at level 30 Smithing. As with most daggers, steel daggers can be poisoned.

Players must bring Veliaf a steel dagger during In Search of the Myreque.
1209: The mithril dagger is a dagger made out of mithril. Mithril daggers can be smithed from a single mithril bar at level 50 Smithing. Each mithril dagger created grants 50 experience. Mithril daggers are the fifth strongest daggers, the next strongest being the adamant dagger. Like all mithril weapons, mithril daggers require 20 Attack to wield. As with most daggers, this weapon can be poisoned. Players can purchase this dagger from the Varrock Swordshop.
1211: The adamant dagger is a dagger made of adamantite. It can be created by using one Adamant bar and a hammer on an anvil at level 70 Smithing, granting 62.5 Smithing experience. As with most daggers, it can be poisoned.
1213: The rune dagger is a dagger made from rune. Rune daggers can be made from a single rune bar at level 85 Smithing. Each rune dagger created grants 75 experience. Rune daggers are the third-strongest daggers, behind the dragon dagger and the abyssal dagger. Like most rune weapons they require 40 Attack to wield. As with most daggers, this weapon can be poisoned.
1217:
The black dagger is a dagger slightly more accurate than the steel dagger. Like most daggers it can be poisoned, giving an advantage in combat. Like all black weapons, wielding it requires an Attack level of 10.

As with all black and white equipment, the black dagger cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.

1241: The steel spear is a two-handed melee weapon that requires 5 Attack to wield. It can be bought from the Mount Karuulm Weapon Shop or Fortis Blacksmith, or obtained as a drop from monsters. Players who have started learning Barbarian Smithing and have level 35 Smithing may produce a spear at a Barbarian anvil from one steel bar and one willow log, receiving 75 Smithing experience. Smithing spears at the Barbarian anvil requires completion of Tai Bwo Wannai Trio. Like most spears, it can be poisoned.
1243: The mithril spear is a two-handed melee weapon made from mithril requiring 20 Attack to wield. Mithril spears are a members-only weapon. It can be bought from the Mount Karuulm Weapon Shop or Fortis Blacksmith, or obtained as a drop from monsters. Using the Smithing skill, players can create mithril spears on one of the barbarian anvils in either Otto's Grotto or Barbarian Village. However, players must have begun Barbarian Smithing training to be able to smith these spears. Like most spears, the mithril spear can be poisoned.

1267:
The iron pickaxe is a pickaxe that mines on a 7-tick cycle, 1-tick faster than the bronze pickaxe. It can be used in combat or to mine rocks.

As with all pickaxes, players cannot smith an iron pickaxe.
1271:
The adamant pickaxe is a pickaxe that is stronger than the mithril pickaxe, but weaker than the rune pickaxe. It requires an Attack level of 30 to wield, and a Mining level of 31 to mine with.

The adamant pickaxe mines on a 4-tick cycle, unlike other pickaxes. This allows it to be used for tick manipulation in various places, such as mining shooting stars.
1275: The rune pickaxe is the third best pickaxe, after the crystal pickaxe and the dragon pickaxe variants. It mines on a 3-tick cycle and is the best pickaxe in free-to-play. The rune pickaxe requires 41 Mining to use, and 40 Attack to equip. Players lacking 40 Attack can still use it for mining. Like all pickaxes, it cannot be smithed, so it must be obtained from other players or from a shop, as a monster drop, or as a reward from the quest Between a Rock....
1277:
The bronze sword is a low-level weapon made of bronze. It can be purchased from the Varrock Swordshop, or made at level 4 Smithing using 1 bronze bar, granting 12.5 experience.

A bronze sword is given to the player by Vannaka on Tutorial Island.
1281:
The steel sword is a low-level weapon made of steel, stronger than the iron sword. It can be purchased from the Varrock Swordshop, or made at level 34 Smithing using 1 steel bar, granting 37.5 experience. It requires 5 Attack to wield.

Two swords are needed for the In Search of the Myreque quest, along with some other steel equipment.
1285:
The Mithril sword is a sword stronger than the black sword. It requires 20 Attack to wield.

Players can make this sword at level 54 Smithing by using one mithril bar and a hammer on an anvil, granting 50 experience. It can also be purchased from the Varrock Swordshop.
1291: The bronze longsword is a longsword made of bronze. It is the weakest longsword available, and any player can wield it. It requires 2 bronze bars and level 6 Smithing to make, granting 25 experience. The bronze longsword is available for purchase at Varrock Swordshop in Varrock. It is rarely used due to the existence of the iron longsword, which is stronger and has the same requirements. It can be found as a drop from various monsters.
1293: The iron longsword is a longsword stronger than the bronze longsword, but weaker than the steel longsword. Like all other iron weapons, it can be wielded at level 1 Attack. It can be created at level 21 Smithing using two iron bars, granting 50 experience. This longsword can be purchased at Varrock Swordshop.
1301: The adamant longsword is a longsword that is stronger than the Mithril longsword, but weaker than the Rune longsword. Like all other adamant weapons, it requires 30 Attack to wield. Players can make an adamant longsword with 76 Smithing using 2 adamantite bars, granting 125 experience. It can be bought from the Varrock Swordshop for 3,200 coins.
1303: The rune longsword is a longsword requiring 40 Attack to wield. It can be made using 2 runite bars at level 91 Smithing. It is the strongest longsword in free-to-play, surpassing the adamant longsword. Even though it has better melee strength and attack, it underperforms compared to the Rune scimitar due to its attack speed being 25% slower (5 ticks compared to 4). Its higher attack bonus may outperform rune scimitar and rune sword against higher defence monsters.
1305:
The dragon longsword is the third-strongest longsword available in Old School RuneScape, and can only be wielded by players who have at least 60 Attack and have completed the Lost City quest.

As with all dragon weapons, players cannot make this item using the Smithing skill. However, it can be purchased in the Zanaris marketplace from Jukat for 100,000 coins (requires a Diamond for entry). The weapon can also be received as a reward from elite Treasure Trails.

It is a preferred weapon for players buying their first dragon weapon as it has a low cost but can still inflict significant damage. For a long time, prior to the 2005 introduction of the abyssal whip and dragon scimitar, this was the weapon of choice for both player killing and training.

It can be upgraded to the Dragon longsword (bh) with a Dragon longsword imbue scroll, which has a +4 increased stab and +6 slash attack bonus, and a +25% accuracy bonus to the special attack. In addition, the special attack consumes only 15% special attack energy rather than 25%, and is one tick faster (2.4 seconds instead of 3.0 seconds). The upgraded version can only be used for PKing in the Bounty Hunter minigame.
1309:
The iron 2h sword is a two-handed sword that is stronger than the bronze 2h sword. As with other iron weaponry, it can be wielded at level 1 Attack.

Players can make an iron 2h sword with the Smithing skill at level 29 using 3 iron bars, giving the player 75 Smithing experience.
1325:
The steel scimitar is a scimitar made by using 2 steel bars on an anvil, as long as you have a hammer and at least level 35 Smithing, granting 75 experience. Players can purchase this scimitar from Zeke's Superior Scimitars in Al Kharid.

Players require 5 Attack to wield steel weapons.
1327:
The black scimitar is a scimitar with a slightly higher attack bonus than the steel scimitar. It requires level 10 Attack to wield.

A black scimitar can be found in King Lathas' castle in East Ardougne. The respawn rate of a black scimitar here is about 12 minutes and 30 seconds. It requires level 61 Thieving to access. It can also be bought from Briget's Weapons.

As with all black and white equipment, the black scimitar cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
1329: The Mithril scimitar is a scimitar stronger than the black scimitar. Like all mithril weapons, it requires 20 Attack to wield. It can only be used in combat. Players can make a mithril scimitar with the Smithing skill at level 55 using 2 mithril bars, giving 100 experience.
1331:
The adamant scimitar is the fourth strongest scimitar in the game, behind rune, gilded and dragon. Like most adamant weapons, it requires 30 Attack to wield.

Players can make it with 75 Smithing using two adamantite bars, earning 125 experience. The scimitar can also be obtained from killing monsters, and is a reward from the quest The Feud.

Smithing an adamant scimitar in the Resource Area is a task for the Wilderness Hard Diary.

A bronze warhammer is a warhammer made with 3 bronze bars, requiring 9 Smithing, yielding 37.5 Smithing experience.

It can be purchased from Skulgrimen's Battle Gear and Vigr's Warhammers for 61 coins.

One can substitute a regular hammer when banging the big door at the entrance of Bandos' Stronghold in the God Wars Dungeon.

The mithril warhammer is a warhammer stronger than the black warhammer, being made out of mithril. It may be used as an effective way of killing monsters weak to crush, such as earth warriors. Unlike other mithril weapons, it requires level 20 in Strength to wield.

Players can make a mithril warhammer with the Smithing skill at level 59 using 3 mithril bars, giving the player 150 Smithing experience. Members can purchase this warhammer from Skulgrimen's Battle Gear in Rellekka, and Vigr's Warhammers in Keldagrim.

The mithril warhammer can be used as a substitute for a regular hammer when banging the big door at the entrance of Bandos' Stronghold in the God Wars Dungeon.

1349:
The iron axe is the second weakest axe in Old School RuneScape, being slightly better than the bronze axe. It can be used in combat or in Woodcutting to cut trees. An iron axe has the same level requirements as a bronze axe, making it the better choice for new players.

The success rate for chopping a log is approximately 150% that of the Bronze axe.

Players can make an iron axe with the Smithing skill at level 16 using one iron bar, giving the player 25 Smithing experience. Players can purchase this axe from Bob's Brilliant Axes in Lumbridge and Aemad's Adventuring Supplies. in Ardougne.
1359:
The rune axe is in the third-best tier of Woodcutting axes available to members and is the best tier axe available to free-to-play players. It is outclassed by the crystal axe, infernal axe, 3rd Age axe, and dragon axe, and is equivalent to the gilded axe (which is also available in free-to-play). Level 41 Woodcutting is required to use this axe.

Like any Woodcutting axe, its primary use is as a tool to cut trees in order to obtain logs and gain experience in the Woodcutting skill. As with all axes, it does not need to be wielded to cut down trees, but will work from the inventory. The success rate for receiving a set of logs when chopping a tree with a rune axe is approximately 350% that of a bronze axe, or 17% better than an adamant axe. It can also be used as a weapon for melee combat; the player must have an Attack level of 40 to wield this axe.

Players can make a rune axe with the Smithing skill at level 86 using one runite bar, granting 75 Smithing experience. It can be purchased from Perry's Chop-chop Shop for 40,960.
1363:
The iron battleaxe is the second-weakest battleaxe in Old School RuneScape, being more powerful than the bronze battleaxe. Like all iron weapons, it can be wielded at level 1 Attack.

Players can make an iron battleaxe with level 25 Smithing using three iron bars, giving 75 experience. It is a slashing weapon, which makes it good for monsters with a slash weakness. Players can purchase this battleaxe from Brian's Battleaxe Bazaar in Port Sarim and Bob's Brilliant Axes shop in Lumbridge.
1373:
The rune battleaxe is the fourth strongest battleaxe, with zombie axe being the strongest, followed by the leaf-bladed battleaxe and the dragon battleaxe. Like most rune weapons, it requires 40 Attack to wield.

Players may make a rune battleaxe with 95 Smithing by using 3 rune bars at an anvil with a hammer, giving the player 225 Smithing experience.

Any monster that has access to the rare drop table can also drop the rune battleaxe.
1377:
The dragon battleaxe is a one-handed axe requiring 60 Attack and the completion of Heroes' Quest to wield. Though not commonly used as a primary weapon, it has a useful strength-boosting special attack that can be activated before switching to a more powerful weapon to attack with.

As with most dragon equipment, the dragon battleaxe cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
1379:
A staff is a cheap magic weapon which provides modest magical bonuses and the autocast option when equipped. Due to not possessing any elemental features and offering poor combat stats, it is only useful as a very cheap option for autocasting.

The staff can most easily be purchased from Zaff's staff shop in Varrock. It can also be bought on the Grand Exchange, obtained through other players or dropped by various enemies.

Although it is obtainable for a lower price than other staffs, investing into an elemental staff will save a lot more over time in rune costs.
1381:
A staff of air is the basic air elemental staff. It provides unlimited amounts of air runes as well as the autocast option when equipped. All elemental staves offer the same Magic bonuses and only differ by the type of rune they supply and their Melee stats.

The staff can be purchased from various shops across Gielinor, including Zaff's Superior Staffs! in Varrock. It can also be bought on the Grand Exchange, obtained through other players, dropped by various enemies, or obtained as a reward from beginner and easy clue caskets.

Players with access to a crystal ball within a player-owned house may change the element of this staff.
1385:
A staff of earth is the basic earth elemental staff. It provides unlimited amounts of earth runes as well as the autocast option when equipped. All elemental staves offer the same Magic bonuses and only differ by the type of rune they supply and their Melee stats.

The staff can be purchased from various shops across Gielinor, including Zaff's Superior Staffs! in Varrock. It can also be bought on the Grand Exchange, obtained through other players, dropped by various enemies, or found as a continually spawning item in the lava maze.

Players with access to a crystal ball within a player-owned house may change the element of this staff.
1387:
A staff of fire is the basic fire elemental staff. It provides unlimited amounts of fire runes as well as the autocast option when equipped. All elemental staves offer the same Magic bonuses and only differ by the type of rune they supply and their Melee stats.

The staff can be purchased from various shops across Gielinor, including Zaff's Superior Staffs! in Varrock. It can also be bought on the Grand Exchange, obtained through other players, or dropped by various enemies.

Players with access to a crystal ball within a player-owned house may change the element of this staff.

When equipped, players are granted the fiery attribute and will therefore receive additional damage in PvP from the special effects of Pearl bolts (e) and Pearl dragon bolts (e).
1391:
A battlestaff is a members-only magic weapon which provides standard magical bonuses, heightened melee bonuses, and the autocast option when equipped. It requires 30 Attack and 30 Magic to wield. Due to not having any elemental features, this staff has limited long-term use. Its advantage over basic tier elemental staves and other lesser staves are its melee and magic bonuses.

The staff can be purchased from Zaff's Superior Staffs! in Varrock after the completion of the quest What Lies Below, and he'll stock 15 to 120 extra staves daily for players who have fully completed task tiers of the Varrock Diary (they can be obtained by interacting with the barrel in the north-west corner of the shop). The magic store owner in the Wizards' Guild and Baba Yaga on the Lunar Isle also stock them. It can also be bought on the Grand Exchange, obtained through other players, dropped by various enemies, or fletched from Celastrus bark with level 40 Fletching.

Battlestaves can be used to make elemental battlestaves. By using the appropriate (air, water, earth, fire) charge orb spell on an Obelisk with an unpowered orb in their inventory, a player can make an elemental orb, which can then be used on a battlestaff to make the corresponding elemental battlestaff. Elemental battlestaves can be upgraded to mystic staves by giving 40,000 to Thormac after the completion of the quest Scorpion Catcher. After completion of the Hard Kandarin Diary and Elite Kandarin Diary, Thormac will only require 30,000 and 20,000 respectively.
1397:
The air battlestaff is an elemental staff requiring 30 Attack and 30 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of air runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

This staff can be created at level 66 Crafting by combining an air orb and battlestaff. It can also be upgraded to a mystic air staff by paying Thormac 40,000 coins to upgrade it (less with the completion of certain Kandarin Diaries). The mystic air staff is an even stronger alternative, providing better melee and magic stat bonuses.
1399:
The earth battlestaff is an elemental staff requiring 30 Attack and 30 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of earth runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

This staff can be created at level 58 Crafting by combining an earth orb and battlestaff. It can also be upgraded to a mystic earth staff by paying Thormac 40,000 coins to upgrade it (less with the completion of certain Kandarin Diaries). The mystic earth staff is an even stronger alternative, providing better melee and magic stat bonuses.
1403:
The mystic water staff is an elemental staff requiring 40 Attack and 40 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of water runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

This staff can be created after the completion of the quest Scorpion Catcher by taking a water battlestaff and 40,000 to Thormac. After completion of the Hard Kandarin Diary and Elite Kandarin Diary, Thormac will only require 30,000 or 20,000 respectively.
1420:
The Iron mace is a mace made of iron. It is the second weakest mace available in the game. It requires level 1 Attack to wield, and can be created by using an iron bar on an anvil (as long as the player has level 17 Smithing). It can be bought at Flynn's Mace Market in Falador.

It can be found in the Edgeville jail and in a house to the east of the Ardougne market.
1430: An adamant mace is a mace that requires level 30 Attack to wield. Players can make an adamant mace with the Smithing skill at level 72 using 1 Adamant bar, giving 62.5 Smithing experience. Players can purchase this mace from Flynn's Mace Market in Falador or the weapons shop in the Warriors' Guild, and is also dropped by Twisted Banshees.
1432:
A rune mace is a mace made of runite. It requires 40 Attack. It can be made at level 87 Smithing using one Rune bar.

It is currently the sixth-strongest mace in the game, surpassed by the Void knight mace, Barronite mace, Dragon mace, Tzhaar-ket-em, and the Inquisitor's mace. It is the second strongest free-to-play mace, behind the Barronite mace which has a higher crush and strength bonus, but a lower prayer bonus.

The rune mace can be purchased from Scavvo's Rune Store in the Champions' Guild for a price of 14,400 coins after obtaining 32 quest points. It can also be purchased from Spike's Spikes in Outer Fortis for 18,720 coins, only requiring access to Varlamore.

The rune mace can be combined with Scurrius' spine on an anvil using a hammer to create the bone mace, requiring 35 Smithing. Alternatively, Historian Aldo can do so for a fee of 50,000 coins.
1434:
The dragon mace is a one-handed spiked weapon and the strongest of the standard maces. It can only be wielded by players who have an Attack level of at least 60 and who have completed the Heroes' Quest.

The mace can be purchased for 50,000 coins at the Happy Heroes' H'emporium in the Heroes' Guild, or from other players.

It can also be obtained as a reward from elite clues and master clues.

It can be upgraded to the Dragon mace (bh) with a Dragon mace imbue scroll, which has a +4 increased stab and crush attack bonus. In addition, the special attack consumes only 15% special attack energy rather than 25%, and rolls against 60% of the target's crush defence rather than 100%. The upgraded version can only be used for PKing in the Bounty Hunter minigame.

As with most dragon equipment, the dragon mace cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
1436:
Rune essence is a raw material used in the Runecraft skill that can be crafted into low-level runes, namely air, mind, water, earth, fire, and body runes. Unlike runes, rune essence does not stack. Players need pure essence to craft any other type of rune, which can only be mined in members worlds.

There are a few ways of obtaining rune essence, other than by trading with other players.

Free players may mine rune essence in the rune essence mine, unlocked after completing the Rune Mysteries quest. To reach these mines, players need to be teleported by one of several NPCs. In members worlds, players will also mine Rune essence until reaching level 30 Mining when they will automatically mine pure essence. Mining from one of the rocks that have an unlimited supply of essence gives 5 Mining experience per essence. A pickaxe is needed, just like any other mining activity.
1438:
The air talisman is a talisman that allows players to enter the Air Altar. At the altar, the player can use the Runecraft skill to turn rune essence or pure essence into air runes.

Also at the Air Altar, an air talisman can be combined with a silver tiara to make an air tiara for 25 Runecraft experience by using the tiara on the altar while having an air talisman in the inventory. This consumes the talisman, but the air tiara can be used the same as an air talisman and can be worn, opening an inventory slot to carry another essence.

Air talismans can be used to create combination runes. The talisman is consumed when used as the "secondary" talisman to make these runes.

Air talismans can be obtained as a reward from the Rune Mysteries quest, or as drops from various monsters.
1440: An earth talisman is a type of talisman that lets the player access the Earth Altar. Use the talisman on the altar to get inside to create earth runes. You can also access the Earth Altar by using an earth tiara, which can be equipped to save inventory space and is made using the earth talisman. When you make an earth tiara, you are granted 32.5 Runecraft experience. If you are a member, it can be used to runecraft dust runes at the Air Altar, mud runes at the Water Altar, or lava rune at the Fire Altar. The earth talisman is consumed in the process.
1442: A mysterious power emanates from the talisman...
1444: A mysterious power emanates from the talisman...
1446:
A body talisman is a talisman used in the Runecraft skill. It allows players to enter the Body Altar and create body runes from rune, pure, or daeyalt essence.

At the Body Altar, a body talisman can be combined with a tiara to make a body tiara for 37.5 Runecraft experience by using the tiara on the altar. This makes the talisman disappear, but the body tiara also grants access to the Body Altar when worn.

Making body tiaras is one of the fastest runecraft training methods for free to play, making these talismans desired by these players. Because of this, body talismans are relatively expensive on the Grand Exchange.
1448:
The mind talisman is a talisman used to access the Mind Altar located between Ice Mountain and Goblin Village. It can be combined with a tiara to make a mind tiara for 27.5 Runecraft experience at the Mind Altar by using the tiara on the altar. This makes the talisman disappear, but the tiara can be used in just the same way and can be worn.

One is required to create a mind tiara for the Easy Falador Diary.
