1470:
The red bead is a bead used in Imp Catcher quest. It is a drop from Imps and is returned to Wizard Mizgog in the Wizards' Tower along with Black bead, White bead and Yellow bead to finish the quest.

The bead can also be used to bait traps when hunting imps.
1472:
The Yellow bead is a bead used in the Imp Catcher quest. It is returned to Wizard Mizgog in the Wizards' Tower along with a black bead, a white bead and a red bead to finish the quest. It can be obtained by killing imps.

The bead can also be used to bait traps when hunting imps.
1513:
Magic logs are logs that can be acquired using the Woodcutting skill from magic trees. Cutting magic trees requires a Woodcutting level of 75 or higher and yields 250 Woodcutting experience per log cut. Due to the slow speed at which magic trees are cut at this level, it is advised that players wait until they have a Woodcutting level of at least 85 before chopping magic trees. Players can expect to gain up to 130 magic logs per hour using a dragon axe.

Magic logs can be fletched into unstrung magic shortbows with a Fletching level of 80, granting 83.3 Fletching experience, or into unstrung magic longbows with a Fletching level of 85, granting 91.5 Fletching experience.

Magic logs can also be burnt with a Firemaking level of 75, granting 303.8 Firemaking experience.

Magic logs are needed for three quests: twelve for Desert Treasure I, one for Mourning's End Part I, and three for unlocking the Gnome Stronghold balloon route (requirement for Monkey Madness II), requiring sixteen magic logs in total.

Ultimate Ironmen can permanently store magic logs with the Friendly Forester log storage or balloon transport log storage.

6 magic logs can be used to light an Abyssal lantern, requiring 75 Firemaking.
1515: Logs cut from a yew tree.
1517:
Maple logs are received from cutting maple trees requiring a Woodcutting level of 45 and yield 100 Woodcutting experience (110 with Kandarin Medium Diary) per log. Maple logs can be burned with a Firemaking level of 45, giving 135 experience per log. Maple logs can also be fletched into different items: arrow shafts, maple shortbow (u), maple longbow (u), maple stock and maple shield.

Because of their low price and the moderate experience they provide, maple logs are commonly used for training Firemaking.

6 maple logs can be used to light an Abyssal lantern, requiring 45 Firemaking.
1519: Logs cut from a willow tree.
1521: Logs cut from an oak tree.
1539: Keeps things in place fairly permanently.
1540: This provides partial protection from dragonbreath attacks.
1550: Garlic is an item used in several quests. Although it cannot be eaten on its own, it is used in Cooking in making Spicy sauce and in Herblore in making Guthix balance potions.
1573:
Doogle leaves are herbs that players can use on a raw sardine to make a seasoned sardine. They then feed the seasoned sardine to Fluffs, a cat in the Gertrude's Cat quest. After the quest, players may still season sardines with the leaves, but the doogle sardines can not be used to feed player-owned kittens.

It may also be needed for the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest as a possible seasoning for Fycie, Bugs or Rantz.

They are found on the ground south of Gertrude's house (west of Varrock), in Feldip Hills (directly west of the swamp where you can fill your ogre-bellows and catch the toads during the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest), and east of Rellekka, near the swaying tree.
1592: A ring mould allows a player to make rings through the Crafting skill out of gold bars and possibly gems by using them on a furnace. It can be bought at various crafting shops, and an unlimited amount can also be taken from a tool store 4 in a player-owned house.
1599: Used to make holy symbols of Saradomin.
1601:
Diamonds are precious gems used mainly in Crafting. They can be cut from uncut diamonds with a chisel at level 43 Crafting, yielding 107.5 experience.

A diamond is required to enter the Zanaris marketplace.
1605: Emeralds are precious gems used mainly in Crafting. They can be cut from uncut emeralds with a chisel at level 27 Crafting, yielding 67.5 experience.
1611:
Jade is a semi-precious gem used mainly in Crafting. It can be cut from an uncut jade with a chisel at level 13 Crafting, yielding 20 experience. There is a chance to unsuccessfully cut the jade, resulting in a crushed gem and 5 experience.

One jade is used in the Legends' Quest.
1615:
Dragonstones are rare gems which can be cut from uncut dragonstones, requiring 55 Crafting and yielding 137.5 experience. It can then be made into dragonstone jewellery by using a furnace along with a gold bar and a mould.

Monsters with access to the rare drop table have a chance to drop cut dragonstones.

Dragonstones from the Mage Training Arena minigame are different, providing pizazz points when enchantment spells are used on them and they cannot be taken outside the enchanting chamber.

5 dragonstones can be given to Olbertus in the Forthos Dungeon to receive a temple coin and unlock the Sacred Bone Burner.
1617:
An uncut diamond is a precious gem used in Crafting. It can be cut with a chisel to make a diamond, requiring 43 Crafting and yielding 107.5 experience.

Uncut diamonds can be obtained in several ways: randomly while mining ores, as drops from monsters (mainly those which have access to the rare drop table), gem shops, or as a reward from certain minigames and random events. They are also a common reward from Managing Miscellania.

With level 40 Mining and the quest Shilo Village completed, players can mine the gem rocks in Shilo Village. Gem rocks may also appear while playing the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup activity, where players can mine them 3 times. Another method to get uncut diamonds is by cracking wall safes in the Rogues' Den, but this requires level 50 Thieving.

An uncut diamond is a reward from the Troll Romance quest and is dropped by the Slagilith during One Small Favour.
1619: This would be worth more cut.
1621: This would be worth more cut.
1623: This would be worth more cut.
1625: This would be worth more cut.
1627: This would be worth more cut.
1629: This would be worth more cut.
1631: This would be worth more cut.
1637:
The sapphire ring is made by using a gold bar on a furnace while having a sapphire and a ring mould in one's inventory. Making it requires a Crafting level of 20, and gives 40 experience.

Grum's Gold Exchange in Port Sarim buys at better price than High Alchemy, depending on his current stock. If he has no sapphire rings for sale, he buys the first for 630 coins.

They are dropped by Crawling Hands, and can also be obtained from bird nests. The sapphire ring can be enchanted into a ring of recoil by members with the Lvl-1 Enchant spell.
1639:
The Emerald ring is made by using a gold bar on a furnace whilst having an emerald and ring mould in the inventory. Making it requires a Crafting level of 27, and gives 55 experience.

The ring has no stats but can be enchanted using Lvl-2 Enchant ( 27 ) to make a ring of dueling.

Emerald rings can be sold to Grum's Gold Exchange in Port Sarim, starting at 892 coins each when none are in stock.
1643:
The diamond ring is made by using a gold bar, a cut diamond and a ring mould on a furnace. Making it requires a Crafting level of 43, and gives 85 experience.

The diamond ring can be enchanted into a ring of life by members through the use of the Lvl-4 Enchant spell.
1654: I wonder if this is valuable.
1656: I wonder if this is valuable.
1658:
The emerald necklace is made by using a gold bar on a furnace with an emerald and a necklace mould in your inventory. It requires a Crafting level of 29 and provides 60 experience when made.

The emerald necklace can be enchanted into a binding necklace by casting Lvl-2 Enchant. This requires a Magic level of 27, a cosmic rune and three air runes.

Emerald necklaces can be sold to Grum's Gold Exchange in Port Sarim, starting at 997 coins each if there are none in stock.
1660: I wonder if this is valuable.
1662:
A Diamond necklace is made by using a gold bar, a diamond, and a necklace mould on a furnace. This requires level 56 Crafting and gives 90 Crafting experience.

A diamond necklace can be enchanted into a phoenix necklace by using the Lvl-4 Enchant spell. This requires level 57 Magic, one cosmic rune, and ten earth runes.
1664: I wonder if this is valuable.
1673: It needs a string so I can wear it.
1675: It needs a string so I can wear it.
1677:
An emerald amulet (u) can be made at level 31 Crafting by using a gold bar on a furnace while carrying a cut emerald and an amulet mould. This grants the player 70 Crafting experience. The amulet can then be strung with a ball of wool to create a strung emerald amulet, granting an additional 4 experience. The strung amulet can be enchanted into an amulet of defence using the Lvl-2 Enchant spell, requiring level 27 Magic.

This amulet can also be strung with a magic string instead, turning it into a pre-nature amulet. This amulet can then be enchanted into an amulet of nature.
1679: It needs a string so I can wear it.
1681:
A diamond amulet (u) is the unstrung version of the regular diamond amulet. It is made by using a gold bar on a furnace, while having a cut diamond and an amulet mould in the inventory.

Level 70 Crafting is required to make one, yielding 100 experience. When used with a ball of wool, it becomes a diamond amulet, giving 4 experience. After it is strung, it can be enchanted into an amulet of power, requiring level 57 Magic and yielding 67 experience.
1683:
A dragonstone amulet (u) is the unstrung version of the regular dragonstone amulet. It is made by using a gold bar on a furnace, while having a cut dragonstone and an amulet mould in the inventory.

Level 80 Crafting is required to make one, and crafting this item grants 150 experience. Stringing this item using a ball of wool gives 4 experience.

After it is strung, it can be enchanted into an Amulet of glory, which requires level 68 Magic and yields 78 experience. This is the highest level item that can be made with a dragonstone.
1694: I wonder if I can get this enchanted.
1696:
The emerald amulet is created by using a gold bar on a furnace while also carrying a cut emerald and an amulet mould. This requires 31 Crafting and grants 70 Crafting experience. The resulting unstrung amulet is then used with a ball of wool, granting an additional 4 experience.

It has no stat bonuses, but can be enchanted with the Lvl-2 Enchant spell to become an Amulet of defence which gives some defensive bonuses.

Emerald amulets can be sold to Grum's Gold Exchange in Port Sarim, starting at 892 coins each if there are none in stock.
1698: I wonder if I can get this enchanted.
1700:
A diamond amulet is an amulet created by using a ball of wool on a diamond amulet (u). Doing so, grants 4 Crafting experience.

The unstrung diamond amulet is created by using a gold bar and a diamond on a furnace with an amulet mould in the inventory. It is the fourth highest level amulet that can be created. This requires a Crafting level of 70 and provides 100 Crafting experience when made.

It can be turned into an amulet of power with Lvl-4 Enchant granting 67 magic experience.

An easier way for P2P ironmen to obtain one without level 70 Crafting is to loot the H.A.M. Store rooms.

The diamond amulet is the highest level craftable object that F2P can make.
1702:
The dragonstone amulet is an amulet worn in the neck slot. It is made by stringing an unstrung dragonstone amulet with a ball of wool or the String Jewellery spell. The unstrung amulet requires 80 Crafting and is made by using a gold bar on a furnace with a cut dragonstone and an amulet mould in the inventory.

Crafting one in the Neitiznot furnace is a task in the Elite Fremennik Diary.

The amulet can be enchanted with the Lvl-5 Enchant spell into an amulet of glory, where it gains the ability to teleport to Edgeville, Musa Point, Al Kharid, and Draynor Village when charged at the Fountain of Heroes, Fountain of Uhld and the Fountain of Rune.
1712: A dragonstone amulet with 4 magic charges.
1714: Unstrung symbols can be made at 16 Crafting with a silver bar and a holy mould at a furnace, granting 50 crafting experience. It can be used with a ball of wool to create an unblessed symbol. This can then be taken to Brother Jered who will bless it at level 31 Prayer (including F2P), or it can be blessed at level 50 Prayer using a completed Holy book.
1716:
Unblessed symbols are made by using a ball of wool with an unstrung symbol, granting the player 4 Crafting experience.

Players with a Prayer level of 31 or higher can have their unblessed symbols blessed by Brother Jered in the Edgeville Monastery, turning them into holy symbols.

A player with a Prayer level of 50 or higher can bless a symbol themselves by using a completed Holy book or book of balance at the expense of 2 Prayer points with the holy book and 7 Prayer points with the book of balance.
1718: A blessed holy symbol of Saradomin.
1720: Unstrung emblems can be used with a ball of wool to create an unpowered symbol. The Spirit of Scorpius in the Grave of Scorpius will bless an unpowered symbol, resulting in an unholy symbol, for players who have completed the Observatory Quest. Players with an Unholy book or a Book of Balance and a Prayer level of at least 50 can bless their own unpowered symbols to create unholy symbols at a cost of 4 Prayer points each.
1725:
The amulet of strength is an enchanted ruby amulet. Players frequently use it to increase their max hit. At level 50 Crafting, players can craft a ruby amulet. With at least 49 Magic, Lvl-3 Enchant can be cast on a ruby amulet to create an amulet of strength.

A trimmed version of the amulet of strength is available from medium clue scrolls.
1727:
An amulet of magic is an amulet that gives a Magic attack bonus when worn. It is created by casting Lvl-1 Enchant on a sapphire amulet. It is one of the cheapest and most common amulets in the game because of the low Crafting level to craft it, how common sapphires are, and the low Magic level to enchant the amulet.

A normal amulet of magic, as well as its trimmed variant are both possible reward for the completion of easy Treasure Trails.
1729: An enchanted emerald amulet of protection.
1731:
An amulet of power offers a good balance of attack and defence bonuses for all classes of combat. It is created by casting Lvl-4 Enchant on a diamond amulet, and has no requirements to be worn.

This item is a less expensive option for players who do not wish to buy an amulet of glory. It lacks the glory's teleportation capabilities and has weaker attack and Prayer bonuses, but has the same strength bonus as well as higher defence bonuses.

This amulet is currently the best overall amulet for F2P players, although the amulet of strength is better in some cases, such as fighting low defence targets with melee.

A helpful way for P2P Ironmen to obtain one is by looting the H.A.M. Store rooms for a diamond amulet, and then enchanting it with 57 Magic. Shipwreck Salvaging at Mercenary shipwrecks (73 Sailing) also commonly provides them.
1733: Used with a thread to make clothes.
1734:
Thread is used along with a needle to make armour out of leather, dragon leather and cured yak-hide. Each thread spool has 5 uses before it is consumed. A "use" means an action performed, not number of leathers used (e.g. making vambraces, which use 1 hide each, consumes thread at the same rate as making chaps, which use 2 hides each).

After completion of Death on the Isle, a Costume needle can be used for crafting without needing thread.
1735:
Shears can be bought in almost any general store for 1 gp. They are required to shear wool from sheep, and are needed for the Sheep Shearer quest if you choose to gather the wool yourself. They are also needed for the quest A Tail of Two Cats.

They can be picked up off of the table in Fred the Farmer's house for the quest Sheep Shearer. It can also be found in Hosidius, in the building just north of the estate agent.
1737: I think this came from a sheep.
1739: I should take this to the tannery.
1743:
Hard leather is made by taking cowhides to a tanner. The lunar spell Tan Leather can also be used at level 78 Magic, and tans up to 5 cowhides at once into hard leather.

Combined with thread and a needle, it can be used to make hardleather bodies at level 28 Crafting, granting 35 crafting experience.

With a hammer and 15 bronze nails, members can attach two hard leathers onto an oak shield to create a hard leather shield. Doing so requires level 41 Crafting and grants 70 experience.

Hard leather can also be obtained as rare loot from baby implings.

One piece of hard leather is required for Animal Magnetism.
1745: It's a piece of prepared green dragonhide.
1747: Black dragonhide (also called Black d'hide by tanners) is a 100% drop from black dragons, brutal black dragons, lava dragons, and the King Black Dragon. The hide can be tanned to become black dragon leather by paying a tanner or by using the Tan Leather lunar spell. A tanner will charge 20 coins for each hide, or 45 in Canifis. Tanners can be found in Al Kharid, the Ranging Guild, Canifis, the Crafting Guild, Auburnvale, and Forthos Dungeon.
1749: The scaly rough hide from a Red Dragon.
1751:
Blue dragonhide (also known as blue d'hide) is a 100% drop item from blue dragons when killed. Players can take hides to a tanner to make blue dragon leather for a fee of 20 coins at a tanner (45 coins from Sbott in Canifis) or by using the Tan Leather lunar spell. Tanners can be found in Al Kharid, the Ranging Guild, Forthos Dungeon, Canifis, the Kebos Lowlands, Auburnvale and the Crafting Guild.

Members can craft pieces of blue dragonhide armour from blue dragon leather with level 66 Crafting.
1753: The scaly rough hide from a Green Dragon.
1755:
A chisel is a tool used in the Crafting skill to cut and shape hard non-metals, mainly gems and limestone. Chisels are also used in Fletching to cut gems into bolt tips. Chisels can be purchased for 1 coin at all general stores, except for those in Dorgesh-Kaan and Ardougne. There is a free-to-play chisel spawn in the Crafting Guild.

At level 15 Construction, members can make a tool store 1 for the workshop room of their house, which will provide an unlimited supply of chisels.
1757:
Brown aprons are used to enter the Crafting Guild. They can be purchased from several clothing stores, such as Thessalia's Fine Clothes store in the centre of Varrock, for 2 coins.

A brown apron can be obtained from the Tool store 3 built in the Workshop of a player-owned house. Members can also claim them from Malignius Mortifer after the Swan Song quest.
1761:
Soft clay is used to create items in the Crafting and Construction skills and to make magic tablets. It can be created by using a container of water such as a vial of water, jug of water, or bucket of water on clay, by using the Humidify spell, or by mining clay rocks whilst wearing a bracelet of clay. It is used on a potter's wheel to craft various Crafting items.

The only place to mine soft clay directly is in the Trahaearn mine, where soft clay rocks can be found. In addition, wearing a bracelet of clay in this mine can yield 2 soft clays per action, whereas mining clay rocks elsewhere yields only a single soft clay per action.

In addition to mining soft clay in Prifddinas, soft clay packs can be bought from Prospector Percy's Nugget Shop in Motherlode Mine for 10 golden nuggets each, Dusuri's Star Shop at the Mining Guild entrance in Falador for 150 stardust each, and Belona's Mining Guild Mineral Exchange for 10 unidentified minerals each. Each soft clay pack contains 100 Soft Clay.
1763: A little bottle of red dye.
1765: Yellow dye is a dye that can be created by taking 2 onions and 5 coins to Aggie in Draynor Village, or 2 onions and 25 coins if taken to Ali the dyer in Pollnivneach. It can also be bought in Lletya from Oronwen for 6 coins. It can also be found in the farmhouse featured in Getting Ahead, south of the Farming Guild, located in the shelves next to the stairs in the house. Yellow dye can be combined with red dye to create orange dye, and with blue dye to create green dye. It can be used to dye normal capes yellow.
1767:
Blue dye can be obtained from Aggie in Draynor Village in exchange for 2 woad leaves and 5 coins, or from Ali the dyer in Pollnivneach in exchange for 2 woad leaves and 25 coins. It can also be purchased from Oronwen in Lletya, Guinevere in Prifddinas, or Xochitl in Tal Teklan.

Blue dye is mainly used in the Goblin Diplomacy, Land of the Goblins, Ghosts Ahoy and Mourning's End Part I quests. Blue dye can be used with a black cape (or any other colour) to create a blue cape. It can also be used to turn a black robe into a blue robe.
1769:
Orange dye is a dye made by combining red dye and yellow dye. Its main use is in the quest Goblin Diplomacy, when the player must use the dye on goblin mail. This item can also be bought from the Lletya Seamstress for 6 coins. In order to access the shop, one must have at least started the Mourning's End Part I quest.

Players can also obtain red and yellow dye from Aggie in Draynor Village provided she is given the ingredients needed and 5 coins per bottle of dye. Players can then combine the red and yellow dye to make orange dye.
1771: A little bottle of green dye.
1773: A little bottle of purple dye.
1775: Hot glass ready to be blown into useful objects.
1777: I need a bow stave to attach this to.
1779:
Flax is a resource that can be picked from plants in various locations around Gielinor. Multiple can be collected from the same plant. Flax can also be harvested from a hops patch after planting flax seeds with 18 Farming.

It is used to make bow strings at a spinning wheel, requiring 10 Crafting, yielding 15 Crafting experience. Flax can also be spun via the Spin Flax Lunar spell. It is also used to spin linen yarn or as payment to protect hemp plants (x6). Linen yarn can be used to build a linen trawling net or woven into bolts of linen, which can be used to upgrade masts and sails on a player's boat.

Completing the Kandarin Diary allows players to exchange noted flax with the flax keeper once a day in exchange for bow strings. The easy diary unlocks 30 per day, medium 60 per day, hard 120 per day, and elite 250 per day.

Flax in the Tree Gnome Stronghold does not exist in Deadman Mode worlds.
1781:
Soda ash is made into Molten glass to make glass items in Crafting. Soda ash is made using seaweed, giant seaweed, swamp weed, or edible seaweed on a range, oven, or fire. Smelting it with a bucket of sand in a furnace or the Lunar spell Superglass Make produces molten glass.

It can be purchased from Trader Stan's Trading Post at charter ships for 5 coins; the closest one to a bank is in Port Khazard. Another option close to a bank is the Corsair Cove shop, which is about 10 tiles farther from a bank but may be more likely to have soda ash in stock.
1783: A bucket of sand can be obtained by using an empty bucket with a sand pit or sand pile. They may also be obtained from Drew by mining sandstone and depositing it in the grinder next to him. They are a key component in creating molten glass, which is often used in Crafting and Construction, either via a furnace along with soda ash or by casting Superglass Make along with soda ash, seaweed or giant seaweed.
1785: A glassblowing pipe is a tool used to make items from molten glass using the Crafting skill. It is required to make glass items. The item can be obtained from Fritz the Glassblower's house found in the south-western area of Entrana, taken from a tool store 3 in a player-owned house (required 35 Construction), from Grandpa Jack's house (from Fishing Contest quest), bought from the Piscatoris Fishing Colony after finishing Swan Song, or bought from charter ship locations (from the crew).
1787: I need to put this in a pottery oven.
1789: I need to put this in a pottery oven.
1791: I need to put this in a pottery oven.
1793:
Woad leaves can be harvested from a flower patch after planting woad seeds. They are used to make blue dye and, by extension, green and purple dye. Players must take two woad leaves and 5 coins to Aggie to make blue dye, which is enough to dye one item.

They can either be grown through Farming or bought from Wyson the gardener in Falador Park. Offering him 20 coins provides the best value since he actually gives two for being so generous. Adding them to a compost bin makes regular compost.
1794: Bronze wire can be created by players with level 4 in Smithing by using one bronze bar on an anvil with a hammer in your inventory. A total of 7 are used in quests, such as Creature of Fenkenstrain (3 required, unnoted), Recipe for Disaster/Freeing Pirate Pete (3 required) and Shilo Village (1 required).
1823: A full waterskin with four portions of water.
1831: A completely empty waterskin - you'll need to fill it up.
1854: Allows you to pass through the Shantay pass into the Kharid Desert.
1859: I need to cook this first.
1861:
Ugthanki meat is a type of food that restores 3 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw ugthanki meat, granting 40 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt meat. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Ugthanki meat is unusual as despite lacking a cooking requirement, it never stops burning altogether even at level 99. At levels up to 82, the chance to burn this meat is higher on a range than on a fire.

Ugthanki meat is used to make ugthanki kebab which restores 19 hitpoints.
1865: Nicely baked pitta bread. Needs more ingredients to make a kebab.
1869: A mixture of tomatoes in a bowl.
1871: A mixture of onions in a bowl.
1873: Strips of ugthanki meat in a bowl.
1875: A mixture of chopped onions and tomatoes in a bowl.
1877:
Ugthanki & onion is an intermediate product towards making an ugthanki kebab. It is made by chopping an onion and a piece of cooked Ugthanki meat into a bowl with a knife.

If players add a tomato, this makes kebab mix, which allows players to make an Ugthanki kebab if some pitta bread is added. The pitta bread requires level 58 Cooking, but the rest can be made at level 1.
1879:
Ugthanki & tomato is an intermediate product towards making an ugthanki kebab. It is made by chopping a tomato and a piece of cooked Ugthanki meat into a bowl with a knife.

If players add an onion to make kebab mix, they can make an Ugthanki kebab if some pitta bread is added. The pitta bread requires level 58 Cooking, but the rest can be made at level 1.
1881: Kebab mix is an intermediate product towards making an ugthanki kebab. Combining it with pitta bread makes an ugthanki kebab, yielding 40 Cooking experience.
1885:
The ugthanki kebab is a type of food which restores 19 Hitpoints. It can be obtained by chopping a tomato, an onion, and a piece of cooked ugthanki meat into a bowl with a knife, then using the resulting kebab mix with a baked pitta bread. Level 58 Cooking is required to make the pitta bread, but the rest may be made at Cooking level 1. There is a chance to fail when creating one with a low Cooking level, instead creating a Ugthanki kebab (bad).

The player will exclaim Yum! in contentment if any hitpoints were restored when eaten.
1887:
A cake tin is an item used to bake cakes. Players need to add an egg, a pot of flour and a bucket of milk on to the cake tin and used in an oven.

They can be found in the Cooks' Guild, bought from any general store (except for the ones in Port Phasmatys, Ardougne, Port Khazard, Canifis, Keldagrim, Auburnvale, and Burthorpe), bought from the Culinaromancer's Chest in Lumbridge, or taken from the wooden shelves from a player-owned house. The cake tin also respawns at the house with an anvil in the level 21 Wilderness.

Once baked, the cake tin will separate from the cooked cake, unlike the pie dish, where it comes with the pie.

One cake tin is needed for the quest Troll Romance to make wax.
1891:
Cake is a type of food that restores 12 Hitpoints in total, 3 bites each healing for 4. It can be obtained by baking an uncooked cake on a cooking range, requiring level 40 Cooking and granting 180 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt cake. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 74.

Stealing a cake from the Ardougne Baker's Stall is an easy Ardougne Diary task.
1905: Probably the finest ale in Asgarnia.
1907:
The wizard's mind bomb is a type of ale that restores 1 Hitpoint and temporarily boosts Magic by +2 (+3 if level 50+ Magic) while draining Attack, Strength and Defence by ⌊Level×0.05⌋+1 (see table below). It can be obtained through brewing at level 34 Cooking, granting 314 experience per batch. It is brewed using 2 buckets of water, 2 barley malt, 4 yanillian hops, and a pot of ale yeast. It can also be bought from several shops.

The stronger, mature version of the ale is the mature wmb.

It is required for the quest Dragon Slayer I, and may also be used in Below Ice Mountain in place of a regular beer.
1909:
Greenman's ale is a type of ale that restores 1 Hitpoint and temporarily boosts Herblore by 1 while also draining Attack, Strength, and Defence by 3 when consumed. It can be obtained through brewing at level 29 Cooking, granting 281 experience per batch. It is brewed using 2 buckets of water, 2 barley malt, 4 harralander, and a pot of ale yeast. The stronger, mature version of the ale is the Greenman's ale (m).

One is required for the quest Recipe for Disaster/Another Cook's Quest.
1911: Dragon bitter is a type of ale that restores 1 Hitpoint and temporarily boosts Strength by 2 while draining Attack by 5% + 2. It can be obtained through brewing at level 39 Cooking granting 347 experience. It is brewed using 4 krandorian hops, 2 buckets of water, 2 lots of barley, and a pot of ale yeast. The stronger, mature version of the ale is the dragon bitter(m).
1913: A pint of thick dark beer.
1915: A murky glass of some sort of drink.
1917: Beer is a type of ale that restores 1 Hitpoint and temporarily boosts Strength by 2% + 1, while draining Attack by 6% + 1. Unlike other ales, it cannot be created through brewing.
1919:
Beer glasses are obtained by creating them via glassblowing, drinking certain beverages (such as beer), or by taking them shelves in the Sorceress's house. You can also get a variant of beer glass from the kitchen shelves (Wooden shelves 2 or higher) of a player-owned house, though they will disappear upon leaving the house.

A quick way to acquire beer glasses would be to buy drinks in the Burthorpe pub The Toad and Chicken, then go down into the Rogues' Den, and repeat. Drink afterwards. Another method to obtain them quickly is by searching the wall shelves in the Sorceress' house (from the Sorceress's Garden minigame), in the very south-east of Al Kharid.

The barmaids in the Rising Sun Inn buy empty beer glasses (both noted and unnoted) through dialogue for 2 coins each.

One beer glass is used in the quest: Forgettable Tale...
1925:
A bucket is one of the most common items available. They can be purchased cheaply from most general stores and can also be found in many locations throughout the game. Buckets are commonly used for skills such as Crafting, Cooking and Farming.

Buckets can contain any of the following items:

The fastest way to obtain buckets in bulk is to purchase empty bucket packs containing 100 noted empty buckets. These packs can be bought at general stores and farming shops for 500–875 coins each depending on the stock available.

Another way to quickly obtain an inventory of buckets is to search a larder in a player-owned house, remove buckets of milk and then right-click to "empty" them. This is also the fastest way to get milk.

Note that one may deposit and withdraw up to 1000 buckets from the tool leprechauns located at almost every Farming patch; no Farming level is required to do this.
1927:
A bucket of milk is a Cooking ingredient used to make a variety of drinks and foods such as choc saturdays and cakes, as well as several feeders. Players can use a bucket on a dairy cow or dairy buffalo to create a bucket of milk, or simply click on the cow or buffalo with at least one empty bucket in the inventory.

Players can turn a bucket of milk into chocolatey milk by adding chocolate dust, or add milk to nettle tea (though this does not add any effects). Depending on their Cooking level, Members can use a dairy churn to turn a bucket of milk into a pot of cream, a pat of butter, or a piece of cheese.

A bucket of milk is required to complete the quests Cook's Assistant, Gertrude's Cat, Plague City (to make a Hangover cure), and the Skippy and the Mogres miniquest (to make a hangover cure).

This, alongside the chocolatey milk, milky mixture, and hangover cure, can be stored in a bottomless milk bucket. Each bottomless milk bucket can only store one type of dairy product at a time.
1931:
A pot is an item that can be used to hold a variety of liquids or powdery substances, such as flour.

Pots can be purchased from charter ship shops as well as most general stores. They can also be found as item spawns on various counters and tables through Gielinor, including the ground-floor kitchen in Lumbridge Castle. Alternatively, they can be made by forming soft clay on a potter's wheel, then firing the resulting unfired pot in a pottery oven.

An empty pot is the icon representing a general store on the world map.

It is worth noting Toothy's Pickaxes is right next to a bank chest, making this shop the best place to buy pots in bulk.
1933:
A pot of flour is a Cooking ingredient used to produce several types of dough when combined with water.

Using an empty pot on a barrel of flour is a faster alternative to having to get grain and use a windmill. One barrel is in the kitchen of Sinclair Mansion after starting the Murder Mystery quest and another barrel is located on the 1st floor of Gordon and Mary's farm.
1939:
Swamp tar is a thick substance found in the Lumbridge Swamp, Mort Myre Swamp, and in tar barrels.

Swamp tar can be turned into swamp paste, which is used for various repairing purposes. It can also be distilled into lamp oil, which is used as fuel for various light sources, or be used to make guam, marrentill, tarromin, harralander, and irit tar, which are used as bait and ammunition for salamanders.
1941:
Swamp paste is made by mixing flour with swamp tar to make raw swamp paste, and then cooking the mixture on a fire, yielding 2 Cooking experience. It cannot be cooked on a range. It is possible to burn the tar, though it is automatically discarded. Swamp tar spawns in Lumbridge Swamp and Mort Myre Swamp.

To make a large amount of swamp paste from swamp tar, use a barrel of flour at either the Sinclair Mansion or Gordon and Mary's farm. Bring as much swamp tar as needed and 26 pots, Gordon's farm also has a pot spawn. Click the barrel to fill the pots, then combine with the swamp tar to create raw swamp paste. Repeat this until the desired amount is obtained, then cook it. A permanent fire is recommended for large amounts. There is a permanent fire at the base of Mount Karuulm, very near the fairy ring and in front of the shack with a rope spawn.

Swamp paste can also be bought from the Trader crewmembers at any of the ports in the Charter ship network, the Khazard General Store (south of Ardougne), and Rasolo (west of the Fishing Guild) are very useful for some of the quests listed below. It is also sold at the Mort'ton Builder's Store.

Swamp paste also tends to be rewarded in abundance when unlocking chests within the Shades of Mort'ton minigame.

Unlike swamp tar, swamp paste cannot be combined with herbs to form ammunition for a Salamander using the Herblore skill.
1942:
Raw potatoes are a food item that can be picked from fields around Gielinor or grown through the Farming skill at level 1 with potato seeds. They heal 1 hitpoint when eaten raw. When picking potatoes from fields, members may randomly receive 1 potato seed.

They are used in the following recipes:

Baked potato (must be cooked on a range, not a fire)

Veg ball (Gnome cooking)

Stew

Curry

Fish pie (admiral and regular, which temporarily boost Fishing level by 5 and 3, respectively)

Raw potatoes are purchasable from various stores for 1 coin each. Hudo at the Grand Tree has a stock of 10; Cobado's Groceries a stock of 10; Frenita in Yanille a stock of 5; and Wydin in Port Sarim a stock of 1, to name a few.

Members can store up to 10 potatoes in an empty sack, creating a sack of potatoes. 1 sack of potatoes is needed to protect growing onions. Adding potatoes to a compost bin makes regular compost.
1947:
Grain is obtained by picking from wheat fields growing in many places in Gielinor. They are also dropped by goblins and imps. It is used for Cooking. Six grain can be given to nearby gardeners to watch over flax grown in a hops patch.

One quick way is to get grain next to the hops patch in Yanille and go east to the bank in Yanille. Another is to use the canoe transport system on the River Lum. One could take the canoe to the Champions' Guild wheat field, then fill their inventory, then return to Edgeville to bank the wheat using the canoe. The wheat fields are also used to access Puro-Puro.

10 grain is required for Eadgar's Ruse.
1949:
A chef's hat is a white hat that grants players access to the Cooks' Guild with a Cooking level of 32. Aside from this, it has little practical use and is purely cosmetic.

It can be obtained as a drop from multiple monsters, most notably goblins, and can be purchased from the Shayzien Styles store in Shayzien.

Members can obtain an infinite supply from Teak shelves 2 in a player-owned house using the Construction skill.
1955:
Cooking apples are primarily used as an ingredient to make apple pies. They can be obtained from the Cooks' Guild, Culinaromancer's Chest, Logava Gricoller's Cooking Supplies, or alternatively, harvested from an apple tree grown from an apple tree seed in a fruit tree patch by a player with a Farming level of 27.

Baskets of apples (which contain 5 apples each) can be used in the Farming skill to pay farmers to watch planted trees. One basket is needed to watch willows and strawberries, while four baskets are needed to watch a banana tree.
1959:
Pumpkins are the first holiday food rare and second holiday rare to be dropped, the first being the scythe. Pumpkins can be obtained by completing one of the Halloween holiday events that occur once per year. This also rewards the player with all other holiday items associated with Halloween.

If you plan to sell your pumpkin, it is recommended that you put it in note form to avoid accidentally eating it.

When eaten, the pumpkin heals 14 hitpoints. However, due to their price, it is not recommended to consume pumpkins, as they heal just as much as a swordfish, which is much cheaper.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 10 June to 17 June) as part of a rare item drop.

Since the 2014 Halloween Event, Jagex decided to host a number of events in-game, most of which were live-streamed. They gave community leaders and other familiar faces an item that could be used to scatter pumpkins. Doing this allows for more consistent and varied events throughout the holiday period.
1961:
Easter eggs are edible holiday items. Two easter eggs can be obtained by completing one of the Easter holiday events that occur once per year. This also rewards the player with all other holiday items associated with Easter.

Consuming an easter egg will restore 14 hitpoints, which is the same amount of hitpoints as swordfish and pumpkins. Due to their limited availability and resulting price, easter eggs are not recommended as food.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 21 July to 28 July) as part of a rare item drop.
1971:
Kebabs are a camel meat delicacy which can be purchased in Al Kharid and Keldagrim-East for 1 coin each, or at Pollnivneach for 3 coins each. The Drunken Dwarf, Mysterious Old Man, Sandwich Lady, and Rick Turpentine random events may also grant the player a free kebab.

Unlike normal food which restores a fixed amount of Hitpoints, kebabs have varied healing quantities when consumed. A player with 86–99 Hitpoints can expect to be healed 11 health on average.

Kebabs cannot be made through the Cooking skill. They can be used on a compost bin to make regular compost.
1978:
A cup of tea is a drink which restores 3 Hitpoints and temporarily boosts Attack by 2 + 2% (rounded down); it will also instantly cancel the effect of the goading potion. Upon drinking a cup of tea, the player will exclaim Aaah, nothing like a nice cuppa tea! and an empty cup will remain in the player's inventory.

Tea may be purchased at Ye olde Tea Shoppe in Varrock or stolen at the nearby Tea stall with 5 Thieving.

A tea flask may be used to store up to five cups of tea, which will have the standard effect when consumed.
1985:
Cheese is a food item which heals 2 hitpoints when eaten. Its primary use is an ingredient in other dishes, including pizza and a baked potato with cheese.

Cheese can be bought from Port Sarim, in the Grand Tree, or from the Culinaromancer's chest in Lumbridge. Members can make some by using a bucket of milk on a dairy churn at level 48 Cooking, giving 64 Cooking experience. A pot of cream can also be churned into cheese, giving 46 Cooking experience, as well as a pat of butter or not garlic butter, which both give 23.5 Cooking experience.

Cheese also spawns in Aggie's house in Draynor Village, and the cooking shop in the Bandit Camp (Wilderness). Cheese may also be found in teak larders inside of player-owned houses.

It is used in the Witch's House quest, the Ratcatchers quest, and optionally in the Mourning's End Part II quest.
1989:
Half full wine jugs are rewards given out during various holiday events. Drinking a half full wine jug will restore 7 Hitpoints, and like normal wine, will temporarily decrease Attack by 2.

A regular jug of wine cannot be drunk to make a half full wine jug, nor can two half full jugs be decanted to make a full jug. Interestingly, the half full wine jug heals more than half of a regular jug of wine.

It is not advised to drink half full wine jugs as they are more expensive than most other food items that heal just as much or more. They are more valuable as a collector's item.
2003: It's a meat and potato stew.
2007: This could liven up an otherwise bland stew.
2011:
Curry is a type of food that restores 19 Hitpoints when eaten. An empty bowl will remain after consumption. It can be obtained by cooking uncooked curry on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 60 Cooking and granting 280 experience when successful. When cooking, there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt curry. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 74.

At 50 Construction, a demon butler can be hired, who can serve curry in player-owned houses. The number of curries served is equal to the number of people in the house, up to 10.

Curry is popular for fighting the Chaos Elemental and Chaos Fanatic, as the left-over empty bowls prevent these enemies' special attacks from un-equipping worn equipment into what would otherwise be empty inventory slots.
2015: Vodka is a clear spirit that can be obtained from Heckel Funch in the Gnome Stronghold, The Asp & Snake Bar at Pollnivneach, Jossik in the Lighthouse, Atlazora's Rest in Outer Fortis, or The Flaming Arrow in Civitas illa Fortis. There is also a chance of receiving a bottle during the King's Ransom quest.
2019:
Gin is an alcoholic drink used in making gnome cocktails. It heals 5 hitpoints, increases a player's Strength by 5% + 1, and decreases Attack by 2% + 3 when drunk.

It can be found at Blurberry's bar in the Grand Tree and Jossik's shop in the Lighthouse.
2021: Brandy is an alcoholic drink which can be purchased at Jossik's store in the Lighthouse, at the Tree Gnome Stronghold in Heckel Funch's store or at the Asp & Snake Bar at Pollnivneach. It is an ingredient in the gnome cocktail Blurberry special. It heals 5 hitpoints, increases a player's Strength by 5% + 1 and decreases Attack by 2% - 3 when drunk. Unlike the other types of alcoholic drinks bought from stores, brandy has a cone-shaped bottle.
2023:
The cocktail guide has a collection of recipes for the various gnome cocktails for you to make. It's useful for the Gnome Restaurant minigame or if you just want to make the cocktails for yourself.

You can get the book from Blurberry, Heckel Funch, Rasolo, or from the bookcase in your house. The book will not be available in your bookcase until completing the mixing tutorial with Blurberry.
2025:
A cocktail shaker is an item used in Gnome cooking to make cocktails. It can be purchased from Grand Tree Groceries or Funch's Fine Groceries in the Grand Tree for 2 coins, or through dialogue with the Blurberry Bar barmen for 20 coins. One also spawns in Grand Tree Groceries.

Ingredients can not be used on the shaker directly; the "mix-cocktail" option opens an interface where players must click "create" to make the drink. Doing so will create an intermediate mixed drink, still in the shaker, which can then be poured into a cocktail glass while having the appropriate garnish in the inventory.
2026: Empty cocktail glasses are used to make Gnome cocktails. They can be bought from Heckel Funch in the Grand Tree. There is also a respawn right next to him. They can also be obtained by drinking gnome cocktails, a poison chalice, or the cocktails from the Pandemonium pub.
2040:
A premade wiz blz'd is a drink that can be bought at Blurberry Bar in the south-east corner of the 1st floor of the Grand Tree. Pre-made drinks cannot be used in the Gnome Restaurant minigame. Like the wizard blizzard, the premade wiz blz'd heals 5 hitpoints and boosts Strength by 6% + 1 levels, but reduces Attack by 2% - 3 levels.

Drinking it will leave behind a cocktail glass and give the messages:
2048:
Pineapple punch is a drink that can be made at level 8 Cooking, granting 70 experience points. It heals 9 hitpoints. To mix a pineapple punch, a player needs a lemon, 2 oranges, 3 pineapples, a lime, a cocktail shaker, a knife, and a cocktail glass.

To make it:

Use the "mix-cocktail" option on the shaker, and select pineapple punch.

Use the knife on the remaining pineapple and select "dice".

Use the knife on the lime and select "dice".

Use the knife on the orange and select "slice."

Use the cocktail shaker on the glass or select "pour mixed punch" on the cocktail shaker.

Drinking it will leave behind a cocktail glass and give the messages: You drink the cocktail. It tastes great.
2054:
Wizard blizzard is a drink that can be made at level 18 Cooking, granting 110 Cooking experience. When consumed, the wizard blizzard heals 5 hitpoints and boosts Strength by 6% + 1 levels, but reduces Attack by 2% - 3 levels.

The ingredients for wizard blizzard are: two bottles of vodka, one bottle of gin, one orange, one lime, and one lemon. To make the wizard blizzard, put all of the ingredients into a cocktail shaker, next pour the contents of the cocktail shaker into a cocktail glass. Finally, add pineapple chunks and lime slices.

Drinking it will leave behind a cocktail glass and give the messages:
2064:
The Blurberry special can be mixed with 1 vodka, 1 brandy, 1 gin, 1 orange, and 2 lemons. It can be finished by adding 1 equa leaf, 1 sliced lime, 1 diced lemon, and 1 diced orange as a garnish. This requires 37 Cooking to make.

All of these ingredients can be purchased at Funch's Fine Groceries and cost a total of 30 coins per Blurberry special made (not including cocktail shaker, cocktail glass, or knife). A Premade blurb' sp. (premade Blurberry special) can be purchased at the Blurberry Bar for 30 coins.

It heals 7 Hitpoints, increases Strength by 5% + 2 levels, and reduces Attack by 2% - 3 levels.

A Blurberry special (fresh or premade) may be given to Harold during the Death Plateau quest to make the gambling section of the quest far easier, as it will cause him to become so drunk he assumes you win every dice game you play with him.

Drinking it will leave behind a cocktail glass and give the messages:
2074:
A chocolate saturday is an gnomish alcoholic drink that can be made at level 33 Cooking, granting 170 Cooking experience. It is used in the Gnome Restaurant minigame. It heals 5 Hitpoints, lowers Attack by 2% - 3 levels and increases Strength by 5% + 2 levels.

The ingredients are whisky, equa leaves, a bucket of milk, some chocolate dust, a pot of cream and a chocolate bar. Access to a range is also required to complete the beverage. To mix it, players need a cocktail shaker, and a cocktail glass.

There is a premade choc s'dy spawn in Brimstail's cave.

Drinking it will leave behind a cocktail glass and give the messages:
2080:
Short green guys (commonly abbreviated to SGG) are drinks that can be made at level 20 Cooking, granting 120 Cooking experience. They heal 5 hitpoints, boost Strength by 5% + 1 levels, and reduce Attack by 2% - 3 levels. Short green guys are a good way to cheaply train without leaving the Gnome Stronghold, since they require only one type of fruit, have cheap ingredients, and only require one chopped/sliced item.

Creating a short green guy requires one vodka, three limes, one sliced lime, and one equa leaf.

Drinking it will leave behind a cocktail glass and give the messages:
2084:
A fruit blast is a type of drink that restores 9 Hitpoints when consumed. It can be obtained by mixing 1 pineapple, 1 orange, and 1 lemon. You must then finish the cocktail by adding lemon slices as a garnish, requiring level 6 Cooking to complete. To create the cocktail, click "Mix-cocktail" on a cocktail shaker. All ingredients and tools can be bought from Funch's Fine Groceries just east of the Blurberry Bar.

Ashes can be added to a fruit blast to create a dirty blast, which is a requirement for the first part of Recipe for Disaster. A premade fr' blast will NOT work for the quest; ashes can only be added with a regular fruit blast.

A fruit blast may also be obtained from the Ocean Man, or by using the Level 3 certificate from The Dig Site quest on Curator Haig Halen and choosing a drink.

Drinking it will leave behind a cocktail glass and give the messages: You drink the cocktail. It tastes great.
2102:
A lemon is a food item that heals 2 hitpoints when eaten. It is generally used as an ingredient in gnome cooking, in cocktails such as the fruit blast, pineapple punch, the wizard blizzard, and the blurberry special. Players can use a knife to cut the lemon into lemon chunks or lemon slices, which are also used in making cocktails.

Lemons cannot be produced through the Farming skill. However, they can be used to make regular compost.

Players can buy lemons from Heckel Funch (20 in stock) and Hudo (10 in stock, closer to bank) in the Grand Tree for 2 coins a piece. They can also (with 25 Thieving) be thieved from the fruit stalls in Hosidius and the Kourend Castle courtyard.
2104:
Lemon chunks are used in gnome cooking. One can obtain them by using a knife on a lemon and choosing the option to dice the lemon.

Lemon chunks are used as an ingredient in a Blurberry special. It is used in the second step of preparing the drink, and must be in the inventory along with orange chunks, equa leaves and a sliced lime to be able to pour a mixed special into a cocktail glass.
2106:
Lemon slices are used in gnome cooking. Players can obtain them by using a knife on a lemon.

Lemon slices are used as an ingredient in a fruit blast. It is used in the second step of preparing the drink, and must be in the inventory to be able to pour a mixed blast into a cocktail glass.
2108: An orange is a fruit that can be grown as part of the Farming skill. Oranges are used in several gnome cooking recipes, and can be used with a knife to create orange slices or orange chunks. You can give a basket of oranges to a farmer as payment to protect a maple tree (farming). It heals 2 hitpoints regardless of the state the orange is in (whole, sliced or chunks). Oranges can be added to a compost bin to make regular compost. 3 spawns are present on an inaccessible island populated by pygmy hippos east of Kastori, the northernmost spawn can be Telegrabbed from the western coast of the Avium Savannah.
2110:
Orange chunks are used in gnome cooking. You can obtain them by using a knife on an orange and selecting the "Dice" option.

Orange chunks are used when making a fruit batta. They are added to a half baked batta along with 4 equa leaves, 1 lime chunks and 1 pineapple chunks to create an unfinished batta (fruit).

Orange chunks are also used when making a blurberry special. They are used in the final step of making the drink, and must be in the inventory along with 1 lemon chunks, 1 equa leaves, and 1 sliced lime to pour a mixed special into a cocktail glass.
2112:
Orange slices are a food item that players can obtain by using a knife on an orange. Eating orange slices will heal 2 hitpoints. Orange slices are needed in the Goblin part of Recipe for Disaster.

Orange slices are used in gnome cooking as an ingredient in a pineapple punch cocktail. They are used in the final step of creating the drink, and must be in the inventory along with 1 lime chunks and 1 pineapple chunks to pour a mixed punch into a cocktail glass.

Oranges can be obtained from Farming in a tree patch, or from shops and NPCs at the Grand Tree.
2114:
A pineapple is a fruit that can be found growing just south of Brimhaven or on a player grown Pineapple plant. Additionally, they may be purchased from Trader Crewmembers operating Trader Stan's Trading Post, Funch's Shop from Heckel Funch, or from Hudo in the Grand Tree Groceries store.

Pineapples provide an easy way to make supercompost by putting it into a compost bin, as they are relatively cheap and easy to obtain. It can be sliced or diced with a knife. Slicing the pineapple will yield 4 pineapple rings, each healing 2 Hitpoints. Dicing the pineapple yields one pineapple chunks, an ingredient used in gnome cooking, which also heals 2 Hitpoints when consumed. When slicing the pineapple into pineapple rings if you don't have enough space in your inventory, the rings will drop to the ground instead.

10 pineapples are also used as a payment for papaya trees.

Even though there is an eat option, you cannot eat a pineapple, attempting to do so will result in this message You can't eat it whole; maybe you should cut it up. as you can eat it after cutting it with a knife.

For Ironman accounts, pineapples are the most accessible ingredient for making supercompost, as they are sold at Trader Stan's Trading Post.
2116:
Pineapple chunks are a food item that heals 2 hitpoints when consumed. Players can make pineapple chunks by using a knife on a pineapple or a tenti pineapple by choosing "Dice".

The main use for pineapple chunks is as an ingredient in other foods; for example, members can use them to make a pineapple pizza with level 65 Cooking.

Pineapple chunks are mostly used in Gnome cooking, where they are an ingredient in a fruit batta. They are also used in making drinks such as pineapple punch, wizard blizzard, and drunk dragon.
2118:
Pineapple rings are a members-only Cooking ingredient that are used on plain pizzas to create pineapple pizzas.

Pineapple rings are obtained by using a knife on a pineapple or a tenti pineapple and choosing the "slice" option. 4 pineapple rings are obtained for each pineapple that is sliced. If the "dice" option is chosen, the player will receive Pineapple chunks instead.

If eaten, it heals 2 hit points.
2120:
A lime is a members-only green fruit used in Gnome Cuisine, most often used in Gnome cooking. It can be diced with a knife into lime chunks, or sliced with a knife into lime slices. These both heal 2 Hitpoints each.

Unlike most other fruits, it cannot be grown using the Farming skill. Instead, they must be bought from Hudo's groceries and Heckel Funch in the Grand Tree. It is also available from the market seller in Pollnivneach, gotten as drop from gnomes throughout Tree Gnome Stronghold or it can be stolen at the fruit stall in Hosidius or in the Kourend Castle courtyard.

Limes are compostable – they will make regular compost.

A lime may also be one of the three items required during the quest Fairytale I - Growing Pains in order to obtain the magic secateurs.
2128:
Equa leaves are ingredients utilised in gnome cooking that heal 1 hitpoint each. They are used in almost all gnome food, and have little other use, besides possibly in the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest.

They can be purchased at the two food stores on the 1st floor of the Grand Tree in the Tree Gnome Stronghold. Several respawn points are located in the south-east of Feldip Hills.
2130:
A pot of cream can be made by using a bucket of milk on a dairy churn at 21 Cooking. It provides 18 Cooking experience. They can also be purchased from the Culinaromancer's Chest in the Lumbridge Castle cellar, after you're at a certain point in the Recipe for Disaster quest as well as from Hudo or Heckel Funch at the Tree Gnome Stronghold.

Pots of cream can be further churned into a pat of butter. When eaten, the pot of cream heals 1 hitpoint.

It is used in recipes for the following items:

Drunk dragon

Choc saturday

Chocolate bomb
2132: I need to cook this first.
2134: I need to cook this first.
2136: I need to cook this first.
2138:
A Raw chicken is an uncooked food item dropped by chickens or roosters. They are also sold at Rufus' Meat Emporium in Canifis and Wydin's Food Store in Port Sarim.

There is also a crate in Wydin's shop in Port Sarim that provides unlimited raw chicken. A white apron is required to enter the room which contains the crate.

Raw chicken can be cooked into cooked chicken by using it on a fire, a range, or an ogre spit-roast. Doing so requires only level 1 Cooking for the fire and the range, and grants 30 experience points. The ogre spit-roast requires level 30 Cooking. At level 34 Cooking, raw chicken can no longer be accidentally burnt.

Raw chicken is used with together with a raw swordfish to make a swordchick in Creature Creation after completion of Tower of Life.
2142:
Cooked meat is a type of food that restores 3 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking various raw meats on a fire or cooking range, granting 30 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt meat. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Cooked meat is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 34, or 31 when using the Lumbridge range.

Cooked meat is used in the making of stews, pies, and steak sandwiches, or as a topping on pizzas.

Unlike most food, players can deliberately burn cooked meat by using it on a fire or cooking range. One burnt meat is required for Witch's Potion.
2150:
A swamp toad is a small creature with removable legs. Doing so yields toad's legs in place of the swamp toad. Toad's legs heal for 3 Hitpoints, are used as the second ingredient for agility potions (toadflax potion unf), and the gnome cooking foods: Tangled toad's legs, toad batta, and toad crunchies.

Collecting a swamp toad at the Gnome Stronghold is a requirement for the easy Western Provinces Diary.

The text "You pull the legs off the toad. Poor toad. At least they'll grow back." appears in the chat box after pulling the legs off.

These swamp toads cannot be used to fill ogre bellows; only swamp toads found around Feldip Hills will fill them. Attempting to do so results in the chatbox message stating "The chompy bird doesn't like this species of toad."
2164:
A batta tin is used for making battas in the Gnome Restaurant minigame. It can be obtained in the Grand Tree by buying from the Gnome Restaurant food shop owned by Hudo, by searching the nearby cupboard to find one, or by looting it from the gnomes in the stronghold.

If one gianne dough is added into the tin a raw batta is created, and if this is cooked over the gnome cooker or any other range, half baked batta will be made. From here, any of the battas in the gnome cuisine can be made. Examples of battas include worm batta, toad batta, cheese and tomato batta, fruit batta, and vegetable batta.

Please see gnome cooking for more information on gnome cuisine.
2165: A shallow tray used for baking crunchies in.
2166:
A gnomebowl mould is an item used in gnome cooking. It can be bought in the Grand Tree by talking to Hudo in the north-west corner on the 1st floor, or it can be acquired for free by searching the tree gnome kitchen cabinet at the northernmost part of the Grand Tree for a "gnome bowl".

Adding gianne dough to the mould will create a raw gnomebowl, the basis for gnomebowl cooking.
2167:
Gianne's cook book is a cook book written by Aluft Gianne. It is full of Gnome recipes, and useful for the Gnome Restaurant minigame, or if players want to make gnome foods for themselves.

The cook book can be obtained from Aluft Gianne himself, Hudo the nearby grocer, or from the bookcase in a player-owned house. The book will not be available in your bookcase until completing the cooking tutorial with Aluft Gianne snr.. It mentions Pukkamay, a great Gnome cook.

Note that this book does not contain Gnome cocktail recipes, as these recipes are written in the The Blurberry Cocktail Guide.
2169:
Gnome Spice is an ingredient used to make spicy sauce and certain gnome foods. It can be bought from Grand Tree Groceries, run by Hudo in the Grand Tree. It will never run out while making Gnome foods.

To create spicy sauce, gnome spice is used with chopped garlic. This uses up the gnome spice.

When placing it into nest atop the Aldarin mill and then logging out of the game, it will transform into an iron pickaxe.
2171: Gianne dough is an ingredient in gnome cooking used to make gnomebowls, gnome crunchies, and gnome battas. It can be bought from Hudo in the Grand Tree. Gianne dough cannot be cooked by itself; instead, players must use the dough on a crunchy tray, batta tin, or gnomebowl mould and then precook it on a range. It was probably named after Aluft Gianne snr., the gnome cook. 100 Gianne dough is also given as a reward for completing the Gnome Restaurant training.
2187:
A tangled toad's legs is a food that players consume in one bite, healing 15 hitpoints. Players may need to make one as part of Training part I for the Gnome Restaurant minigame. Premade tangled toad's legs are sold by gnome waiters in the north-west corner of the 1st floor of the Grand Tree for 160 coins, with 3 in stock.

Members can make a tangled toad's legs via gnome cooking with 40 Cooking, yielding 185 experience. Like all gnome foods, they stop burning at Cooking level 38.

This food is an order in the Gnome Restaurant minigame and may also be obtained by completing an order through a Gnome restaurant Reward token. Like all gnome cooking, premade versions cannot be used in the minigame.

Gianne dough, gnomebowl moulds, cheese, equa leaves, dwellberries, and gnome spice can be bought from Hudo who is located in the north-west corner the 1st floor of the Grand Tree. While toad's legs are not sold, swamp toads may be found in the swamp north-west of the Grand Tree, in the Tree Gnome Stronghold.

During the The Path of Glouphrie quest, Gianne jnr. asks the player to deliver a long-standing Aluft Aloft Gnome Food Delivery Service order of tangled toad's legs to the gnome Longramble. While this is not required to progress the quest, if the player completes the delivery, Longramble will give the player a mint cake as payment.
2195:
A vegetable ball is a food that players consume in one bite, healing 12 hitpoints. Players may need to make one as part of Training part I for the Gnome Restaurant minigame. Premade veg balls are sold by gnome waiters in the north-west corner of the 1st floor of the Grand Tree for 150 coins, with 3 in stock.

Members can make a vegetable ball via gnome cooking with 35 Cooking, yielding 175 experience. Like all gnome foods, they stop burning at Cooking level 38.

This food is an order in the Gnome Restaurant minigame and may also be obtained by completing an order through a Gnome restaurant Reward token. Like all gnome cooking, premade versions cannot be used in the minigame.

Gianne dough, gnomebowl moulds, onions, potatoes, and Gnome spice can be bought from Hudo who is located in the north-west corner the 1st floor of the Grand Tree.
2203: Rock-climbing boots are an unobtainable item released along with the Grand Exchange as a joke. It is impossible to actually buy it, because the item only appears when searching the Grand Exchange, and is not an item that can actually be obtained.
2209:
Chocchip crunchies are a food that players consume in one bite, healing 7 hitpoints. Players may need to make one as part of Training part I for the Gnome Restaurant minigame. 2293:
Meat pizza is a type of pizza that restores 16 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 8. It can be obtained by using cooked meat or cooked chicken on a plain pizza, requiring 45 Cooking and granting 26 experience.

When the first bite is eaten, the message You eat half of the meat pizza.is displayed. The second bite gives the message You eat the remaining meat pizza..
2297:
Anchovy pizza is a type of pizza that restores 18 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 9. It can be obtained by using anchovies on a plain pizza, requiring 55 Cooking and granting 39 experience.

Anchovy pizzas are the highest healing food per slot in free-to-play and are also a type of fast food.

Pizza halves can be attached together to remake a full pizza.
2301:
Pineapple pizza is a type of pizza that restores 22 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 11. It can be obtained by using pineapple chunks or pineapple rings on a cooked plain pizza, requiring 65 Cooking and granting 45 experience. It is recommended to cut the pineapple into rings, as this yields four rings for use on multiple pizzas, compared to the single chunk if dicing it. Pineapple pizza is one of the highest healing foods in the game and are also a type of fast food.

100 noted pineapple pizzas can be given to Yama to initiate a fight that is identical to the aether catalyst, oathplate shard, and diabolic worm acquisition contract fights, as a way to practice these fights in exchange for standard loot rolls.

A Cook in a player-owned house can make a pineapple pizza for the player.
2307: Bread dough is made by mixing either a bucket of water, bowl of water, or jug of water with a pot of flour. It can be used on a range to make a loaf of bread at level 1 Cooking, granting 40 experience and healing 5 hitpoints when consumed. It is one of the most basic items used for the Cooking skill. Players will also get a pot of flour and a bucket of water to make bread dough on Tutorial Island, as a tutorial for cooking.
2309: Bread is a type of food that restores 5 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by baking bread dough on a cooking range, granting 40 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt bread. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Bread is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 38, or 34 when using the Lumbridge range. Bread may also be bought or stolen from the Ardougne Baker's Stall in the Ardougne marketplace.
2313:
A pie dish is used in Cooking to bake pies. Players must add a pastry dough (a pot of flour and either a jug of water, a bucket of water, or a bowl of water combined) to the pie dish to form a pie shell. It then can be filled by the filling of choice. Afterwards, the pie can then be baked in an oven. Players can create this in a pottery oven.

Despite unfired pie dishes requiring 7 Crafting to make, turning an unfired pie dish into a pie dish has no Crafting requirement and can be done at level 1.
2315:
A pie shell is used to make various kinds of pie. It is made by using a pastry dough on a pie dish. Players can fill a pie shell with any of several fillings to make a raw pie which must be cooked on a range.

Possible fillings include: redberries for redberry pie, cooked meat or cooked chicken for meat pie, or cooking apple for an apple pie and many more. Members have access to a wider variety of fillings from mud pies to summer pies.
2317:
An uncooked apple pie is an uncooked food item made by using a cooking apple on a pie shell that has already had pastry dough added to it. Players need at least level 30 Cooking to make it. If successfully cooked, an apple pie provides 130 Cooking experience.

The uncooked pie can be cooked on a range (but not a fire) to make an apple pie. However, there is a risk that the pie will burn and become a burnt pie. Like other pies, apple pies can also be cooked with the Lunar spell Bake Pie without the chance of burning.

A convenient place to make uncooked apple pies and cook them is the Cooks' Guild, which requires level 32 Cooking and a Chef's hat to enter. All of the ingredients needed to make apple pie are found around the guild, as it has 3 cooking apple spawns, a pie dish respawn, a jug respawn, a sink, a mill, wheat, and cooking ranges.
2319: An uncooked meat pie is made by adding cooked meat or cooked chicken to a pie shell. It can be cooked to make meat pie, or if unsuccessful, a Burnt pie.
2321: An Uncooked berry pie is made by adding Redberries to a Pie shell. Its cooked variant is a redberry pie.
2323:
Apple pie is a type of pie that restores 14 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 7. A pie dish will remain after both bites are consumed.

It can be created by baking an uncooked apple pie on a cooking range, requiring level 30 Cooking and granting 130 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 63. Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.

Apple pie is a possible task from Romily Weaklax in the Cooks' Guild. Three apple pies and three meat pies are given to the player when starting Nature Spirit.

2341: Oomlie meat in a palm leaf pouch. It just needs to be cooked.
2343:
Cooked oomlie wrap is a food made from cooking a wrapped oomlie. It heals 14 Hitpoints when eaten, and gives the message "You eat the oomlie meat; it tastes very gamy."

Cooked oomlie wraps can be cooked with a Cooking level of 50 or higher, granting 30 Cooking experience.

Cooking a raw oomlie on a fire will always burn it. Attempting to do so gives the message "The meat is far too delicate to cook like this. Perhaps you should wrap something around it to protect it from the heat."

To protect the raw oomlie, it must be wrapped with a palm leaf, which is obtained by shaking a leafy palm tree. This creates a wrapped oomlie. There are three of these trees located near the water pool in the centre of the Kharazi Jungle. Additionally, eating an oomlie wrap is a hard task in the Karamja Diary.
2347:
A hammer is a tool used for smithing items on an Anvil, and it is vital to level the Smithing skill. Hammers can be bought from most general stores and will never break. Alternatively, players can obtain a hammer by talking to the Master smithing tutor at the West Varrock anvil. A hammer is also used in the Construction skill when making furniture, and it is required for some minigames. At 15 Construction, members can make a Tool store 1 for the workshop room of their house; this tool store provides an unlimited supply of hammers.

A hammer is required to access Bandos' stronghold in the God Wars Dungeon; warhammers are an acceptable substitute.

The Imcando hammer can be used instead of a hammer when performing tasks like Construction or Smithing.
2351:
An iron bar is a bar of refined iron. It can be created through the Smithing skill at level 15 by using iron ore on a furnace, granting 12.5 Smithing experience. When smelting iron ore, there is a 50% chance that it will be too impure; it disappears, yielding no Smithing experience nor an iron bar. However, wearing a ring of forging, casting Superheat Item, or using the Blast Furnace would give a 100% success rate.

An iron bar can be smithed on an anvil through the Smithing skill to create iron weapons and armour. When smithed, each bar grants 25 experience, with a maximum of 125 being given for the iron platebody.
2355:
A silver bar is a bar of metal, refined through the Smithing skill by smelting a silver ore in a furnace, requiring 20 Smithing and granting 13.7 Smithing experience. It may also be bought (or stolen) from a silver merchant, such as the one in Ardougne market, or from other players.

The primary use of a silver bar is to create jewellery with the Crafting skill. To craft silver bars into jewellery players must use a silver bar on a furnace with a proper mould in their inventory. If players wish to craft jewellery with gems inset, the cut gems must be present in the player's inventory before crafting the jewellery. One silver bar is used during the Creature of Fenkenstrain quest, and another during Shadow of the Storm.

Unlike gold bars, which cannot be made into weapons, silver bars can be made into silver sickles. They can also be ground to silver dust in the Ectofuntus grinder for use as an ingredient in the guthix balance potion.

Currently, smelting a silver bar yields a profit of 41.

One effective method of gathering silver bars is exchanging reward tokens gained for completing Temple Trekking minigame. This method is commonly used by ironman players, as it can net upwards of 1000 silver bars per hour.
2366:
The shield left half is an item that can be joined with the right half to create the dragon square shield with level 60 Smithing. Joining the right half with the left half nets 75 Smithing experience. The other half of the shield is sold by Siegfried Erkle in the Legends Guild Shop of Useful Items for 750,000 coins.

This item is a rare drop from the rare drop table. Wearing a ring of wealth will increase the chances of receiving one from the rare drop table. Goraks fought in the Gorak Plane are likely droppers of the shield left half, with a drop rate of 1/243.75 (with a ring of wealth equipped) if Fairytale II - Cure a Queen and Legends' Quest have been completed.

Skotizo is the monster most likely to drop the shield left half, with a drop rate of 1/100, and is the only monster to have it on its standard drop table.

The intricate pouch from Guardians of the Rift has a chance to contain the shield left half, as well as other dragon items.

Creating a dragon square shield from the two halves in West Ardougne is a hard task in the Ardougne Diary.
2368:
The shield right half is an item which can be bought in the Legends' Guild or the Myths' Guild for 750,000 coins. It can be combined with the shield left half (provided that you have 60 Smithing) to form the dragon square shield. A hammer and anvil is needed to combine the shield.

Creating a Dragon square shield from the two halves in West Ardougne is a hard task in the Ardougne Diary.
2370: Steel studs can be smithed from a steel bar at an anvil with level 36 Smithing, granting 37.5 experience. They can then be used on leather bodies with level 41 Crafting or leather chaps with level 44 Crafting, to make studded bodies and studded chaps respectively.
2466:
Yellow flowers are a type of flower that can be harvested after planting mithril or adamant seeds.

When planting the seeds, players have an option to either pick the flowers (and obtaining a random coloured flower) or leave them planted on the ground. A player only has one chance to pick their flowers; if they refuse to do so, they will not get the option again unless they plant another seed. Flowers that are left on the ground will stay there temporarily for around 5 minutes.

Flowers can be wielded in the weapon slot, and are classified as a fun weapon in legacy duels within the Emir's Arena because it gives the wielding player negative bonuses.

2550: A ring of recoil is created by using Lvl-1 Enchant on a sapphire ring. When worn, a small percentage of damage received is dealt to the attacker; it has limited uses before it shatters. They can be used to charge a ring of suffering for the same recoil effect.
2568:
A ring of forging gives smelting iron ore a 100% success rate of creating an iron bar while it is worn. It can be made by casting Lvl-3 Enchant on a ruby ring, or by paying 250 coins with a ruby ring to Murky Matt in the south-east quadrant of the Grand Exchange.

A newly-enchanted ring has 140 charges. Each time the player smelts an iron ore while wearing the ring, one charge is consumed; after all charges are consumed, the ring crumbles to dust. If the player auto-smelts more iron ores than the number of remaining charges, the smelting will stop once the ring crumbles. The number of charges is specific to the player, not the ring, so swapping, dropping, or alching rings before 140 charges are used will not reset the number of smelts the player has left before a ring breaks. Players can right-click a ring of forging to either "check" how many charges remain in it or "break" it and reset the next one they use to its maximum charges.

When smelting multiples of an ore at the Edgeville furnace while wearing Varrock armour, there is a chance to smelt 2 bars at once. If this activates while smelting iron with a ring of forging, 2 charges from the ring will be used.
2570:
The ring of life is a diamond ring that has been enchanted with Lvl-4 Enchant. While worn, if the wearer is attacked and has 10% or less of their Hitpoints remaining, the ring automatically teleports the wearer to their respawn point. The ring crumbles to dust after one use. A Defence cape can be worn for the same effect, which does not destroy itself on activation. An Escape crystal can be configured to provide the same effect and more.

The ring does not guarantee total safety, as a player wearing one will still die if they are hit from above 10% of their maximum Hitpoints to zero (for example, being hit 15 while at 15 hitpoints), and it will not cure poison. Self-inflicted damage, such as guzzling a dwarven rock cake or using a locator orb, can also activate the effect. If it is worn along with a phoenix necklace, the necklace effect will trigger first. In PvP, the Tele Block spell will prevent a player's ring of life from activating.

It is one the few items whose teleports will work up to level 30 Wilderness, while most other means of teleportation will not work above level 20 Wilderness.

In Wintertodt, the ring will activate if warmth drops below 10%.

Upon the completion of medium Ardougne Diary, the teleport destination can be toggled to East Ardougne.

A ring of life is a reward from the The Lost Tribe quest.

When the ring of life effect procs, a player wearing the ring of life will be teleported and the following chat message will appear: Your Ring of Life saves you and is destroyed in the process.
