Moonlight mead is a type of ale that restores 4 Hitpoints. It can be obtained through brewing at level 44 Cooking, granting 380 experience. It is brewed using 2 buckets of water, 2 barley malt, 4 mushrooms, and a pot of ale yeast. The stronger, mature version of the ale is the moonlight mead(m).

It can be bought for 5 coins from Roavar in the Hair of the Dog tavern, located in Canifis.

Upon drinking, the chatbox will state "You drink the foul smelling brew. It tastes like something just died in your mouth."
2961: A silver sickle can be made at 18 Crafting with a silver bar and a sickle mould at a furnace, granting 50 Crafting experience. It can be turned into a Silver sickle (b) during Nature Spirit quest, and can also be blessed after the quest by dipping it in the pool of water in the nature spirit's grotto. A blessed sickle can be used to cast Bloom; when cast, this spell drains your prayer slightly, and if you are in the Mort Myre Swamp, it may grow fungi, saplings and golden pears on rotting logs, branches, and small bushes respectively, which can be used to fill a druid pouch.
2970:
Mort myre fungi can be obtained in Mort Myre Swamp. It can be used to add 1 charge to a Druid pouch or to make super energy potions. They are also required to bait and catch wild broavs.

It is obtained by casting Bloom with a Druidic spell or blessed silver sickle (both obtained during the Nature Spirit quest) near rotting logs. All variants and flail upgrades of the blessed silver sickle can also cast Bloom. Alternatively, they can be obtained as a drop from certain monsters or by chopping sulliuscep mushrooms.

Collecting Mort myre fungi to sell is an effective way of making money, as they are valued by players due to their use in the Herblore skill.

It is a possible item requirement in Fairytale I - Growing Pains.
2972:
Mort myre stems can be obtained by operating a silver sickle (b) near rotting branches on the ground in Mort Myre Swamp. Each stem can be used to add 2 charges to a druid pouch for use as protection from ghasts.

It is a possible item requirement in Fairytale I - Growing Pains.
2974:
A mort myre pear is obtained during or after the Nature Spirit quest. It appears when the Bloom spell is cast, using a silver sickle(b) near certain small bushes in the Mort Myre Swamp. Each pear can be used to add 3 charges to a druid pouch for use as protection from ghasts. However, they are not common, and it is generally easier to find Mort myre fungi or Mort myre stems.

It is a possible item requirement in Fairytale I - Growing Pains.

Snapdragons are used to make super restore potions and sanfew serums with a Herblore level of 63 and a Herblore level of 65 respectively. To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create a snapdragon potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient.

According to the book Gielinor's flora - herbs, snapdragon is native to the rocky areas of Tirannwn, and is supposedly named due to its resemblance of the face of a dragon.

The mystic lava staff is an elemental staff requiring 40 Attack and 40 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of earth and fire runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

This type of elemental staff is the best (once you've reached or surpassed level 87 Magic) for getting enchantment points when training Magic at the Mage Training Arena. It is also useful for Enfeeble-alching.

This staff can be created after the completion of the quest Scorpion Catcher by taking a lava battlestaff and 40,000 to Thormac. After completion of the Hard Kandarin Diary and Elite Kandarin Diary, Thormac will only require 30,000 or 20,000 respectively.

It can also be obtained as a potential drop from Abyssal Sires, a potential reward from Barbarian Assault, traded by other players, and bought on the Grand Exchange.

Players can use a lava staff upgrade kit obtained from Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing to cosmetically enhance their mystic lava staff, creating a mystic lava staff (or). This only alters its appearance, and becomes untradeable. It can be reverted, but the kit will not be retained.

Shaikahan bones are dropped by The Shaikahan when it is killed, which requires a Karambwan paste-poisoned spear or hasta. Note that any kills prior to Tai Bwo Wannai Trio will not yield any bones. Shaikahan bones give 25 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

75 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

75 XP when offered at the Sacred Bone Burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

87.5 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit or at the Chaos Temple.

100 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of Shaikahan bonemeal.
3125: Fairly big bones which smell distinctly of Jogre.
3138: Potato cactus is an item that is used with the Herblore skill as a secondary ingredient when creating magic potions and battlemage potions. Potato cactus can also be selected as one of the 3 of 31 items needed for Fairytale I - Growing Pains as well as 1 of 50 items for Mourning's End Part II. They can be grown in a cactus patch by planting potato cactus seeds, requiring level 64 Farming. Eight are also used to pay Taylor to look after a player's Celastrus tree. Collecting 5 of them while inside the Kalphite Lair is a requirement for the Easy Desert Diary.

3142:
Raw karambwan are octopodes native to the tropical island of Karamja. Catching one requires 65 Fishing and a karambwan vessel using raw karambwanji as bait after completing the fishing portion of the Tai Bwo Wannai Trio quest. Each catch yields 50 Fishing experience. The karambwan fishing spots are north of the Karamja Shipyard and east of the harpie bug swarms at fairy ring code DKP, or alternatively fished at sea while on a raft.

To be able to cook a karambwan thoroughly, players must speak to Tinsay in his hut after completing the Tai Bwo Wannai Trio quest. When using a raw karambwan on a fire or cooking range, two options of cooking are given: poorly or thoroughly. Cooking poorly requires 1 Cooking, but yields a poison karambwan and 80 Cooking experience. Cooking poison karambwans is typically the fastest way to level Cooking from level 1, as Karambwans can be cooked faster than other food. Cooking thoroughly requires 30 Cooking yielding a cooked karambwan and 190 Cooking experience. Karambwan stop burning at 99 Cooking, 93 Cooking at the Hosidius Kitchen, or 86 Cooking at the Hosidius Kitchen after completing the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary.

Catching a karambwan is a medium Karamja Diary task, while cooking a karambwan thoroughly is a hard Karamja Diary task.
3144:
Cooked karambwan is a type of fish that restores 18 Hitpoints when eaten. They can be obtained by cooking raw karambwan on a fire or cooking range. Cooking a karambwan requires level 30 Cooking, and grants 190 experience when successful.

In order to produce a cooked karambwan, the player must first complete Tai Bwo Wannai Trio and afterwards talk to Tinsay in the southernmost hut in Tai Bwo Wannai. If the player has not done this, cooking a raw karambwan will instead produce a poison karambwan. Players may burn a karambwan while cooking one, resulting in a burnt karambwan; the burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 99 on both ranges and fires. It is possible to use tick manipulation to cook each raw karambwan in one tick rather than the standard four to increase Cooking experience rates.

When eaten, the message You eat the Karambwan. is displayed.

Karambwans are commonly used as a fast food, a subtype of food that incurs non-standard attack or eating delays when consumed. Karambwans may be consumed after other foods without delay; this does not work if the karambwan is eaten first, and does not work when eating two karambwan in a row. This technique (commonly referred to as combo eating) can be further enhanced by drinking a dose of Saradomin brew after your alternative food item, and before your karambwan (food>brew>karambwan).

Additionally, karambwans add a delay of two ticks before the player can attack again, while most other foods have a delay of three ticks.

Karambwans may also be used in tick manipulation to improve rates. This is only recommended for non-ironman players. For example, you can start your usual 3-tick timer using your herb and tar, then on the next cycle, you eat a cooked karambwan instead. This effectively allows you to 2.5-tick certain actions, such as barbarian fishing.
3157:
Karambwan vessels are fishing instruments used for catching karambwan in the northern coastal waters of Karamja. The player receives one during the Tai Bwo Wannai Trio quest, and they can later be purchased from Tiadeche's Karambwan Stall in Tai Bwo Wannai Village for 2 coins. It requires level 5 Fishing to use, although karambwan cannot be caught until 65.

To fish using a karambwan vessel, players must first learn from Lubufu, an aged fisherman that lives near Brimhaven. After finishing the quest, the spot beside him becomes inaccessible and the vessel can be used only in eastern Karamja, near a fairy ring (combination DKP).

Raw karambwanji are used as bait and are occasionally consumed without a karambwan being caught.

It cannot be used with the ash sanctifier.

A thin snail is a piece of raw meat dropped by snails in Mort Myre Swamp. It may be cooked on either a range or a fire, requiring level 12 Cooking. This yields 70 experience and thin snail meat, which heals 5 to 7 hitpoints in one bite.

When used on a pestle and mortar it can be used to create blamish snail slime provided you have a sample bottle in your inventory to collect it. The slime can be used to create blamish oil which is used for an oily fishing rod.

It may also be used in Fairytale I - Growing Pains as a quest item for magic secateurs.

It can be ground with a pestle and mortar to produce blamish snail slime used in the blamish oil for the Heroes' Quest. This requires you to have a sample bottle in your inventory to collect it.

Alternatively, it can be made without the Crafting requirement by giving two bark, two fine cloth, and 6,000 coins to Wizard Jalarast at the Wizards' Tower. They can also be obtained by looting ninja implings found in Puro-Puro or around Gielinor.

Alternatively, it can be made without the Crafting requirement by giving four bark, four fine cloth, and 37,000 coins to Wizard Jalarast at the Wizards' Tower. An alternative to this is the Lunar torso which has slightly lower defence stats.

Alternatively, they can be made without the Crafting requirement by giving a bark, a fine cloth, and 1,000 coins to Wizard Jalarast at the Wizards' Tower. They have similar bonuses as Iron boots, except for the better magic bonuses.

Fiyr remains are an item found and used in the Shades of Mort'ton minigame. To obtain these remains, the player must kill fiyr shades, located behind a solid silver door in the Shade Catacombs. Shades encountered during Temple Trekking may also drop fiyr remains.

To burn the fiyr remains, first place magic, ironwood, redwood or rosewood pyre logs on a funeral pyre, followed by the fiyr remains, then light the pyre with a tinderbox. This will grant the player Firemaking and Prayer experience (see table). Once burned, a silver or gold shade key, or some coins, will appear next to the pyre.

Gold keys give unrestricted access to all areas of the Shade Catacombs and can open gold rewards chests, while silver keys give access to all areas up to the fiyr area in the north-west corner of the catacombs and can open silver rewards chests.

Coins and keys dropped by cremating these remains will not despawn for five minutes, and cannot be taken by other players during this time. When dropped by the player, they will despawn and become visible to others at the normal rate.

The Flamtaer hammer is an item used during the Shades of Mort'ton minigame. It is a replacement for the regular hammer when building the temple, and is approximately 75% faster. It acts as an invisible +40 Crafting boost while rebuilding the temple in the Shades of Mort'ton minigame. The Flamtaer hammer can be bought from Razmire Keelgan at the Mort'ton general store or from Rasolo the Wandering Merchant near Baxtorian Falls.

It can also be obtained from the keys made from shade remains when looting various chests in the Shade Catacombs.
3749:
The archer helm can be purchased from the Skulgrimen's Battle Gear for 78,000 coins after completing The Fremennik Trials quest. Players must have a Defence level of at least 45 and have completed The Fremennik Trials quest in order to wear it. It is also a possible reward from the High Gamble in Barbarian Assault.

The archer helm is commonly worn by players in the Wilderness, as its low cost makes it easy to replace for both standard and ironman accounts if lost to a player killer.
3751:
The berserker helm is a mid-levelled melee-based helmet. Players must have level 45 Defence and also have completed the quest The Fremennik Trials in order to wear it. It can be purchased from Skulgrimen's Battle Gear shop in Rellekka for 78,000 coins. It's also a possible reward from Barbarian Assault High Gambles or a drop from a dagannoth.

This helmet is favoured among combat pures for being the second lowest level headgear to offer a Strength bonus, which offers the same strength bonus as a helm of Neitiznot and an obsidian helmet.

The berserker helm's defensive bonuses are roughly on par with the rune full helm. More specifically, the berserker helm is slightly better than the rune full helm in both stab and crush defence, but is slightly worse in slash defence.

Skulgrimen's Battle Gear will buy this helmet from a player for 42,000 coins, which is more than the High Level Alchemy price of 36,000 coins.

3755: The farseer helm is a piece of Fremennik armour. To wear a farseer helm, players must have completed The Fremennik Trials quest and have a Defence level of at least 45. To obtain this helmet you can buy one from Skulgrimen in Rellekka for 78,000 coins, trade with another player or receive one as a drop from Dagannoth. It can also be obtained through gambling points in the Barbarian Assault minigame and as loot from sorting Fremennik salvage.

A keg of beer is a large barrel of ale that restores 15 Hitpoints and temporarily boosts Strength by 10% +2, while draining Attack by 50% + 5 (see table below).

It can be bought in the Rellekka Longhall for 325 coins, provided that the player has completed The Fremennik Trials quest. It can also be bought from the merchant Rasolo for 500 coins, who is north of Ardougne near Baxtorian Falls. A special keg of beer can be found on the table in the longhall, which is swapped out with a low alcohol keg during The Fremennik Trials in order to win the drinking contest.

Upon drinking it, the chatbox states, "You chug the keg. You feel reinvigorated... ...but extremely drunk, too." while the player character raises the keg above their head and chugs the entire barrel. This also causes the perspective of the player's screen to swing back and forth for a minute, as if their character is drunk. This can be stopped by teleporting.

Kegs of beer can also be sold to Askeladden on Waterbirth Island. He will buy them for 500 before The Fremennik Trials and 700 after. He will not buy noted kegs of beer, however.
3803:
A beer tankard is a type of ale that restores 4 Hitpoints and temporarily boosts Strength by 4% + 2 while draining Attack by 10% +2.

Players can buy a tankard of beer from Thora the Barkeep in the Rellekka Longhall Bar. The spawn within the bar cannot be taken unless you have started The Fremennik Trials; Manni the Reveller will tell you to get your hands off his beer. Unlike other ales, it cannot be brewed.

After drinking the beer, the message reads "You quaff the beer. You feel slightly reinvigorated... but very dizzy too".

Steel boots are boots made from steel, requiring level 5 Defence to wear. To obtain steel boots, players can either obtain them as a drop from Pyrefiends and Harpie bug swarms, defeated using the Slayer skill, or from trading with another player.

As with all metal boots, this piece of armour cannot be made using the Smithing skill.
4129:
Adamant boots are a pair of boots made of adamantite. The player needs at least 30 Defence to wear these armoured boots. These are the first tier of metal boots to offer a strength bonus. Players without the required Defence level can choose to wear climbing boots instead, which have one more strength bonus, but lower defence bonuses.

As with all metal boots, this piece of armour cannot be made using the Smithing skill.
4131:
Rune boots are a pair of boots made of runite. They require a Defence level of 40 to equip. Players without the required Defence level can choose to wear climbing boots instead, which have the same strength bonus but lower defence bonuses.

As with all metal boots, this piece of armour cannot be made using the Smithing skill.

The granite maul is a two-handed melee weapon that requires 50 Strength and Attack to wield. They are dropped by gargoyles (75 Slayer required), which are in the Slayer Tower.

Players can use a granite clamp to cosmetically enhance the granite maul. This causes the maul to become untradeable, and the clamp is not returned upon reverting the maul back to its original state.

Players can use an ornate maul handle to enhance the granite maul into a granite maul (ornate handle), which reduces its special attack cost from 60% to 50%.

The granite clamp and ornate handle are obtained from Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing.

Using a bag of salt on a rockslug with 5 or more Hitpoints has no effect but will still consume a bag of salt.

A bag (or pile) of salt is required during Icthlarin's Little Helper.
4162:
A rock hammer is Slayer equipment that is required to kill gargoyles. Players can buy a rock hammer from any Slayer Master for 500 coins.

While damage can be done to them with a regular weapon at 75 Slayer, the hammer must be used on gargoyles to finish them off when they have 10 hitpoints or less left, unless the player has unlocked the Gargoyle Smasher ability via spending 120 Slayer reward points, which allows players to automatically use the hammer to finish off the gargoyle.
4164:
A facemask is a Slayer item worn on the headgear armour slot, requiring level 10 Slayer to wear, which cannot be boosted. The facemask can be bought from any Slayer Master for 200 coins. There is a facemask spawn inside a locked cage on the top floor of Kourend Castle, however the only way to pick it up is with telegrab.

It must be worn when fighting dust devils and smoke devils, otherwise they will dramatically decrease players' stats.

Wearing a facemask will prevent infection from Nex's virus attack.

While mining volcanic sulphur deposits in the Lovakengj sulphur mine, wearing a facemask will significantly reduce the damage poison gas clouds inflict on players.

During Mourning's End Part II, a dwarf named Thorgel will agree to trade the player a death talisman in return for a list of items, which includes a facemask.

This item is required to craft a Slayer helmet.
4166: These will protect my ears from loud noise.
4168:
The nose peg is a piece of Slayer equipment, requiring level 60 Slayer to wear, making it the second highest level slayer item. It can be bought from any Slayer Master. It is one of the items used to craft a Slayer helmet, which also has its nose protection ability.

When worn, the peg protects the player from the special attack of the aberrant spectre which, if not equipped, will cause a rapid and significant reduction in the player's stats and hitpoints.
4207:
A crystal weapon seed is an elven crystal that can be turned into crystal weapons. Completing the Gauntlet will yield a chance of gaining these seeds. The crystal weapon seed can be bought from Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 12 Last Man Standing points.

This seed can be restored into a crystal bow, a crystal shield, or a crystal halberd, the latter only with completion of the Hard Western Provinces Diary. Before completion of Song of the Elves, Ilfeen is the only one to offer this service to the player. She can be found at either of two clearings in Isafdar, teleporting between them periodically. If the player is mid-quest, and she is occupied with the fight against Lord Iorwerth, an Elven Scout will fulfil her role. After completion of the quest, Ilfeen is found in Prifddinas, slightly south of the house portal.

After completion of Song of the Elves, players may enchant the seeds themselves at a Singing bowl, requiring 78 Crafting and Smithing.

Players can also exchange the weapon seed for 10 crystal shards by speaking to Amrod in Prifddinas' Hefin Inn. The seed can additionally be traded to Pennant in Prifddinas for one crystal acorn, which can be grown into a crystal tree that yields up to 28-32 crystal shards when harvested.

When converting a crystal seed to a crystal bow and crystal shield, they cannot be traded or be used for high alchemy.

An airtight pot is a quest item used in One Small Favour and Swan Song. It is made by using a pot lid on an empty pot.

An airtight pot must be given to the Apothecary in Varrock during the events of One Small Favour. In Swan Song, an airtight pot is used to hold bone seeds to create an army of skeleton mages.
4438: This needs firing, then it should fit on a normal-sized pot.
4440: Pot lids are items that when used on pots create an airtight pot, an item required for the One Small Favour and Swan Song quests. They can be created by using a piece of soft clay on a Potter's wheel and then firing the unfired pot lid in a Pottery oven.
4456: It's a bowl of hot water.
4458:
A cup of water is an item made by using an empty cup on a water source. Nettles cannot be added to this item — they must be instead added to a bowl of water, and add Nettle tea to an empty cup.

A cup of water cannot be used to counter the desert heat effect.
4460: A cup of hot water is created by using a bowl of hot water on an empty tea cup or by heating a cup of water on a range or fire. It is solely used to make a Guthix rest potion. It is not drinkable like tea is, and it can do nothing by itself.
4517: This could feed a family of gnomes for a week!
4522:
Oil lamps are a light source for use in dark places. Like all low-quality light sources, it is recommended that several lamps are used if this is the only option, and a tinderbox is available in case the lamp goes out.

Empty oil lamps can be made using the Crafting skill at level 12 by glassblowing molten glass, or bought from Dorgesh-Kaan or from other players. To light it, players require level 12 in Firemaking. Note that the oil lamp must be filled with lamp oil to be lit.

An oil lamp can be combined with an oil lantern frame (forged from iron) to make an oil lantern for 50 Crafting experience. Combining the lantern frame with the lamp does not require a furnace or anvil, but does require 26 Crafting.

As it is an open light source, it can set off gas explosions in certain parts of the Lumbridge Swamp Caves.
4525: An oil lamp with no oil in it.
4527:
The empty candle lantern is an incomplete light source used in the Firemaking skill.

The empty candle lantern can be filled with a white candle or black candle to make a candle lantern. It can then be lit to use as a light source in dark areas. Lighting the candle lantern requires a tinderbox and level 4 Firemaking. No experience is received when lighting a candle lantern.

Candle lanterns are recommended for the Lumbridge Swamp Caves, as they have a lower chance of igniting the swamp gas, which will cause an explosion and damage the player. However, a better alternative is a bullseye lantern, and if that is not available then an oil lantern will suffice.
4529: A candle in a glass cage.
4532: A candle in a glass cage.
4535: Put oil in to complete it.
4537: The oil lantern is the second best lightable light source in the game (requiring 26 Firemaking to light), only inferior to the Bullseye lantern. Combining the lantern frame with the lamp does not require a furnace or an anvil. The oil lantern must be filled with lamp oil before it can be lit.
4540: An oil lantern frame can be made by members with level 26 Smithing from an iron bar, giving 25 Smithing experience. It is used to make an oil lantern which can be made with level 26 Crafting by using an oil lamp with the frame then filling the resulting empty oil lantern with lamp oil at the chemist's west of Rimmington. Oil lanterns can be lit with a tinderbox at level 26 Firemaking.
4542: Lantern lens are used with a bullseye lantern (unf) to make a bullseye lantern. A cut sapphire can then be used on the lantern to extract the lantern lens and produce a sapphire lantern at the same time.
4544: You need to add a lens before you can use it.
4546: You need to add lamp oil before you can use it.
4551: You don't want to wear it inside-out.
4593: A fake beard can be bought from Ali Morrisane in Al Kharid or the Pollnivneach general store. It mainly serves as a quest item.
4595: The karidian disguise is an unobtainable item that only appears when searching the Grand Exchange. It is presumably an item intended for use during The Feud quest, but was replaced by the desert disguise during development for unknown reasons.
4600: A handy little club made out of willow.
4608:
A super kebab is a kebab that has had red hot sauce added to make it spicy. They are sold by Ali the Kebab seller for 5 coins. Much like the normal kebab, the super kebab has a 5/8 chance to restore Hitpoints by 3 + 7% of the player's Hitpoints level. It also has a 1/32 chance of reducing any stats except Hitpoints.

To make a super kebab, the player must use red hot sauce (obtained from Ali the Kebab seller) on either a normal kebab or ugthanki kebab. A strange-smelling ugthanki kebab will also work.
4668: Garlic powder is created by using a pestle and mortar on garlic. It is used with a blessed pot to defeat Dessous during the Desert Treasure I quest. The item can be created at anytime, regardless the player having started or completed the quest.
4675:
The ancient staff is a one-handed magical weapon that can be used to autocast spells from the Ancient spellbook and standard spellbook. It requires 50 Attack and 50 Magic to wield, along with completion of Desert Treasure I. The staff is decorated with the symbol of Zaros.

It is frequently used in high-level player-killing due to its high magical accuracy. It, along with its upgraded versions, are the only items that have negative Prayer bonus.

Similarly to bladed staves, this staff has an attack speed of 4, making it a suitable weapon for melee combat, displaying similar stats as those of the rune scimitar with slightly higher strength bonus and lower attack bonus. It is outclassed in melee combat by the granite hammer, which also requires 50 Attack to wield, with an additional requirement of 50 Strength.

The staff may be bought once from Eblis for 80,000 coins after completing Desert Treasure I. For this reason, Ironmen are not recommended to alch or drop it because it is used in a master clue step, and the only other way the staff can be acquired is either as a rare drop from several boss monsters or as a very rare drop from mummies in the Ancient Pyramid.
4689:
A pile of salt is an item that can be made by using a bucket of saltwater on the suntrap in Sophanem. It is created during the quest Icthlarin's Little Helper.

This item cannot be used in place of a bag of salt to kill rockslugs.
4694: A combined Water and Fire Rune.
4695: A combined Air and Water Rune.
4696: A combined Air and Earth Rune.
4697: A combined Air and Fire Rune.
4698:
Mud runes are combination runes. They count as two separate runes: one water rune and one earth rune. Thus, any spell requiring one water rune, one earth rune, or both will spend only one mud rune.

They can be created with the Runecraft skill, purchased with pizazz points from the Mage Training Arena, or looted from essence implings with 42 Hunter.

Mud runes can be ground with a pestle and mortar to create ground mud runes. One ground mud rune is required to complete The Eyes of Glouphrie.

When equipped, the mud battlestaff and mystic mud staff provide an unlimited number of mud runes.
4699: A combined Earth and Fire Rune.
4708:
Ahrim's hood is magic armour worn in the headwear slot that is part of Ahrim the Blighted's set of barrows equipment. To wear Ahrim's hood, a player must have 70 Defence and 70 Magic.

Players may opt to use a farseer helm instead of Ahrim's hood, unless the set effect or damage bonus is desired. Compared to the farseer helm, Ahrim's hood has higher level requirements to wear but no quest requirements, and provides +1% Magic damage bonus. However, the hood provides an identical magic attack bonus and incurs repair costs.

Being part of Ahrim's barrows set, if Ahrim's hood is worn along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Ahrim's barrows set the player's successful magic attacks have a chance of temporarily lowering the opponent's Strength level. This is cumulative with other effects that lower strength, namely the spell Enfeeble.

Additionally, wearing Ahrim's set with an amulet of the damned will allow players to autocast Ancient Magicks, and also grant players a 25% chance of dealing a hit with 30% increased damage.
4710:
Ahrim's staff is a one-handed magic weapon that is part of Ahrim the Blighted's set. To wield Ahrim's staff, the player must have 70 Magic and 70 Attack. It increases Magic damage by 5%.

If Ahrim's staff is wielded along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Ahrim's barrows set, the player's successful magic attacks have a chance of temporarily lowering the opponent's Strength level. This is cumulative with other effects that lower strength, namely the spell Enfeeble.

It is able to autocast Standard combat spells as well as being one of the few weapons able to autocast Arceuus combat spells. Karil's crossbow is a two-handed ranged weapon that is part of Karil the Tainted's set. It requires 70 Ranged to wield. It fires bolt racks, which break upon firing. When equipped with the other three pieces of Karil the Tainted's set the wearer will receive the set effect, which has a chance to temporarily lower their target's Agility level. Additionally, if an amulet of the damned is worn alongside the set, there is also a 25% chance for each attack to deal a second hit for half the damage of the first.

Unlike standard crossbows, it is wielded in both hands. Furthermore, regular crossbows fire fewer, more powerful shots, meaning Karil's crossbow is actually similar in function to a shortbow; this gives it a potentially higher damage per second, at the expense of the shield slot. The crossbow has an attack range of 8. Longrange increases attack range by 2.

This weapon is comparable to a magic shortbow and its imbued counterpart. While Karil's offers a longer range, a +15 or +9 greater ranged attack bonus respectively, and a passive chance to hit twice when using the full Karil set and amulet of the damned, the magic shortbow variants offer identical strength when using amethyst arrows, which are not guaranteed to be consumed with each shot. In addition, the magic shortbows do not degrade. Players on a budget or fighting monsters with low ranged defence may find the magic shortbow to be the preferable option.

Unlike other bolts, they always disappear after being fired and cannot be retrieved by Ava's devices.
4745:
Torag's helm is melee armour worn in the headwear slot that is part of Torag the Corrupted's set of Barrows equipment. To wear Torag's helmet, a player must have 70 Defence.

Being part of Torag's barrows set, if Torag's helmet is worn along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Torag's barrows set the player gains a set effect. Damaging melee attacks have a chance of lowering the victim's run energy by 20%.

Torag's helmet is not commonly used due to its lack of Strength or Prayer bonuses. Furthermore, the set effect is considered mediocre. As a result, it is inexpensive compared to the other barrows helmets. However, it is often used in PKing, especially by ranged tanks, as there are few other inexpensive helm options for rangers and the negative ranged attack bonus is small.

For more details on the mechanics and strategies for this equipment, see the set page.

Torag's hammers are a two-handed blunt weapon that is part of Torag the Corrupted's set of barrows equipment. To wield Torag's hammers, a player must have 70 Attack and Strength.

Being part of Torag's barrows set, if Torag's hammers are wielded along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Torag's barrows set the player gains a special effect: damaging melee attacks have a chance of lowering the victim's run energy by 20%.

Torag's hammers have lower popularity and value compared to other Barrows weapons, as the hammers have a lower strength bonus and Torag's special effect is not as useful in combat. However, they have a high crush bonus and can be one of the more likely out of the melee Barrows weapons to hit as most armours have less crush defensive bonus than slash.

Like the glacial temotli, sulphur blades, and Earthbound tecpatl, the hammers perform two independently rolled hits per attack. The maximum damage of each hit is determined by calculating the combined max hit as normal and dividing it by two. If the combined max hit is odd, one max hit is rounded up while the other is rounded down (e.g., 45 → 22 + 23). This unique effect is useful when fighting NPCs with negative flat armour, such as the Blue Moon, as the flat damage increase gets applied to each hitsplat separately.

If Verac's flail is wielded along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Verac's set, the player receives the Defiler set effect. With this set effect active, player attacks have a chance (averaging 1/4) of hitting through an opponent's defence and prayer entirely. This effect can be devastating towards tank opponents who rely on high defence. With this set effect, Verac's flail can be considered one of the best weapons for certain PvM situations.

4820:
Iron nails are nails made with an iron bar on an anvil with a hammer in the player's inventory, requiring level 19 Smithing, yielding 15 iron nails and granting 25 Smithing experience per bar. Additionally, players can obtain iron nails in sets of ten from the workbench north of the tanner in the Kebos Lowlands. They can also be bought from a few shops, most notably the Sawmill, as well as the Shipyard, which can be teleported to for free by any Shipwright found at major ports.

Iron nails can be used to construct certain types of wooden furniture. With 18 Fletching, they can be used on flighted ogre arrows to create iron brutal arrows, granting 2.6 Fletching experience per arrow. With 56 Crafting, fifteen iron nails can be used with a willow shield and two pieces of snakeskin to craft a snakeskin shield, granting 100 Crafting experience per shield.

4824:
Rune nails are the second strongest type of nail. They are made by using a runite bar on an anvil with a hammer in the player's inventory, requiring 89 Smithing, yielding 15 rune nails and granting 75 Smithing experience per bar.

Rune nails can be used to construct certain types of wooden furniture. They rarely break but are expensive relative to other types of nails. With 56 Construction, five rune nails can be used along with two mahogany planks to repair broken bridges in the Hallowed Sepulchre, granting 700 Construction experience; without a hallowed hammer in the player's inventory, there is a chance of failing to repair the bridge and breaking nails in the process. With 77 Fletching, they can be used on flighted ogre arrows to create rune brutal arrows, granting 12.5 Fletching experience per arrow. With 83 Crafting, fifteen rune nails can be used with a redwood shield and two pieces of black dragon leather to craft a black d'hide shield, granting 172 Crafting experience per shield.

Rune nails are required for use in Shipbuilding components at the Runite and Ironwood tier.

Three zombies found in Tarn's Lair, near the Odovacar banker, drop rune nails at a 1/25 rate.
4825: An unstrung comp bow is made by using a knife on Achey tree logs with wolf bones in the inventory. Stringing it with a Bow string creates a Comp ogre bow. Level 30 Fletching and partial completion of Zogre Flesh Eaters is required.
4827:
The comp ogre bow was released with the quest Zogre Flesh Eaters and is made by using a knife on an achey tree logs with wolf bones in a player's inventory to create an unstrung comp bow, which can then be strung with a bow string to create the finished bow. This requires 30 Fletching, and grants 45 experience. This is the only composite bow that can be made through the Fletching skill. It can fire any type of brutal arrow, as well as ogre arrows.

When compared to the normal ogre bow, the comp bow has the same attack bonus and a faster attack speed, but a shorter range. It requires 30 Ranged to wield.

In order to equip this bow, players must first speak with Grish after reaching a certain point in the Zogre Flesh Eaters (before the final battle).

Players can select the "Check kills" option on the ogre bow or comp ogre bow to check how many chompy birds they have killed in the Chompy bird hunting activity, to see if they qualify for a Chompy bird hat. After scratching 100,000 notches on a comp ogre bow, there will be no more space to continue tracking chompy kills.
4830:
Fayrg bones are bones available from looting ogre coffins, which will often break lockpicks and decrease players' thieving abilities upon opening using thieving methods.

Fayrg bones give 84 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

252 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

252 XP when offered at the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

294 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit.

335 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl.

336 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of fayrg bonemeal.

402 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl with jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

588 XP on average when offered at the Chaos Temple in the Wilderness. Each offering gives 294 XP, which is the same as the gilded altars with two burners lit, but with an additional 50% chance to not consume the bones.

If burying the fayrg bones in Jiggig, there's a 1 in 3 chance to give no Prayer experience, and to instead spawn a skogre. The skogre will despawn after 5 minutes. A message in the chatbox appears "The creature rises from the grave... again!".
4832: Ancient ogre bones from the ogre burial tomb.
4834:
Ourg bones are bones obtained by killing Slash Bash, the boss from Zogre Flesh Eaters, stealing them from ogre coffins via the Thieving skill, or using keys dropped by zogres and skogres on nearby chests. As Slash Bash cannot be respawned after he has been killed once, ourg bones cannot be farmed from the boss.

Ourg bones give 140 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

420 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

420 XP when offered at the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

490 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two lit burners.

560 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of ourg bonemeal.

560 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl.

672 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl with jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

980 XP on average when offered at the Chaos Temple in the Wilderness. Each offering gives 490 XP, which is the same as the gilded altars with two burners lit, but with an additional 50% chance to not consume the bones.

Due to only being able to obtain them once from Slash Bash, and ogre coffins being slow to loot, Ourg bones are relatively rare, and as a result are generally much pricier than bones that provide similar Prayer experience.

Ourg bones provide the second most Prayer experience of all bones in the game, surpassed only by superior dragon bones. Unlike superior dragon bones, they do not have a Prayer level requirement to offer them, and grant almost as much experience.

Being part of Karil's barrows set, if Karil's leathertop is worn along with the other three pieces of Karil's set, the player's attacks gains a special effect: on successful attacks with Karil's crossbow against another player, there is a 25% chance that it may temporarily lower that player's Agility level by 20%. Additionally, if an amulet of the damned is worn alongside the set, there is also a 25% chance for each attack to deal a second hit for half the damage of the first.

For more details on the mechanics and strategies for this equipment, see the set page.
4950:
Karil's leatherskirt is Ranged armour worn in the legwear slot that is part of Karil the Tainted's set of Barrows equipment. To wear Karil's leatherskirt, a player must have 70 Defence and 70 Ranged.

Karil's leatherskirt gives the third highest magic defence for the leg slot at +35, following Armadyl chainskirt's +40, and Masori chaps (f)'s +46. The skirt has the same offensive bonuses as the black d'hide chaps, while offering higher defence in all but Slash in which it is on par.

Being part of Karil's barrows set, if Karil's leatherskirt is worn along with the other three pieces of Karil's set, the player's attacks gains a special effect: on successful attacks with Karil's crossbow against another player, there is a 25% chance that it may temporarily lower that player's Agility level by 20%. Additionally, if an amulet of the damned is worn alongside the set, there is also a 25% chance for each attack to deal a second hit for half the damage of the first.

For more details on the mechanics and strategies for this equipment, see the set page.
4956:
Torag's helm is melee armour worn in the headwear slot that is part of Torag the Corrupted's set of Barrows equipment. To wear Torag's helmet, a player must have 70 Defence.

Being part of Torag's barrows set, if Torag's helmet is worn along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Torag's barrows set the player gains a set effect. Damaging melee attacks have a chance of lowering the victim's run energy by 20%.

Torag's helmet is not commonly used due to its lack of Strength or Prayer bonuses. Furthermore, the set effect is considered mediocre. As a result, it is inexpensive compared to the other barrows helmets. However, it is often used in PKing, especially by ranged tanks, as there are few other inexpensive helm options for rangers and the negative ranged attack bonus is small.

For more details on the mechanics and strategies for this equipment, see the set page.
4962:
Torag's hammers are a two-handed blunt weapon that is part of Torag the Corrupted's set of barrows equipment. To wield Torag's hammers, a player must have 70 Attack and Strength.

Being part of Torag's barrows set, if Torag's hammers are wielded along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Torag's barrows set the player gains a special effect: damaging melee attacks have a chance of lowering the victim's run energy by 20%.

Torag's hammers have lower popularity and value compared to other Barrows weapons, as the hammers have a lower strength bonus and Torag's special effect is not as useful in combat. However, they have a high crush bonus and can be one of the more likely out of the melee Barrows weapons to hit as most armours have less crush defensive bonus than slash.

Like the glacial temotli, sulphur blades, and Earthbound tecpatl, the hammers perform two independently rolled hits per attack. The maximum damage of each hit is determined by calculating the combined max hit as normal and dividing it by two. If the combined max hit is odd, one max hit is rounded up while the other is rounded down (e.g., 45 → 22 + 23). This unique effect is useful when fighting NPCs with negative flat armour, such as the Blue Moon, as the flat damage increase gets applied to each hitsplat separately.

4986:
Verac's flail is a two-handed spiked weapon that is part of Verac the Defiled's set of barrows equipment. To wield Verac's flail, a player must have 70 Attack. The flail shares many similarities to a mace, notably its attack styles and stat distribution, though it attacks one tick slower.

If Verac's flail is wielded along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Verac's set, the player receives the Defiler set effect. With this set effect active, player attacks have a chance (averaging 1/4) of hitting through an opponent's defence and prayer entirely. This effect can be devastating towards tank opponents who rely on high defence. With this set effect, Verac's flail can be considered one of the best weapons for certain PvM situations.
4992:
Verac's brassard is melee armour worn in the body slot that is part of Verac's equipment. To wear Verac's brassard, a player must have 70 Defence.

Verac's brassard offers significantly less melee and ranged protection than Guthan, Torag and Dharok's platebodies (which all have equal stats), however it is better than the Rune platebody, with the exception of having -1 stab defence bonus. Because of this, Verac's brassard is rarely seen being used outside of the full set. However, Verac's brassard does not penalise ranged and magic attack bonuses nearly as much as regular melee armour.

If Verac's brassard is worn along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Verac's set, the player receives the Defiler set effect. Raw cave eels are fish that require a Fishing level of 38 to be caught and grants 80 fishing experience per catch, as well as a Cooking level of 38 to be cooked; doing so turns it into a cave eel. They can be used with Giant frog legs on the life altar in Creature Creation to make a frogeel.

They can be caught with a Fishing rod and bait in the Lumbridge Swamp Caves, the Dorgesh-Kaan South Dungeon, and the Ruins of Camdozaal.

Cave eels or slimy eels are the primary ingredients in the popular Dorgeshuun dish eel sushi. The eel is presumably served raw and wrapped in swamp weed. However, the dish cannot be made by the player. It is also a possible item needed to obtain the magic secateurs in Fairytale I - Growing Pains.

It is recommended to bring extra fishing bait when catching these in case raw slimy eel is caught instead.

Willow seeds may be grown into a willow which gives willow logs. Planting one requires level 30 Farming. It costs 1 basket of apples to protect as payment to the farmer, and takes roughly 240 minutes (4 hours) to finish growing. Willow seeds can be obtained by searching a bird nest, looting nature implings or by doing Wintertodt.

If this tree becomes diseased, using secateurs or magic secateurs on it to prune the diseased leaves will bring it back to a healthy state and will yield leaves.

By using secateurs on a fully grown willow tree, the player can harvest willow branches. These branches start to grow only after the tree's health has been checked, at a rate of 1 every 5 minutes, up to a maximum of 6 grown at a time.

In order to plant a new one, the tree must be chopped and then dug up, rewarding the player with willow roots. The amount of roots given depends on the player's Farming level (boosts can be used):

At level 30, a player obtains one willow root.

At level 38 a player obtains two willow roots.

At level 46, a player obtains three willow roots.

At level 54, a player obtains four willow roots.

Magic seeds are high-level tree seeds. At level 75 Farming, magic seeds may be planted in plant pots with a gardening trowel and watered to become magic saplings.

After about 8 hours it will be a fully grown magic tree, granting 13,913.8 Farming experience when inspected, and can then be cut to yield magic logs (and grant Woodcutting experience). After the tree has been cut down, it will regrow after 2 minutes. Using a spade on the cut tree roots before the tree has regrown yields magic roots and makes the tree patch available for planting a new tree. Alternatively, you can ask the nearby gardener to chop down the tree for 200 coins. This instantly removes the tree whether or not it has been cut down from the patch, making the patch available for a new seed to be planted, but no magic roots are obtained.

The farmer next to the patch will protect a growing magic tree if it becomes diseased, in exchange for 25 coconuts. If buying the magic sapling and coconuts on the Grand Exchange, it will cost around 108,818 per tree, assuming one pays a gardener. If this tree becomes diseased, using secateurs or magic secateurs on it to prune the diseased leaves will bring it back to a healthy state and will yield leaves.

In order to plant a new one, the tree must be chopped and then dug up, rewarding the player with magic roots. The amount of roots given depends on the player's Farming level (boosts can be used):

At level 75, a player obtains one magic root.

At level 83, a player obtains two magic roots.

At level 91, a player obtains three magic roots.

At level 99, a player obtains four magic roots.

Magic seeds may be found rarely in bird nests, which can be obtained randomly while Woodcutting or from Managing Miscellania, as well as doing bird house runs.

Paying Prissy Scilla to protect a magic tree is an elite task in the Western Provinces Diary. Obtaining at least 3 Magic roots at once when digging up your magic tree in Falador is an elite task in the Falador Diary.

They can be made by planting a pineapple seed in a filled plant pot, with a gardening trowel in your inventory, and then watering the pineapple seedling with a watering can or by using Humidify. When watered, the seedling will sprout into a sapling in one crop cycle (0-5 minutes).

Planting the sapling in a fruit tree patch, with a spade in your inventory, will give 57 Farming experience. It will grow into a pineapple tree after 960 minutes (16 hours), which gives 4,605.7 Farming experience.

Players can ask the gardener to protect their tree from disease whilst it grows, which requires payment of 10 watermelons. This payment can be noted.

Calquat saplings are saplings that can be used to grow calquat trees at level 72 Farming.

They can be made by planting a calquat seed in a filled plant pot, with a gardening trowel in your inventory, and then watering the calquat seedling with a watering can or by using Humidify. When watered, the seedling will sprout into a sapling in one crop cycle (0-5 minutes).

Planting the sapling in a calquat tree patch in Tai Bwo Wannai Village, The Summer Shore or Kastori, with a spade in your inventory, will give 129.5 Farming experience. It will grow into a calquat tree after 1,280 minutes (21 hours and 20 minutes), which gives 12,096 Farming experience.

Players can ask Imiago, Guppa or Tziuhtla to protect their tree from disease whilst it grows, which requires payment of 8 poison ivy berries. This payment can be noted.

A tiara is an item that can be created at a furnace from a silver bar along with a tiara mould and level 23 Crafting, granting 52.5 Crafting experience.

They are a purely cosmetic head slot item, though they can be turned into a talisman tiara, used in the Runecraft skill, acting as an equipable talisman (head slot), saving an inventory space over a normal talisman. It also allows the player to enter a particular runic altar by left-clicking on the corresponding mysterious ruins, saving time.

To create a talisman tiara, the player must have a tiara and the corresponding talisman in their inventory, and use the talisman or tiara on the altar of that particular rune. For example, a player who wishes to create an air tiara must enter the Air Altar ruins, and use the tiara on the altar with an air talisman in their inventory. The talisman itself is lost in the process. Tiaras cannot be imbued during Guardians of the Rift as attempting to enter an altar during the minigame with a tiara in your inventory will result in the chat dialog, "You should leave your tiara behind. There's no telling what the rift will do to it."

The fire tiara is a warm clothing object for Wintertodt.

While an air tiara is equipped, the mysterious ruins to the Air Altar have a left-click "Enter" option, freeing up an inventory slot that the air talisman would otherwise occupy.

Iron arrows are stronger than bronze arrows, and are compatible with most bows. Iron arrows can be made at level 15 Fletching by using 15 iron arrowtips on 15 headless arrows, granting 37.5 Fletching experience. As with most arrows, they can be poisoned.

Iron arrows can be purchased from Lowe's Archery Emporium in Varrock.
5621:
Rune arrows are stronger than adamant arrows, are stackable, and can be used on any bow of yew or stronger. They can be created through the Fletching skill at level 75 by using 15 rune arrowtips on 15 headless arrows, granting 187.5 Fletching experience. As with most arrows, they can be poisoned.

Rune arrows with a Magic shortbow (i) are a powerful weapon for Ironmen before obtaining the Toxic blowpipe, however they are outclassed by Karil's crossbow.

Players may also obtain 50 rune arrows from the Ranging Guild in exchange for 2,000 archery tickets, or obtain 300 at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing in Ferox Enclave in exchange for 3 Last Man Standing points.

5630:
Steel darts are Ranged throwing weapons. To wield steel darts, players must have at least level 5 Ranged. They can be obtained by either using the Smithing and Fletching skills or trading with another player. Steel darts can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

To create steel darts, the player must have completed the Tourist Trap quest and have at least level 34 Smithing and level 37 Fletching. Each steel bar will create 10 steel dart tips and the player will receive 37.5 Smithing experience. When feathers are added the player will receive 10 steel darts and 7.5 Fletching experience per steel dart.

Steel darts have almost the same stats and speed as iron knives, which are often used for Ranged training at lower levels - however, they are far cheaper in price than iron knives due to people training Fletching.

A steel dart is one of the possible items requested by the rowdy dwarf during the Forgettable Tale quest.
5631:
Black darts are ranged throwing weapons. To wield black darts, players must have at least level 10 Ranged.

Black darts cannot be made with the Fletching skill and instead are obtained through monster drops. The only monsters to drop black darts are Burthorpe soldiers. This makes black darts rather rare and hard to obtain. Black darts can be poisoned and they can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.
5632:
Mithril darts are Ranged throwing weapons made from mithril that are only available to members. Mithril darts require level 20 Ranged to wield. They can be obtained by either using the Smithing and Fletching skills or trading with another player. Mithril darts can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

Mithril darts are one of the most cost effective Ranged training weapons for lower level players, as they have an extremely quick rate of fire and cost very little compared to similar training methods like throwing knives or arrows. They can be bought in large numbers from the Grand Exchange, costing less than half of what similar tier ranged ammunition costs.

To create mithril darts the player must have completed The Tourist Trap quest and have at least level 54 Smithing and level 52 Fletching. Players can smith mithril bars into mithril dart tips. Each mithril bar creates 10 mithril dart tips and gives the player 50 Smithing experience. Feathers or Stripy Feathers then must be added to create the mithril darts. 11.2 Fletching experience is rewarded per mithril dart.
5633:
Adamant darts are Ranged throwing weapons. To wield the player must have at least 30 Ranged. They can be obtained by either using the Smithing and Fletching skills or trading with another player. Adamant darts can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

To make adamant darts, the player must have completed the Tourist Trap quest and have at least 74 Smithing and 67 Fletching. Each adamant bar will create 10 adamant dart tips and the player will receive 62.5 Smithing experience. When feathers are added the player will receive 10 adamant darts and 15 Fletching experience per adamant dart.
5634:
Rune darts are throwing weapons requiring level 40 Ranged to wield. They are created by combining rune dart tips with feathers. Rune darts can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

To create rune darts the player must have completed the Tourist Trap quest and have at least level 89 Smithing and level 81 Fletching. Players can smith rune bars into rune dart tips. Each rune bar creates 10 rune dart tips and gives the player 75 Smithing experience. Feathers then must be added to create the rune darts. 18.8 Fletching experience is rewarded per rune dart.

Smithing and fletching 10 rune darts while in Varrock is required to complete the Elite Varrock Diary. Fletching a rune dart is required to complete a master clue scroll skill challenge assigned by Sherlock.

Bronze knives are the lowest level throwing knives available, and do not require a Ranged level to wield. They can be poisoned, and due to being one-handed, can be wielded alongside a shield.

Bronze knives can be created from a bronze bar at level 7 Smithing. Each bar makes 5 knives, and grants the player 12.5 Smithing experience. The knives can also be purchased from Martin Thwait's Lost and Found shop in the Rogues' Den, requiring 50 Thieving and 50 Agility.

Throwing knives are among the fastest weapons in the game (along with darts), and are commonly used for player-killing, training Ranged, or tagging enemies for barraging.

They can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

Throwing knives are among the fastest weapons in the game (along with darts), and are commonly used for PKing or training Ranged. Iron knives can be purchased from Martin Thwait's Lost and Found shop in the Rogues' Den with 50 Thieving and 50 Agility.

Mature greenman's ale is a type of ale that restores 2 Hitpoints and temporarily boosts Herblore by 2, while also draining 2 Attack and Strength when drunk. It can be obtained through brewing at level 29 Cooking, granting 281 experience per batch. It is the stronger, or 'mature' version of a greenman's ale, with a 5% chance (increased to 64% with "the stuff") for your batch to become matured during brewing.

Compared to the non mature version, this ale restores 1 more Hitpoint, boosts an additional 1 Herblore level, while no longer draining Defence and draining 1 less Attack and Strength.

Ale yeast is the final essential ingredient added to the fermenting vat to begin the fermenting process for brewing ales and cider which lasts between 21 and 32 hours, or 135 hours if the stuff is added.

It can be purchased from any of the four brewery workers, Blandebir on the 1st floor of the Laughing Miner Pub in eastern Keldagrim for 25 coins, Lucrezia in the Moonrise Brewery and Winery for 25 coins, Vasile beneath the Myreque's Rest for 25 coins, or Metarialus underneath the The Green Ghost pub in Port Phasmatys, for 5 ecto-tokens. Players must have an empty pot to put the yeast in and can either talk to the brewery workers or use the pot on them.

In Keldagrim, a pot spawn can be found near the vat. In Port Phasmatys, empty pots can be purchased from the Port Phasmatys General Store.
5769:

They are created by using a knife on a calquat fruit picked from calquat trees, requiring 72 Farming to grow.

Ales in beer glasses cannot be used to fill a calquat keg.

Jute fibres can be harvested from a hops patch after planting jute seeds. They are used in Crafting to weave empty sacks and drift nets or as payment to protect sweetcorn (x10).

Adding them to a compost bin makes regular compost.
5933: A branch from a willow tree.
5935:
Coconut milk is an ingredient for several high-level Herblore potions. It is made by cracking a coconut open with a hammer, and then using the resulting half coconut on an empty vial. This produces a vial of coconut milk and a supercompostable coconut shell.

Coconut milk is used in making antidote+, antidote++, weapon poison(+), and weapon poison(++) potions. Coconut milk is the base of these potions as opposed to an ingredient, meaning players must add the ingredients to the vial of coconut milk in the same way as they would add them to a vial of water when creating other potions. These potions yield four doses upon creation instead of the usual three.
5937: A vial of extra strong weapon poison, for spears and daggers.
5940: A vial of super strong weapon poison, for spears and daggers.
5943: 4 doses of extra strong antipoison potion.
5945: 3 doses of extra strong antipoison potion.
5947: 2 doses of extra strong antipoison potion.
5949: 1 dose of extra strong antipoison potion.
5952: 4 doses of super strong antipoison potion.
5954: 3 doses of super strong antipoison potion.
5956: 2 doses of super strong antipoison potion.
5958: 1 dose of super strong antipoison potion.
5968: A fruit basket filled with tomatoes.
5970: A curry leaf is a large, yellow-green leaf which can be picked from a curry tree, which is grown from a curry tree seed in a fruit tree patch using the Farming skill. Level 42 Farming is required to grow curry trees. Farmers will look after a growing curry tree in exchange for 5 full baskets of bananas (these may be noted). They can also be looted from gourmet or eclectic implings.
5974:
A coconut is obtained from a palm tree, which can be grown from a palm sapling in a fruit tree patch, provided that one has level 68 Farming. Players can pay a gardener a fee of 15 papayas to watch over the tree while it grows. A fully grown palm tree grows one coconut per 40 minutes up to a maximum of six per tree.

A hammer can be used on a coconut to create a half coconut, which can be used on an empty vial to gain coconut milk and a coconut shell. Coconut milk is needed for making certain high-level potions using the Herblore skill, such as antidote+, weapon poison(+), antidote++ and weapon poison(++); coconut shells can also be used to make supercompost.

Players can pay 15 coconuts to a farmer to look after their growing Dragonfruit sapling, or 25 coconuts to a farmer to look after a Magic sapling.
5980:
Calquat fruit can be grown at level 72 Farming on a calquat tree. Picking each fruit gives 48.5 experience, with 6 fruits per tree when fully grown. To protect the tree from disease while growing, players may pay the nearby gardener 8 poison ivy berries.

Calquat fruit can be hollowed out with a knife to make calquat kegs, which can hold up to four pints of player-brewed ale. They can also be put in a compost bin to make supercompost.

Despite being inedible to players, calquat fruit can be fed to white Broodoo victims during the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup minigame, dealing high damage. This is convenient for players who have the requisite 72 Farming level to plant a calquat tree in the Tai Bwo Wannai farming patch.

According to the book Gielinor's flora - fruit, calquat fruit has tough, woody skin and hollow interior and is the largest known fruit in Gielinor.
5986:
Raw sweetcorn is a food item that can be picked from fields in Outer Fortis, Kastori, or grown through the Farming skill at level 20 with sweetcorn seeds in allotment patches. When picking sweetcorn from fields, players may randomly receive 1 sweetcorn seed. When planted in an allotment patch, Sweetcorn can be protected with 10 Jute fibres.

They are used in Cooking to make tuna potatoes. Cooking sweetcorn gives a decent amount of experience and thus is one of the ways that low-level members train their Cooking skill.

9 sweetcorn are needed to protect growing apple trees. Adding them to a compost bin makes regular compost.

Sweetcorn can be used at a windmill to get the pot of cornflour required to free Sir Amik Varze in the Recipe for Disaster subquest.
5988:
Cooked sweetcorn is a type of food that can be obtained by cooking sweetcorn on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 28 Cooking and granting 104 experience when successful. Players may burn the sweetcorn while cooking one, resulting in burnt sweetcorn; the burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 53 on both ranges and fires. When eaten it heals 1+10% of total hitpoints, rounded down.

Cooked sweetcorn may also be put in a bowl (giving a bowl of sweetcorn), and then mixed with a cooked tuna, with a knife in your inventory at level 67 Cooking, to make tuna and corn. This mixture heals 13 hitpoints when eaten, but may also be added to a baked potato with butter at level 68 Cooking. This makes a tuna potato, which heals 22 hitpoints.
5992:
Apple mush is made by putting four cooking apples into an apple press, crushing them, and filling a bucket with the resulting product.

Brewing cider requires four apple mush in the fermenting vat, therefore 16 cooking apples are needed in total to make a full brew of eight beer glasses or two calquat kegs of cider or mature cider.
5994:
Hammerstone hops can be harvested from a hops patch after planting hammerstone seeds. They are used in brewing dwarven stouts.

Adding them to a compost bin makes regular compost.
5998:
Yanillian hops can be harvested from a hops patch after planting Yanillian seeds. They are used in brewing wizard's mind bombs or as protection payment for mahogany trees (x25).

Adding them to a compost bin makes regular compost.
6004: A bittercap mushroom (or bittercap) is a type of fungus. While they are not edible without further preparation, they are non-poisonous and have a variety of culinary and other uses.
6014:
Rosemary can be harvested from a flower patch after planting rosemary seeds. It is used to make imp repellent. Fully grown rosemary will protect cabbages from disease.

Rosemary has very limited practical uses. The most productive use of rosemary (once harvested) is to add it to a compost bin to make regular compost. Players can also use it to make impling jars, but the process is complex, slow, and there are easier ways to obtain them.
6018:
Poison ivy berries can be harvested from a bush patch after planting poison ivy seeds. They are used in Herblore to make weapon poison(++) or as protection payment for calquat trees (x8).

Adding them to a compost bin makes supercompost.

Harvesting poison ivy berries from the patch near the Ardougne Monastery is a task in the hard Ardougne Diary.

Using poison ivy berries on the Rocky pet will change his appearance to Ziggy, a tanuki.
6020:
Leaves are dropped by baby tanglefoot (after the Fairytale I - Growing Pains quest) in Zanaris and tanglefoot in the Nightmare Zone, or when using any secateurs to cure any bush or tree of disease. They can be used to create compost in compost bins.

They can also be obtained from events while participating in the Forestry activity. Unlike other tree leaves, they cannot be obtained from cutting down regular trees. Leaves can be used to craft Forester's rations.
6022: A pile of Oak tree leaves.
6024: A pile of Willow tree leaves.
6026: A pile of Yew tree leaves.
6028:
Maple leaves are obtained from cutting maple trees, at a rate of 1 in 4 when the Forestry kit is in the player's inventory or equipped. They are used in creating Forester's rations, as well as compost in compost bins.

They can also be obtained by using secateurs to cure a planted maple tree of disease.
6030:
Magic leaves are obtained from cutting magic trees, at a rate of 1 in 4 when the Forestry kit is in the player's inventory or equipped. They are used in creating Forester's rations, as well as compost in compost bins.

They can also be obtained by using secateurs to cure a planted magic tree of disease.

Players without 75 Woodcutting will not be eligible to receive magic leaves from forestry events.
6032:
Compost is an item used in the Farming skill to reduce the chance of a farming patch becoming diseased per growth stage by 50 %. When used on a farming patch, each bucket grants 18 Farming experience.

It also increases the minimum yield and maximum number of harvests received from allotments, hops and herbs. The minimum number of herbs per harvest increases to 4. This also applies to giant seaweed patches underwater and celastrus bark from a fully grown celastrus seed.

Compost can be upgraded into supercompost by using one dose of compost potion on either a bucket of regular compost, or a compost bin filled with regular compost. Supercompost can also be made directly without a compost potion, by filling the compost bin with higher-level produce. It can be upgraded further into ultracompost by using 25 volcanic ash on the bin of supercompost, while big compost bins, such as the one in the Farming Guild, require 50 volcanic ash.
6034:
Supercompost is a superior version of compost that is used in the Farming skill to reduce the chance of a farming patch becoming diseased per growth stage by 4/5. When used on a farming patch, each bucket grants 26 Farming experience.

In addition, it also increases the minimum yield and maximum number of harvests received from allotments, hops and herbs. The minimum number of herbs per harvest increases to 5 (when compared with compost). This also applies to giant seaweed patches underwater and Celastrus bark from a fully grown Celastrus seed.

As a rule of thumb, supercompost should only be used on farming patches that produce a valuable harvest (such as high-level herbs) and/or provide significant experience for each item harvested (such as watermelons). Supercompost does not increase the yield of trees, fruit trees, cactus, or bush patches; therefore, it is not recommended to treat those patches with supercompost if you plan to pay a gardener to watch over them, since there is no benefit other than the extra 26 experience granted.

Players can add two volcanic ash to a bucket of supercompost, add 25 volcanic ash to a compost bin, or add 50 volcanic ash to a big compost bin that contains supercompost, to upgrade it to ultracompost.

6038: I could use this to make jewellery.
6043: The roots of the Oak tree.
6045:
Willow roots are roots that have been dug up from a tree patch by a player after growing and then chopping down a willow tree using the Farming skill. A spade is needed to dig up these roots. The number of roots obtained depends on the player's Farming level.

Willow roots can be used to make supercompost, or spun on a spinning wheel to make crossbow strings.
6047:
Maple roots are roots that have been dug up from a maple tree planted in a tree patch. It can be added to a compost bin to make supercompost like all tree roots, or be spun on a spinning wheel to make a crossbow string.

Maple roots can be obtained from digging up a maple tree grown by players, requiring 45 Farming, a maple seed, and 45 Woodcutting to cut the tree into a stump, or as a reward from Vale offerings in the Vale Totems minigame. They must plant the seed in a plant pot filled with soil, water it from a watering can, and transfer the sapling to a tree patch. After the tree has grown, they must then chop it down with an axe (to obtain maple logs), and then use a spade on the stump to dig it up. They will then receive the roots.
6049: The roots of the Yew tree.
6051:
Magic roots are the roots of the magic tree which is obtained with the Farming skill. Players with level 75 Farming may plant a magic sapling in a tree patch. They can also be obtained from the Vale Totems minigame.

Once the tree has grown, the player may use an axe to chop the tree down to a stump, and then use a spade on the stump to dig up the tree roots, clearing the patch for another tree, and putting the magic root into the farmer's inventory.

If the roots are not immediately dug up, the tree will respawn and it may be cut down again. Multiple roots can be obtained at higher Farming levels, and boosts can be used to obtain more roots. 1 root is obtained at 75, 2 at 83, 3 at 91, and 4 at 99.

Obtaining at least 3 magic roots when digging up a magic tree stump in Falador Park is an elite task in the Falador Diary.

As with all tree roots, magic roots may be used in a compost bin to make supercompost, or a spinning wheel to make crossbow string. Magic roots may also be spun into magic string by using them on a spinning wheel with level 19 Crafting which is used to make the amulet of nature. Magic roots are also a component in the Herblore skill to make antidote++. Due to the cost of growing magic trees, it's not recommended to use magic roots for crossbow strings as they can also be made from sinew.

A Rock-shell helm is a members-only melee helmet that requires 40 Defence and the completion of The Fremennik Trials quest to wear. To obtain a rock-shell helmet, a player must bring 1 dagannoth hide, 1 rock-shell chunk, and 5,000 coins to Skulgrimen in Rellekka. Aside from appearance, it is identical to the rune full helm.

Jarvald wears a rock-shell helm and will inform the player on how to obtain one.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Rockshell armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
6129:
The rock-shell plate is a piece of melee armour with stats almost identical to the rune platebody. To wear a rock-shell plate, players must have at least 40 Defence and have The Fremennik Trials quest completed. The plate can be considered as a second alternative to the rune platebody, as completing the Dragon Slayer I quest isn't a requirement to wear the rock-shell plate. The rock-shell plate also has a slightly better range attack bonus than the rune platebody and does not interfere with the effects of Ava's device so it may be viable for a range tank setup.

To obtain a rock-shell plate, players can either bring 3 dagannoth hides, 1 rock-shell shard, and 10,000 coins to Skulgrimen in Rellekka, or receive it as a drop from Dagannoth Rex.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Rockshell armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

To obtain rock-shell legs, players can either bring 2 dagannoth hides, 1 rock-shell splinter, and 7,500 coins to Skulgrimen in Rellekka, or receive them as a drop from Dagannoth Rex.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Rockshell armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

6215:
The poison broodoo shield is a special members only shield. The shield requires 25 Defence and 25 Magic to wear. When created, the shield comes with 10 charges.

Broodoo shields have a passive effect when used in combat, similar to the black mask; when damage is taken it has a 10% chance of draining the opponent's Defence stat by 1, and then 5% of their remaining total. The chance for the ability to occur happens whenever an enemy attacks the player adjacently. The enemy must still have over half of its Hitpoints and the affected skill must be at its base level for it to be affected. The shield works even if you are not fighting back and at any distance from the enemy.

The number following the name of the broodoo shield represents the number of charges left on the shield, starting at 10. Every time the special attack is used, this amount will decrease by one. There is no way to recharge the shield after the charges have been depleted, but it does not affect the shield or its defensive bonuses once they are all used.

6281: Thatch spar light is harvested during the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup minigame. They are obtained by hacking light jungle with a machete, earning favour at the same time. These are used to repair and reinforce Tai Bwo Wannai's village fences with a machete for 0.1% favour. Alternatively, they can be cut to skewer sticks with a machete. Skewer sticks are used with a spider carcass to cook a spider on stick.

Gout tubers are a rare seed and food obtained from Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup. It can be planted in a herb patch requiring 29 Farming and completion of Eadgar's Ruse to grow goutweeds. Due to its rarity, it is often only used for the medium Karamja Diary task of trading Safta Doc a gout tuber, 3 specific unnoted gems, and trading sticks for a gem machete. It cannot be planted at the disease-free Troll Stronghold herb patch, nor the patch at Weiss. Although gout tubers may be planted, they cannot be stored in the Seed vault or a Seed box. As with other herbs, it is not possible to pay a nearby gardener to watch over goutweed plants, nor will a fully-grown white lily plant protect them from disease.

Goutweed can be traded to Sanfew in Taverley, for a random herb per goutweed. Growing goutweed to trade with Sanfew is not recommended. The herbs received from Sanfew are random and gout tubers are very costly compared to standard herb seeds. If goutweed itself is needed, players should obtain it from the cellar at the Troll Stronghold due to the tuber's rarity and high trade value for its use in the medium Karamja Diary.

Gout tubers are edible. When eaten, a gout tuber heals 12 Hitpoints and restores 50 run energy. Eating one results in the message "You eat the tuber. Hmmm, peculiar taste! It heals some run energy. It heals some health anyway."

Gout tubers will be turned to rotten food if you are attacked by a Ghast in the Mort Myre swamp.

The Tzhaar-ket-om, also known as the obsidian maul, is a two-handed blunt weapon that requires a Strength level of 60 to wield. It is affected by the Berserker necklace, receiving a 20% damage increase when the necklace is worn. It is also affected by the Obsidian armour (helmet, platebody and platelegs) which will increase the melee attack and melee strength by 10%. These damage bonuses do stack with each other. It is part of the set of obsidian weapons.

Two of these are used to build an obsidian fence at level 83 Construction in a player's superior garden.

The maul is used commonly by Obsidian maulers in player-killing because the only requirement is a Strength level of 60, which makes it possible to have a low Combat level while being able to deal high amounts of damage. However, one major drawback of this weapon is its poor attack speed.

With Karamja Gloves 1 or higher, players can purchase the maul by selling 7223 chaos runes to TzHaar-Mej-Roh's Rune Store.

Players can attach a Tzhaar-ket-om ornament kit, obtained from hard Treasure Trails, to create a Tzhaar-ket-om (t). This is only cosmetic, and does not affect the maul's stat bonuses. It can be dismantled, returning the maul and ornament kit.
