A mud battlestaff is a mud elemental staff which provides unlimited amounts of water and earth runes as well as the autocast option when equipped. It requires 30 Attack and 30 Magic to wield.

The mystic mud staff is an even stronger alternative, providing better melee and magic stat bonuses. It is obtained by taking the mud battlestaff and 40,000 to Thormac. (Reduced to 30,000 or 20,000 with completion of the hard and elite Kandarin diaries respectively.)

Wielding a mud battlestaff is ideal for curse spells, as almost all of them use both water and earth runes.

The staff is only obtainable as a potential drop from Dagannoth Prime. For ironmen unable or unwilling to farm this boss until (and if) the staff is dropped, there are two alternatives in order to have infinite water & earth runes at the same time: using an earth staff with a tome of water that is charged with at least one soaked page, or a using a water staff with a tome of earth that is charged with at least one soiled page. Given that only combat spells drain charges from the tomes, the staff + tome combo will provide unlimited water and earth runes when casting spells such as Bones to Peaches or Lvl-5 enchant (e.g. for training Magic at the Mage Training Arena) without the need for recharging the tome.
6563:
The mystic mud staff is an elemental staff requiring 40 Attack and 40 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of earth and water runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

Wielding a mystic mud staff is ideal for curse spells, as almost all of them use both water and earth runes. The precursor to this staff (Mud battlestaff) is only obtainable as a potential drop from Dagannoth Prime. For ironmen unable or unwilling to farm this boss until (and if) the staff is dropped, there are two alternatives in order to have infinite water & earth runes at the same time: using an earth staff with a tome of water that is charged with at least one soaked page, or using a water staff with a tome of earth that is charged with at least one soiled page. Given that only combat spells drain charges from the tomes, the staff + tome combo will provide unlimited water and earth runes when casting spells such as Bones to Peaches or Lvl-5 enchant (e.g. for training Magic at the Mage Training Arena) without the need for recharging the tome.

This staff can be created after the completion of the quest Scorpion Catcher by taking a mud battlestaff and 40,000 to Thormac. After completion of the Hard Kandarin Diary and Elite Kandarin Diary, Thormac will only require 30,000 or 20,000 respectively.

The seercull is a Fremennik bow that requires a Ranged level of 50 to wield, and fires arrows up to Amethyst. Compared to a magic shortbow, it has a slower rate of fire and a different special attack which is more effective against mages. In addition, its normal and rapid fire attacks have one more range than that of a shortbow, and its long range attack is equivalent to that of a composite bow. It is a comparable weapon to the Magic comp bow.

The name can be attributed to the combination of the word seer (another word for "mage" or "wizard") and the word cull (another word for "kill"), in other words, the mage-killer. This is a fitting name because of the effect of its special attack and its examine text.
6729:
Dagannoth bones are bones dropped by Dagannoth Rex, Dagannoth Prime, and Dagannoth Supreme. They are not obtained as drops from regular Dagannoth, who only drop standard bones.

Dagannoth bones give 125 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

375 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

375 XP when offered at the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

437.5 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit.

500 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of dagannoth bonemeal.

500 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl, or 600 XP when offered with a jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

875 XP on average when offered at the Chaos Temple in the Wilderness. Each offering gives 437.5 XP, which is the same as the gilded altars with two burners lit, but with an additional 50% chance to not consume the bones.

It can be imbued using 650,000 Nightmare Zone reward points or 325,000 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements, 260 Soul Wars Zeal Tokens, or a Scroll of Imbuing, purchased for 200 Emir's Arena reward points, which doubles the magic attack and defence bonuses, and increases the magic damage bonus from 0.2% to 0.5%.

The dragon axe is the second best axe in the game after its direct upgrade, the crystal axe, and is tied with the 3rd Age axe. It is 10% more efficient at chopping logs than the rune axe.

Like all axes, it is both a weapon (requiring 60 Attack to wield) and a tool (requiring 61 Woodcutting to use).

As with most dragon equipment, the dragon axe cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
6750:
A black desert shirt is an item of clothing that players may find useful when doing the Shadow of the Storm quest. They can make it by using black dye on a normal desert shirt. This can also be done with a desert robe to create a black desert robe.

The quest requires players to be wearing at least three black garments, in order to look evil. Players may already be wearing a desert shirt (since the main part of the quest takes place in the Kharidian Desert), and black mushrooms can be found locally.

This makes it a convenient choice to make the ink and use it to dye the shirt, though players will also need an empty vial and a pestle and mortar with them.

The black desert robes will not protect players from the desert heat effect. This is stated in a warning message shown when attempting to dye them.

6760:
The Guthix mjolnir is a two-handed weapon. There are no level requirements to wield this item. To obtain one, a player can either find it during The Enchanted Key miniquest or trade with another player.

Each mjolnir can only be obtained once per account, as the Enchanted key will disintegrate after the player finds all of the treasure. Once this happens, the key cannot be re-obtained.

As its name implies, the Guthix mjolnir is affiliated with the god Guthix. It is tipped with a symbol associated with Guthix, the Tear of Guthix.
6764:
The Zamorak mjolnir is a two-handed weapon. There are no level requirements to wield this item. To obtain one, a player can either find it during The Enchanted Key miniquest or trade with another player.

Each mjolnir can only be obtained once per account, as the Enchanted key will disintegrate after the player finds all of the treasure. Once this happens, the key cannot be re-obtained.

As its name implies, the Zamorak mjolnir is affiliated with the god Zamorak. It is tipped with Zamorak's symbol of horns.

It can be equipped for protection against the Zamorakian followers in the God Wars Dungeon.
6794:
Choc-ice can be bought from a local vendor named Rokuh in Nardah, who runs Rok's Chocs Box. They are sold for 30 coins each, and heal 7 Hitpoints when eaten. If a bar of choc-ice is brought while venturing through the desert, it will automatically be consumed when the desert heat sets in, providing both its healing effect as well as quenching the player's thirst. That said, manually eating choc-ice does not reset nor delay the onset of desert heat. Choc-ice can nevertheless come in handy as an alternative to bringing waterskins to the desert. Although waterskins are refillable and provide up to 4 uses each, choc-ice has the advantages of being essentially weightless and serving a dual purpose as a food. This can be particularly useful when scaling the Agility Pyramid.

Waterskins have priority over choc-ices when under the influence of desert heat, and will be consumed first if the player is carrying both in their inventory. Bars of choc-ice can also occasionally melt while in the desert, regardless of any other measures taken to combat the heat, prompting the message: Your choc ice evaporates in the desert heat.

Choc-ices were invented by Rokuh, who sold them to the people of Nardah when their town had become cursed and they could no longer draw water from its wells. Rokuh bought a box imbued with a powerful ice spell, ensuring its contents would never melt, even under the harsh desert sun. He used this magical box (possibly an ice cooler) to store his new invention: a confection made of an iced cream coated with a layer of chocolate, which he called choc-ice. Even after the curse has been lifted from Nardah upon completion of the Spirits of the Elid, its inhabitants remain eager consumers of the treat.

Karamel, an enemy from Recipe for Disaster, drops a choc-ice when she is killed.
6809:
Granite legs are platelegs which require 50 defence and 50 strength to be worn. They can only be obtained by killing Skeletal Wyverns.

Compared to dragon platelegs and rune platelegs, they have a greater ranged defence bonus at the cost of worse melee defences. They also have 10 more negative magic attack bonus compared to metal platelegs and plateskirts, which can be beneficial for splashing.
6812:

216 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

216 XP when offered at the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

252 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit.

288 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of wyvern bonemeal.

290 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl, or 348 XP when offered with a jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

504 XP on average when offered at the Chaos Temple in the Wilderness. Each offering gives 252 XP, which is the same as the gilded altar with two burners lit, but with an additional 50% chance to not consume the bones.
6814: Fur is an item dropped by werewolves. It can be sold to Baraek for 12 coins, or 20 with the Ring of Charos(a). It has no other use other than a few quests.
6889:
A mage's book is a book in the shield slot, requiring 60 Magic to wield. It is tied with the ancient wyvern shield for the third-best Magic attack bonus in the shield slot, behind the arcane spirit shield and the Elidinis' ward (f), but it has no Melee or Ranged defensive bonuses. The mage's book is popular among combat pures because there is no required Defence level. It gives a Magic damage bonus of 2%.

It can be obtained by playing the Mage Training Arena minigame for:

It is the most expensive reward available from the Mage Training Arena minigame. It takes 5.3 hours on average to acquire the mage's book when playing efficiently and using the best spells. Acquiring the book yields a profit of 3,356,160 while using the appropriate staves.
6891: A book about the Training Arena.
6908: The beginner wand is a one-handed staff, and the weakest of the wands, requiring 45 Magic to wield. It can be obtained by either exchanging pizazz points at the Mage Training Arena or buying one from another player.
6910: The apprentice wand is a one-handed staff and wand that can be wielded with 50 Magic. It can be obtained by either exchanging pizazz points at the Mage Training Arena or buying one from another player.

Due to its difficulty to obtain, the chilli potato is not a commonly cooked or eaten item unless received as a monster drop. Similar foods such as potato with cheese heal more and are easier to obtain.
7056: A baked potato with egg and tomato.
7058: A baked potato with mushroom and onions.
7060:
The tuna potato is a type of food that restores 22 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by following the steps to combine various items (listed below). To follow all the preparation steps requires level 68 Cooking and grants 10 Cooking experience for a grand total of 309.5 Cooking experience (all the necessary steps).

The tuna potato is the second highest instant-health single consumption food, behind the marlin, alongside the dark crab, anglerfish, bluefin and manta ray. The tuna potato has the lowest Cooking requirement of these, but has the highest weight and is tedious to mass-produce. For a comparison to other items that provide healing, see food.
7062: Chilli con carne is a food that heals 5 Hitpoints. It can be used with a potato with butter to create a chilli potato at level 41 Cooking, providing 165.5 Cooking experience.
7064: A bowl of scrambled eggs and tomato.

Mushroom & onion can be created by players with level 57 Cooking. The full process of making mushroom & onion gives 120 experience, but the final step gives none. Eating Mushroom & onion restores 11 hitpoints.

To make mushroom and onion, obtain a knife, mushroom, onion, and two bowls:

Use a mushroom with a bowl and cook it on a range to make fried mushrooms.

Use an onion with another bowl and cook it on a range to make fried onions.

Finally use one bowl on the other bowl.

Mushroom and onion may be added to a potato with butter to make mushroom potato.

Tuna and corn is food and a cooking ingredient that can only be created by members with a Cooking level of 67. It can be created by using a bowl of sweetcorn on cooked tuna with a Fletching knife equipped, or while a knife is in your inventory, or by adding cooked sweetcorn to a bowl of chopped tuna, or by using a bowl of sweetcorn on chopped tuna.

It heals 13 hitpoints. Making all ingredients for tuna and corn from scratch provides you with 204 Cooking experience.

It is mostly used as one of the final ingredients for a tuna potato, which heals 22 hitpoints. To make a tuna potato, use a tuna and corn with a potato with butter at level 68 Cooking.
7070: Minced meat is made by using cooked meat on a bowl while having a knife in your inventory. It can be eaten to restore 2 Hitpoints. Alternatively, spicy sauce can be used on minced meat to make chilli con carne.

At level 13 Cooking, a player can cook an uncooked egg on a range or fire. This produces a scrambled egg and grants 50 Cooking experience. The scrambled egg can either be eaten or combined with a tomato to make egg and tomato topping, used in making an egg potato.

7082: A bowl of fried Bittercap mushrooms.

It can be made by using a bowl on a cooked sweetcorn; this does not require a knife, nor does it provide any Cooking experience. As food, when eaten, it provides healing identical to cooked sweetcorn, namely 1+10% of total hitpoints, rounded down. A bowl of sweetcorn is called "Sweetcorn" in-game. This may cause confusion among players as raw sweetcorn has the same in-game name.

Wearing the boots will protect the player against a variety of electric-based attacks, including:

Reducing the max hit of a Killerwatt's ranged attack from 13 to 6

Reducing the damage dealt by a rune dragon's electric attack from 2-5 to 0-2

Reducing damage taken from the electric ball attack by 40% if it does not pass through Verzik Vitur during the second phase of the fight

Nullifying the 10 damage taken during Darkness of Hallowvale, when improperly using the large ornate key directly on the door to the Meiyerditch Laboratories, rather than suspending it from the nearby vampyre statue

A mud pie is a special type of pie that does not restore Hitpoints, and instead can be used as an equipable weapon for PvP. The pie does no damage and is not stackable, but can be thrown at other players to reduce the target's current run energy by 25%, rounded down. Mud pies have no effect on NPCs. When throwing a mud pie, a pie dish will drop underneath the target. As mud pies are considered a thrown weapon, a player targeted by mud pies should wear armour with high Ranged defence to lower their accuracy.

It can be obtained by baking a raw mud pie on a cooking range, requiring level 29 Cooking and granting 128 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 63. Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.

Mud pie is a possible task from Romily Weaklax in the Cooks' Guild.

Garden pie is a type of pie that restores 12 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 6. It also temporarily boosts Farming by 3. A pie dish will remain after both bites are consumed.

When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 68. Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.

Baking a wild pie at the Nardah clay oven is a requirement for the Elite Desert Diary.

Summer pie is a type of pie with two bites that restores 11 Hitpoints, 10% run energy, and grants a +5 temporary skill boost to Agility per bite. A pie dish will remain after consumption.

It can be created by baking a raw summer pie on a cooking range, requiring level 95 Cooking and granting 260 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Summer pies never stop burning altogether even at level 99, unless the player is wearing a Cooking cape. Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.

Summer pies are a type of 1 tick (0.6 seconds) fast food, meaning you can eat them in succession with less delay than standard food which adds a 3-tick (1.8 second) penalty. Because of this short eat delay, summer pies can restore health quicker than manta rays, making them more efficient for healing up a lot of lost health in the same amount of ticks. However, as each half adds 3 ticks of attack delay, they are less efficient in combat than other high-healing foods.

The +5 Agility boost makes summer pies a great food for use in Agility training, increasing the chance to pass obstacles while restoring Hitpoints lost from failing any. It may also be used to pass Agility level requirements in quests, Agility courses, shortcuts or any other activities with an Agility requirement. Not all requirements can be boosted, such as Dragon Slayer II, the Ape Atoll Agility Course or Saradomin's Encampment in the God Wars Dungeon. The Preserve prayer may be used to extend the duration of the boost.

Summer pies are popular for fighting the Chaos Elemental or Chaos Fanatic as the empty pie dish prevents their special attacks from un-equipping Worn Equipment due to a full inventory.

Successfully baking a summer pie inside of the Cooks' Guild is an elite Varrock Diary task.

Cornflour is an unobtainable item released alongside Recipe for Disaster. It is assumed to be made by using Sweetcorn on a Windmill, but this requires a pot, and results in a pot of cornflour instead.

It was presumably created as a parallel to the discontinued item Flour, as the method of using a pot on a dropped heap of flour still existed ingame.

A pot of cornflour is made by grinding raw sweetcorn in a windmill. This is made in the same fashion as flour, but instead of wheat, raw sweetcorn is put into the hopper.

Its only use is during the Freeing Sir Amik Varze subquest of Recipe for Disaster as one of the ingredients needed to make the creme brulee supreme for Sir Amik Varze. It is used with the milky mixture to make the cornflour mixture.

The windmill on Harmony Island cannot be used to make cornflour.

A raw jubbly is obtained by killing a jubbly bird or jubster during, or after, the Recipe for Disaster quest (after having begun saving Skrach Uglogwee).

It can be cooked with 41 Cooking on the spit located near Rantz or the one located at Jiggig. Cooking a raw jubbly yields 160 experience and produces a cooked jubbly. There is no level that Jubbly will "stop burning" except indirectly at 99 Cooking via a Cooking skill cape or a Max Cape.

The gadderhammer is a two-handed members-only maul. There are no combat requirements for wielding the gadderhammer. To obtain the gadderhammer the player must defeat Gadderanks during In Aid of the Myreque. Even though it can be purchased from another player or the Grand Exchange, it cannot be wielded until Gadderanks is defeated.

This weapon cannot be made using the Smithing skill. It has a very similar appearance and combat animation to the granite maul, and stats similar to an Adamant warhammer.

If lost, the gadderhammer can be bought from Burgh de Rott's general store owner, Aurel, for 3,000 coins.

The gadderhammer does extra damage against shades (similar to the keris versus kalphites), possessing a 25% damage bonus against shades as well as a 5% chance to deal double damage. The bonus damage when employed against shades stacks with the benefits provided by a salve amulet (e) and Void Knight equipment.

Despite its name, the gadderhammer does not act as a replacement for a hammer, unlike the Imcando hammer.

Snake hides are obtained from Swamp snakes from the Temple Trekking minigame. When killed, a swamp snake becomes a dead swamp snake, and a player may use a knife on these remains to obtain 2 to 5 snake hides.

The snake hide can be tanned into snakeskin by a tanner, at a cost of 20 coins. Tanners can be found in Al Kharid, the Ranging Guild, Canifis, Forthos Dungeon and the Crafting Guild. Members can craft the snakeskins into snakeskin armour.

The Varrock teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to Varrock. Players can create this item on any regular lectern as long as they have 1 law rune, 3 air runes, 1 fire rune, and 1 soft clay and at least level 25 Magic, giving 35 experience.

This tablet can be made regardless of the player's current spellbook.

As with all tablets, the player does not need to have the required Magic level to cast the spell in order to use the tablet, and the player does not receive any Magic experience upon using the tablet.

Players who have completed the Medium Varrock Diary can switch the location of the teleport to the Grand Exchange by right-clicking the teleport tablet or spell and changing the destination. This applies to all further Varrock Teleport tablets, until the player changes it back, not just the one they are currently using.
8009:
The Falador teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to Falador.

Players can create this item on an eagle lectern, a teak eagle lectern, or a mahogany eagle lectern. To make it, level 37 Magic, 1 law rune, 3 air runes, 1 water rune, and 1 soft clay is required, which grants 48 experience. A single Falador tablet can be obtained from Marlo's crate, a reward from the Daddy's Home miniquest.

This tablet can be made and used regardless of the player's current spellbook. The user does not need the relevant Magic level to use the tablet, which shares the same rule with all tablets not including Ardougne tablet, house tablet, and Watchtower teleport, as they require quests or having a player-owned house.

The Camelot teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to Camelot.

Players can create this item on a Teak eagle lectern, a Mahogany eagle lectern, or a Marble Lectern as long as they have 1 law rune, 5 air runes, and 1 soft clay and at least level 45 Magic, granting 55.5 experience. In addition to using air runes, a player may also use a staff of air to reduce the cost and allow for an extra inventory slot.

This tablet can be made regardless of the player's current spellbook. As with all tablets, the user does not need to have the relevant Magic level to use this tablet.

The teleport to house is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to their player-owned house. Players can right-click to choose whether they teleport inside or outside of their house.

Players can create this item on a mahogany eagle lectern (requiring 67 Construction) or marble lectern (77) as long as they have 1 law rune, 1 air rune, 1 earth rune, and 1 soft clay and at least level 40 Magic. Combination runes and staves can be used, allowing for two spaces to be freed by using a dust staff. You gain 30 Magic experience for each tablet you create, and each tablet takes 4 ticks (2.4 seconds) to make.

This tablet can be made regardless of the player's current spellbook. As with all tablets (except for the Ardougne teletab), the user does not need to have the relevant Magic level to use it. All tablets, including this one are an efficient method of earning money and Magic experience. They are very popular with players, as they take up 1 inventory space, making a good 1-click teleport and great for tablet making/Construction training. A good strategy for making tablets is to carry law runes, noted soft clay and coins while wielding a dust staff; make the tablets at a player-owned house in Rimmington, and use Phials to un-note the soft clay for 5 coins per note, then repeat the process.

The Dorgeshuun crossbow is a crossbow requiring level 28 Ranged to equip. It is often used to train Ranged at low to medium levels, due to it having several advantages over similar crossbows with the same level requirements. It has the same attack bonus as an iron crossbow. It has an attack speed that is one tick faster than most other crossbows, and it is able to fire bone bolts, which are significantly cheaper than most other ammunition of similar strength. The fact it is a crossbow also gives it an advantage over shortbows, allowing the use of the shield slot for defensive or offensive purposes. Despite the bone bolts being roughly equivalent to iron bolts in ranged strength, the Dorgeshuun crossbow's faster attack speed means that its damage-per-second output when firing bone bolts is comparable to that of a regular crossbow firing steel or even mithril bolts (depending on the player's exact Ranged level).

It can be bought from Nardok in the Dorgeshuun Mines after the completion of The Lost Tribe quest. Completion of this quest is not required to equip it, however, meaning it can be purchased from other players and used without completing this quest. It can fire metal bolts up to iron, except silver bolts, and is the only crossbow that can use bone bolts. Note, however, that bolts containing unique tips and their (e) variants are not able to be fired from it.

This crossbow is the only crossbow with an attack speed of 5. This makes it 1 tick faster than most crossbows - it is only slower than the Karil's crossbow, the hunters' crossbow, and its upgraded variant, the hunter's sunlight crossbow, which all have an attack speed of 4. It should be noted that the Karil's crossbow is two-handed.

Weighing only 2.267kg, it is also the lightest crossbow in the game, making it ideal to use along with the mithril grapple when conservation of run energy is necessary, such as in the Hallowed Sepulchre.
8882:
Bone bolts are ammunition that can be bought after completion of The Lost Tribe quest. They can only be used with the Dorgeshuun crossbow, a popular choice for training ranged due to its faster speed than regular crossbows. Unlike other ammunition, it requires 28 Ranged to equip.

Due to their low price and ease of access from Nardok's Bone Weapons, having a base price of only 3 coins each, bone bolts are generally considered a very cost-effective method of training Ranged at lower levels. Assuming non-stop use of the Dorgeshuun crossbow on rapid, the player can fire 1,500 bolts per hour, which only costs 10,500 coins per hour if buying the bolts from the Grand Exchange.

Despite the bone bolts being roughly equivalent to iron bolts in ranged strength, the Dorgeshuun crossbow's faster attack speed means that its damage-per-second output when firing bone bolts is comparable to that of a regular crossbow firing steel or even mithril bolts (depending on the player's exact Ranged level).

If not buying the bolts from the Grand Exchange, buying bone bolt packs is recommended in order to save costs, since the cost per bolt can rapidly increase when buying the bolts individually. As with other bolts, their ranged strength is higher than most arrows with similar level requirements. The Dorgeshuun crossbow is 1 tick (0.6 seconds) slower to fire than shortbows, which balances out the higher strength of the bolts.

Despite not being made of metal, bone bolts do function with Ava's devices obtained from the completion of Animal Magnetism.

Iron bolts are the third-weakest bolts, stronger than blurite bolts. Iron bolts may be shot from iron or better crossbows. As with most bolts, they can be poisoned, however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips.

Iron bolts may be created by players. First, a player must smith unfinished iron bolts. This requires a Smithing level of 18, and for each iron bar a player smiths they will get 10 unfinished iron bolts and 25 Smithing experience. Then a player must attach flights to the bolts. Attaching flights to each bolt requires a Fletching level of 39 and 1 feather, granting 1.5 Fletching experience per bolt.

Iron bolts may be tipped with pearl. To tip the bolts with pearl, a player must have a Fletching level of 41 and use pearl bolt tips with the iron bolts, granting 3.2 Fletching experience for each pearl bolt tip attached and making the iron bolts into pearl bolts. Pearl bolts can then be enchanted; more information on enchanting them is available under pearl bolts.
9144:
Runite bolts (or rune bolts) are a type of crossbow ammo. They can be fired using a rune, dragon, dragon hunter, Armadyl, or Zaryte crossbow. Runite bolts provide +115 Ranged strength, making them tied with amethyst broad bolts for fourth strongest type of crossbow ammunition in the game, being surpassed by dragon bolts, onyx-tipped, and dragonstone-tipped rune bolts which provide +122, +120, and +117 respectively. They require a Ranged level of 61 to equip.

Runite bolts can be made by first smithing runite bolts (unf). This requires a Smithing level of 88 and a runite bar. Each bar will make 10 unfinished runite bolts and grant 75 Smithing experience. Attaching feathers to each bolt requires a Fletching level of 69, granting 10 Fletching experience per bolt. As with most bolts, they can be poisoned, however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips.

Unlike all other runite equipment in the game, runite bolts do not use the shorthand 'rune' in their name.
9145:
Silver bolts are ranged ammunition that can be fired from iron crossbows or better. They have a Ranged Strength bonus higher than blurite bolts but lower than iron bolts.

To produce silver bolts, players with at least 21 Crafting must use a silver bar on a furnace with a bolt mould in their inventory. This will return 10 unfeathered silver bolts and 50 Crafting experience. Attaching feathers to the bolts with 43 Fletching will complete them and grant the player 25 Fletching experience.

They are a type of silver weaponry and are one of the few ammo types able to be used to effectively kill Vampyre Juvinates.

A steel crossbow is a crossbow stronger than the iron crossbow but weaker than the mithril crossbow. It requires a Ranged level of 31 to wield, and can use bolts up to and including steel bolts. It has an attack range of 7 increased to 9 with longrange.

Steel crossbows can be made through the Fletching skill at level 46; a player must first cut a teak stock for the crossbow from teak logs, granting 27 Fletching experience. Then, a player must add steel limbs to the stock with a hammer in their inventory, granting 54 experience and making an unstrung steel crossbow. Finally, a player must string the crossbow with a crossbow string, granting 27 experience. Creating a steel crossbow from raw materials grants 108 Fletching experience in total.
9181:
A mithril crossbow is a crossbow that is stronger than the steel crossbow but weaker than the adamant crossbow. It requires a Ranged level of 36 to wield, and can fire bolts up to and including mithril bolts. It has an attack range of 7 increased to 9 with longrange.

Mithril crossbows can be made through the Fletching skill at level 54; a player must first cut a maple stock for the crossbow from maple logs, granting 32 Fletching experience. Then, a player must add mithril limbs to the stock with a hammer in their inventory, granting 64 experience and making an unstrung mithril crossbow. Finally, a player must string the crossbow with a crossbow string, granting 32 experience. Creating a mithril crossbow from raw materials grants 128 Fletching experience in total.
9183:
An adamant crossbow is a crossbow that is stronger than the mithril crossbow but weaker than the rune crossbow. It requires a Ranged level of 46 to wield, and can fire bolts up to and including adamant bolts. It has an attack range of 7 increased to 9 with longrange.

Adamant crossbows can be made through the Fletching skill at level 61; a player must first cut a mahogany stock for the crossbow from mahogany logs, granting 41 Fletching experience. Then, a player must add adamantite limbs to the stock with a hammer in their inventory, granting 82 experience and making an unstrung adamant crossbow. Finally, a player must string the crossbow with a crossbow string, granting 41 experience. Creating an adamant crossbow from raw materials grants 164 Fletching experience in total.
9185:
The rune crossbow is a crossbow that is stronger than the adamant crossbow but weaker than the dragon crossbow. It requires a Ranged level of 61 to wield, and can fire up to and including runite bolts. It is one-handed so it can be equipped alongside a shield, such as an anti-dragon shield or god book. It has an attack range of 7 increased to 9 with longrange.

Rune crossbows can be made through the Fletching skill at level 69; a player must first cut a yew stock for the crossbow from yew logs, granting 50 Fletching experience. Then, a player must add runite limbs to the stock with a hammer in their inventory, granting 100 experience and making an unstrung rune crossbow. Finally, a player must string the crossbow with a crossbow string, granting 50 experience. Creating a rune crossbow from raw materials grants 200 Fletching experience in total, and doing so within Witchaven and/or Yanille is a task for the elite Ardougne Diary.

Ironmen may obtain a rune crossbow by defeating the crazy archaeologist. The rune crossbow is commonly used among ironmen and low-level players for Slayer tasks, and for TzHaar Fight Cave, due to the ease of obtaining broad bolts and the ability to equip a shield. For Slayer tasks, a magic shortbow with rune or amethyst arrows is often a stronger weapon.

The rune crossbow is commonly used even for high-level content due to its ability to fire ruby and diamond bolts. The dragon, Armadyl, Zaryte, and dragon hunter crossbows are stronger alternatives.

Using a Shattered relics variety ornament kit on the crossbow will change its appearance into that of an rune crossbow (or).
9187:
Jade bolt tips are attached to the tips of blurite bolts or dragon bolts and can then be enchanted. Once jade bolt tips have been attached to the bolts, they become jade bolts and jade dragon bolts respectively.

Jade bolt tips can be created through the Fletching skill. A player must have a Fletching level of 26 and take a cut jade and use a chisel with it to make 12 jade bolt tips, granting 2 Fletching experience.

Attaching jade bolt tips to blurite bolts requires a Fletching level of 26, and for each jade bolt tip attached to a blurite bolt, a player is granted 2.4 Fletching experience. Attaching jade bolt tips to dragon bolts requires a Fletching level of 84, granting 2.4 Fletching experience per bolt.
9188:
Red topaz bolt tips are attached to the tips of steel and dragon bolts, which can then be enchanted. Once red topaz bolt tips have been attached to steel or dragon bolts, they become topaz bolts and topaz dragon bolts, respectively.

Red topaz bolt tips can be created through the Fletching skill. A player must have a Fletching level of 48 and take a cut red topaz and use a chisel with it to make 12 red topaz bolt tips. Attaching red topaz bolt tips to steel bolts also requires 48 Fletching, and gives 4 experience.
9190:
Emerald bolt tips are attached to the tips of mithril and dragon bolts, which can then be enchanted. Once emerald bolt tips have been attached to mithril or dragon bolts, they become emerald bolts and emerald dragon bolts, respectively.

Emerald bolt tips can be created through the Fletching skill. A player must have a Fletching level of 58 and take a cut emerald and use a chisel with it to make 12 Emerald bolt tips, giving 5.5 experience.
9192:
Diamond bolt tips can be attached to adamantite bolts or dragon bolts, and can then be enchanted. Once diamond bolt tips have been attached, the bolts become diamond bolts or diamond dragon bolts, respectively.

Diamond bolt tips can be created through the Fletching skill. A player must have a Fletching level of 65 and take a cut diamond and use a chisel with it to make 12 diamond bolt tips, giving 7 experience.
9193:
Dragonstone bolt tips are attached to the tips of runite and dragon bolts, which can then be enchanted. Once dragonstone bolt tips have been attached to runite or dragon bolts, they become dragonstone bolts and dragonstone dragon bolts, respectively.

Dragonstone bolt tips can be created through the Fletching skill. One must have 71 Fletching and take a cut dragonstone and use a chisel with it to make 12 dragonstone bolt tips, granting 8.2 Fletching experience per dragonstone. To avoid misclicking, players will receive a message to confirm cutting the dragonstone into bolt tips. There is a "Make - x" option for this, and it takes about 70 seconds per inventory of cut gems chiselled into tips.

Attaching dragonstone bolt tips to runite bolts to make dragonstone bolts also requires 71 Fletching, and gives 8.2 experience for each dragonstone bolt tip attached to a runite bolt.
9236: Enchanted Opal tipped Bronze Crossbow Bolts.
9238: Enchanted Pearl tipped Iron Crossbow Bolts.
9239: Topaz bolts (e) are steel bolts tipped with enchanted red topaz. Topaz bolts can be enchanted through the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Red Topaz) by a player with level 29 Magic. The spell enchants 10 red topaz bolts at a time.
9240: Enchanted Sapphire tipped Mithril Crossbow Bolts.
9241: Emerald bolts (e) are mithril bolts tipped with enchanted emerald. Emerald bolts can be enchanted through the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Emerald) by a player with level 27 Magic. The spell enchants 10 emerald bolts at a time. Like mithril and emerald bolts, firing them requires a mithril crossbow, or better.
9242: Enchanted Ruby tipped Adamantite Crossbow Bolts.
9243: Diamond bolts (e) are adamant bolts tipped with enchanted diamond. Diamond bolts can be enchanted by using the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Diamond) by a player with 57 Magic. The spell enchants 10 diamond bolts per cast and uses 2 law runes, 1 cosmic rune, and 10 earth runes.
9244: Dragonstone bolts (e) are runite bolts tipped with enchanted dragonstone. Dragonstone bolts can be enchanted through the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Dragonstone) by a player with level 68 Magic. The spell enchants 10 dragonstone bolts at a time. They require 61 Ranged to wield. Dragonstone bolts (e) can be purchased from Justine located at the Last Man Standing Minigame in Ferox Enclave, who sells 20 for 3 points.
9245: Enchanted Onyx tipped Runite Crossbow Bolts.
9287:
Iron bolts are the third-weakest bolts, stronger than blurite bolts. Iron bolts may be shot from iron or better crossbows. As with most bolts, they can be poisoned, however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips.

Iron bolts may be created by players. First, a player must smith unfinished iron bolts. This requires a Smithing level of 18, and for each iron bar a player smiths they will get 10 unfinished iron bolts and 25 Smithing experience. Then a player must attach flights to the bolts. Attaching flights to each bolt requires a Fletching level of 39 and 1 feather, granting 1.5 Fletching experience per bolt.

Iron bolts may be tipped with pearl. To tip the bolts with pearl, a player must have a Fletching level of 41 and use pearl bolt tips with the iron bolts, granting 3.2 Fletching experience for each pearl bolt tip attached and making the iron bolts into pearl bolts. Pearl bolts can then be enchanted; more information on enchanting them is available under pearl bolts.
9291:
Runite bolts (or rune bolts) are a type of crossbow ammo. They can be fired using a rune, dragon, dragon hunter, Armadyl, or Zaryte crossbow. Runite bolts provide +115 Ranged strength, making them tied with amethyst broad bolts for fourth strongest type of crossbow ammunition in the game, being surpassed by dragon bolts, onyx-tipped, and dragonstone-tipped rune bolts which provide +122, +120, and +117 respectively. They require a Ranged level of 61 to equip.

Runite bolts can be made by first smithing runite bolts (unf). This requires a Smithing level of 88 and a runite bar. Each bar will make 10 unfinished runite bolts and grant 75 Smithing experience. Attaching feathers to each bolt requires a Fletching level of 69, granting 10 Fletching experience per bolt. As with most bolts, they can be poisoned, however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips.

Unlike all other runite equipment in the game, runite bolts do not use the shorthand 'rune' in their name.
9292:
Silver bolts are ranged ammunition that can be fired from iron crossbows or better. They have a Ranged Strength bonus higher than blurite bolts but lower than iron bolts.

To produce silver bolts, players with at least 21 Crafting must use a silver bar on a furnace with a bolt mould in their inventory. This will return 10 unfeathered silver bolts and 50 Crafting experience. Attaching feathers to the bolts with 43 Fletching will complete them and grant the player 25 Fletching experience.

They are a type of silver weaponry and are one of the few ammo types able to be used to effectively kill Vampyre Juvinates.

9336:
Red topaz bolts are steel bolts tipped with red topaz bolt tips. Red topaz bolts can be created through the Fletching skill. A player must first have 48 Fletching and take a cut red topaz and use a chisel with it to make 12 red topaz bolt tips, granting 3.9 experience. Attaching red topaz bolt tips also requires 48 Fletching, and each red topaz bolt tip attached to a steel bolt gives 3.9 experience. Once the red topaz bolt tips have been attached, the steel bolts become red topaz bolts.

Red topaz bolts can be enchanted through the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Red Topaz) with level 29 Magic. The spell enchants 10 Red topaz bolts at a time, and once they are enchanted they become Topaz bolts (e) and gain a special ability.
9338:
Emerald bolts are mithril bolts tipped with emerald bolt tips, requiring level 36 Ranged to use.

Emerald bolts can be created through the Fletching skill. A player must first have a Fletching level of 58 and take a cut emerald and use a chisel with it to make 12 emerald bolt tips. The emerald bolt tips can then be attached to mithril bolts to make emerald bolts. Attaching 10 emerald bolt tips to 10 mithril bolts grants 55 Fletching experience. Note that these bolts require a crossbow of level 36 to fire.

Emerald bolts can be enchanted through the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Emerald) by a player with level 27 Magic. The spell enchants 10 emerald bolts at a time, and once they are enchanted they become emerald bolts (e) and gain a special ability.
9340:
Diamond bolts are adamant bolts tipped with diamond bolt tips. They are the fourth strongest gem tipped bolt in the game. These bolts can be created using the Fletching skill. 65 Fletching is required to make these bolts, and 7 Fletching experience is rewarded per bolt created.

Diamond bolts can be enchanted with the Enchant Crossbow Bolt spell, producing Diamond bolts (e). This requires 57 Magic. The spell enchants 10 bolts at a time.
9341:
Dragonstone bolts are runite bolts tipped with dragonstone. Dragonstone bolts can be created at level 71 Fletching skill by attaching dragonstone bolt tips to runite bolts. For every dragonstone bolt tip attached to a runite bolt, a player is granted 8.2 Fletching experience.

Players can enchant dragonstone bolts by using the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Dragonstone), producing dragonstone bolts (e). The spell itself requires a soul rune, cosmic rune, and 15 earth runes. The spell requires 68 Magic and enchants 10 dragonstone bolts at a time.
9377: Iron bolts (unf) are unfinished bolts made from using an iron bar on an anvil with a hammer, requiring 19 Smithing, yielding 10 iron bolts (unf) and 25 Smithing experience. Using a feather on one makes an iron bolt, requiring 39 Fletching, and yielding 1.5 Fletching experience per bolt.
9380:
Adamant bolts(unf) are unfinished bolts made from using an adamantite bar on an anvil with a hammer, requiring 73 Smithing, yielding 10 adamant bolts(unf) and 62.5 Smithing experience. Using a feather on one makes an adamant bolt, requiring 61 Fletching, and yielding 7 Fletching experience per bolt.

These are often made for training Smithing and Fletching due to high demand of adamant bolts, ruby bolts, and diamond bolts.
9381: Runite bolts (unf) are unfinished bolts made from using a runite bar on an anvil with a hammer, requiring 88 Smithing, yielding 10 runite bolts (unf) and 75 Smithing experience. Using a feather on one makes a runite bolt, requiring 69 Fletching, and yielding 10 Fletching experience per bolt.
9382: Silver bolts (unf) are unfinished bolts made from using a silver bar on a furnace with a bolt mould, requiring 21 Crafting, yielding 10 silver bolts (unf) and 50 Crafting experience. Using a feather on one makes a silver bolt, requiring 43 Fletching, and yielding 2.5 Fletching experience per bolt.
9418: A mithril grapple tipped bolt - needs a rope.
9419: A mithril grapple tipped bolt - needs a rope.
9420:
Bronze limbs are crossbow limbs made from a bronze bar, requiring 6 Smithing and yielding 12.5 Smithing experience.

Bronze limbs are attached to a wooden stock to make a bronze crossbow (u), requiring 9 Fletching and yielding 12 Fletching experience.
9423:
Iron limbs are crossbow limbs made from an iron bar, requiring 23 Smithing and yielding 25 Smithing experience.

Iron limbs are attached to a willow stock to make an iron crossbow (u), requiring 39 Fletching and yielding 44 Fletching experience.
9425: A pair of steel crossbow limbs.
9427: A pair of mithril crossbow limbs.
9429: A pair of adamantite crossbow limbs.
9431:
Runite limbs are crossbow limbs made from a runite bar, requiring 91 Smithing and yielding 75 Smithing experience.

Runite limbs are attached to a yew stock to make a runite crossbow (u), requiring 69 Fletching and yielding 100 Fletching experience.

Smithing runite limbs within Witchaven and/or Yanille is required for completing one of the elite Ardougne Diary tasks.
9434:
A bolt mould is an item that is used for making silver bolts through the Crafting skill. It can be purchased from the crafting stores in Rimmington, Al Kharid, or Civitas illa Fortis for 25 coins.

Crafting silver bolts with the bolt mould requires level 21 Crafting, provides 50 Crafting experience points per silver bar used, and produces ten silver bolts (unf) per bar.

This mould is not required for crafting any other unfinished bolts.
9436:
Sinew can be used on a spinning wheel by a member with 10 Crafting to create crossbow string, granting 15 Crafting experience. It is created through the Cooking skill, by using a piece of raw beef (not of the undead kind), raw boar meat, raw impaler meat, or raw bear meat with a range and choosing to make sinew, granting 3 Cooking experience.

Sinew can also be created by using a knife on a damaged monkey tail, requiring 10 Crafting.
9444: A willow stock is made by using a knife on willow logs, requiring 39 Fletching, and yielding 22 Fletching experience. Attaching iron limbs to it makes an iron crossbow (u), requiring 39 Fletching, and yielding 44 Fletching experience. A crossbow string can be attached to the unfinished crossbow to make an iron crossbow.
9450: A mahogany stock is made by using a knife on mahogany logs, requiring 61 Fletching, and yielding 41 Fletching experience. Attaching adamantite limbs to it makes an adamant crossbow (u), requiring 61 Fletching, and yielding 82 Fletching experience. A crossbow string can be attached to the unfinished crossbow to make an adamant crossbow.
9459: A steel crossbow (u) is made by using a teak stock with steel limbs, requiring 46 Fletching and yielding 54 Fletching experience. Attaching a crossbow string to it makes a steel crossbow, also requiring 46 Fletching and yielding an additional 27 Fletching experience.
9461: A mithril crossbow (u) is made by using a maple stock with mithril limbs, requiring 54 Fletching and yielding 64 Fletching experience. Attaching a crossbow string to it makes a mithril crossbow, also requiring 54 Fletching and yielding an additional 32 Fletching experience.
9463: An adamant crossbow (u) is made by using a mahogany stock with adamantite limbs, requiring 61 Fletching and yielding 82 Fletching experience. Attaching a crossbow string to it makes an adamant crossbow, also requiring 61 Fletching and yielding an additional 41 Fletching experience.
9465:
A runite crossbow (u) is made by using a yew stock with runite limbs, requiring 69 Fletching and yielding 100 Fletching experience.

Attaching a crossbow string to it makes a rune crossbow, also requiring 69 Fletching and yielding an additional 50 Fletching experience.

Making a runite crossbow (u) within Witchaven and/or Yanille is required for completing one of the elite Ardougne Diary tasks.
9469:
The grand seed pod is a single-use teleport item that can be obtained as a rare reward from Wingstone, Penwie, Brambickle, and Professor Manglethorp in the Gnome Restaurant minigame. Seed pods are stackable. They can take players to the Grand Tree, and have two right-click options: launch and squash.

Launching the seed pod will take players to the top floor of the Grand Tree, through Captain Lamdoo and a glider, but it can only be used outdoors. This option will also give the player 100 Farming experience. Squashing the seed will take players to the Grand Tree (to the ground floor by King Narnode Shareen) faster than Launching it, but the Farming experience will not be given, and will temporarily drain their Farming skill by 5 levels.

Unlike most teleports, which stop working above level 20 Wilderness, the Grand seed pod is among the few items whose teleports can still be used up to level 30 Wilderness.

The upgraded version of this item, the Royal seed pod, is obtained upon completion of Monkey Madness II, and has unlimited charges. It does not offer the Launch option and does not affect Farming (experience or level drain).

This item was once commonly used to lure players. Although scams involving this item have fallen out of favour, players should still exercise caution when the grand seed pod is involved. Most of these lures involve the victim dropping valuable items and then proceeding to Squash or Launch the pod.
9470: The gnome scarf is a possible reward from the Gnome Restaurant activity. Players have a 1/17 chance of receiving this from Captain Daerkin and Captain Ninto. The scarf has no stats, but it can function as warm clothing in Wintertodt reducing damage taken, and is the only tradeable neck slot item to do so. It is often used for fashion purposes.
9472:
Gnome goggles are a possible reward from the Gnome Restaurant minigame. Players have a 1/17 chance to obtain them as a reward from Captain Daerkin or Captain Ninto, which are accessible with hard deliveries. The gnome goggles are part of the gnome pilot set which also includes the gnome scarf.

Goggles can be combined with the Bomber cap from the Enlightened Journey quest by talking with Auguste, resulting in a Cap and goggles. As the cap and goggles can be stored, though not the goggles themselves, this provides a means of storing the goggles in the armour case (as part of the bomber jacket costume).
9629: As used by King Tyras' personal guard.
9634:
A Vyrewatch top is a piece of the Vyrewatch clothing set that can be bought from Trader Sven's Black Market Goods in Meiyerditch and reduce the chances of being spotted by the Vyrewatch patrols when worn.

In the quest, Sins of the Father, the Vyrewatch top is upgraded to the Vyre noble top by Polmafi Ferdygris
9636:

In the quest, Sins of the Father, the Vyrewatch legs are upgraded to the Vyre noble legs by Polmafi Ferdygris.

In the quest, Sins of the Father, the Vyrewatch shoes are upgraded to Vyre noble shoes by Polmafi Ferdygris.

A proselyte harness m can be obtained after completing the Slug Menace quest by buying it from Sir Tiffy Cashien in Falador. It may be opened to obtain Proselyte armour.

The set contains: Proselyte sallet, Proselyte hauberk, and the Proselyte cuisse.
9670:
A proselyte harness f can be obtained after completing the Slug Menace quest by buying it from Sir Tiffy Cashien in Falador. It may be opened to obtain proselyte armour.

The set contains: proselyte sallet, proselyte hauberk, and the proselyte tasset.
9672:
The proselyte sallet is a piece of Temple Knight Armour that requires 30 Defence, 20 Prayer, and completion of The Slug Menace quest to equip. It is only exceeded by the god mitres and sunfire fanatic helm in Prayer bonus for the helmet slot.

It has the exact same bonuses as an Adamant full helm, except that it offers +4 Prayer bonus. Like other Proselyte equipment, it is white with a dark-gold trim.

This piece of armour cannot be made using the Smithing skill. Although this armour is trimmed, it cannot be obtained from any Treasure Trail.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the proselyte armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
9674:
The proselyte hauberk is a piece of Temple Knight Armour that requires 30 Defence, 20 Prayer, and completion of The Slug Menace quest to equip. It shares the second highest Prayer bonus of any body slot equipment with the 3rd Age druidic robe top and the Elite black platebody, only beaten by the Sunfire fanatic cuirass. It has similar bonuses to those of an Adamant platebody with a +8 Prayer bonus, and is slightly lighter. Oddly enough, it does not stop Ava's devices from gathering arrows.

Like other Proselyte equipment, it is white with a dark-gold trim.

This piece of armour cannot be made using the Smithing skill. Although this armour is trimmed, it cannot be obtained from any Treasure Trail.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the proselyte armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
9676:
The proselyte cuisse is a piece of Temple Knight Armour that requires 30 Defence, 20 Prayer, and completion of The Slug Menace quest to equip. Along with its tasset counterpart, it is tied with the 3rd Age druidic robe bottoms and the Zealot's robe bottom for the second highest Prayer bonus of any leg slot equipment, beaten only by the Sunfire fanatic chausses.

It has the same bonuses as Adamant platelegs, except that it offers +6 Prayer bonus and weighs less. Like other Proselyte equipment, it is white with a dark-gold trim.

This piece of armour cannot be made using the Smithing skill. Although this armour is trimmed, it cannot be obtained from any Treasure Trail.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the proselyte armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
9678:

It has the exact same bonuses as an Adamant plateskirt, except that it offers +6 Prayer bonus and weighs less. Like other Proselyte equipment, it is white with a dark-gold trim.

This piece of armour cannot be made using the Smithing skill. Although this armour is trimmed, it cannot be obtained from any Treasure Trail.

9731:
A mind shield is an upgraded version of the elemental shield, offering an additional +3 magic defence bonus over the latter. It is made during and after the Elemental Workshop II quest in the elemental workshop dungeon.

Making the shield requires 30 Smithing, a primed mind bar, a hammer, and a slashed book in the inventory. Right-click the "Smith" option on a workbench in the elemental workshop to smith the shield, which grants the player 30 Smithing experience. Equipping a mind shield requires completion of Elemental Workshop II.

Warning: When attempting to smith a mind shield, having a beaten book, but no slashed book, will automatically create a mind helmet, not a mind shield.

A mind shield can be used as partial protection against the icy breath of skeletal wyverns and wyverns. When worn, it reduces the maximum damage of wyvern icy breath attacks to 10.
9733:
A mind helmet can be made during and after the Elemental Workshop II quest in the Elemental Workshop dungeon from a primed mind bar while having a beaten book in your inventory.

Creating a mind helmet is a medium achievement in the Kandarin Diary.
9735:
Goat horn is an item dropped by goats, billy goats, and Wyrmscraig goat.

A box trap is a type of trap used in the Hunter skill to catch ferrets, embertailed jerboas and chinchompas. Using a box trap requires the specific Hunter level needed for the prey, as well as partial completion of the Eagles' Peak quest.

Whenever prey passes a trap, it has a chance of either being caught in the trap or evading it. If the prey is successfully caught, the box trap will close in around the animal and start shaking, at which point the player will have the option to "check" the trap for loot and experience. If the prey evades the trap, the trap will simply close, at which point the player will have to reset it.

Box traps may be bought from Aleck's Hunter Emporium in Yanille, the Nardah Hunter Shop in Nardah, or Imia's Supplies in the Hunter Guild. One can also be obtained for free by searching the crate adjacent to the bookcases in the north-western house at Land's End. They can also be obtained from Hunter kits.

A snowy knight is a members-only item that is made by catching a snowy knight butterfly with a butterfly jar in their inventory. This requires level 35 Hunter using a (magic) butterfly net and gives 44 experience points. Players with level 45 Hunter can catch them barehanded. These butterflies can be found in Weiss, the Rellekka Hunter area, outside the Farming Guild, or on Mons Gratia.

Once caught, players can right-click "Release" the filled butterfly jar to restore 15 hitpoints. In a multi-combat zone, the item may be used on another player to provide the same healing to them and up to three players within a 5x5 area of the target. Players must have Accept Aid toggled on to receive the healing. The empty butterfly jar will remain in the inventory after use.

With a pestle and mortar, players can combine the jarred butterfly with raw hunter meat to create snowy knight mix (2). Unlike other hunter's mixes, the snowy knight mix has a reduced "per-use" effect than the jarred butterfly, but has a greater overall effect (restoring only 8 hitpoints per use, with a total of 16 across two doses).

A magic box is a type of trap used in the Hunter skill. The magic box trapping technique is used to catch imps. With 71 Hunter, the player may set up a magic box. When an imp passes the trap, it may be caught, but only when the player is not standing on the trap.

If the prey is successfully caught, the magic box will enclose the imp inside the box. Doing this creates an Imp-in-a-box, which can be used to bank 2 items or stacks of items, although it cannot be used while in combat or above level 30 Wilderness.

Adding bait (any bead) to a trap will increase the catch rate by +3%. It is not possible to smoke magic boxes, unlike other hunter traps, to increase the catch rate. Doing so yields the message, Imps steal so many human items, they're unlikely to be worried by human smells. Due to the low increase of the catch rate, as well as the impracticality and cost of bringing beads to bait the traps, it is generally considered not worth baiting the trap.

Magic boxes, as well as magic imp box packs containing 100 magic boxes, may be bought from Aleck's Hunter Emporium. in Yanille, the Nardah Hunter Shop. in Nardah, or Imia's Supplies in the Hunter Guild.

Having a magic box in your inventory prevents you from entering the Puro-Puro mini-game. Since magic boxes can be stored inside the Huntsman's kit, players can store the magic box before going inside the Puro-Puro mini-game. Players who attempt to activate the magic box within the mini-game will receive the message, You can't set up a trap here.

Chinchompas are one-handed, multi-target, stackable Ranged weapons requiring level 45 Ranged to wield. Chinchompas can be obtained by box trapping grey chinchompas in the Piscatoris Hunter area, the Kourend Woodland, or on the Isle of Souls. This requires 53 Hunter and completion of the Eagles' Peak quest, and will give the player 198.4 Hunter experience per catch. They have a catch rate of about 146/255 at 53 Hunter and a guaranteed chance to catch at 95 Hunter. To use chinchompas in combat, they must be wielded in the weapons slot. Chinchompas are thrown like darts or throwing knives; however, they explode on impact. In PvM, they can hit up to 11 targets in a 3x3 area. In PvP, the cap is 9 targets. They cannot be picked up again from the ground after being thrown, and Ava's device does not return them.

When throwing a chinchompa at a group, the accuracy roll is based on the targeted NPC. If you miss on this target, you will miss on all targets. If you hit on this target, you will hit on all targets. The damage rolls are done independently per target. The max hit for the targeted NPC is calculated normally, however the max hit used for the damage roll on the additional targets is the max hit for the initial target with the boosts from Salve and Avarice removed. The accuracy roll made on the initial target uses the 'heavy' ranged defence for determining the opponent's defence roll.

Fuses are used to describe the attack speed for throwing chinchompas. It is just another name for the conventional styles of ranged training.

Short fuse (accurate): 4 ticks

Medium fuse (rapid): 3 ticks

Long fuse (longrange): 4 ticks
10034:
Red chinchompas are one-handed multi-target stackable Ranged weapons requiring level 55 Ranged to wield. Red chinchompas can be obtained by box trapping carnivorous chinchompas, requiring 63 Hunter and completion of the Eagles' Peak quest.

To use chinchompas in combat, they must be wielded in the weapons slot. Red chinchompas are thrown like darts or throwing knives; however, they explode on impact. In PvM, they can hit up to 11 targets in a 3x3 area. In PvP, the cap is 9 targets. They cannot be picked up again from the ground after being thrown and Ava's device does not return them. In multiple target attacks, the chinchompa simply rolls at the target's defence values; if it hits, then all other nearby targets are also hit, regardless of their Defence level and ranged defence bonuses. If it misses, then none of the targets take damage. The accuracy roll made on the initial target uses the 'heavy' ranged defence for determining the opponent's defence roll.

Using red chinchompas is widely regarded as the second fastest way to train Ranged and Hitpoints; however, this method is very costly. Catching red chinchompas is also popular among high-level Hunters as it gives fast experience and is profitable.

Fuses are used to describe the attack speed for throwing chinchompas. It is just another name for the conventional styles of ranged training.

Short fuse (accurate): 4 ticks

Medium fuse (rapid): 3 ticks

Long fuse (longrange): 4 ticks

Gloves of silence are a pair of thieving gloves requiring 54 Hunter to wear. When worn, the gloves increase your success chance while pickpocketing by 5%, eventually breaking after 62 failed pickpockets.

To make the gloves, players must bring two unnoted Dark kebbit furs from the Piscatoris falconry area (level 57 Hunter) and 600 coins to the Fancy Clothes Store in Varrock, to Pellem in the Hunter Guild, or to Prifddinas' Seamstress. Before they break, the gloves can be repaired by using one dark kebbit fur on them, while having one spool of thread, a knife, and a needle in your inventory; repairing them requires level 64 Crafting but does not grant any experience.

After completing the medium Ardougne diaries, the gloves become ineffective when used in Ardougne and will not degrade, as the 10% increased chance of success the diary provides is higher than that of the gloves and both bonuses do not stack. Upon completion of the hard Ardougne diaries, this extends to the rest of Gielinor and the gloves become completely obsolete. This effect does not require an Ardougne cloak of any tier to be worn.

Players with access to rogue equipment (minimum of 50 Agility and 50 Thieving to obtain) may choose to forgo using the gloves of silence, as wearing the full rogue set guarantees double rewards for pickpocketing. If wearing the gloves instead of the Rogue gloves with the rest of the rogue set, you instead have a 60% chance to double pickpocketing loot (since you lose both the 15% chance from the gloves and the 25% full set bonus), and therefore receive ~20% less loot, while gaining more XP per hour due to less failures. Due to stun timers on failed pickpocketing being longer than the action of pickpocketing itself, the 5% increased success rate results in 7-25% increased XP rates from pickpocketing, depending on base pickpocketing chance.

Polished buttons are obtained by polishing regular buttons. When polished, one receives 5 Crafting experience.

One may get the buttons by pickpocketing H.A.M. members, digging in the Level-1 or Level-3 digsite east of Varrock, opening Ogre coffins, or by inspecting the Port Khazard trawler net after participating in the Fishing Trawler.

They are used in the Animal Magnetism quest.
10564:
The granite body is a piece of body armour that requires 50 Defence and 50 Strength to wear. Players who have killed the Penance Queen can purchase it from Commander Connad, located on the ground floor of the Barbarian Outpost, for 95,000 coins. It is the only reward from the Barbarian Assault minigame that is not obtained with honour points.

The granite body is the most commonly used piece of the granite armour set, being similar in price to the rune platebody while providing better defensive bonuses. While the granite helm and granite boots similarly outclass their rune counterparts, the latter is significantly more expensive and the former competes with the more common Fremennik helmets.

Even though it is seen as low-level armour, the granite body has slightly higher defensive bonuses than the Fighter torso, except the slash defence, which is 1 lower. However, the granite body's lack of a strength bonus means the fighter torso is more commonly used for slayer tasks and general melee training, where maximizing one's damage output outweighs defensive bonuses. Compared to the dragon chainbody, the granite body provides better range defence and stab defence but is weaker by 9 and 19 points in slash and crush respectively. The granite body does not interfere with Ava's devices, this combined with its modest ranged penalty can make it a decent choice for Range Tank in PvM.

Purchasing and equipping a granite body is a requirement for the hard Kandarin diary. It must be purchased from Commander Connad to meet the requirement for the task, requiring the player kill the Penance Queen at least once.
10589:
Granite helm is a helmet that can be obtained by killing terror dogs or from High Level Gambles at Barbarian Assault. 50 Strength and 50 Defence are required to equip the helm. It has slightly better stats than the rune full helm but slightly worse stats than the dragon med helm.

The granite helm has superior ranged defensive stats compared to rune and dragon (but inferior to the dragon full helm). This also applies to other pieces of granite equipment.

10812:
Split logs are made from arctic pine logs when they are used on a woodcutting stump. The logs require level 56 Woodcutting to split, giving 5 Woodcutting experience per log split, or 140 per inventory. Players wearing Lumberjack clothing will receive the appropriate bonus experience. It takes 50 seconds to convert an entire inventory of arctic pine logs to split logs.

Split logs are used to repair the bridges in the quest The Fremennik Isles. Apart from training Woodcutting, they have no other use.

Hair is a drop obtained by killing yaks outside the village of Neitiznot. Players can use it on a spinning wheel to make rope using the Crafting skill. Making a rope requires level 30 Crafting and grants 25 Crafting experience.

The players who paid Vanligga Gastfrihet's taxes during or after The Fremennik Isles can buy them from her shop (located north of the longhall in Jatizso) for a price starting at 2 coins each with a stock of 50. She is very close to a bank, so purchasing hair from her is a faster method of obtaining than killing yaks.

It can be obtained by killing a Yak on Neitiznot or by trading with the shop Contraband yak produce on Jatizso. The shop is convenient due to its proximity to a bank.

Yak-hides are a 100% drop from yaks. They can be cured for 5 coins by Thakkrad Sigmundson on Neitiznot. Cured yak-hide can be crafted into yak-hide legs and yak-hide bodies with the use of a needle and thread.

After partially completing The Fremennik Isles quest, players can also buy yak-hides from Contraband yak produce in central Jatizso.

Cured yak-hides are obtained by taking a yak-hide to Thakkrad Sigmundson on Neitiznot and paying him 5 coins to cure it. They can also be bought from the Contraband yak produce store on Jatizso starting at 110 coins each.

Cured yak-hides can be crafted into yak-hide legs and yak-hide bodies with the use of a needle and thread. Yak-hide legs require one cured yak-hide and 43 Crafting, while yak-hide bodies require two cured yak-hides and 46 Crafting. 10824:

Yak-hide armour counts as warm clothing for the Wintertodt.

Frog-leather chaps are a piece of frog-leather armour that can be bought from Reldak's Leather Armour in the market place of Dorgesh-Kaan. It can also be looted from the Dorgesh-Kaan average chests, specifically from the chests in Zanik's house, which require 52 Thieving to unlock. Frog-leather armour cannot be created through the Crafting skill.

Wearing the chaps requires level 25 in Defence and Ranged. Despite having lower requirements to equip, studded chaps have better stats than frog-leather chaps.
10958: Boots made out of frog hide.
10973:
Light orbs can be used to fix magical lamps in Dorgesh-Kaan. Level 52 Crafting and Firemaking is needed to fix a lamp, giving 500 Crafting experience and 500 Firemaking experience. When a player has replaced 50 light orbs they will receive the message "You have replaced 50 orbs and have gained extra experience." The bonus received is 2,500 Crafting and Firemaking experience. This can be repeated indefinitely.

Broken lamps are found on all three floors. The large street lamps throughout Dorgesh-Kaan never need replacing. Broken lamps can be hard to distinguish from a distance. There are always ten broken lamps, and once one is fixed, a new one will break. Broken lamps are unique to each player and are the same for the player no matter what world the player is on.

In addition to attaching cave goblin wire to empty light orbs via the Crafting skill (requires 87 Crafting, granting 104 experience), complete light orbs are sometimes obtained from Dorgesh-Kaan Average Chests, specifically from the chest on the 2nd floor in Oldak's house. Empty orbs are obtained by looting a chest only slightly more frequently than completed light orbs.

A light orb is needed for a Sherlock elite clue scroll step, and one must be crafted for a master clue scroll.
10978:
Swamp weed is a plant dropped by two Slayer monsters, Cave bugs and Molanisks, in the Dorgesh-Kaan South Dungeon. One of the uses is to cook it on a range for soda ash. Players can also catch it with a net while fishing for Frog spawn in Lumbridge Swamp Caves, giving 1 experience point. Swamp weeds are not stackable.

Swamp weed is also used by the Dorgeshuun cave goblins as a common cooking ingredient, as it is one of the few green plants that grow in or near Dorgesh-Kaan. An example of this can be seen in eel sushi, in which swamp weed is wrapped around raw cave eel or raw slimy eel.
10999: The goblin book is an item that is an uncommon drop from goblins. After completing the Another Slice of H.A.M. quest, members can re-obtain it from the bookcase in their player-owned houses, under the name The Book of the Big High War God.
11037:
The brine sabre is a one-handed weapon that requires 40 Attack to wield. It is dropped by brine rats in the small cave accessed during Olaf's Quest. The brine sabre is a slightly better alternative to a rune scimitar, boasting 2 higher strength and slash attack bonuses when compared to the former. However, it is significantly more expensive due to the fact it is only dropped by the rarely-killed brine rat at a low rate.

Brine sabres can finish off rockslugs without the use of a bag of salt. It is also one of the few weapons that can be used to kill lobstrosities.

It can also be obtained in your house if you have a tool store 4 in your workshop.

A bracelet of clay allows players to mine soft clay instead of hard clay. It is made by enchanting a sapphire bracelet with the Lvl-1 Enchant spell.

A single bracelet can mine 28 soft clay, after which it disintegrates. The player can check how many more soft clay it can mine by equipping it and then right-clicking "check." The number of charges is stored per player, not per bracelet, so equipping another bracelet will not reset the number of charges a player has.

The bracelet can be useful for making magic tablets in a player-owned house, as the Rimmington and Hosidius mines both contain clay and are very close to a house portal.

When mining soft clay rocks in the Trahaearn mine, the bracelet of clay allows players to mine two soft clay at once.

An emerald bracelet can be enchanted into a Castle wars bracelet using the Lvl-2 Enchant spell by players with level 27 Magic, granting 37 experience.

Dragonstone bracelet is a piece of jewellery crafted by using a gold bar and a dragonstone at a furnace with a bracelet mould in their inventory at level 74 Crafting, giving 110 Crafting experience. It is wielded in the hand slot of the player.

It can be enchanted at level 68 Magic into a combat bracelet.
11118:
The combat bracelet is a dragonstone bracelet that has been enchanted by the Lvl-5 Enchant spell.

A combat bracelet can be recharged at the totem pole in the Legends' Guild, or at the Fountain of Uhld in the Myths' Guild, or by casting Recharge Dragonstone, giving it four charges. Players who have completed Legends' Quest can also recharge it at the Fountain of Rune, giving it six charges.

The bracelet provides useful teleports to combat-related guilds. The bracelet also informs its wearer of their current Slayer task count every 10 kills (i.e. "You still need to kill x0 monsters to complete your current Slayer assignment"). This feature only works if the bracelet is charged.

Like other dragonstone jewellery, it is one of the few items whose teleports will work up to level 30 Wilderness, while most other means of teleportation will not work above level 20 Wilderness.

The bracelet also provides combat bonuses comparable to those of mithril gloves from the Culinaromancer's Chest. Compared to mithril gloves, the bracelet has +1 attack bonuses and -1 defensive bonuses in all attack styles except magic.

The berserker necklace is an onyx necklace enchanted by the Lvl-6 Enchant spell. When worn, it increases the amount of damage the wearer does when wielding an obsidian melee weapon (Toktz-xil-ak, Tzhaar-ket-om, Tzhaar-ket-em, or Toktz-xil-ek) by 20%. However, in exchange it lowers the wearer's melee accuracy and the player's defences against all combat styles. This bonus stacks with the bonus provided from wearing the Obsidian armour set (helmet, platebody, and platelegs). It also stacks with slayer helmet and Void Knight equipment.

Players can attach a Berserker necklace ornament kit, obtained from hard Treasure Trails, to create a Berserker necklace (or). This is only cosmetic, and does not affect the necklace's stat bonuses. It can be dismantled, returning the necklace and ornament kit.
11130: Yep, this is most definitely valuable!
11133:
The regen bracelet is an enchanted bracelet that is worn in the hand slot. It is created by casting Lvl-6 Enchant on an onyx bracelet, requiring level 87 Magic and granting 97 Magic experience.

When worn, it doubles the player's natural Hitpoints regeneration amount, healing 2 Hitpoints per minute instead of the standard 1 Hitpoint per minute. The effect of the regen bracelet stacks with either the Rapid Heal prayer or with the Hitpoints cape (which do not stack with each other); using either of these in conjunction with a regen bracelet effectively quadruples the natural rate of Hitpoint regeneration, increasing it to 2 Hitpoints per 30 seconds. This is a very helpful perk during activities that deal low amounts of continuous damage, reducing the need to bank frequently or rely on outside sources of healing. Examples of activities where it is helpful include fighting weak but accurate NPCs, doing Pyramid Plunder, subduing the Wintertodt (doubles warmth regeneration), chopping Sulliusceps, mining in the Volcanic Mine, or fighting Zalcano.

In addition, the offensive and defensive bonuses provided by the bracelet are better than those of the combat bracelet and mithril gloves. This, combined with the fact that it has no requirements to equip, makes it the best-in-slot melee hand slot item for players with 1 Defence.

A baby impling jar is the result of successfully catching a baby impling, while also having an empty impling jar. Baby impling jars are not that commonly looted because of the low value of the loot. Instead, the jar can be traded in singularly to Elnock Inquisitor for 3 empty impling jars. This allows the player to collect 3 more higher level implings for them to loot.

You can trade 3 of this jar, along with two young impling jars and one gourmet impling jar to Elnock for a vial of imp repellent.
11240: A young impling in a jar. Don't trap me, man.
