A gourmet impling jar is the result of successfully catching a Gourmet impling, while also having an empty impling jar. It requires 28 Hunter to catch a gourmet impling.

This jar can be traded in singularly to Elnock Inquisitor for 3 empty impling jars.

One gourmet impling jar, along with three baby impling jars and two young impling jars, can be traded to Elnock for a vial of Imp repellent. Alternatively, three gourmet impling jars, along with two earth impling jars and one essence impling jar, can be traded for a magic butterfly net.
11244:
An earth impling jar is the result of successfully catching an Earth impling while having an empty impling jar. It requires 36 Hunter to catch an earth impling.

This jar can be traded in individually to Elnock Inquisitor for 3 empty impling jars.

Players can also trade Elnock two Earth impling jars along with three Gourmet impling jars and one Essence impling jar for a magic butterfly net.
11246:
An essence impling jar is the result of successfully catching an essence impling, while also having an empty impling jar. It requires 42 Hunter to catch an essence impling.

This jar can be traded in singularly to Elnock Inquisitor for 3 empty impling jars.

One essence impling jar of this jar, along with three gourmet impling jars and two earth impling jars, can be traded to Elnock for a magic butterfly net. Alternatively, players can trade three of this jar, two eclectic impling jars and one nature impling jar for a jar generator.
11248:
An eclectic impling jar is the result of successfully catching an eclectic impling in the Impetuous Impulses minigame.

This jar can be traded in singularly to Elnock Inquisitor for 3 empty impling jars, but this is not recommended due to its high value.

You can trade two of this jar, three essence impling jars and one nature impling jar for a jar generator.
11256:
The dragon impling jar is the result of successfully catching a dragon impling, requiring level 83 Hunter. The dragon impling is second only to the Lucky impling as the rarest and most difficult to catch impling in Impetuous Impulses.

As can be done with all impling jars, the dragon impling jar can be traded in singularly to Elnock Inquisitor for three empty impling jars. This is not recommended, due to the fact that dragon impling jars are worth vastly more than three empty jars.

The market value of dragon impling jars is considerably more than all but a few of the possible loot items from it, notably dragon darts or dragon dart tips. Their price is high due to the chance of said expensive items, the rarity of the dragon impling itself, as well as players opening dragon impling jars for elite clue scrolls. Clue hunters will buy implings in bulk for the ability to obtain clues faster than any other method in the game for a high cost. You can't take dragon impling jars onto Entrana, as looting them may give you weapons.

11284:
A dragonfire shield is an upgraded anti-dragon shield, and one of the best shields in the game behind the elysian spirit shield and Dinh's bulwark. Equipping it requires 75 Defence and having started Dragon Slayer I. It retains the same dragonfire protection as the anti-dragon shield and it also provides partial protection against the icy breath of wyverns, like the dragonfire ward, elemental shield, and mind shield.

When uncharged, it is tradeable and offers slightly more defensive bonuses than a mithril sq shield, however, each charge it gains increases melee defensive bonuses and the range defensive bonus by 1 for a total of +50 at maximum for those four defensive stats. To charge the shield, dragonfire needs to be absorbed from dragonfire or icy breath attacks while it is equipped. Bottled dragonbreath can also be used to charge the shield.
11286:
The draconic visage is a very rare item obtained from many high-levelled dragons, as well as Skeletal Wyverns. It was supposedly created by the Dragonkin as a way to channel dragonfire.

Players with 90 Smithing (can be boosted) can combine an anti-dragon shield with a draconic visage at an anvil to create a dragonfire shield. Doing so grants 2,000 Smithing experience. If the player doesn't have the required Smithing level, they can take the draconic visage to Oziach in Edgeville, who will assist in creating the shield for a payment of 1,250,000 coins. Completion of the quest Dragon Slayer I is required for Oziach to make the shield.

The following dragons or wyverns do NOT drop the draconic visage: baby dragons, green dragons, blue dragons, red dragons, brutal green dragons, bronze dragons, revenant dragons, Fossil Island wyverns and quest bosses like Elvarg and Galvek. For a list of dragons that do drop the draconic visage, see the 'item sources' section.

Roe is a food and ingredient used in the Barbarian Herblore to make Barbarian mixes. It can be obtained by using a knife to cut open Leaping salmon and Leaping trout, which are caught through Barbarian fishing with the Barbarian rod. The chance of receiving roe will scale with Cooking level, and depends on which fish is being cut.

Roe can be used with the respective two dose potions to make Attack mix, Strength mix, Restore mix, Antipoison mix, and Relicym's mix. All other Barbarian mixes require caviar as the additional ingredient. Roe can also be eaten to restore 3 hitpoints or used as bait to catch more fish while Barbarian fishing.

Players training fishing can either deposit the roe at a nearby bank such as the Bank Chest at Barbarian Assault for later use, or use the roe along with the fish offcuts as baits for more Barbarian fishing. Roe is only used as bait when there are no other fishing bait types or offcuts in the inventory.

11785:
The Armadyl crossbow is a ranging weapon that requires a Ranged level of 70 to wield, and can fire up to and including dragon bolts. It is dropped only by Commander Zilyana. This item counts as an Armadyl item in the God Wars Dungeon.

The crossbow has an attack range of 8, and the longrange combat style will increase it by 2.

The Armadyl crossbow can be combined with a nihil horn and 250 nihil shards to create the Zaryte crossbow.
11789:
The mystic steam staff is an elemental staff requiring 40 Attack and 40 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of water and fire runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

This staff can be created after the completion of the quest Scorpion Catcher by taking a steam battlestaff and 40,000 to Thormac. After completion of the Hard Kandarin Diary and Elite Kandarin Diary, Thormac will only require 30,000 or 20,000 respectively.

It can also be obtained through other players and bought on the Grand Exchange.

Players can use a steam staff upgrade kit, obtained from Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing, to cosmetically enhance their mystic steam staff, creating a mystic steam staff (or). This only alters its appearance, and it becomes untradeable. It can be reverted, but the kit will not be retained.
11791:
The staff of the dead is a one-handed bladed staff that requires 75 Magic and 75 Attack to wield. It is dropped by K'ril Tsutsaroth, and counts as a Zamorakian item while in the God Wars Dungeon and in the desert Bandit Camp. It is one of several one-handed staves which boost magic damage by 15%.

When a combat spell is cast with the staff, there is a 1/7 (~14.2%) chance that the staff will negate the rune cost for that spell.

The staff can autocast Flames of Zamorak, Crumble Undead, Magic Dart, elemental combat spells from the Standard spellbook, and combat spells from the Arceuus spellbook. It is not, however, able to autocast ancient magicks.

Being a bladed staff, it is notable for its offensive melee stats, which are unusually high for a Magic weapon. Its stats slightly surpass that of a dragon scimitar while having the same attack speed when using melee. However, when using magic spells, it offers an attack speed of 5.

The staff may be upgraded into the toxic staff of the dead, the staff of light, or the staff of balance.

The Armadyl helmet is an item that can be obtained from Kree'arra and his bodyguards in the God Wars Dungeon, or as an extremely rare drop from an Armadylean/Bandosian guard from elite coordinate clues. Along with the Armadyl chestplate and chainskirt, it is part of the Armadyl armour set, and requires 70 Defence and Ranged to wear.

The helmet has the second highest ranged attack bonus of any item in the headwear slot behind the Masori mask, however, it penalises both melee and mage attack bonuses and lacks any ranged strength bonuses which makes the helm somewhat undesirable.

The Bandos chestplate provides a +4 Strength bonus, and more defensive bonuses than comparable body armours such as the fighter torso and inquisitor's hauberk. Despite seemingly being made of metal, the Bandos chestplate does not interfere with Ava's devices.

Dragon boots are melee footwear requiring 60 Defence to wear. Like most other dragon items, they cannot be made using the Smithing skill.

Dragon boots offer the third-highest strength bonus of any boots in the game, while also offering some of the best defensive stats available for the feet slot. Coupled with their affordable price, they are popular among players for all melee combat purposes, even after all other Dragon armour being used has been replaced.

Broad arrowheads are made into broad arrows when used with headless arrows, requiring 52 Fletching and broader fletching to be unlocked with 300 Slayer reward points from Slayer masters, yielding 150 experience per 15 arrows.

Broad arrows are used in Slayer to kill Kurasks and Turoths. They are more powerful than mithril arrows and slightly less powerful than adamant arrows, but are untradeable.

They are purchased for 55 at all slayer equipment shops from any Slayer master. They can also be purchased in bulk as broad arrowhead packs.
11875:
Broad bolts (or broad-tipped bolts) are bolts used for a crossbow. They provide the same ranged strength as adamant bolts (+100). Players can buy a set of 250 for 35 Slayer reward points from any Slayer master. Broad bolts, or their arrow equivalents, are required by players who intend to slay Turoth or Kurasks using Ranged.

Broad bolts require 55 Slayer and 61 Ranged to equip. They can be fired only by a rune crossbow, dragon hunter crossbow, dragon crossbow, Armadyl crossbow, or Zaryte crossbow.

Players with 55 Fletching and who have unlocked the "Broader fletching" ability for 300 Slayer reward points can make broad bolts by adding feathers to unfinished broad bolts, which are purchased from any Slayer master for coins. Broad bolts are fletched 10 at a time and give 3 Fletching experience per bolt, or 30 experience per set of 10 bolts made.

Players with 76 Fletching can create amethyst broad bolts by adding amethyst bolt tips to ordinary broad bolts. This also requires having unlocked "Broader Fletching" through a Slayer master. Doing this will give 10.6 Fletching experience per bolt, or 106 experience per set of 10 bolts made.

Fletching broad bolts is a common method of training Fletching for Ironman players, as unfinished broad bolts can be purchased in bulk.

In terms of stats, the ward provides melee defence identical to that of a dragon square shield but provides a moderate amount of Magic defence instead of providing Ranged defence. The shield carries a substantial Magic attack bonus but negative melee and Ranged attack bonuses. Because of this the shield is ideal for mages, but unsuitable for other combat. The shield also has a Magic damage bonus of 2%.

A raw dark crab is a members-only fish found in the Wilderness. Dark crabs require a Fishing level of at least 85 and give 130 Fishing experience per catch. A lobster pot is used to catch dark crabs, along with dark fishing bait. Dark fishing bait can be obtained as a drop from various monsters in the Wilderness or bought from other players at the Grand Exchange.

They require a Cooking level of at least 90 to cook and give 215 Cooking experience per fish. It is advised to cook raw dark crabs at the Hosidius Kitchen due to their high burn rate, as they are still possible to burn even at 99 Cooking. Alternatively, wearing a Cooking cape will ensure 100% cook-success rate due to its perk.

Completion of the Elite Wilderness Diary greatly increases the catch rate of these fish, from 16% to 34% at 99 Fishing -- a 112.5% increase, more than doubling the base rate. As such, it is highly recommended that players complete the Elite diary prior to fishing dark crabs. If staying in the area for extended trips, these fish and any other items can be turned into banknotes using Piles in the Resource Area for a fee of 50 coins per item.

Dark Crab fishing spots in the Resource Area are some of the few fishing spots in Gielinor that do not relocate and can be fished in perpetuity, encouraging low-effort skill training. However, this method of training is ill-advised, as player killers may enter the Resource Area to catch fishers off-guard. If a player utilizes the Fishing Barrel and it is kept on death, any fish stored in the barrel will be kept. Players also may utilize the Looting Bag to store their raw or cooked crabs for very low risk and doubling their inventory without utilizing Piles, where both the bag and crabs within will be consumed if the player is killed.

The combat bracelet is a dragonstone bracelet that has been enchanted by the Lvl-5 Enchant spell.

A combat bracelet can be recharged at the totem pole in the Legends' Guild, or at the Fountain of Uhld in the Myths' Guild, or by casting Recharge Dragonstone, giving it four charges. Players who have completed Legends' Quest can also recharge it at the Fountain of Rune, giving it six charges.

The bracelet provides useful teleports to combat-related guilds. The bracelet also informs its wearer of their current Slayer task count every 10 kills (i.e. "You still need to kill x0 monsters to complete your current Slayer assignment"). This feature only works if the bracelet is charged.

Like other dragonstone jewellery, it is one of the few items whose teleports will work up to level 30 Wilderness, while most other means of teleportation will not work above level 20 Wilderness.

The bracelet also provides combat bonuses comparable to those of mithril gloves from the Culinaromancer's Chest. Compared to mithril gloves, the bracelet has +1 attack bonuses and -1 defensive bonuses in all attack styles except magic.

The mystic smoke staff is an elemental staff requiring 40 Attack and 40 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of air and fire runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

Like the smoke battlestaff, it provides a 10% increase in accuracy and damage when casting spells from the standard spellbook; this bonus also applies to curse spells.

The occult necklace is a magical amulet that requires 70 Magic to wear. It is dropped by the smoke devil and its boss variant. Wearing it increases the player's Magic damage by 5%, and is the only amulet to give such a bonus. This 5% bonus will also stack with existing boosts, such as the staff of the dead and the imbued slayer helmet. The salve amulet(ei) does not apply its damage bonus to other hit targets when barraging. The 3rd Age amulet possess slightly higher magic accuracy but lacks magic strength. Thus, aside from using single target magic damage against undead mobs, or in situations where landing a single spell is pivotal, it is the best neck slot item for magic damage output.

A combination of the occult necklace and staff of the dead while using Ice Barrage would increase a player's max hit to 36, from an original maximum of 30. The max hit increases to 40 if using a black mask (i) or slayer helmet (i) on a Slayer task.

Players can attach an occult ornament kit, obtained from master clue scrolls, to cosmetically enhance the necklace, creating an occult necklace (or). This only alters its appearance, and gives no stat enhancements. It can be dismantled, returning the necklace and ornament kit.

Amylase crystals are a potion secondary ingredient used in the creation of stamina potions. A player can mix amylase crystals with a super energy potion at 77 Herblore to make a stamina potion. One amylase crystal creates a single dose of stamina potion from a super energy(1), and as such, four amylase crystals are required to create a stamina potion(4) from a super energy(4). One crystal is required per dose, granting 25.5 Herblore experience each. Amylase crystals can be bought from Grace found in the Rogues' Den, Worm Tongue at the Colossal Wyrm Remains, and Pirate Jackie the Fruit found in the Agility Arena Store in the form of an amylase pack. One amylase pack contains 100 amylase crystals, costs 10 marks of grace, 60 Brimhaven vouchers, or 100 Termites, and can create 25 stamina potion(4).

An Amulet of chemistry or Alchemist's amulet can be used (provided the super energy potion is less than 4 doses; see Amulet of chemistry#Mechanics).

The Ghorrock teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to the Frozen Waste Plateau in level 45 Wilderness, provided that they have completed Desert Treasure I.

Because this tablet teleports players to the Wilderness, a warning will appear upon clicking the "Break" option on the tablet. This can be toggled by right-clicking the "Configure" option.

Players can create this item on the ancient lectern by the altar inside the Ancient Pyramid with a piece of soft clay, 2 law runes, and 8 water runes, as well as level 96 Magic while being on the Ancient Magicks spellbook.

The player does not need to have the relevant Magic level to use the tablet, which shares the same rule with all tablets and the player will not receive any experience, although making the teleport tablet does give 106 experience in Magic.

The Senntisten teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to the Digsite Exam Centre, providing that they have completed Desert Treasure I.

Players can create this item on the ancient lectern by the altar inside the Ancient Pyramid with a piece of soft clay, 2 law runes, and 1 soul rune, as well as level 60 Magic while being on the Ancient Magicks spellbook.

The player does not need to have the relevant Magic level to use the tablet, which shares the same rule with all tablets and the player will not receive any experience, although making the teleport tablet does give 70 experience in Magic.

The magic shortbow scroll is an item that can be used on a magic shortbow to create a magic shortbow (i), which will make its special attack consume 50% of the player's special attack energy down from 55% and increase its ranged attack bonus to +75 from +69.

The scroll can be purchased from Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 5 Last Man Standing points, or obtained as a rare drop from monsters in the Wilderness Slayer Cave.

After being imbued by the magic shortbow scroll, the bow cannot be reverted, and there's no way to reclaim the scroll. On death, players who lose the magic shortbow (i) will drop a regular magic shortbow for the person who killed them.
12789:
A clue box, when held in the inventory, allows a player to keep a single clue scroll, scroll box, or reward casket in their inventory after dying in the Wilderness, at which point the clue box is deleted. The clue/casket protected is in addition to whichever protected items would normally stay in the inventory. Clue boxes do not protect clues for Ultimate Ironman players.

Following the Trouver System Rework, untradeable items like clues and caskets go to the grave where they can be reclaimed for free, so the clue box is all but obsolete, saving only a trip to the grave or to Death's Office.

Clue boxes can be purchased from Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 5 Last Man Standing points, though considering the other items on offer at that price, it is seldom advisable to do so.

Only the bottom-rightmost scroll/casket in one's inventory is protected; carrying multiple clue boxes does not produce additional effects. The Items Kept on Death interface does not distinguish the scroll/casket a clue box would protect, though it does indicate that the box would always be lost.

It is recommended to avoid opening a reward casket in the Wilderness while holding a clue box, as the clue box will still be lost on death along with any non-protected items gained from opening the casket.

Saradomin's tear is a crystalised tear that is said to have been shed by Saradomin himself, created when he wept over the wounds of Commander Zilyana, who became seriously injured in the Battle of Annakarl during the God Wars.

It can be purchased from Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 150 Last Man Standing points.

When attached to a Saradomin sword, it creates Saradomin's blessed sword, which adds +18 to slash attack and +6 to strength bonus. 75 Attack is required to wield Saradomin's blessed sword. Like the abyssal tentacle, it will consume the Saradomin sword after it has dealt 10,000 hits, leaving players with Saradomin's tear upon fully degrading.

When using the items on each other, there will be a warning message that states A blessed Saradomin sword is untradeable, with an Attack requirement of 75. After 10,000 hits, the sword crumbles to dust, and you get the Tear back.
12817:
The elysian spirit shield requires 75 Defence and 75 Prayer to wield.

It is made by attaching an elysian sigil, a rare drop from the Corporeal Beast, to a blessed spirit shield using a hammer at an anvil; this process requires 90 Prayer and 85 Smithing. Players without the required skill levels to create the shield may ask Abbot Langley in the Edgeville Monastery to combine the sigil and the blessed spirit shield, for a fee of 1,500,000 coins.

This shield has superior Melee and Ranged defence bonuses compared to the arcane and spectral spirit shields, as well as a powerful passive effect. It has the highest crush defence in the shield slot. In terms of mitigating damage taken, the elysian spirit shield is one of the most powerful shields in Old School RuneScape.
12819: The elysian sigil can be attached to a blessed spirit shield to make an elysian spirit shield. To attach the sigil to the blessed spirit shield, players need 90 Prayer and 85 Smithing. It is a very rare drop from the Corporeal Beast. Players without the required skill levels to create the shield may ask Abbot Langley in the Edgeville Monastery to combine the sigil and the blessed spirit shield, for a fee of 1,500,000 coins.
12821: An ethereal shield with a spectral sigil attached to it.
12823: A sigil in the shape of a spectral symbol.
12825:
The arcane spirit shield requires 75 Defence, 65 Magic and 70 Prayer to wield.

It is made by attaching an arcane sigil, a rare drop from the Corporeal Beast, to a blessed spirit shield using a hammer at an anvil; this process requires 90 Prayer and 85 Smithing. Players without the required skill levels to create the shield may ask Abbot Langley in the Edgeville Monastery to combine the sigil and the blessed spirit shield, for a fee of 1,500,000 coins.

Abbot Langley can also remove the sigil from the shield, though this destroys the blessed spirit shield; this is usually done in order to use the sigil to fortify Elidinis' ward into an Elidinis' ward (f).

The shield's defensive bonuses are identical to the blessed spirit shield, but provides an additional Magic attack bonus of +20 and Magic damage bonus of +3%. Its counterpart, the spectral spirit shield, instead provides a Magic defence bonus of +30 and a unique passive effect.
12827:
The arcane sigil is an item obtained as a rare drop from the Corporeal Beast. It can be attached to a blessed spirit shield to create an arcane spirit shield, as well as an Elidinis' ward to create Elidinis' ward (f).

Creating an arcane spirit shield requires level 90 Prayer and 85 Smithing. Alternatively, players can ask Abbot Langley to create it for them for 1,500,000 coins.

Meanwhile, fortifying Elidinis' ward requires level 90 Prayer and 90 Smithing, as well as 10,000 soul runes. Unlike the arcane spirit shield, Abbot Langley cannot help players to fortify the ward, though he can remove the sigil from an arcane spirit shield, destroying the blessed spirit shield in the process.
12831:
The blessed spirit shield requires 70 Defence and 60 Prayer to wield. To make this shield, players must use a holy elixir with a normal spirit shield, which requires 85 Prayer. Ironmen may note this level cannot be boosted as prayer boosts do not affect the base level. Once blessed, players may apply spirit sigils to enhance the shield. Attaching a sigil onto the shield requires 90 Prayer and 85 Smithing.

This shield's stats are comparable to the stats of the arcane and spectral spirit shield. It differs only in lacking the higher magic attack and defence stats of the enhanced shields. This shield is a good choice for any player using melee because of its substantial defence bonuses and prayer bonus. Its crush defence bonus is also one point higher than that of a completely charged Dragonfire shield. Players who use Magic or Ranged may also find this shield useful due to its lack of negative stats.

The target teleport scroll is an item that can be read to unlock the Teleport to Target spell, which requires level 85 in Magic to use.

It can be purchased at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 250 Last Man Standing points, or at the Bounty Hunter Store for 500 Bounty Hunter points. There will be a confirmation message when the player attempts to read the scroll.

The granite clamp is an item that can be used on the granite maul or granite maul (ornate handle) to alter the maul's appearance. It is a purely cosmetic addition.

The clamp can be purchased at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 25 Last Man Standing points.

Upon using the clamp, the maul becomes untradeable and the kit is consumed. The maul may be reverted to a granite maul again by selecting the "revert" option. The clamp will not be returned upon reverting the ornate granite maul.

The ornate maul handle, which reduces the maul's special attack cost to 50%, can be used before and after attaching the granite clamp.

An old school bond, commonly referred to as a bond, is an item that allows a player to pay for membership, both for Old School RuneScape and RuneScape 3, on their account. Bonds can be purchased from Jagex for real-world money or in RuneScape for in-game money, keeping RuneScape as a free-to-play game. Bonds can be redeemed in-game for membership or traded with other players for coins or items, providing a means for players to buy membership with in-game items or (indirectly) in-game items with real-world money. Bonds are the only item that can be obtained in-game through a purchase with real-world money.

When bought with real-world money from Jagex, tradeable bonds are added to the bond pouch. These bonds may be traded with other players, sold on the Grand Exchange, or used on another player to donate it to them for free, including on ironmen players. Any of these transfers makes the bond untradeable and unable to be donated.

Players can convert untradeable bonds into tradeable bonds again by choosing the "Convert" option and paying 10% of a tradeable bond's current Grand Exchange value (1,184,402 coins). The total cost of buying and converting a bond (e.g. to buy a gift bond with GP) is 13,028,419 coins. Conversely, the net value of converting and then selling a gifted bond is 10,659,615 coins. Buying a bond with GP and then immediately re-selling it is usually not profitable due to the conversion fees, though it can be profitable to buy one, convert it, and then re-sell it much later.

Players can store up to 100 bonds (tradeable, untradeable, or a mix of both) in their bond pouch. This is a feature of each player's Old School RuneScape account rather than an in-game item, and can be accessed via the Account Management interface. Attempting to buy more from the in-game interface whilst it is full will result in a game message stating Your bonds pouch is full. Please empty it before buying more. However, players can continue to buy additional bonds via the game's website, albeit they will not be given until there is sufficient space within the bond pouch when the player next logs in; a game message accompanies this, stating Your Bond Pouch is too full to hold your recent purchase. The game will try again next time you log in, if there is space then.

Bonds can never be dropped, destroyed, alchemised, or sold in shops. They are always kept on death, even when inside the Wilderness. The only way a player can get rid of a bond, other than by using it, is by trading it or feeding it to an abyssal leech.

Players may only buy or sell one bond per Grand Exchange slot. They are the only item that ironmen are permitted to purchase on the Grand Exchange via a special ironman-only interface.

A smouldering stone is a stone dropped by Cerberus and, much more rarely, hellhounds. It can be used to upgrade the dragon axe, dragon harpoon, and dragon pickaxe into the infernal axe, infernal harpoon, and infernal pickaxe, respectively. These infernal tools have a 1/3 chance to instantly process and destroy a resource (using a charge and granting half of the normal processing experience gained in Firemaking, Cooking, and Smithing, respectively), begin with 5,000 charges, and will function as their dragon variant when all charges are depleted. Another smouldering stone or another dragon tool of that type must be used to recharge it. At current Grand Exchange prices, one charge costs approximately 644.77 coins.

Skills cannot be boosted to create infernal tools using the smouldering stone; the player must have the required base levels of either 85 Firemaking for the infernal axe, 85 Smithing for the infernal pickaxe, or 85 Cooking and 75 Fishing for the infernal harpoon. The conversion process is permanent, and the upgraded tools are untradeable.

When dropped by a hellhound, a message will appear in the player's chatbox: Something hot drops from the body of your vanquished foe.

Sandworms are bait used with a fishing rod to catch anglerfish. They can be purchased from Tynan's Fishing Supplies in Port Piscarilius or caught on the shores of Piscarilius, in the north-east area directly east of the bank and just north of Tynan.

When the player reaches 15 Hunter, sandworms can be caught on the shores of Piscarilius by digging sandworm castings with a spade and buckets. Each bucket will fill with either sand or sandworms, with the latter yielding 10 Hunter experience. Harvesting a bucket of sandworms gives between 1 and 5 sandworms and returns the bucket.

Digging sandworms is also a decent method of low-level moneymaking, netting upwards of 100,000–150,000 coins per hour.

Diabolic worms can be used instead, acting as a direct upgrade to sandworms. They are only dropped by Yama, but vastly improve the speed of catching anglerfish.

The Anglerfish is a type of fish that restores 3-22 Hitpoints depending on your Hitpoints level (see table below). Unlike other foods, anglerfish may also heal above your maximum hitpoints up to the amount restored, with a maximum of 121 hitpoints if the player has a base level of 99 hitpoints. This does not apply if the player is in combat in a PvP area, whether with another player or a non-player character.

It can be obtained by cooking raw anglerfish on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 84 Cooking and granting 230 experience when successful. When cooking, there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt anglerfish. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. It will only stop burning entirely if the player is wearing a Cooking cape or using Cooking gauntlets at level 97 (87 if elite Kourend & Kebos Diary is completed while cooking at the city kitchens).

When at level 93 Hitpoints or higher, the Anglerfish is the second highest instant-health single consumption food, behind the marlin, alongside the dark crab, tuna potato, bluefin and manta ray. The anglerfish has the ability to overheal unlike the others, though the dark crab has the lowest weight.

The tuna potato has the lowest Cooking requirement, but highest weight. Cooked moonlight antelope and cooked dashing kebbit heal 26 and 23 health respectively, but part of the healing is delayed, making them not always practical in the same situations.

Grape seeds can be planted in a vine patch at the Hosidius Vinery at level 36 Farming in order to grow a grape vine, which will yield grapes. Grape seeds can be obtained from the Tithe Farm for 2 points per seed.

Players will need to use saltpetre on the patches with a gardening trowel in order to treat the soil before planting the grape seeds. Afterwards, Gallow will watch over your grapes for free. Sulphorous fertilizer can be used on the patches to increase the yield by 20%.

Once fully grown, players can check the grape vine's health for 625 Farming experience and can harvest the grapes (or Zamorak's grapes if players have a sufficient amount of Bologa's blessings in their inventory). The amount of grapes harvested from a fully grown grape vine is random, much like harvesting herbs, but has a minimum number of five grapes per seed (five harvest lives). Players with higher Farming levels can expect substantially more grapes from each vine. After all the grapes have been harvested, the grape vine will die and players will have to clear the farming patch with a spade.

Players can attach a torture ornament kit, obtained from master clue scrolls, to create an amulet of torture (or). This is purely cosmetic, and does not affect the amulet's stat bonuses. It can be dismantled, returning the amulet and ornament kit.
19570: Bronze javelin tips are items that can be made at level 6 Smithing, granting 5 javelin tips and 12.5 experience per bronze bar. They can be fletched into bronze javelins at level 3 Fletching when used with javelin shafts, which are made by using regular logs with a knife, granting 15 experience per 15 javelins made.
19572: Iron javelin tips are items that can be made at level 21 Smithing, granting 5 javelin tips and 25 experience per iron bar. They can be fletched into iron javelins at level 17 Fletching when used with javelin shafts, which are made by using regular logs with a knife, granting 30 experience per 15 javelins made.
19582:
Dragon javelin tips are attached to javelin shafts to make dragon javelins, requiring 92 Fletching, and yielding 225 Fletching experience per 15 javelins made.

In order to obtain them as a drop from most sources (e.g dragons and dragon implings), players must have completed Monkey Madness II, or they will not be dropped at all. The only exceptions to this rule are Scorpia and the Desert Treasure II bosses.

As with most dragon equipment, dragon javelin tips cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.

The Arceuus library teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport north of the Grand Library of Great Kourend.

Players can create this item on the Arceuus lectern in the Ouditor's house with 1 law rune, 2 earth runes, and at least level 6 Magic while being on the Arceuus spellbook. In addition, a dark essence block is required to substitute soft clay.

The player does not need to have the relevant Magic level to use the tablet, which shares the same rule with all tablets and the player will not receive any experience, although making the teleport tablet does give 10 experience in Magic.
19617:
The Mind altar teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to the entrance of the Mind Altar.

Players can create this item on the Arceuus lectern in the Ouditor's house with 1 law rune, 2 mind runes, and level 28 Magic while being on the Arceuus spellbook. In addition, a dark essence block is required to substitute soft clay.

The Salve graveyard teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to the River Salve graveyard, by the ghouls at the entrance to Mort Myre Swamp.

If the player has not completed the Priest in Peril quest and spoke to Drezel before entering Morytania, they will receive a message in the chatbox stating You must have completed Priest in Peril and received Drezel's warning to cast this spell.

Players can create this item on the Arceuus lectern in the Ouditor's house with 1 law rune, 2 soul runes, and level 40 Magic while being on the Arceuus spellbook. In addition, a dark essence block is required to substitute soft clay. Making the teleport tablet grants 30 experience in Magic.

The player does not need to have the required spellbook or Magic level in order to use this tablet, but using the tablet does not grant any experience.
19621:

Players can create this item on the Arceuus lectern in the Ouditor's house with 1 law rune, 1 earth rune, 1 soul rune, and level 48 Magic while being on the Arceuus spellbook. In addition, a dark essence block is required to substitute soft clay.

The player does not need to have the relevant Magic level to use the tablet, which shares the same rule with all tablets and the player will not receive any experience, although making the teleport tablet does give 50 experience in Magic. The Ape atoll teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to the Ape Atoll Dungeon. Completion of Monkey Madness I is required to use this tablet. Neither the post-quest 10th squad training from Daero nor Freeing King Awowogei Recipe for Disaster subquest need to be completed.

Players with level 90 Magic can create this item on the Arceuus lectern in the Ouditor's house if they have the Arceuus spellbook enabled. This requires 2 law runes, 2 soul runes, 2 blood runes, and a dark essence block instead of the soft clay required for most magic tablets. Making the tablet grants 100 Magic experience, the same as casting the Ape Atoll Teleport spell. It is not required to have Monkey Madness I completed in order to make a tablet.

As with all magic tablets, the player does not need to have the relevant Magic level to use the tablet, but using the tablet does not grant the player any experience.

Creating an Ape Atoll teleport tablet is a task for the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary.

Redwood logs are logs received from cutting redwoods, which are found in the Woodcutting Guild or can be grown from a redwood sapling in the Farming Guild (with level 90 Farming). They require a Woodcutting level of 90 to chop and yield 380 Woodcutting experience per log.

Redwood logs can be burnt with a Firemaking level of 90, giving 350 experience per log. They can be fletched into 105 arrow shafts, a redwood shield, or a redwood hiking staff. They are also used in creation of redwood pyre logs, redwood bird house, building a redwood fence in the superior garden of a player-owned house, lighting the Abyssal lantern (requiring 90 Firemaking), or to craft a perfected quetzal whistle.

A dodgy necklace is an opal necklace enchanted via the Lvl-1 Enchant spell.

While equipped, the necklace provides a 25% chance to prevent the player from being stunned and damaged while pickpocketing NPCs. The necklace begins with 10 charges; one charge is consumed each time the necklace successfully prevents damage. When the last charge is consumed, the necklace crumbles to dust. This stacks multiplicatively with the spell Shadow Veil, where Shadow Veil will attempt to avoid the stun first for a total of 36.25% chance to not take damage from a failed pickpocket. As the player cannot fail a pickpocket attempt on a knocked out NPC, damage taken during blackjacking can only be received by failing a knockout; as such, a dodgy necklace will have no effect on blackjacking.

As in the case of other enchanted items of jewellery (such as the ring of forging), the charges stored on this necklace are specific to the player, not the item itself. This means that players will lose a dodgy necklace after 10 uses irrespective of the particular one they have equipped, and all dodgy necklaces will show the same charge when checked.

Depending on the NPC being pickpocketed, one necklace can prevent 10 to 50 damage and 40 to 60 seconds of being stunned.

A bracelet of slaughter is a topaz bracelet enchanted via the Lvl-3 Enchant spell.

When worn, there is a 25% chance for a Slayer task kill to not count as a kill towards it, but still granting the appropriate Slayer experience (excluding TzTok-Jad and TzKal-Zuk). This results in Slayer tasks lasting 33.3% longer on average. This effect is the inverse of the expeditious bracelets effect. Note that the bracelet needs to be worn only for the tick the Slayer XP drop appears for the effect to occur. This means that for the rest of the fight, other bracelets or gloves can be worn such as the Barrows gloves. The effects of the bracelet make it an ideal switch choice when completing desirable tasks, primarily bosses when inventory space is not an issue.

All bracelets of slaughter share the same pool of 30 charges, with a charge consumed every time the worn effect is activated. When the last charge is consumed, the number of charges will reset to 30, and the worn bracelet will disappear. Dropping or alching a bracelet will not reset the shared charges; the only way to reset the charges at will is to use the right-click "break" option to sacrifice a bracelet early. In addition, the elite Combat Achievements rewards add a 10% chance for the bracelet to regenerate rather than disappearing, allowing it to be used for another set of charges.

On average, you will need 1 charge per 3 assigned monsters. So, an estimate of the number of charges can be calculated as C=x3 , where C is the charges required and x is the assigned slayer count. For example, an assigned slayer count of 132 results in: C=1323=44.

Players can estimate the number of bracelets required per task by dividing the number of charges required by 30 and rounding up. In this example, the number of bracelets required is ⌈4430⌉=⌈1.46⌉=2, so the player will need 2 bracelets of slaughter. You can also simply divide the assigned slayer count by 90 to receive the same answer.

At the current price of the bracelet, the price per extra kill is about 63.83.

Ultracompost is the most potent version of compost, outclassing supercompost, that is used in the Farming skill to greatly reduce the chance of a farming patch from becoming diseased per growth stage by 90% (compared to 50% for compost and 80% for supercompost). This effect stacks with the effect provided by the iasor plant. When used on a farming patch, each bucket grants 36 Farming experience.

In addition, it also increases the minimum yield and maximum number of harvests received from allotments, hops, and herbs. This also applies to giant seaweed patches underwater, Celastrus bark from a fully grown Celastrus seed, and Crystal shards from a fully grown Crystal tree.

The minimum number of herbs increases from five to six (when compared to supercompost) and the overall crop yield increases around 20% on average. The combined effects increase expected yield per patch to about 8.6 herbs at high Farming levels.

As a rule of thumb, ultracompost is nearly always worth using as it boosts the yield of valuable patches, providing additional experience and gold overall, and is typically more cost effective and easier to manage than paying to protect a patch with a gardener.

However, ultracompost does not increase the yield of trees, fruit trees, cactus, bush patches, and flower patches; using it only protects these crops from disease.
21486: Plant this in a plantpot of soil to grow a sapling.
21488: Plant this in a plantpot of soil to grow a sapling.
21490: A seaweed spore - plant in a seaweed patch.
21512: Feed and catch the birds by placing this in the right spot.
21515:
An oak bird house is used to set bird house traps on Fossil Island requiring 14 Hunter. It can be made at 15 Crafting using oak logs on a clockwork with a chisel and hammer yielding 20 experience.

Once placed in a bird house space, it becomes an oak birdhouse trap.

Bird houses must be baited with 10 hop seeds (5 if Wildblood), 10 allotment seeds, 10 flower seeds, 10 low level herb seeds (guam, marrentill, tarromin, harralander), or 5 high level herb seeds (ranarr and above). After approximately 50 minutes when the birdhouse is full, it can be emptied, granting 168 Hunter experience.
21518: Feed and catch the birds by placing this in the right spot.
21521: Feed and catch the birds by placing this in the right spot.
21543:
Calcite is an item that is used with pyrophosphite on a mycelium pool in order to recalcify fossils into enriched bones, which are used on the eastern strange machine in the House on the Hill to gain Prayer experience.

It is dropped by monsters found on Fossil Island, and can be mined from boulders inside the Volcanic Mine. It can also be purchased for 70 points each from Petrified Pete's Ore Shop.
21555: Numulites are a form of currency used on Fossil Island. They are obtained from doing just about anything on Fossil Island, such as killing monsters, chopping sulliusceps, tracking herbiboars, digging the soil east of the Museum Camp, mining in the Volcanic Mine, and looting chests and clams in the mermaid's domain. They can also be obtained by trading fossils with the Fossil Collector. An equipped ring of wealth will automatically pick up numulite drops from killed monsters if its coin-collection feature is enabled.
21622:
Volcanic ash is obtained from mining ash piles found around the Fossil Island Volcano. Doing so requires level 22 Mining and grants 10 experience per drop, regardless of the number of ash mined at once.

They can also be obtained as drops from various monsters on Fossil Island including wyverns in the Wyvern Cave.
21626:
A sulliuscep cap is an item obtained from chopping down sulliusceps. Players have a 1/100 chance of receiving the cap while chopping sulliusceps.

They are used as an ingredient in mushroom pies, a food item that boosts Crafting by 4 levels.
21634:
The ancient wyvern shield is a magical shield requiring a Magic level of 70 and a Defence level of at least 75 to equip, as well as having started Dragon Slayer I. It is one of the best Magic shields in the game, with stats comparable to that of the arcane spirit shield when fully charged, although it only has a 2% Magic damage bonus while having negative Melee and Ranged attack bonuses. However, it provides far superior stab and slash defence.

The shield provides both dragonfire protection and greater protection against the icy breath of wyverns and frost dragons. Unlike the elemental, mind, and dragonfire shields, the ancient wyvern shield will also grant an immunity against the freezing effect from a wyvern's icy breath, as well as reducing the damage, which can make it somewhat ideal when killing wyverns despite penalizing melee and ranged. This immunity, on the other hand, does not extend to any other freezing effect (such as KBD, Vorkath, etc).

When the shield is obtained, it is uncharged and offers similar defensive bonuses to those of an adamant sq shield. When fully charged, it offers melee and magic defensive bonuses slightly higher than those of the dragonfire shield while having far worse ranged defence.
21637: The wyvern visage is an item obtained as a very rare drop from Fossil Island wyverns found in the Wyvern Cave. Skeletal Wyverns do not drop the wyvern visage; they drop the draconic visage instead.
21643:
Granite boots are boots made out of granite rock. They require level 50 Defence and Strength to equip, offering strength bonus and defensive stats superior to rune boots. Unlike most melee boots, they also provide a Ranged defence bonus.

They are obtained as a drop from wyverns in the Wyvern Cave.

The boots also help to protect the wearer from the extremely hot ground of the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon. Because they offer a strength bonus, unlike the boots of brimstone and the boots of stone, they are the most powerful offensive boots for melee attack styles within the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon if the player has not completed the elite Kourend & Kebos diary.
21646:
The granite longsword is the fourth strongest longsword available in Old School RuneScape, and can only be wielded by players who have at least 50 Attack and Strength.

It is obtained as a drop from wyverns in the Wyvern Cave. Despite a high slash accuracy bonus, its 5 tick attack speed means it is outperformed by the granite hammer's 4 tick attack speed, making the hammer better for training.
21649:
A merfolk trident can be bought from Mairin's Market in the underwater area of Fossil Island for 400 mermaid's tears obtained from Underwater Agility and Thieving.

It is one of the few weapons that allow the player to swim while wielding it. Its main purpose is aiding with drift net fishing, where it gives an increased chance to scare off fish shoals into the net. It shares this effect with the trident of the seas. The trident has no Attack level requirements and is a 2-handed weapon.

When attempting to equip the trident underwater, players will receive the following message: "WARNING! If you have this item equipped you can not swim. Deeper water will kill you." However, once inside the shallow water of the Hunter area, it is possible to safely equip the merfolk trident by selecting "I'll steer clear of deeper water but wield this anyway." It is not possible to swim through the seaweed door with a weapon equipped.

The trident can be charged with up to 10 pufferfish, which will let players use the Channel option to regain breath underwater, as with regular pufferfish.

The merfolk trident can be stored in a player's tackle box.
21652: A very large net, too big to be used by hand.
21684: An uncooked mushroom pie is made by adding a sulliuscep cap to a pie shell. It can be baked with level 60 Cooking to make a mushroom pie, granting 200 Cooking experience when successfully baked. Obtaining a sulliuscep cap requires level 65 Woodcutting in order to cut the Sulliusceps found in the Sticky Swamp portion of Fossil Island which can be accessed via the Bone Voyage quest.
21730: The blackened heart of the Grotesque Guardians.
21733: Some sturdy Bandos boots, made sturdier with the blackened tourmaline core of the Grotesque Guardians.
21736:
Granite gloves are a pair of melee-oriented gloves dropped by the Grotesque Guardians, requiring level 50 Defence and Strength to equip.

Stats-wise, they are similar to adamant gloves, but have superior crush bonuses and melee defences.
21739:
The granite ring is a defensive ring dropped by the Grotesque Guardians that can be found on the Slayer Tower's rooftop. Level 50 Defence and Strength are required to wear it.

It can be imbued using 500,000 Nightmare Zone reward points or 250,000 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements, 200 Soul Wars Zeal Tokens, or a Scroll of Imbuing, purchased for 200 Emir's Arena reward points, doubling its stats.
21742:
The granite hammer is a warhammer dropped by the Grotesque Guardians. Level 50 Attack and 50 Strength is required to wield it.

It acts as a rock hammer in the inventory and when equipped - it will automatically smash gargoyles even if the player does not have the gargoyle smasher perk unlocked. The granite hammer also has a 30% Golembane effect, dealing 30% extra damage and accuracy against all golem-type creatures. This stacks multiplicatively with the slayer helmet's bonuses.

Unlike standard warhammers, the granite hammer features an attack speed of 4, matching the speed of more commonly used melee weapons (such as scimitars and the abyssal whip), which results in significantly more damage over time. Thus, in terms of overall power, the granite hammer is roughly between the rune scimitar and dragon scimitar.
21745: Stones aren't very useful in this capacity.
21754:
A rock thrownhammer is slayer equipment that is required to kill gargoyles. Unlike the rock hammer, the rock thrownhammer can be used to finish off gargoyles without having to do so within melee distance. This is useful for finishing off gargoyles when ranging from a safespot, or when finishing off Dawn. Since they are consumed upon usage, players should buy enough thrownhammers for their slayer task.

While damage can be done to them with a regular weapon at 75 Slayer, the thrownhammer must be used on gargoyles to finish them off when they have 10 hitpoints or less left, unless the player has unlocked the Gargoyle smasher ability via spending 120 slayer reward points, which allows players to automatically use the thrownhammer to finish off the gargoyle.

Players can buy a rock thrownhammer from any Slayer Master for 200 coins each.

They can only be obtained by using feathers on unfinished dragon bolts. Doing so requires level 84 in Fletching and grants 12 experience per bolt.

They are enchanted via the Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Dragonstone) spell by a player with level 68 Magic, enchanting 10 bolts per cast. This creates enchanted dragonstone dragon bolts, which are a superior version of enchanted dragonstone bolts.
21973: Dragon crossbow bolts, tipped with onyx.
21975:
Crushed superior dragon bones are a secondary ingredient used to create super antifire potions, which require level 92 Herblore to make. They can be obtained by using a pestle and mortar with superior dragon bones, which in turn can be obtained by killing Vorkath or frost dragons.

They can be stored in a reagent pouch while superior dragon bones cannot, which can allow saving inventory space when fighting Vorkath repeatedly.
21994: Two doses of fishy super anti-firebreath potion.
21997: One dose of fishy super anti-firebreath potion.
22003:
The dragonfire ward is a ranged shield requiring a Ranged level of 70 and a Defence level of 75 to equip, as well as having started Dragon Slayer I. It offers the second highest Ranged Attack and Ranged Strength bonus for the shield slot in the game, only beaten by the twisted buckler.

The ward offers two special characteristics: it acts like a regular anti-dragon shield in terms of dragonfire protection, and it provides partial protection against the icy breath of wyverns, like the elemental, mind, and dragonfire shields. This immunity does not extend to draconic creatures capable of producing a similar effect (KBD, Vorkath, etc).
22006: It looks like this could be attached to a shield somehow.
22097:
A dragon metal shard is an item that can be purchased from the Myths' Guild Armoury for 1,800,000 coins, which requires the completion of Dragon Slayer II to access.

The shard can be used alongside a dragon metal slice and a dragon sq shield to create a dragon kiteshield. Doing so requires level 75 Smithing, and grants the player 1,000 experience.

Alternatively, it can be used alongside a dragon metal lump and a dragon chainbody to create a dragon platebody. This requires level 90 in Smithing, and grants the player 2,000 experience.
22100: A badly damaged slice of dragon metal.
22103: Dragon metal lumps are dropped by rune dragons. The lump, along with a dragon metal shard and a dragon chainbody, is used to create a dragon platebody. Doing so requires level 90 in Smithing and grants the player 2,000 experience.
22111:
The dragonbone necklace is a necklace that is dropped exclusively by Vorkath. Wearing the necklace requires level 70 in Prayer, and currently offers the highest Prayer bonus of any piece of equipment available in Old School RuneScape.

When worn, it will restore Prayer points as bones are buried (even if buried via the bonecrusher). This effect does not stack with the Catacombs of Kourend Prayer restoration effect, and does not grant Prayer points for scattering demonic ashes.

The dragonbone necklace can be combined with the bonecrusher and a hydra tail to create the bonecrusher necklace, which combines the effects of both the dragonbone necklace and the bonecrusher.

The amount of points restored are as follows:

Bones, Burnt bones, Monkey bones, Wolf bones, and Bat bones restore 1 prayer point.

Big bones, Jogre bones, Zogre bones, Wyrmling bones, Shaikahan bones, and Small ninja monkey bones restore 2 prayer points.

Baby dragon bones, Bull bones, Wyrm bones, and Strykewyrm bones restore 3 prayer points.

Dragon, Frost dragon, Wyvern, Drake, Dagannoth, Hydra, Fayrg, Raurg, and Lava dragon bones restore 4 prayer points.

Superior dragon bones, Giant bones, and Ourg bones restore 5 prayer points.
22118: A mysterious power emanates from the talisman...
22121: A tiara infused with the properties of wrath.
22124:
Superior dragon bones are obtained as a guaranteed drop from killing Vorkath and as an uncommon drop from killing frost dragons. They can be crushed with a pestle and mortar to create crushed superior dragon bones, which is a secondary ingredient in super antifire potions, requiring level 92 Herblore to create.

Unlike other types of bones, superior dragon bones require a Prayer level of 70 (unboostable) to use, and give 150 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

450 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

450 XP when offered at the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

525 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit.

600 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of superior dragon bonemeal.

605 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl, or 726 XP when offered with a jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

1050 XP on average when offered at the Chaos Temple in the Wilderness. Each offering gives 525 XP, which is the same as the gilded altars with two burners lit, but with an additional 50% chance to not consume the bones.

Superior dragon bones provide the most Prayer experience of any bone in the game, but they are very expensive, making them the top-tier choice for efficient training when cost is not a concern. When used at a gilded altar, they require 38.84 coins per experience, while regular dragon bones use 13.05 coins per experience. As such, the most economical use is as a secondary for making super antifire potions.

The staff of light inherits all of the staff of the dead's effects. The only differences between them is that the staff of light autocasts the Saradomin Strike god spell rather than the Flames of Zamorak god spell, and is unable to autocast Arceuus combat spells. In addition, it counts as both a Saradominist and a Zamorakian item while in the God Wars Dungeon and in the Desert Bandit Camp.

The staff of light cannot be upgraded with a magic fang to provide the additional magic attack bonus and toxic effect given to the toxic staff of the dead.
22299: A mysterious artifact of ancient times, precious to emblem traders.

The statuette cannot be given to him in Edgeville. A chisel can be used on the ancient relic to break it into 32,000 revenant ether.

22324:
The Ghrazi rapier is a one-handed stab weapon obtainable as a rare drop from the Theatre of Blood. It requires level 80 Attack to wield. It provides the highest strength and stab bonus out of any weapon for its attack speed. This makes the rapier tied with the blade of Saeldor and the Inquisitor's mace for the melee weapon with the highest damage output for general use, although it is outperformed by the Osmumten's fang against high defence monsters and Scythe of Vitur against large monsters.

The Ghrazi tribe was the most vicious vampyre tribe on Vampyrium. This rapier was once wielded by a fearsome Ghrazi warlord who was slain in battle by Verzik Vitur's father, who gave it to Verzik.

The rapier can be combined with a holy ornament kit to make a Saradomin-themed holy Ghrazi rapier. This cosmetic upgrade won't change the stats in any way, but it will make the rapier count as a Saradomin item in the God Wars Dungeon.
22326:
The Justiciar faceguard is obtained as a rare drop from the Theatre of Blood. It is part of the justiciar armour set, and requires level 75 Defence to equip.

When the full set of Justiciar armour is equipped, the player gains a set effect: all combat damage taken is reduced (except in PvP). The exact formula for the amount of damage reduced is bonus3000, where bonus is the player's defence bonus for that particular style. For example, if an enemy was using a crush style attack, and the player has a crush defence bonus of +450, then 15% of the damage (450/3,000) is reduced.

The Justiciar faceguard is counted as a Saradomin item in the God Wars Dungeon.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Justiciar armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

The Avernic defender hilt is an add-on that can be received as a reward from the Theatre of Blood. When used with a dragon defender, the Avernic defender will be created after a confirmation message. This process can be reversed, but the hilt will not be returned.

Avernic weaponry was common amongst Zarosian forces in the Second Age, crafted by Avernic demon smiths in the liquid fires of Infernus. Today, they are incredibly rare, and Verzik Vitur's Avernic defender is one of the few to remain, a relic from her time in the service of Zaros. Due to its age, the full defender has been destroyed, and only the hilt remains.

When the hilt is inspected, the chatbox message states You raise the hilt, inspecting each section carefully. It looks as though it could combine with a powerful parrying dagger.

22595: A blue salt, that when burned with other salts provides various benefits.
22597:
Urt salt is a type of salt that can be mined from urt salt rocks in the Salt Mine beneath Weiss after the completion of Making Friends with My Arm. Along with Te salt and Efh salt, it can be used to light fire pits that provide benefits (such as a permanent light source), and it is also used to create stony basalts. Mining Urt salt requires 72 Mining and is mined in chunks of 2-7 scaling with the player's level, granting the player 5 experience per salt mined. Mining enhancers do not work here.

700 Urt salt is required to construct all the available permanent fires (1 dehumidification, 3 eternal light, 1 nourishment, 1 unseasonal warmth). 250 Urt salt is required to construct an Eternal brazier on a boat. 300 Urt salt is required to attune a portal to Troll Stronghold in a Portal Chamber in a Player Owned House, and 3000 Urt salt is required to attune a Portal Nexus. Players will also need 250 Te, Efh, and Urt salts to build an Eternal brazier on each of their boats. Assuming the brazier is built on 5 boats (the current maximum), 1250 of each salt would be needed in total.

Zuriel's staff (bh) is a one-handed magic weapon requiring level 75 Magic and 30 Attack to wield, and is purchased from the Bounty Hunter Store for 300 points.

As with all Ancient Warriors' equipment from Bounty Hunter, it is initially purchased in inactive form, and must be charged with 5,000,000 coins before it can be used by the player. Upon dying in PvP, the coins used to activate the item are given to the killer, and players are left with the inactive item.

In addition, it can only be used within Daimon's Crater, Castle Wars, Clan Wars, Soul Wars, the TzHaar Fight Pit, and both the player-owned house and Clan Hall combat rings; attempting to attack anything outside the listed areas will result in the player being interrupted from doing so.

22786:
Hydra bones are the remains obtained from killing hydras or the Alchemical Hydra, which give 110 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

330 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

330 XP when offered at the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

385 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit.

440 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of hydra bonemeal.

465 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl, or 558 XP when offered with a jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

770 XP on average when offered at the Chaos Temple in the Wilderness. Each offering gives 385 XP, which is the same as the gilded altars with two burners lit, but with an additional 50% chance to not consume the bones.

Burying them while wearing a dragonbone necklace will restore 4 prayer points.

Hydra bones provide the fourth highest amount of Prayer experience per bone in the game, behind dagannoth bones, ourg bones, and superior dragon bones.
22789: An uncooked dragonfruit pie is a pie made by adding a dragonfruit to a pie shell. It can be baked with level 73 Cooking to make a dragonfruit pie, granting 220 Cooking experience when successfully baked.
22795:
Dragonfruit pie is a type of pie that restores 20 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 10. It also temporarily boosts Fletching by 4, the second highest boost available, and the highest reliable boost. A pie dish will remain after both bites are consumed.

It can be created by baking a uncooked dragonfruit pie on a cooking range, requiring level 73 Cooking and granting 220 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Dragonfruit pies never stop burning altogether even at level 99, unless the player is wearing a Cooking cape or using the Hosidius kitchen. Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.

22829:
Common tench are fish that can be caught on Molch island using the Cormorant's glove. Requiring 56 Fishing and 51 Hunter to catch, they provide 40 fishing experience and 45 hunter experience.

Before attempting to fish them, players must speak with Alry the Angler to obtain the Cormorant's glove. This item functions similarly to the Falconer's glove used in the hunter skill. Players must click on rapidly moving fishing spots and can obtain a variety of fish, including the Common tench.

Common tench require no bait to catch directly, however King worms are initially required to feed the cormorant. After caught, a knife can be used to cut the tench to obtain stackable Fish offcuts which can be used as a substitute for the king worms. Cutting the fish provides 10 Cooking experience.
22832:
Mottled eel are fish that can be caught on Molch island using the Cormorant's glove. Requiring 73 Fishing and 68 Hunter to catch, they provide 65 fishing experience and 90 hunter experience.

Before attempting to fish them, players must speak with Alry the Angler to obtain the Cormorant's glove. This item functions similarly to the Falconer's glove used in the hunter skill. Players must click on rapidly moving fishing spots and can obtain a variety of fish, including the Mottled eel.

Mottled eel require no bait to catch directly, however the cormorant is initially required to be fed either with fish offcuts or King worms, the latter of which are easily found in the island. After catching a Mottled eel, a knife can be used to cut the eel to obtain stackable fish offcuts which can be used as a substitute for the king worms. Cutting the fish provides 20 Cooking experience.
22835: A descendant of the salamander family.
22856: This sapling is ready to be replanted in a Celastrus patch.
22859:
Redwood saplings are saplings that can be used to grow redwood trees at 90 Farming. They are made by planting a redwood seed in a filled plant pot, with a gardening trowel in your inventory, then watering the redwood seedling with a watering can or by casting Humidify. When watered, the seedling will sprout into a sapling in one crop cycle (0-5 minutes).

Planting the sapling in the redwood tree patch in the Farming Guild, requiring a spade, yields 230 Farming experience. It will grow into a redwood tree after 6,400 minutes (4 days, 10 hours, and 40 minutes), and yields 22,450 Farming experience when checked.

Players can ask the gardener to protect their tree from disease whilst it grows, which requires payment of 6 dragonfruits. This payment can be noted.

Once the tree has fully grown, it can be cut down like a regular redwood tree, as it will regrow unlike other self-grown log giving trees. This method of cutting redwoods may be preferable for players looking to AFK more, as you don't compete with other players and the bank deposit is closer. However; you will lose out on the Woodcutting Guild's invisible +7 boost to Woodcutting, making it slightly slower overall.

It is not possible for players to clear the redwood tree patch; Alexandra must be paid 2,000 coins to clear it.
22866:
Dragonfruit saplings are saplings that can be used to grow dragonfruit trees at level 81 Farming.

They can be made by planting a dragonfruit tree seed in a filled plant pot, with a gardening trowel in your inventory, and then watering the dragonfruit seedling with a watering can or by using Humidify. When watered, the seedling will sprout into a sapling in one crop cycle (0-5 minutes).

Planting the sapling in a fruit tree patch, with a spade in your inventory, will give 140 Farming experience. It will grow into a dragonfruit tree after 960 minutes (16 hours), which gives 17,335 Farming experience.

Players can ask the gardener to protect their tree from disease whilst it grows, which requires payment of 15 coconuts. This payment can be noted.
22871:
Redwood tree seeds are seeds used in the Farming skill. At level 90 Farming[boostable], redwood seeds may be planted in plant pots with a gardening trowel and watered to become redwood saplings. They can be obtained from bird nests, monster drops, the brimstone chest, Larran's big chest or by completing farming contracts.

After planting the sapling in a redwood tree patch found in the Farming Guild and waiting for it to fully grow, which takes over four days (106.7 hours), the plant will grow into a redwood tree which can be cut to yield redwood logs (and grant Woodcutting experience). Planting the redwood sapling yields 230 experience, and checking its health gives 22,450 experience. Alexandra will look after a player's redwood patch in exchange for 6 dragonfruits.

When cut down, the tree will automatically regrow after a period of time. Players cannot clear the patch on their own; they must pay Alexandra 2,000 coins to do so.

One seed can be used on the skilling pet Tangleroot to change its appearance.
22873:
Potato cactus seeds are a type of seed that can be planted in a cactus patch found in Al Kharid or the Farming Guild. They require level 64 Farming to plant and produce a potato cactus. Growth time is approximately 70 minutes. Players can harvest potato cacti from the mature plant.

Potato cactus seeds can be obtained as drops from various monsters, in seed packs awarded from farming contracts, or by pickpocketing a master farmer.

A nearby gardener will watch over your growing potato cactus plant in exchange for 8 snape grass.
22877:
Dragonfruit tree seeds are the highest level fruit tree patch seeds. At 81 Farming, a dragonfruit tree seed can be planted in a plant pot to make a dragonfruit seedling, which grows into a dragonfruit sapling; the sapling can be planted in a fruit tree patch to be grown into a dragonfruit tree. Dragonfruit trees, when fully grown, bear dragonfruit.

A nearby gardener will watch over your growing dragonfruit tree at the cost of 15 coconuts.

Dragonfruit trees, like all fruit trees, ideally take six 160-minute farming cycles to fully grow, but certain factors can delay this. Dragonfruit trees are usually fully grown within 24 hours, however.

Dragonfruit tree seeds may be found rarely in a bird nest, which can be obtained randomly while Woodcutting, emptying Birdhouses or from Managing Miscellania. They can also be obtained via farming contracts from the Farming Guild, as loot from opening the brimstone chest, Larran's small or big chest or as rare drops from the Hespori, alchemical hydra, demonic gorillas, lizardman shamans, and Vorkath.

One seed can be used on the skilling pet Tangleroot to change its appearance.
22879:
Snape grass seeds can be planted at level 61 Farming. 3 seeds are sown in an allotment patch to grow snape grass plants, which yield snape grass: a Herblore secondary ingredient. They take 1 hour and 10 minutes to grow.

A nearby gardener will watch over growing snape grass plants for 5 jangerberries. Fully grown white lilies in a nearby flower patch will also protect the snape grass from disease.

These seeds can be stolen from master farmers. They may also be obtained from various monsters, Farming Guild seed packs, and the Wintertodt reward cart.

The amulet of bounty is useful for saving snape grass seeds, providing a saving of 23,274 coins per charge.

8 snape grass are needed to protect growing potato cactus.
22887:
White lily seeds can be planted in a flower patch at level 58 Farming to yield a white lily. When fully grown, it protects all neighbouring allotments from disease.

A nearby gardener will not watch over a growing white lily plant. It is recommended to use ultracompost when planting them.

They can be obtained as a drop from the Hespori, from a seed pack bought from Tithe Farm, or bought from other players.

Using one seed on the Tangleroot pet will change its appearance to a white lily variant.
22929:
A dragonfruit is obtained from a dragonfruit tree, which can be grown from a dragonfruit sapling in a fruit tree patch, provided that one has level 81 Farming. Players can pay a gardener a fee of 15 coconuts to watch over the tree while it grows. A fully grown dragonfruit tree grows one dragonfruit per 30 minutes up to a maximum of six per tree.

When eaten, a dragonfruit heals 10 hitpoints. They are an ingredient in dragonfruit pies, which require level 73 Cooking to bake and boost a player's Fletching level by 4 when eaten.

Ten dragonfruits can also be used on a vial to create bottled dragonbreath, which can be used on a sulphur vent on Mount Karuulm to "power" it (this process will burn the player for 2 damage if they are not wearing ice gloves). Once powered, it can be used on a dragonfire shield or ward to fully charge it instantly.

Players may pay 6 dragonfruits to Alexandra in the Farming Guild to have her look after a planted redwood tree. Players can also pay a gardener 8 dragonfruits to look after a planted rosewood tree.
22932:
White lilies are flowers that can be harvested from a flower patch after planting white lily seeds. Fully grown white lilies protect all neighbouring allotments from disease.

White lilies have very limited practical uses after being harvested. The most productive use of white lilies (once harvested) is to add them to a compost bin to make supercompost.
22935: A length of celastrus wood, ready for fletching.
22949:
The Battlefront teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to the ancient grave just outside the Battlefront in the Kebos Lowlands.

Players with 23 Magic and the Arceuus spellbook enabled can create this item on the Arceuus lectern in the Ouditor's house with 1 law rune, 1 earth rune, 1 fire rune, and a dark essence block instead of the soft clay required for most magic tablets. This grants 19 Magic experience.

As with all magic tablets, the player does not need to have the relevant Magic level to use the tablet, but will not receive any experience for using it.
22951: A pair of heat resistant boots charged with the claw of the ferocious Drake.
22957: The claw of a ferocious drake. They could be combined with the boots of stone.
22960: The tooth of a ferocious drake. They could be combined with holy sandals.

Players do not have to learn Barbarian Smithing via the Barbarian Training miniquest to do this. Players do however need to have completed the smithing portion of the miniquest in order to wield the repaired hasta.
22966:
The hydra's claw is an item dropped by the Alchemical Hydra. It can be combined with the Zamorakian hasta to create the dragon hunter lance.

When attempting to create the dragon hunter lance, a warning will appear in the chatbox stating that the process cannot be reversed, and a confirmation will appear afterwards asking if players would like to proceed with the alchemical combination.
22975:
A brimstone ring is a ring created by combining three untradeable components — the hydra's eye, fang, and heart; players cannot receive a duplicate of these until obtaining each of the other pieces.

The ring provides the combined offensive and defensive stats of the archers, berserker, warrior, seers, treasonous, and tyrannical rings, though it cannot be imbued.

The ring also has a passive effect when worn that improves its effectiveness to rival the seers ring (i) when using Magic. Each time the player attacks using a spell or magical attack (powered staves included), there is a 25% chance that the target's defensive roll will be reduced by 10% for that attack. When this occurs, there will be a game chat message Your attack ignored 10% of your opponent's magic defence. Note the reduction doesn't affect multiple targets when barraging or hitting multiple opponents. The effect is limited to the single intended target you select.
22978:
The dragon hunter lance is a one-handed spear and dragonbane weapon created by using a hydra claw on a Zamorakian hasta. Equipping the lance requires level 78 Attack as well as completion of the Firemaking (not the pyre step), Fishing, and Smithing sections of the Barbarian Training miniquest.

The lance's dragonbane passive effect is its 20% increased accuracy and damage when fighting draconic creatures, such as dragons, wyverns, and the Great Olm (but excluding Elvarg and revenant dragons). This stacks multiplicatively with both Void Knight equipment and the Slayer helm (i).

Like the Zamorakian hasta, it will act as a Zamorak item within the God Wars Dungeon; though the lance lacks the hasta's prayer and defensive bonuses and special attack, while sporting a lower strength bonus.

When attempting to create the dragon hunter lance, a warning will appear in the chatbox stating that the process cannot be reversed, and a confirmation will appear afterwards asking if players would like to proceed with the alchemical combination. Should the player confirm, the chatbox will state: You successfully combine the Hydra claw and the Zamorakian hasta to create the Dragon hunter lance.
22983:
Hydra leather is dropped by the Alchemical Hydra. It is used to make ferocious gloves, by placing it on the piece of machinery just south-west of the large pool in Lithkren Vault, requiring Dragon Slayer II and a hammer. The gloves can be reverted to leather using the same machinery.

When Hydra leather is inspected, the chatbox message states This leather looks pretty tough to work with... Maybe the dragonkin had a way. When the gloves are created, the chatbox message states By feeding the tough to work leather through the machine, you manage to form a pair of gloves.
22988: The hydra tail is an item dropped by hydras and the Alchemical Hydra. It can be combined with the dragonbone necklace and bonecrusher to create the bonecrusher necklace, which combines the effects of both. There will be a confirmation message before combining them; this can be reversed.
