23188:
The Guthix d'hide shield is a leather shield, aligned with the god Guthix (does not count as a god item in God Wars Dungeon). It shares the same bonuses as a black d'hide shield, but with an additional +1 prayer bonus. Equipping the shield requires 40 Defence and 70 Ranged.

Along with other blessed dragonhide armour pieces, it cannot be made using the Crafting skill. Players can receive it as a reward from completing hard Treasure Trails.

This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room, provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface.
23191:
The Saradomin d'hide shield is a leather shield, aligned with the god Saradomin. It shares the same bonuses as a black d'hide shield, but with an additional +1 prayer bonus. Equipping the shield requires 40 Defence and 70 Ranged. This item is not required to assemble the Saradomin dragonhide set.

Along with other blessed dragonhide armour pieces, it cannot be made using the Crafting skill. Players can receive them as a reward from completing hard Treasure Trails.

It does count as Saradomin armour in the God Wars Dungeon. This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room, provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Larran's key is a key obtained from killing monsters while on a Slayer task given by Krystilia. It is used to open Larran's small and big chests.

The exact odds of receiving a key scales with the monster's Combat level. For levels 1-80, the probability follows a curve between 1/1972 at level 1 to 1/100 at level 80. For levels 81 or higher, the odds are between 1/99 and 1/50, scaling linearly and capping at level 350, as reflected in the equation below.

If it concerns a Slayer monster (meaning it requires a certain Slayer level to kill), the drop chance is increased by 20%. In addition, any monster killed within the Wilderness Slayer Cave has a further 15% increased chance to drop a key. Superior slayer monsters that spawn as part of Krystilia's tasks will always drop a key on death.

The probability P of obtaining a key when killing a monster with combat level L is given by:

P={1⌊310×(80−L)2⌋+100if L∈(0,80]1⌊−527×L⌋+115if L∈(80,350]150L∈(350,∞)

Larran's keys are always dropped on player death, even if there are fewer than 3 items kept on death. If killed by another player, keys are lost to the killer. If killed in PvM, the keys always go to your gravestone.

The crystal tool seed is an elven crystal that can be turned into the crystal axe, crystal harpoon, or crystal pickaxe, using 120 crystal shards and the dragon counterpart on a singing bowl. It can be obtained as a drop from Zalcano.

The crystal tools start off at 10,000 charges and degrades, like other crystal equipment. One charge is depleted for each time an item is obtained using the tool, with some exceptions for particular uses of the axe and pickaxe where the crystal version has no additional benefit (duplicates from items such as the Varrock armour do not deplete an extra charge). The player may add charges with crystal shards, with each shard granting 100 charges, up to a maximum of 20,000 charges. Dismantling a crystal tool will return the dragon equivalent and crystal tool seed to the player and doing so will lose all crystal shard charges that were previously loaded.

Players can also exchange the tool seed for 100 crystal shards by speaking to Amrod in Prifddinas' Hefin Inn.

A dangerous death in PvP causes the crystal tools to revert to their dragon equivalents which will then be dropped for the killer. All crystal shards will be lost as well.

A trouver parchment is a consumable scroll, purchased from Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 18 Last Man Standing points or obtained as a drop from killing monsters in the Wilderness Slayer Cave.

The parchment is used to "lock" and prevent certain unprotected untradeable items from being destroyed if killed in PvP combat beyond level 20 Wilderness. Players will need to give the parchment and pay 500,000 to Perdu for each item they lock; multiple items can be locked simultaneously, but will require additional parchments for each one.

At current prices, it costs 764,909 to purchase a parchment from the Grand Exchange and pay Perdu to use it on an item.

A list of every eligible item to be locked (l) with the Trouver parchment can be found here.
24219:
The Swift blade is a one-handed weapon purchased from Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 350 Last Man Standing points.

It is one of the only four melee weapons with an attack speed of 3, with the other ones being the ham joint, goblin paint cannon, and mystic cards, with the latter two also being two handed weapons only. The swift blade also exclusively uses Stab and Slash attack styles whereas the others use Crush, and the mystic cards have negative combat stat bonuses whereas the others have no bonuses.

Due to having no Attack level requirement, the Swift blade is the best-in-slot weapon for training Defence pures and combines well with the stab bonus given by the Ardougne cloaks.

This item is also commonly used in the Theatre of Blood for the Nylocas room because of its fast attack speed. It is preferred over the Goblin paint cannon and the Ham joint because its attack styles are not shared with the dragon warhammer, allowing players to keep the dragon warhammer on an accurate attack style, while having the swift blade on an aggressive style. In addition, the swift blade is slightly more accurate than a ham joint when used with a defender, as defenders have +2 higher stab accuracy compared to crush.

Blighted manta rays heal 22 Hitpoints, and are considered to be among the best foods in the game.

Attempting to eat the manta ray outside the Wilderness prints the message The blighted manta ray can be eaten only in the Wilderness.
24592:
Blighted anglerfish are a variant of anglerfish that can only be eaten while inside the Wilderness, Ferox Enclave, Mage Arena bank, PvP Worlds, Castle Wars lobby, and Clan Wars. 15 can be purchased at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 1 Last Man Standing point or at the Soul Wars Reward Shop for 10 Zeal Tokens.

Similarly to anglerfish, blighted anglerfish can heal above maximum Hitpoints (making the maximum Hitpoints possible 121). Overheal does not apply if the player has been attacked or damaged (including zeroes) inside a PvP area within the past 16 ticks (9.6s), whether from a player, monster, or environmental source. There is a small exception: when fighting an NPC in a single-way or singles-plus combat area, you can overheal as soon as the NPC dies rather than waiting 16 ticks.
24595:
Blighted karambwan are a variant of cooked karambwan that can only be eaten while inside the Wilderness, Ferox Enclave, Mage Arena bank, PvP worlds, Castle Wars lobby, and Clan Wars healing 18 hitpoints. 12 can be purchased at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 1 Last Man Standing point or at the Soul Wars Reward Shop for 10 Zeal Tokens.

Unlike most other food, they can be consumed nearly instantly with no delay after consuming another food item, known as "combo eating"; this makes them a favourable item for player killing. The "combo eating" tactic can be enhanced further by drinking a dose of saradomin brew alongside a karambwan and the base food item, enabling a player to heal over 50 hitpoints very rapidly.

Attempting to eat the karambwan outside the Wilderness prints the message The blighted karambwan can be eaten only in the Wilderness.

Blighted ancient ice sacks are an item that allows players to cast any ice spell within their Magic level without needing the runes for it. However, it can only be used inside the Wilderness, Ferox Enclave, Mage Arena bank, PvP worlds, Castle Wars, Clan Wars, and Soul Wars, and the Ancient Magicks spellbook must be active.

30 can be purchased at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 1 Last Man Standing point or at the Soul Wars Reward Shop for 10 Zeal Tokens.

Blighted ancient ice sacks function like runes, meaning having one in the inventory allows an ice spell to be cast via the spellbook. This also means autocasting with Ancient Magicks staves is an option.

Upon its removal, blighted entangle sack was given its function.

24623:
The divine battlemage potion is a stat-boosting potion that increases the player's Magic level by 4, and the player's Defence level by 5 + 15% of the player's Defence level for 5 minutes. During these 5 minutes, the player's Magic and Defence levels will not drain below the maximum boost of the potion. Although natural stat drain is disabled, a player's stats can still be decreased or increased by the use of other spells and potions.

Once the 5 minutes are over, any stats normally boosted by the potion will be reduced back to their base level; Preserve does not affect the duration of the potion. Drinking this potion will also damage the player by 10 Hitpoints. Trying to drink the potion with less than 11 Hitpoints will instead prompt the message: You need more than 10 hitpoints to survive the power of a divine potion.

Players are unable to cast Boost Potion Share to share the effect across a group of players.

It is created by using crystal dust on a battlemage potion, requiring 86 Herblore.

Mixing divine battlemage potions yields 0.5 experience per dose.

A swampbark body is a piece of swampbark armour worn in the body slot, requiring level 50 Magic and 50 Defence to equip. The body can be made with level 48 Runecraft by bringing a splitbark body and 500 nature runes to the Nature Altar. Doing so requires players to have first learnt the secret to infuse the armour via reading the runescroll of swampbark.

In addition to their stats, the helm, body, and legs increases the duration of bind spells by 2 ticks (1.2 seconds), with the full set increasing the duration by 6 ticks (3.6 seconds). For comparison, Ice Barrage binds players for 32 ticks (19.2 secs).

Bind: 8 ticks (4.8 secs) to 14 ticks (8.4 secs)

Snare: 16 ticks (9.6 secs) to 22 ticks (13.2 secs)

Entangle: 24 ticks (14.4 secs) to 30 ticks (18.0 secs)

It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.

Urium remains are an item found and used in the Shades of Mort'ton minigame. To obtain these remains, the player must kill urium shades, located behind a solid gold door in the Shade Catacombs.

To burn the urium remains, first place redwood pyre logs or rosewood pyre logs on a funeral pyre, followed by the urium remains, then light the pyre with a tinderbox. This will grant the player 500 Firemaking experience for redwood pyre logs and 590 Firemaking experience for rosewood pyre logs (750 and 885 respectively with elite Morytania Diary complete) and 120.5 Prayer (180.7 with hard Morytania Diary complete) experience. Neither the pyromancer outfit nor zealot's robes give any of their effects when burning shade remains.

Urium remains will always reward the player with either a gold shade key or some coins. Gold keys give unrestricted access to all areas of the Shade Catacombs and open the gold chests in the urium area of the catacombs, which give the best rewards out of all the chests.

Coins and keys dropped by cremating these remains will not despawn for five minutes, and cannot be taken by other players during this time. When dropped by the player, they will despawn and become visible to others at the normal rate.

Soaked pages are a possible catch from fishing at the reward pool with the reward permits from subduing Tempoross, or created at the Book of Storms with desiccated pages and level 50 Runecraft. They are used to charge the tome of water, which gives it additional effects.

Each soaked page adds 20 charges to the tome, and one charge is consumed when any combat spell from the standard spellbook requiring water runes is cast with the tome equipped. Each consumed charge increases damaging spells' accuracy and damage by 10%, non-damaging spells' accuracy by 20%, and curse spells' stat drain effects by 50%. Casting non-combat standard spells, or any spell from other spellbooks requiring water runes, will provide infinite runes and not consume any charges, including Ice spells. Players may remove the pages from the tome should they wish to do so.

An empty tome of water, fish barrel, tackle box, or big harpoonfish can be traded in to the Retired sailor for 25 soaked pages each.

Amethyst darts are Ranged throwing weapons. To wield them, the player must have at least 50 Ranged. They can be obtained by using the Mining, Crafting, and Fletching skills or trading with other players. Amethyst darts can be poisoned and are one-handed, so they can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection. To fletch amethyst darts, the player must have at least 90 Fletching. Amethyst dart tips are combined with feathers, awarding 21 Fletching experience per dart.

Amethyst dart tips can be crafted from amethyst, creating 8 amethyst dart tips and earning 60 Crafting experience for each mineral.

Amethyst darts have a +2 higher Ranged strength bonus compared to rune darts. The strongest dart type, dragon darts, have a +7 higher Ranged strength bonus advantage over amethyst darts. However, dragon darts are much more costly to use.

The Voidwaker gem is one of three pieces of the Voidwaker dropped by Venenatis and Spindel. The gem, alongside the Voidwaker hilt and Voidwaker blade, must be brought to Madam Sikaro in the Ferox Enclave Dungeon, who combines the three parts for a fee of 500,000 coins.

When inspected, a message in the chatbox states "A magical gem. It looks like it could be fitted into a powerful weapon. Perhaps someone in Ferox Enclave would know what it is?"
27690:
The Voidwaker is a melee weapon that requires level 75 Attack to wield. It is acquired by providing the Voidwaker blade, hilt, and gem to Madam Sikaro in the Ferox Enclave Dungeon, who will reassemble the weapon for a fee of 500,000 coins. The three parts are obtained separately as rare drops from Vet'ion, Callisto, and Venenatis (or their lesser counterparts) respectively. Its base stats are roughly comparable to an abyssal whip, and it has one of the most powerful damaging special attacks of any weapon in the game.

Attempting to combine the pieces on your own displays the message You don't think you have the skills to reassemble this weapon yourself..
27785: A mighty sceptre used in long forgotten battles.
28146: With some rope, adamantite bars and steel nails, I can create a sturdy harness.
28149:
The sturdy harness is an item used to combine the log basket and forestry kit into the forestry basket, combining the functionality of both items. This process can be reversed by right clicking the Forestry basket, heading into the configure options, and then choosing the dismantle option.

It is created by using the log brace with 2 ropes, 3 adamantite bars, and 45 steel nails, which requires 75 Smithing and Woodcutting to create.

To create the sturdy harness, combine the log brace with adamantite bars. The sturdy harness must be in your inventory before you can combine the log basket and forestry kit to make the Forestry Basket. The log brace alone will not work, and the combination will have no effect.

Prior to the 23 July 2025 QoL update, most players opted not to make the Forestry Basket because it had to be unequipped to bank their logs. However, this update now allows players to empty a filled log basket without clicking through multiple menus.
28152: A sacrifice to nature in the hope of an increase of yield in logs.
28154: I can use items with this for nature offerings.
28157:
Forester's rations are a stackable item used in Woodcutting. When in the inventory or stored in a Forestry kit, a player wielding or having a felling axe in their inventory (as the highest or equal-highest-tier axe, if multiple axes are carried) will receive 10% more Woodcutting experience each time they successfully chop a tree and gain a 20% chance not to receive a log. One ration is consumed each time a tree is successfully chopped with a felling axe (meaning Woodcutting experience is received), whether or not logs are gathered. When this happens, a game message in the chatbox will state You consume a Forester's ration to fuel a mighty chop. You strike a clean cut without gathering any material.

Sulliusceps are also affected by Forester's rations in the same way as trees that grant logs.

Additionally, if your run energy is under 90%, there is a 30% chance of consuming a forester's ration to restore 20% of your run energy when successfully chopping a tree. Both regular axes and felling axes can trigger this effect. When this happens, a game message in the chatbox will state You consume a Forester's ration and feel energised. if chopping with a regular axe or The Forester's ration restores some of your energy. if chopping with a felling axe.
28159:
The secateurs blade is an item purchased from the Forestry Shop for 20 anima-infused bark, as well as 10 noted oak logs and 5 noted willow logs. These logs can be bought on the Grand Exchange for 515.

With level 35 Woodcutting and Smithing, players can create secateurs attachments by combining the blade and an iron bar; each set will produce 50 attachments.
28161:
Secateurs attachments are a stackable item used in Woodcutting. While in the inventory or stored in a forestry kit, when players receive a leaf from cutting trees (a 1/4 chance for every log cut, regardless of Woodcutting level), a secateurs attachment is consumed and an additional second leaf is obtained.

They can be created by using a secateurs blade, purchased from the Forestry Shop, on an iron bar. This requires level 35 Woodcutting and Smithing, granting 32 Crafting experience; each set will produce 50 attachments.

They will not be consumed when failing to roll for a leaf, nor are they consumed from chopping trees that do not have a corresponding leaf, such as camphor, ironwood, or rosewood trees.
28163:
The clothes pouch is an item that needs to be attached to the Forestry kit or basket (irreversible process) to allow the player to store the lumberjack or Forestry outfit to receive the outfit's benefits without having to wear them. Players can receive a partial amount of Woodcutting experience if at least one piece of either the lumberjack or Forestry outfit is placed inside. The upgraded Forestry kit must be equipped or in the player's inventory to receive the bonus. Players who have achieved level 99 Woodcutting can store both the clothes and cape pouches inside the Forestry kit.

They can be created by using a piece of leather on the clothes pouch blueprint with a thread in the inventory. Doing so requires level 50 Woodcutting and Crafting, and the blueprint is consumed in the process. The kit does not change any interface options when the clothes pouch is attached to the Forestry kit.

If the forestry basket is destroyed while the clothes pouch is attached, new forestry kits from the forestry shop will come with the clothes pouch (with any clothing sets) already installed, along with any set stored with anima-infused bark ghost banked. However, the log basket and brace are lost and must be reacquired.

While the clothes pouch item itself weighs 1kg, when attached to the Forestry kit and with an outfit stored, the Forestry kit weighs 0 kg when worn.
28166:
The clothes pouch blueprint is an item purchased from the Forestry Shop for 10,000 anima-infused bark, as well as 300 noted willow and maple logs. These logs can be bought on the Grand Exchange for 9,600.

With level 50 Woodcutting and Crafting, players can craft a clothes pouch by using a piece of leather on the blueprint whilst having thread in the inventory.
28177:
The felling axe handle is an item used in the process of creating felling axes. Using the handle on any regular axe within a 3x3 area of an anvil, including through walls, with a hammer in the inventory will irreversibly turn it into a felling axe. The felling axe handle is available from the Forestry Shop for 10,000 anima-infused bark and 500 noted oak logs. These logs can be bought on the Grand Exchange for 20,500. While this item is free-to-play obtainable, the felling axes it creates are members-only.

Felling axes take priority over other axes when used to chop trees, even if you're wielding a normal axe.
28193: I need to put this in a pottery oven.
28196:

Players can create the axe by using a felling axe handle on a bronze axe while having a hammer in their inventory and standing next to an anvil; this process is irreversible, but the felling axe itself remains tradeable.

Bronze felling axes will chop at the same speed as a normal bronze axe. If the player is carrying forester's rations however (either in the inventory or inside a forestry kit), they will receive 10% more Woodcutting experience each time they successfully chop a tree and gain a 20% chance not to receive logs when chopping trees (or tree roots in the Rising Roots forestry event), at the cost of consuming one ration. This also results in a 20% chance to not receive anima-infused bark from tree roots.

If the player has no rations on their person, the felling axe will function like a regular bronze axe.

28295:
The berserker icon is an item obtained by using a chisel on a berserker ring.

Players can use a chisel on the berserker ring to create a berserker icon after completing Desert Treasure II. This process requires 80 Crafting(boostable), and is part of the process for creating the ultor ring.

After learning how to combine ring icons from Peer the Seer, the berserker icon can be used on an ultor vestige to create the ultor icon. The icon is then brought to a furnace alongside three chromium ingots and a ring mould to craft the ultor ring. The entire process requires level 90 Magic and 80 Crafting, which can be boosted.
28298:
The archer icon is an item obtained by using a chisel on an archers ring.

After learning how to combine ring icons from Peer the Seer, the archer icon can be used on a venator vestige to create the venator icon. The icon is then brought to a furnace alongside three chromium ingots and a ring mould to craft the venator ring. The entire process requires level 90 Magic and 80 Crafting, which can be boosted.
28304:
The seers icon is an item obtained by using a chisel on a seers ring.

After learning how to combine ring icons from Peer the Seer, the seers icon can be used on magus vestige alongside 500 blood runes to create the magus icon. The icon is then brought to a furnace alongside three chromium ingots and a ring mould to craft the magus ring. The entire process requires level 90 Magic and 80 Crafting, which can be boosted.
28307:
The ultor ring is one of four ancient rings which currently boasts the highest strength bonus of any ring, surpassing the imbued berserker ring by +4. The ring requires players to have killed Vardorvis at least once to wear, which is done during Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire; attempting to wear it otherwise will result in the message The ring slips off your finger. The power within it seems unfamiliar.

The ring requires level 90 Magic and 80 Crafting to create (both being boostable), as well as having learnt how to combine Fremennik ring icons with ancient vestiges via Peer the Seer.

Players who are able to craft the ring must first combine the berserker icon, 500 blood runes, and the ultor vestige, obtained as an untradeable drop from Vardorvis. Next, they must bring the resulting ultor icon to a furnace, alongside three chromium ingots and a ring mould, to craft the ring.

Unlike their predecessors, the Fremennik rings, the ancient rings cannot be imbued.
28310:
The venator ring is one of four ancient rings which currently boasts the highest ranged attack bonus of any ring, surpassing the imbued archers ring by +2, and also being the only ring to offer a Ranged Strength bonus. The ring requires players to have killed the Leviathan at least once to wear, which is done during Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire; attempting to wear it otherwise will result in the message The ring slips off your finger. The power within it seems unfamiliar.

The ring requires level 90 Magic and 80 Crafting to create (both being boostable), as well as having learnt how to combine Fremennik ring icons with ancient vestiges via Peer the Seer.

Players who are able to craft the ring must first combine the archer icon and the venator vestige, obtained as an untradeable drop from the Leviathan. Next, they must bring the resulting venator icon to a furnace, alongside three chromium ingots and a ring mould, to craft the ring.

Unlike their predecessors, the Fremennik rings, the ancient rings cannot be imbued.
28313: An occult ring that grants immense magical power.

It can be acquired as a drop from monsters found during breaches.
28567:

It cannot be opened if there is a player or obstacle in the way that would block the animation of opening it, and attempting to do so gives the message You must have nothing surrounding you to open this trinket..

It can be acquired as a drop from monsters found during breaches, as well as from looting the Deadman's chest.
28570:
The trinket of undead is an item in Deadman Mode that allows players to summon a special thrall of the player's choice, being either TzRek-Zuk, the Kalphite Princess, or Wisp. These thralls function the same as greater thralls, functioning as a melee, ranged, or magic thrall respectively. Though the trinket has no requirements to use, it does have a 10 second cooldown.

Being identical to regular greater thralls, the trinket's thralls always deal successful hits, with the damage roll ranging from 0-3. The damage roll can be increased to 0-15 with the sigil of the augmented thrall.

It can be acquired as a drop from monsters found during breaches, as well as from looting the Deadman's chest.

The tecu salamander is the strongest salamander that can be caught using a net trap and the Hunter skill at level 79, granting 344 Hunter experience, which can be found south-east of Ralos' Rise. Catching a matured tecu salamander is rare, as players often receive immature tecu salamanders instead; when an adult is captured, a message in the game chat will state The salamander is fully grown, you could use this as a weapon.

Tecu salamanders require level 80 Attack, Magic, and Ranged to wield. Irit tar is used as ammunition for the salamander. It is the best salamander to use for the two salamander-required Combat Achievements: The Worst Ranged Weapon and More than just a ranged weapon.

Despite being able to perform Magic and Ranged attacks, this weapon requires the user to be in the opponent's melee distance to attack, potentially reducing the practicality of the two attack styles. However, it can be used to attack enemies from behind fences, and can also attack enemies in diagonal squares, meaning that safespotting is still possible.

When using the Scorch (Slash) and Blaze (Magic) attack styles, the attack speed is 5. When using the Flare (Range) attack style, the attack speed is 4, which is similar in concept to the Rapid style of most ranged weapons, and it will use standard ranged defence, similar to bows.

Warning: This is a live creature; if unprotected it will run away when you die. Should this happen, you will need to buy or catch a new one.

The eclipse atlatl is a non-degradable two-handed ranged weapon that requires level 75 Ranged, 50 Attack, and 50 Strength to equip. It can be obtained as a possible reward from the Lunar Chest in Neypotzli. It uses atlatl darts as ammunition, which can be collected by Ava's devices.

Despite not being strung and using a “throwing” attack animation, the atlatl is categorically a bow and not a thrown weapon, and therefore deals standard-type damage.

Its max hit is determined by the player's melee strength bonus, while accuracy is still based on their ranged bonus, which is a unique mechanic among ranged weapons.

The atlatl's max hit mechanic means it pairs unusually with other equipment; endgame ranged gear is not best-in-slot as usual. Instead, the atlatl performs better against low-defence enemies when used in conjunction with high-strength equipment (e.g. amulet of strength, dragon boots), while end-game tribrid equipment such as Barrows gloves, amulet of fury, and aranea boots will usually outperform specialised ranged gear against high-defence enemies.

Though the atlatl's max hit is based on visible boosts to the player's Strength level (including potions), it does not benefit from melee prayers. Ranged prayers boost both accuracy and damage. Additionally, it uses the melee bonuses from the slayer helmet and salve amulets, but gains increased damage from Void Knight equipment whilst wearing the void ranger helm rather than the void melee helm.

When using the rapid attack style, up to 2,000 darts may be fired per hour. This makes the cost per hour 51,600 with Ava's assembler, 72,240 with Ava's accumulator if not picking up used ammo, or 258,000 if choosing to use a different cape for more damage, such as the Infernal cape.

The attack speed of the Atlatl varies; in player versus monster encounters, its base attack speed is 4, or equal to shortbows. During player versus player combat, its base attack speed is 5, unless the full Eclipse armour set is worn.
29004:
The eclipse moon chestplate is an item that requires level 75 Ranged and 50 Defence to equip, which is obtained as a possible reward from the Lunar Chest in Neypotzli.

As with all Moon equipment it is degradeable, much like Barrows equipment. The armour starts at 3000 charges and loses 1 charge for every 54 seconds in combat, meaning it lasts for 45 hours of continuous combat before breaking. Having an NPC such as Bob and Dunstan repair it costs 1,500,000 coins when fully broken, while repairing it yourself at an armour stand adds a discount of 7,500 coins per Smithing level, reducing the price to 757,500 coins at level 99.

The chestplate, along with all other Eclipse moon armour, functions as a very capable hybrid armour, with its strength bonuses and relatively high ranged bonuses. This is useful in situations where it is desireable to bring fewer armour switches, while still being effective in multiple styles.

Sulphur blades are a two-handed weapon that requires level 55 Attack to wield, obtained as a rare drop from sulphur nagua in Neypotzli. Like their crush and stab equivalents, the glacial temotli and earthbound tecpatl, it performs two independently rolled hits per attack. The maximum damage of each hit is determined by calculating the combined max hit as normal and dividing it by two. If the combined max hit is odd, one max hit is rounded up while the other is rounded down (e.g., 45 → 22 + 23).

Their stats are nearly identical to the dragon scimitar, trading 2 strength bonus for 5 more slash accuracy, although the scimitar paired with a defender is considerably stronger.

As sulphur blades deal damage in two hitsplats, they are very good for training combat on sulphur nagua due to them taking an additional 4 minimum damage for each hitsplat. Additionally, moonlight potions are easy to make nearby and can be used to provide prayer points and melee stat boosts.

Cooked wild kebbit is a type of hunter meat that restores a total of 8 Hitpoints when eaten, 4 are restored immediately, 4 are restored after a delay of 7 ticks (4.2s). The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 50 on both ranges and fires.

A teleport anchoring scroll is an item obtained as loot from zombie pirates and Zombie Pirate's Lockers. It can be read to become permanently impervious to teleport attacks by elder chaos druids and abyssal demons. This effect will not apply to teleport attacks from the Abyssal Sire, the Confusion attack of the Chaos Elemental, or the Tele Block spell.

Players are able to check if they have already read the scroll by right-clicking the "Check" option on the zombie pirate at the shipwreck found east of the Chaos Temple.
29458:
Adamant seeds are a magical type of seed that can be planted almost anywhere to grow some flowers in the ground, and are obtained as loot from zombie pirates and Zombie Pirate's Lockers.

Upon planting the seeds, the player will move one adjacent square east if possible; if there's an obstacle preventing movement to the east, the flowers will attempt to move the player to the west first, then south, then north. Once the flower is grown, players are then given the option to pick them, producing one of nine different colours of flowers.

Adamant seeds are primarily used in PvP activities in the Wilderness, as it forces the user to move one tile, which is useful for when the player is frozen. Mithril seeds, a variant of the item, will move the opposite direction from adamant seeds. The facts that seeds for both directions are available creates opportunities to outplay opponents by alternating which direction to move into while they try to log out from an aggressor by stepping on the frozen aggressor's tile.

When in combat, freshly planted adamant seeds do not provide the player with the option to pick the flowers. Instead, the first option is to "appreciate" the flowers, resulting in the player performing the Bow emote and the flowers remaining on the ground. This was a change that became necessary after a technique to get free hits in PvP against a player target under specific circumstances over and over by planting and picking up flowers was showcased but not extensively used during the finale of Deadman: All Stars.

Seeds are sometimes used to grief players training Hunter and Firemaking as well, as traps and fires cannot be placed on the same tile as a planted flower.
29486:
A cursed amulet of magic is an amulet uniquely dropped by necromancers in Great Kourend. It provides by far the lowest magic damage bonus for any item, at -80%.

The amulet's extreme penalty to magic damage has useful applications. It notably drops the maximum hit of Wind Strike above level 13 Magic from 8 to 2 and the maximum hit of Snare from 3 to 1; this allows Wind Strike or Snare to be used alongside the serpentine helm to apply venom to most NPCs, while still allowing them to regenerate to maximum Hitpoints. This technique is used to envenom while still giving kill credit to restricted accounts such as Ironmen and certain pures.

Against Olm, it can be used to keep his head turning while needing to delay dealing damage.
29577: Torn from the hands of ancient demons.
29580:
The tormented synapse is an item obtained as a rare drop from tormented demons, found in the Ancient Guthix Temple after completion of While Guthix Sleeps.

After reading Duradel's notes, which is obtained by talking to Kuradal and asking her about her father Duradel, players can use the synapse to create high-tier demonbane weapons.

Emberlight and the purging staff can only be made at an anvil, whereas the scorching bow has no such requirements.

You will need a hammer to create the Emberlight and the purging staff.

29784:
Araxyte venom sacs are items dropped by araxytes that serve as both a consumable and as a secondary ingredient used to create extended anti-venom+ potions. Each sac can upgrade one dose of anti-venom+ into a dose of extended anti-venom+, with this process requiring level 94 Herblore.

They can also be eaten to instantly cure venom and poison. Since they function as a normal piece of food, they can be combo eaten with karambwans. They provide immunity to poison for 11.7 minutes and venom for 0–18 seconds at the cost of dealing 4 venom damage a single time to the player; unlike most other sources of self-inflicted damage, this can kill the player. This is mostly done when acquired as a drop mid-trip, whilst the player has run out of anti-venom to drink. As they are stackable, they may also be used as protection from poison for very long trips whilst only taking one inventory space, such as during Dagannoth Kings tasks.

Unlike potions that cure poison or venom, the sacs will incur an attack delay of 3 ticks (1.8 seconds) when eaten, and clicking on the Hitpoints orb when afflicted does not consume one, even if it is the only form of antipoison available.
29796:
The noxious halberd is a two-handed polearm requiring level 80 Attack to wield. It is created by combining three untradeable components — the noxious point, noxious blade, and noxious pommel, all of which are rare drops from Araxxor.

As with all other polearms, the noxious halberd has a range of two tiles. Its most notable traits are that it attacks on a 5-tick cycle rather than 7, has more slash and strength bonus compared to the crystal halberd, and has a 33% chance (50% with a Serpentine helm equipped) to envenom the target (if not venom immune).

The noxious halberd will always deal the player's max hit when hitting the acidic, mirrorback, and ruptura araxytes that hatch during the fight with Araxxor. It can also deal full damage to the Corporeal Beast when on the stab attack style.
29801:
The amulet of rancour is the upgraded variant of the amulet of torture requiring level 90 Hitpoints to wear, providing best in slot melee strength and melee attack bonuses in all three types. It is made with level 86 Crafting by attaching the amulet of torture to an araxyte fang, which is a rare untradeable drop from Araxxor.

Compared to the amulet of torture, the amulet of rancour gains +10 melee attack bonuses and +2 strength bonus, but with negative bonuses for magic and ranged attacks.

The amulet of rancour can be recoloured to an amulet of rancour (s) by speaking to a man at the end of a series of tunnels within the Morytania Spider Cave, each of which have various requirements to pass through as alluded to in the venom-riddled note.
29806:
Aranea boots are a pair of boots dropped by araxytes. With no requirements to wear, they are currently the best-in-slot boots for one-defence pures and zerkers, due to the tribrid stats they have, with a ranged attack bonus between that of mixed hide boots and blessed dragonhide boots, a magic attack bonus equal to infinity boots, and a melee strength bonus equal to dragon boots.

The boots have a special web-negating mechanic that allows players to pass through webs in various locations without the need of a slash weapon. Additionally, the boots also negate certain special attacks once every 8 ticks (4.8 seconds) from arachnid bosses; when this occurs, a game message will state Your Aranea boots let you avoid the spider-based attack. The exception to this is Araxxor's venom cleave, which can be negated only once every 6 attacks, so every 12 seconds (20 ticks).

The following bosses can have their spider-based attacks negated:

Sarachnis' sticky web attack

Venenatis and Spindel's draining webs (The first tick is the only part of this ability negated)

Araxxor's venom cleave during his enrage phase

Araxxor's ranged auto attack; the magic auto attack is not negated.

Verzik Vitur's snapping webs during phase 3

29833: 1 dose of extended super antivenom potion.
29889: Glacial temotli are a two-handed blunt weapon that requires level 55 Attack to wield, obtained as a rare drop from frost nagua and Amoxliatl in the Ruins of Tapoyauik. Like their slash and stab equivalents, the sulphur blades and earthbound tecpatl, it performs two independently rolled hits per attack. The maximum damage of each hit is determined by calculating the combined max hit as normal and dividing it by two. If the combined max hit is odd, one max hit is rounded up while the other is rounded down (e.g., 45 → 22 + 23). As a multi-hit weapon, it is especially useful against monsters that have negative flat armour, such as Nagua, since all successful hits will do extra damage to them.
29895:
Frozen tears are a drop from creatures within the Ruins of Tapoyauik. They are used to charge the Pendant of Ates, in which each tear provides one teleport charge.

100 frozen tears can also be obtained by dismantling an inert Pendant of Ates.
29900:
Varlamorian kebabs can be purchased from Emelio after completion of the quest Meat and Greet, where the player helps him introduce kebabs to Varlamore. Like other kebabs, they heal a variable amount, varying between 3-30 hitpoints. Unlike other kebabs, they cannot drain your stats, and even have a chance to boost Attack, Defence, and Strength levels by 2.

On average, players will be healed by approximately 4 + 10% of their hitpoints level (based on current estimates) when eating a Varlamorian kebab. This is more than a normal kebab, with no risk of stat drain.

Like the standard kebab, Varlamorian kebabs cannot be made through the Cooking skill.
29944: A smooth and rich Aldarin Red that's said to flutter on the tongue.
29947:
Chilhuac Red is an alcoholic drink sold at Moonrise Wines on Aldarin. Drinking it restores 16 Hitpoints and temporarily boosts Firemaking by 1 while draining Attack by 5 and Cooking by 1.

Upon drinking the wine, a message in the chatbox will state, You drink the Chilhuac red. You feel a warmth spreading through you.

According to the book Moonrise Wines, Chilhuac Red has distinct flavours of cherry, jangerberry, marrentill, and mixed spices, pairing well with spicy curries, roasted meats, and kebabs.
29952:

Soiled pages are a possible drop from the Hueycoatl, or created at the Book of Earthen Might with desiccated pages and level 50 Runecraft. They are used to charge the tome of earth, which gives it additional effects.

Each soiled page adds 20 charges to the tome, and one charge is consumed when any earth spell is cast with the tome equipped. Each time a charge is used, it will increase a spell's accuracy and damage by 10%. Casting non-combat standard spells or any spell from other spellbooks spell requiring earth runes will provide infinite runes and not consume any charges. Players may remove the pages from the tome should they wish to do so.

30631: A missing piece from a magical staff.
30634:
The twinflame staff is a one-handed staff requiring level 60 Magic to wield. It is made by combining a battlestaff with the fire element staff crown and ice element staff crown, obtained from looting Branda the Fire Queen and Eldric the Ice King respectively. It acts as an infinite source of fire and water runes when casting spells, like the steam battlestaff.

The staff has an attack and cast speed of 6. It provides a 10% increase in accuracy and damage when casting spells from the standard spellbook, and will automatically cast the appropriate elemental spell for an NPC with a different elemental weakness than what the player is autocasting, provided that the player has the required runes and Magic level for the selected spell. For example, a player with level 75 Magic attacking a moss giant with Wind Wave will instead cast Fire Wave.

When attacking the walls during the Royal Titans fight, if a player has death runes in their inventory and is auto-casting Wave spells, the walls will be attacked using the relevant Blast spell for each type of wall, saving blood runes throughout multiple kills.

Additionally, when casting elemental spells (excluding Strike and Surge spells), the staff will fire off two spells at once; the second hit will land one tick after the first, dealing 40% of the damage dealt by the first, rounded down. Note that the second spell does not give Magic or Hitpoints experience, nor consume runes or any additional charges from the tome of fire or its other variants.

Taking into account the slower attack speed, the additional hit, and the 10% damage bonus, the twinflame staff has an effective damage bonus of 28% for standard spellbook spells. Compared to other autocasting staves, it will typically outperform most options other than the dragon hunter wand (against dragons) and harmonised Nightmare staff until 95 Magic, when Surge spells are at their full power. Compared to powered staves, it is a stronger option for most enemies without an elemental weakness until ~80 Magic. Against opponents with an elemental weakness, it can outperform most powered staves other than the Tumeken's shadow.

The steel ring is an item dropped by the deranged archaeologist. It has no requirements to equip and is the best-in-slot melee defensive ring, surpassing the ring of suffering (i). However, it has no Magic defence, Ranged defence, or Prayer bonuses.

It may be a more useful option for players who cannot afford a ring of suffering, or require better melee tanking equipment for encounters where they won't be attacked with other styles like the Moons of Peril. Other rings that provide offensive bonuses will usually perform better, but the steel ring can be useful for earlier in account progression, as the deranged archaeologist has very low requirements to defeat.

Unlike gold rings, it cannot be made with the Crafting skill using a ring mould at a furnace.

30957: Earthbound tecpatl are a two-handed stab sword that require level 55 Attack to wield, obtained as a rare drop from earthen nagua in the Tonali Cavern. Like their crush and slash equivalents, the glacial temotli and sulphur blades, it performs two independently rolled hits per attack. The maximum damage of each hit is determined by calculating the combined max hit as normal and dividing it by two. If the combined max hit is odd, one max hit is rounded up while the other is rounded down (e.g., 45 → 22 + 23). As a multi-hit weapon, it is especially useful against monsters that have negative flat armour, such as Nagua, since all successful hits will do an extra damage to them.

The greenman carving is an item created with a greenman mask, five ent branches, and one set of yew logs It requires 79 Fletching to produce, granting 70 Fletching experience.

It is used to build a greenman carving in either a dining room, combat room, or throne room in a player-owned house. Removing a built carving will return it to the player's inventory.
31027:
The greenman statue is an item created with a greenman mask, five ent branches, and one set of maple logs. It requires 53 Fletching to produce, granting 55 Fletching experience.

It is used to build a greenman statue in either a normal garden or formal garden in a player-owned house. Removing a built statue will return it to the player's inventory.
31032:
An ent branch is an item received from the Vale Totems minigame, which can be obtained as common loot from rummaging through Vale offerings, or bought directly from Vale Research Exchange for 20 research points.

Ent branches are primarily used to fletch atlatl dart shafts, yielding 100 shafts per branch. When using the "Make-all" option to fletch them into dart shafts, it will fletch 28 branches at a time. They are also used to create a greenman statue or greenman carving to place in a player-owned house.
31034:
The greenman mask is a cosmetic reward from the Vale Totems minigame, which can be obtained from rummaging through Vale offerings at a rate of 1/500, or bought directly from Vale Research Exchange for 500 research points. Ironmen (including group ironmen, despite them being able to trade the mask with fellow group members) with spare masks can trade them in to Ranulph for 125 Vale research points.

Its style can be changed to match various logs by using 300 of their corresponding tree leaves on it. This grants 20 Fletching experience and permanently unlocks that style, allowing players to freely switch between appearances on any mask item once unlocked.

The greenman mask can also be used to create a greenman statue and greenman carving to place in a player-owned house.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room.
31045: A tightly bound bundle of flax.
31049: A redwood hiking staff is a one-handed crush weapon made from a knife and one set of redwood logs. Despite the fact that it is a staff, the redwood hiking staff has no magical ability and cannot autocast any spells. Its primary use is to be used as a totem decoration during the Vale Totems minigame.
31081:
The antler guard is a tribrid shield slot item dropped by mature and elder custodian stalkers.

Requiring only level 50 Prayer to wield, its melee bonuses sit between an adamant and rune defender, ranged bonus between an unholy book and book of law, and magic bonus between that of an elemental tome and book of darkness. It shares the same strength bonus as a rune defender. Additionally, it has +2 ranged strength bonus and +5 prayer bonus. However, the main drawback of the guard is that it penalises all defence bonuses, so it is only recommended when players are not expected to be hit often.
31086:
Broken antlers are obtained as drops from Custodian stalkers within the Stalker Den.

With a chisel, they can be fletched into atlatl dart tips, yielding 100 dart tips per antler.
31088:
Avernic treads are boots that require level 80 in Defence, Strength, Ranged, and Magic to wear. They are dropped in their base form by the Doom of Mokhaiotl, and can be upgraded into stronger variants.

In their base form, the treads already surpass each of the primordial, eternal, and pegasian boots in accuracy and most defensive bonuses as well as providing a ranged strength bonus. However, they have slightly less strength bonus than the primordial boots and no prayer bonus compared to aranea boots.

The treads can be upgraded by adding a pair of primordial, eternal, and pegasian boots onto them. Each pair is added separately, and 4,000 demon tears are required per pair, for a total of 12,000 demon tears.
31099: A magical shard linked to Mokhaiotl.
31106:
The confliction gauntlets are an upgraded variant of the tormented bracelet requiring level 90 Hitpoints to wear, providing best-in-slot magic attack and magic damage bonuses. They are made with level 83 Crafting and level 70 Smithing by attaching the Mokhaiotl cloth, a rare untradeable drop from the Doom of Mokhaiotl, to a tormented bracelet alongside 10,000 demon tears. This process must be done at a bank and is not reversible.

Compared to the tormented bracelet, the gauntlets gain +10 magic attack bonus, some defensive bonuses and a +2% magic damage bonus, alongside a passive effect with one-handed magic weapons.

Demon tears are items used to charge the Eye of Ayak as an alternative to runes, or as part of the materials required to create the avernic treads and confliction gauntlets.

They are primarily obtained as drops from the Doom of Mokhaiotl. Alternatively, they can also be obtained by chopping infected roots in the Ruins of Mokhaiotl with 80 Woodcutting, providing a non-combat method of acquisition similar to that of Zulrah's scales from sacred eels. The Eye of Ayak can also be dismantled for 10,000 demon tears.

It takes 22,000 demon tears to fully upgrade both the Avernic treads (12,000 tears), including its base components, and craft the Confliction gauntlets (10,000 tears).

31487: Umbral coral can be harvested from a coral nursery after planting umbral frags. They are used to make Armadyl brews by first adding one to a vial of water to create an umbral potion (unf), and then adding rainbow crab paste.
31502:
Camphor saplings are saplings that can be used to grow camphor trees at level 66 Farming.

They can be made by planting a camphor seed in a filled plant pot, with a gardening trowel in your inventory, and then watering the camphor seedling with a watering can. When watered, the seedling will sprout into a sapling in one crop cycle (0-5 minutes).

Planting the sapling in a hardwood tree patch, with a spade in your inventory, will give 88 Farming experience. It will grow into a camphor tree after 5,120 minutes (3 days, 13 hours, and 20 minutes).

Players can ask the gardener to protect their tree from disease whilst it grows, which requires payment of 10 white berries. This payment can be noted.
31505:
Ironwood saplings are saplings that can be used to grow ironwood trees at level 80 Farming.

They can be made by planting an ironwood seed in a filled plant pot, with a gardening trowel in your inventory, and then watering the ironwood seedling with a watering can. When watered, the seedling will sprout into a sapling in one crop cycle (0-5 minutes).

Planting the sapling in a hardwood tree patch, with a spade in your inventory, will result in it growing into a ironwood tree after 5,120 minutes (3 days, 13 hours, and 20 minutes).

Players can ask the gardener to protect their tree from disease whilst it grows, which requires payment of 10 curry leaves. This payment can be noted.

31515:
Umbral frags are coral pieces that can be propagated in a coral nursery found in the Coral Nurseries, a location just off the eastern coast of the Great Conch. Compost of any type does not work on coral nursery farming patches.

Umbral frags require level 77 Farming to plant, producing an umbral coral when fully grown. Players can harvest umbral coral from the mature crop, which are used as an ingredient in Armadyl brews.
31541:
Flax seeds can be planted in a hops patch at level 18 Farming to yield flax. Three seeds are required per patch.

31543: A hemp plant seed - plant in a hops patch.
31545: A cotton plant seed - plant in a hops patch.

After planting the sapling in a hardwood tree patch and waiting for it to fully grow, which takes 5,120 minutes (3 days, 13 hours, and 20 minutes), the plant will grow into a camphor tree which can be cut to yield camphor logs (and grant Woodcutting experience).

31549:

31551: Plant this in a plantpot of soil to grow a sapling.
31556:
Swordtip squid is a type of fish that restores 15 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw swordtip squid on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 56 Cooking and granting 150 experience when successful.

When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt swordtip squid. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at level 91, or 85 if using a cooking range.
31561:
Raw jumbo squid is a fish caught by lantern harpooning, requiring level 69 Fishing alongside a lantern and harpoon. With lantern fishing spots exclusive to certain islands at sea, the minimum Sailing level to catch them is 47, the level required to dock at the Onyx Crest.

Raw jumbo squid can be crushed with a pestle and mortar into squid paste, an ingredient used to make haemostatic dressings. At level 71 Cooking, it can also be cooked to make jumbo squid that heals 17 Hitpoints each.

Like most raw fish, it can also be cut with a regular knife or chum facility to create fine fish offcuts to use as bait for various fishing activities. Each cutting action will also give a 1/512 chance of obtaining a squid beak, which is used to create wooden blowpipes. While using a chum facility, it is possible to obtain multiple beaks in one cutting action, depending on which chum facility is used, though the rate per action remains 1/512 regardless of how many squid are processed.
31564: Doesn't look too appetising, but looks can be deceiving.
31569:
Squid paste is made by using a pestle and mortar on raw swordtip or jumbo squids (obtained from lantern harpooning). It is used to make haemostatic poultice, which is the penultimate step in making haemostatic dressings.

Wesley currently does not crush raw squid.
31572:
A squid beak is an item that is used to create wooden blowpipes, obtained while cutting raw swordtip and jumbo squids at a rate of 1/1,024 and 1/512 respectively per cutting action.

If the player is cutting squids on the chum spreader and rolls to receive a squid beak, they will receive squid beaks equal to the number of squids cut on that tick (up to 4 beaks). Cutting squids with a full inventory does not reduce a player's chances, and any offcuts will drop to the ground to make room for the beak if obtained on the first cut of the inventory.

Spirit flakes and rada's blessing can be used for a chance to double catch squid.

Mithril cannonballs are ammunition used for a boat cannon during boat combat. They can be fired from mithril cannons or stronger.

Four can be made from a single mithril bar with level 55 Smithing, granting 34 experience per bar. Smithing cannonballs require the use of an ammo mould, which requires partial completion of Dwarf Cannon to obtain. Alternatively, a double ammo mould (requiring Foundry Reputation to purchase via the Giants' Foundry minigame) allows players to process two bars into eight cannonballs at the same speed as a regular ammo mould processes one bar into four.

Players with level 87 Sailing can further speed up smithing cannonballs by using the ancient furnace in the Grimstone Dungeon, which halves the time it takes to create cannonballs from 8 ticks to 4 ticks. Combining this with a double ammo mould, players can smith cannonballs at four times the normal speed.
31912:
Adamant cannonballs are ammunition used for a boat cannon during boat combat. They can be fired from adamant cannons or stronger.

Four can be made from a single adamantite bar with level 75 Smithing, granting 42.4 experience per bar. Smithing cannonballs require the use of an ammo mould, which requires partial completion of Dwarf Cannon to obtain. Alternatively, a double ammo mould (requiring Foundry Reputation to purchase via the Giants' Foundry minigame) allows players to process two bars into eight cannonballs at the same speed as a regular ammo mould processes one bar into four.

Players with level 87 Sailing can further speed up smithing cannonballs by using the ancient furnace in the Grimstone Dungeon, which halves the time it takes to create cannonballs from 8 ticks to 4 ticks. Combining this with a double ammo mould, players can smith cannonballs at four times the normal speed.

A repair kit is an item that heals 5 health to a boat. Players can simply click the item's "Apply" option whilst on a boat to repair damage, and multiple players can do so at once to rapidly repair the boat. Additionally, crewmates can also repair the boat if instructed to, and depending on their Deckhandiness level may heal more than 5 per kit.

Players can build repair kits with 2 planks, 10 bronze nails, and 5 swamp paste, granting 43.5 Construction experience and yielding 2 kits with the completion of Pandemonium quest. Unlike other repair kits, it can be created without a shipwrights' workbench simply by using the required items on one another in the inventory.

Like food, applying a repair kit incurs the same delay as eating during boat combat.

Dragon metal sheets are an item used in high-level shipbuilding, with some of the best facilities on a boat requiring multiple sheets to build.

With access to the dragon forge upon completion of Dragon Slayer II, players can make dragon keel parts for dragon keels as well as dragon nails (15 per sheet). Two sheets are used to make one keel part, while two keel parts are used to make one set of large dragon keel parts (requiring 4 sheets in total). As such, a total of 20 sheets are required for a dragon keel on a skiff, and 64 sheets for a sloop.

Completion of the Pandemonium quest is also required to be able to use sheets at the forge. Attempting to make something with a dragon metal sheet without having completed the quest displays the chatbox message "You probably shouldn't just go messing around with the dragon sheets without knowing what you're doing."

The best sources for these sheets are killing lava strykewyrms or frost dragons on task, however these can be quite tedious to obtain, especially if the player does not have enough slayer points to skip for them. A slower but more consistent method is completing bounty tasks for great white sharks, orcas, and high-levelled krakens (preferably armoured krakens), as one bounty task for each of these monsters are guaranteed at various notice boards across Gielinor.

Angler's paint is a type of boat paint used to recolour the trim of a player's skiff or sloop via the boat schematics board at the Shipyard. Trimming a boat requires level 25 Sailing and 20 Construction, granting 10 Construction experience. One paint is required for trimming skiffs, while sloops require two.

Angler's paint is received at a rate of 1/18,000 from deep sea trawling, or 1/16,200 from trawling mixed shoals upon a successful roll for a catch. Rod fishing at a shoal and crewmates will not roll for the paint. When receiving the paint, players will receive the message You've received some paint!.

Angler's paint, along with shark, inky, salvor's, and Barracuda paint, can be given to Trader Stan in exchange for merchant's paint.

Salvor's paint is received at a rate of 1/24,000 from sorting martial salvage. Along with angler's, shark, inky, and Barracuda paint, it can be given to Trader Stan in exchange for merchant's paint.

32309:
Raw giant krill is a type of fish caught from giant krill shoals whilst deep sea trawling, requiring level 69 Fishing and granting 112.5 experience per successful catch with a trawling net, or 22.5 if caught with a fishing rod. They can also be caught from shimmering shoals, which can yield other deep sea fish alongside giant krill.

Cooking giant krill requires level 69 in Cooking, resulting in a giant krill and 177.5 Cooking experience. If unsuccessful, it will result in a burnt giant krill instead.
32317:
Raw haddock is a type of fish caught from haddock shoals whilst deep sea trawling, requiring level 73 Fishing and granting 128.5 experience per successful catch with a trawling net, or 25.7 if caught with a fishing rod. They can also be caught from shimmering shoals, which can yield other deep sea fish alongside haddock.

Cooking haddock requires level 73 in Cooking, resulting in a haddock and 180 Cooking experience. If unsuccessful, it will result in a burnt haddock instead.

Raw haddock can also be cut into fish offcuts by using a knife, with a chance (scaling with Cooking level) of receiving a haddock eye, a herblore secondary used to make super fishing potions.
32325:
Raw yellowfin is a type of fish caught from yellowfin shoals whilst deep sea trawling, requiring level 79 Fishing and granting 155.5 experience per successful catch with a trawling net, or 31.1 if caught with a fishing rod. They can also be caught occasionally from shimmering and glistening shoals, which require level 69 and 76 Fishing to catch from respectively.

Cooking yellowfin requires level 79 in Cooking, resulting in a yellowfin and 200 Cooking experience. If unsuccessful, it will result in a burnt yellowfin instead.

Raw yellowfin can also be cut into fine fish offcuts by using a knife, with a chance (scaling with Cooking level) of receiving three yellow fin, a herblore secondary used to make extreme energy potions.
32333:
Raw halibut is a type of fish caught from halibut shoals whilst deep sea trawling, requiring level 83 Fishing and granting 195.5 experience per successful catch with a trawling net, or 39.1 if caught with a fishing rod. They can also be caught occasionally from shimmering and glistening shoals, which require level 69 and 76 Fishing to catch from respectively.

Cooking halibut requires level 83 in Cooking, resulting in a halibut and 212.5 Cooking experience. If unsuccessful, it will result in a burnt halibut instead.
32336:
Halibut is a type of fish that restores 20 Hitpoints when eaten.

It can be obtained by cooking raw halibut on a fire or cooking range. Cooking a halibut requires level 83 Cooking, and grants 212.5 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt halibut. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will only stop burning at level 99 when cooking at the Hosidius Kitchen with the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary completed.

Like cooked karambwan, halibut can be used as a fast food, a subtype of food that incurs non-standard attack or eating delays when consumed. Halibut may be consumed after other foods without delay; this does not work if the halibut is eaten first, and does not work when eating two halibut in a row. This technique (commonly referred to as combo eating) can be further enhanced by drinking a dose of Saradomin brew after your alternative food item, and before your halibut (food>brew>halibut).

A yellow fin is a Herblore secondary used to make extreme energy potions, requiring one fin per dose and granting 21 Herblore experience per fin. It can be obtained by using a knife on a raw yellowfin from deep sea trawling, yielding three yellow fins per yellowfin upon success, whose chance scales with the player's Cooking level.

If cutting on a chum facility, players will receive yellow fins equal to three times the number of yellowfin cut on that tick, assuming a successful cut. For example, a chum spreader can cut 4 yellowfin per tick, yielding a potential 12 yellow fins per tick.

32879:
The aquanite hopper is a ranged offhand requiring level 60 Ranged to equip. It is created by using an aquanite tendon on an anvil whilst having a mithril bar and hammer in the player's inventory, requiring level 60 Smithing and granting 350 experience.

The hopper is a purely offensive shield slot item with no defensive bonuses, but possesses a passive effect in which crossbows are given an 11% chance to fire a second shot when the hopper is equipped. This second shot has 33.3% reduced accuracy, 66.7% reduced damage, and 66.7% reduced enchanted bolt proc chance; if the first shot procs an enchanted bolt effect, the second shot will never do so.
32892:
A cupronickel bar is a metal bar used in shipbuilding, as well as certain island amenities. It can be smelted at level 74 Smithing by using 2 copper ore and 1 nickel ore on a furnace or by using the Superheat Item spell from the standard spell book.

When attempting to make cupronickel bars at the Blast Furnace, up to 14 nickel ore can be deposited at a time. As a result, players should deposit 18 copper ore and 9 nickel ore each run, withdrawing the bars once every three runs for a total of 27 bars per withdraw.
32904:
Camphor logs are logs, which can be cut from camphor trees, requiring 66 Woodcutting to chop and grants 143.5 Woodcutting experience per log. Their primary purpose is to be converted into camphor planks at a sawmill, costing 2,500 coins each, planks which are extensively used for boat upgrades and amenities in the Sailing skill. Alternatively, the Lunar spell Plank Make can allow players to convert them to planks at a lower cost, but at the expense of runes.

Players can also burn these logs with the Firemaking skill for 180 experience at level 66 or above.

Camphor trees are only located on the Great Conch, which requires partial completion of Troubled Tortugans. Players with level 66 Farming can also farm them by planting a camphor sapling at a hardwood tree patch.
32907:
Ironwood logs are logs which can be cut from ironwood trees, requiring 80 Woodcutting to chop and grants 175 Woodcutting experience per log. Players can burn these logs with the Firemaking skill for 220.5 experience at level 80 or above.

Players training Construction can bring ironwood logs to a sawmill to get a ironwood plank at a cost of 5,000 coins each. Alternatively, the Lunar spell Plank Make can allow players to convert them to planks at a lower cost, but at the expense of runes.

Ironwood trees are only located on Sunbleak Island, which requires 72 Sailing to dock at. Players with level 80 Farming can also farm them by planting an ironwood sapling at a hardwood tree patch.
32910:
Rosewood logs are logs which can be cut from rosewood trees, requiring 92 Woodcutting to chop and grants 212.5 Woodcutting experience per log. Players can burn these logs with the Firemaking skill for 268 experience at level 92 or above.

Players training Construction can bring rosewood logs to a sawmill to get a rosewood plank at a cost of 7,500 coins each. Alternatively, the Lunar spell Plank Make can allow players to convert them to planks at a lower cost, but at the expense of runes.

Rosewood trees are only located on Drumstick Isle, which requires level 79 Sailing to dock at. Players with level 92 Farming can also farm them by planting a rosewood sapling at a hardwood tree patch.

Because Drumstick Isle is far from a bank, having a greater teleport focus is recommended to chop large quantities, although this can be rather costly and/or even more time-consuming to obtain. Without the greater teleport focus, using the Prifddinas dock and sailing north to the teal portal is the fastest way to get to the isle. A log basket is recommended to extend trip lengths, and if intending to make planks out of the logs, a plank sack with runes and coins for Plank Make, as well as sawmill vouchers is a further optimisation.

33041:
The thunder khopesh was an unlock in the Grid Master community event. After the player builds a demonic throne in their player-owned house, the player is given the thunder khopesh.

It has a passive effect that grants standard, successful hits a 20% chance to summon a delayed lightning bolt at the target's location, damaging enemies in a 3x3 area for up to 50% of the player's max hit. The lightning bolt will be summoned at the centre of the target's location at the time the effect was triggered.

The lightning does not roll accuracy checks, but it is possible for enemies to move out of the effect between the attack triggering and the attack striking, causing them to avoid the damage entirely. No experience is gained from the damage dealt by the lightning bolts.

It is a corpbane weapon, meaning it does full damage to the Corporeal Beast.

The banner can be displayed by using it on furniture built in the League hall's banner stand space. Ultimate Ironmen can use this as a storage mechanism, but since a player may only build one league hall, only one league banner can be stored in a POH.
33305:
The demonic axe ornament kit is an ornament kit that changes the appearance of the soulreaper axe to the soulreaper axe (o). This process can be reverted at any time, returning the item and ornament kit.

It can be purchased from the Leagues Reward Shop for 10,000 League Points.
33308: Used on Iban's Staff to decorate it in the style of Leagues VI: Demonic Pacts.
33311: Used on a Trident of the Seas or Swamp, to decorate it in the style of Leagues VI: Demonic Pacts.
33342: The demonic quill is an item purchased from the Leagues Reward Shop for 3,000 League points. It can be combined with a slayer helmet to create an oathplate slayer helmet after unlocking the Oath Breaker Slayer Reward, for 200 slayer points.
33359: Can be read to unlock a new home teleport animation.
33362:
The demonic pacts throne scroll is an item purchased from the Leagues Reward Shop for 3,000 League points. It can be used on a demonic throne in a player-owned house throne room to change its appearance to resemble Yama's throne.

Note that the throne scroll can be removed without needing to remove the entire demonic throne.
33365: Used to unlock the Impish overrides for your Arceuus thralls.
33368: The demonic pacts demon butler scroll is a consumable item purchased from the Leagues Reward Shop for 4,000 League points. It can be read to unlock the ability to have your demon butler change his appearance to that of Yama's demon butler by talking to him.
33428:
The trinket of vengeance is an item in Deadman Mode and its seasonal variants Apocalypse and Armageddon which casts the Vengeance spell. Though it has no requirements to use, it retains the 30 second casting cooldown that the spell has.

Like the sigils, trinkets are dropped by most monsters (via the Deadman Mode drop table) and are tradeable on the Grand Exchange.

This trinket is not accessible in Deadman: Annihilation. In Deadman: All Stars Season 3, a version of the trinket that had only two charges before being destroyed was available.

33553:
Seeking bronze arrows are an improved variant of bronze arrows, boasting a +20 ranged attack bonus over their regular variants, as well as increasing the player's minimum hit from 1 to 3 upon a successful hit.

Seeking bronze arrows can be made through several ways:

Attaching bronze arrowtips to seeking headless arrows, granting 19.5 Fletching experience per set of 15.

Using seeking headless arrows on bronze arrows to create them in sets of 150. No experience is given for this.

Using a bucket of bloodwood sap directly on bronze arrows to create them in sets of 15 per bucket. This is never recommended, as the sap can treat higher tier logs that yield higher quantities of seeking arrow shafts per log.

33625:
Letvek are bait for hunting stymphikes, obtained by catching letvek in box traps with 76 Hunter, or through monster drops on Vampyrium.

At high Hunter levels, upwards of 700 letvek can be caught per hour with 3-tick manipulation, yielding approximately 145,000 experience per hour. With 1-tick trap resetting, 160,000 experience per hour is possible.

Letvek will run away if dropped, but they can be placed on a table. Letvek cannot be stored in the huntsman's kit.

33651:
Stymphike feathers are dropped by stymphikes caught using the Hunter skill, as well as from various monsters on Vampyrium.

They may be handed in to the aranei at the Apsul and Virer Hunting Grounds for limited off-task access to venators. Each venator kill requires 30 feathers, costing 2,790 per venator if purchasing from other players.

Stymphike feathers can also be used in place of standard feathers for fletching, when making bolts, darts, and arrows, however they are not able to be used for fly fishing.

Stymphike feathers may be used to pay the aranei scout near the portal to Castle Drakan to move the player's grave near to them, if they had died whilst fighting the Maggot King. Depending on the current prices of stymphike feathers, this may be the most cost-effective way to pay.
33657: Orikalkum gravel is unrefined orikalkum that can be obtained as a drop from venators and the Maggot King. It has no uses other than its high alchemy value.
33661: Venator fangs are an item dropped by venators and the Maggot King. These can be traded in for dragon arrowtips at a 1:1 ratio by speaking to the aranei by the aranei shrines in the Apsul or Virer Hunting Grounds, or by choosing their right-click "Trade-teeth" option.
33663: Venator teeth are an item dropped by venators and the Maggot King. These can be traded in for dragon dart tips at a 1:1 ratio by speaking to the aranei by the aranei shrines in the Apsul or Virer Hunting Grounds, or by choosing their right-click "Trade-teeth" option.
33821: Raw impaler meat is an uncooked food dropped by impaler deer. It can also be obtained from a cupboard in Sugadinti's Hideout during The Blood Moon Rises. When cooked, it behaves like normal meat, and can be made into either sinew or cooked meat.
